Chapter 371: Unidentified Zone (6)
There was only one condition for using the high-tier spatial magic, Absolute Stillness.
“The control of cognitive load.”
No matter the situation, one must maintain the quantity and density of one’s thoughts.
It sounded simple, but this was by no means an easy task.
“First, you must block off the senses that require cognitive processing.”
It was human nature to want to use convenient tools when they were available.
Thus, not only sight and hearing, but even mana detection—the privilege of mana users—had to be avoided.
This was to reduce the amount of cognitive load allocated to the information those senses brought in.
“Next, to exclude emotions, you must attain the state of a clear and tranquil mind—like a bright mirror and still water.”
Confusion, anger, fear, anxiety, doubt.
When humans feel emotions, their cognitive load spikes instantly.
Thus, emotions too must be blocked.
“You’re saying to block both senses and emotions….”
In other words, for that moment, one had to become nothing more than a doll.
Oscar scratched his head.
“Just hearing it makes it sound difficult. Can’t I just crash into it physically and refine it through trial and error?”
“That much, I cannot allow.”
The thought-form nodded firmly.
It was completely different from his usual easygoing demeanor.
With a face more serious than ever, he gave a warning.
“Let me tell you one thing. The reason I lost my wife… was also because of this magic.”
“…!”
The one thing Master Ado had regretted his entire life.
The experience of losing the person most precious to him due to his own mistake.
‘And to think it was because of this magic.’
Oscar, whose vigilance rose instantly, muttered.
“It’s a far more dangerous spell than I thought.”
“It is far more powerful than other spatial magic, and so its danger is equally great.”
To aid understanding, the thought-form lightly drew up some mana.
“Now then, this is reduced to one ten-thousandth of the size and power of the magic I usually use.”
A small mass of mana, about the size of two finger joints, floated before him.
It was barely enough to properly cast a single well-honed Wind Cutter.
“As I said, the activation condition of this magic is absolute stability. Blocking all senses and emotions of both mind and body. It is crucial to drastically reduce cognitive load so that the threads of space cannot have any flow whatsoever.”
“…What happens if you fail?”
“See for yourself.”
The threads around the thought-form all stopped moving at once.
However, perhaps because not all emotions and senses had been completely blocked, two or three threads fluttered slightly.
‘That much is nothing.’
Just as Oscar dismissed it as trivial—
“This is the result of an imperfect casting.”
“…?”
A question rose above Oscar’s head upon hearing those words.
After all, the Absolute Stillness currently displayed had no visible flaws.
‘It still feels as if all time in the area has stopped.’
The magic was confined to a tiny square space, barely 2 centimeters across, in front of the rock where the thought-form sat.
“Well?”
“To be honest, I don’t see much difference from the original—”
Before he could finish speaking—
‘Hm?’
At the very center of Absolute Stillness.
The space around the two or three faintly trembling threads warped without any warning.
That warped space rapidly expanded in the blink of an eye.
“…!”
In the process, it erased everything it touched.
Rock, trees, the ground—nothing was an exception.
By the time one could blink, everything between the two of them had vanished.
It looked as though that portion of space had been cleanly cut out with scissors.
Considering the tiny size of the Absolute Stillness that had been cast, the destructive power was incomprehensible.
“This is the spatial collapse phenomenon that inevitably occurs when Absolute Stillness is incomplete. Once it erupts, even I cannot do anything about it.”
“……”
Did Master Ado lose his wife in the desert while using this magic?
Oscar muttered, his face filled with bitterness.
“It really happens in an instant.”
The rampaging space devoured everything around it in the blink of an eye.
Just as a sword has no eyes, this space too has none.
“That is why you must train and train again until you can use a perfect Absolute Stillness. It is a magic that tolerates not even the slightest mistake. Of course, someone as talented as you may master it faster than the original body.”
“When do you estimate that might be?”
“At least a year.”
A year… too long.
Given that something could happen as soon as tomorrow, there was no room to train leisurely.
Especially now, the quiet Great Emperor was what concerned him most.
Noticing his thoughts, the thought-form spoke.
“No matter how distant the destination, if you take it one step at a time, you will eventually arrive. Do not try to rush it all at once—learn it slowly, as a task of a lifetime.”
That was true.
There was no need to close the fourth spatial rift in haste.
It would be better to resolve everything he was curious about here before closing it.
“Ah, come to think of it….”
Something came to mind, and Oscar asked.
“Have you ever experienced a subspace suddenly changing?”
“The subspace changing? What do you mean?”
“Well….”
Oscar explained what had happened while transferring the dragon’s records into the subspace.
The thought-form frowned.
“…I have no idea what you’re talking about. Does that even make sense?”
“Then would you like to see it yourself?”
“Please!”
As they opened the subspace and moved inside, the thought-form’s eyes widened.
“Well, in all my life… no, I’ve already died. In any case, this is my first time experiencing something like this.”
“What do you think about this phenomenon?”
“Let me take a closer look.”
The thought-form walked around the subspace where information was being engraved, and even viewed some of the memories directly.
In the process, he realized that this was not merely a record and let out an exclamation.
“Ha!”
After pondering for a long time, he seemed to reach his own conclusion and nodded.
“I think I understand what it feels like.”
“Really?”
“Yes. First, let me ask you something. Do you understand what kind of place the subspace is?”
“My master said it is a rift between dimensions.”
“That is correct.”
Using overwhelming mana and spatial magic to tear a crack in a dimension and utilize that opening—
that was the basic mechanism of subspace.
“Subspace is fundamentally an extremely closed-off place. Even the normal concept of time does not apply.”
“Ah, is that why the time ratio changes whenever subspaces are layered?”
“Indeed. After all, you are opening another dimensional rift within a dimensional rift.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The thought-form continued his explanation.
“In my view, this vast record accumulated by the dragon seems to have gone beyond the definition of a mere record.”
“…What do you mean by that?”
“This… is flowing.”
Flowing?
Oscar blinked.
“You mean these massive records have acquired a new property?”
“A number is just a number. But what happens when numbers are connected in sequence?”
“They gain consistency and form certain rules.”
“Exactly. These records, written over billions of years, also seem to contain a great flow of time.”
A flow of time.
Then did that mean the flow of time was being added to his subspace?
“When I went to meet the Sage of the Star, he once said that the attributes of time and space are called divine authority.”
“Time flows endlessly like an unstoppable river, and space stretches infinitely like an unfillable sky. A famous phrase.”
“Then if an unceasing river and the sky mix together, what happens?”
“I do not know.”
The thought-form shrugged.
“Even if the original body were alive, he would not be able to answer that question. It lies in the realm of the unknown.”
“Hmm… I hope nothing strange happens.”
“In my opinion, it will not harm you. Rather… since the concept of time, which did not exist before, is being added, won’t the things you can do increase?”
“Ah.”
The moment he heard that, what came to mind was a personal training room.
He had once tried it before, but failed because the time ratio was forcibly unified.
The thought-form nodded upon hearing this.
“I believe it is entirely possible. Of course, that assumes this engraving process comes to an end.”
“…When on earth will this process finish?”
“Who knows? Perhaps it will not end until before you die.”
The thought-form chuckled.
“More importantly, those lizard fellows must be in quite a panic. Their most treasured possession has fallen into the hands of a mere human.”
“I’ve actually been thinking about how to use this situation.”
According to Seiro, he was only the vanguard.
That meant the entire dragon race would soon return to this star.
‘Even if I know they left to save the star….’
He did not fully believe those words yet.
He intended to verify that part once the engraving process in the subspace was complete.
“Hmm.”
At that moment, the thought-form suddenly clutched his head and staggered.
It was the first time he had shown such a reaction, and Oscar asked in alarm.
“Are you alright?”
After quickly steadying himself, he looked around the subspace and spoke.
“…I am fine, but for now, it would be better to leave this place quickly.”
After coming outside, he sat on a rock to rest and said,
“As you know, I am a thought-form. A being created based on a certain past time period experienced by the original body. But suddenly, the flow of time rushed in, and it seems I was swept up in it.”
“Is that bad?”
“Well… this is also my first time experiencing something like this, so I do not know. But will anything truly happen?”
As always, he smiled lightly.
“The conversation has strayed quite a bit, but what we must do is clear.”
Training.
* * *
Absolute Stillness was a magic that could only be manifested by emptying the senses and emotions and restricting cognitive load to the extreme.
The training method for this was simple, if one could call it that.
“Empty yourself. Everything about you.”
“….”
The training began with emptying.
Emptying the five senses was already somewhat familiar.
He had experienced it once while training to feel the threads of space.
“Discarding the five senses is clean and straightforward.”
His previous life also helped in this regard.
When one rolled through countless battlefields, there were often moments when one had to paralyze one or two sensory organs.
The problem was what came next.
“Emptying emotions is not as easy as it sounds.”
It required attaining an immovable heart that would not waver in any situation.
It was like asking a human to become a dragon.
‘Looking at it now, Edna was truly ruthless. How on earth did she manage this?’
As an observer, the most necessary quality for recording only the truth without personal bias was precisely that immovable heart.
Of course, dragons had near-infinite time, so they could simply achieve it eventually.
‘I’d like to train inside the subspace where time flows slowly, but….’
After that incident, he felt reluctant to enter the subspace together with the thought-form.
There was no harm in being cautious.
That said, training alone was not very meaningful.
It was difficult to judge for oneself whether one had truly emptied all emotions.
On the day when Oscar’s training with the thought-form entered its first month,
a small spatial crack appeared on one side of the forest.

Chapter 372: Unidentified Zone (7)
“Huff, huff.”
Oscar, bracing both hands on his knees, let out ragged breaths.
Drops of sweat falling from his face and hair dripped steadily onto the dirt ground, soaking it.
“Let’s call it a day here.”
“L-Let’s go a little… a little more.”
Oscar hurriedly lifted his head and replied.
At that, the Thoughtform stroked his beard and spoke.
“Come over here and sit for a moment.”
As he, seated on a rock, offered the spot beside him, Oscar reluctantly took a seat.
“Is there something you wish to say?”
“I simply wanted to tell you that you’re following along well. Your speed in emptying your thoughts is improving day by day, isn’t it? Your emotions are also in quite a refined state now.”
“……That alone isn’t enough.”
For the first time in a long while, it felt like he had run into a wall.
It had already been a month since he began training.
And yet, he still couldn’t even grasp the method for emptying his emotions.
“To be honest, it is a bit frustrating. You did say it would take about a year before I started, but I thought I’d be able to do it quickly.”
Entering a state of no-thought was not particularly difficult.
He had already done it countless times in his previous life.
So he assumed no-mind wouldn’t be much different…
It was a misconception born from knowing nothing at all.
“The original body divided the depth of emotions that humans can control into three stages.”
The Thoughtform continued in a calm voice.
“The easiest to control among them are the ‘intervening emotions.’ These are emotions that arise after you feel something, when consciousness intervenes. Simply put, things like irritation, annoyance, or suspicion.”
“They do sound easy to control.”
“With a single deep breath, they can be easily managed.”
These were emotions Oscar had already finished refining.
He wasn’t particularly hot-tempered to begin with, so it hadn’t been difficult.
“The next level, harder to control, is the ‘reflexive emotions.’”
Reflexive emotions.
Raw emotions that burst out before one’s consciousness can even intervene.
“Things like being startled, shrinking back in fear, or instinctive wariness fall into this category.”
For ordinary people, it is impossible to control these through training alone.
It requires perfect control over both mind and body.
“However, you managed to control even this stage after just one month of training.”
“I guess I’m just not the type to get scared easily.”
Perhaps it was because he grew up rough in the back alleys.
His temperament was rather composed.
Even when someone jumped out from behind a wall to scare him as a child, he barely reacted.
So he wasn’t particularly afraid of ghosts, nor did he feel much disgust toward insects.
“What keeps blocking you now is likely the third stage of emotion—the ‘persistent emotions’ that reside at the deepest level.”
“Persistent emotions?”
“Emotions such as lingering attachment, regret, responsibility, or a sense of duty. They rise even when you try not to think about them, and cling stubbornly even when you try to shake them off.”
He saw straight through Oscar’s condition.
“From what I’ve observed, you are feeling impatience right now. Am I wrong?”
“……I can’t deny it.”
“What exactly is making you so uneasy and restless?”
What was making him uneasy and restless?
Oscar posed the question to himself.
‘Is it because of the Great Emperor?’
Of course, it was an undeniable truth that that bastard was a problem.
From the day he met the Great Emperor at the Future Soul Research Institute, every passing minute and second felt precious.
Like someone with a time bomb strapped to the back of his neck, he felt constantly pressed and restless.
‘But that’s not the whole reason.’
Oscar slowly closed his eyes.
The threatening Great Emperor, the flowing time, the events that pressed in without giving him a moment to catch his breath—
All of them contributed to his impatience, yet each one missed the core by a little.
“…….”
His consciousness sank downward, deeper and deeper.
And what Oscar saw there was one thing.
‘So that’s it.’
What remained in the deepest part of his heart were people.
All those who had trusted and followed him until the very end.
They were all smiling brightly, yet he couldn’t even manage the faintest smile.
‘……Because I haven’t repaid them yet.’
When he saw the peaceful world after the Great Emperor disappeared, he thought his choice hadn’t been wrong.
He thought he had atoned to those left behind by restoring the fallen White Tower.
He thought he had faced his ancestors by returning lost magic and legacies to their rightful places.
That was what he believed.
No—what he had mistaken.
Because he thought everything he needed to do was finished.
‘Maybe… the reason I rushed without realizing it was because of that.’
He had received so much, yet hadn’t returned nearly enough.
Perhaps that was why he wanted to repay his debts all the more quickly.
Only then could he stop blaming himself.
‘This impatience didn’t suddenly appear.’
He had carried it ever since the day he made his choice, though it had been hidden until now.
The reason it surfaced was likely because he learned that the Great Emperor wasn’t dead.
That bastard’s existence had acted as a kind of trigger.
‘Is it something like a sense of debt?’
Perhaps it was because he had been an orphan.
He always disliked being indebted to others, and when he owed something, it felt as if a stone had been placed on his chest.
His master had softened that part of him a great deal while they lived together, but it seemed one’s nature couldn’t be completely hidden.
“Hoh.”
As he slowly opened his eyes, the Thoughtform asked,
“Have you found the reason?”
“Yes.”
“What was it?”
“A sense of debt.”
At the explanation that followed, he nodded.
“I see, that makes sense. But then let me ask you one thing. If you were to erase that Great Emperor’s soul, do you think the sense of debt you feel now would disappear cleanly?”
“……No. Somehow, I don’t think it would.”
“And why do you think that?”
After a brief silence, Oscar spoke.
“Those people didn’t follow me just to kill the Great Emperor.”
Even if he had chosen a different path, they would have still followed him.
Because they chose him as a person, not any particular choice.
“Then even if the Great Emperor’s soul is erased, where does your sense of debt come from?”
“……From my choices.”
The choices he made, and what he received as a result.
The sacrifices of his comrades, and what they entrusted to him.
And even himself, now standing atop all of it.
“Compared to what I’ve received, what I’ve given back is far too little.”
“Then what do you think you must do to completely erase that sense of debt?”
One thing was certain—erasing the Great Emperor’s soul alone would not be enough.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
That would merely be removing the immediate problem at hand.
“…….”
After thinking for a long time, Oscar cautiously opened his mouth.
“The things that were left behind.”
The things his comrades entrusted to him as they departed, the things he had to carry on.
When those things were properly settled and no longer needed him—
“When the moment comes that it’s okay even if I disappear… only then do I think I’ll be able to face them without shame.”
“That sounds like you. But it will take an enormous amount of time to reach that point. Which also means you won’t be able to use a perfected Absolute Stillness until then. You know that, don’t you?”
“I do.”
Absolute Stillness was the pinnacle of spatial magic.
He knew that whether or not he could use it would change the course of battle.
And yet, there wasn’t a trace of regret on Oscar’s face.
“Even so, I think this is the only way I’ll feel at ease.”
“Heh, very much like a mage.”
The Thoughtform quietly laughed and stroked his beard.
“As long as you can’t use perfected Absolute Stillness, you won’t even dare challenge the 44th floor.”
“Is it that difficult?”
“Even if it has lost its reason, its base level remains what it is.”
After a brief moment of thought, the Thoughtform spoke.
“We’ll need a second-best option.”
“A second-best option?”
“Indeed. If you cannot use Absolute Stillness through the proper method, shouldn’t we consider another approach? Of course, if the chances are slim or there’s no way to make it work, then we should give up cleanly when the time comes.”
From that moment on, the two of them began putting their heads together, researching a workaround—an expedient alternative.
Since entering a state of no-thought and no-mind had become impossible, they had to grasp even at such straws.
“What if we try using divine power?”
“Hmm. Divine power… divine power, you say.”
“Basically, divine energy clears the mind and improves concentration, so wouldn’t it help in some way?”
In theory, it wasn’t much different from a high-grade supplement.
“I’m not sure. Borrowing divine power would help dilute and reduce negative emotions, but it wouldn’t completely empty emotions themselves, would it? In that case, it won’t be of much help.”
Alright, then we’ll just let divine power keep playing with the Great Emperor…
Oscar introduced a new “supplement.”
“What about the energy of extreme cold?”
“Hmm. Extreme cold, extreme cold… extreme cold?”
The Thoughtform muttered in a slightly intrigued voice.
“Not bad. In fact, it’s said that extreme yin elixirs and essences such as Extreme Ice Crystals or Ten-Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng can freeze even emotions.”
“Uh… I’ve actually consumed something called an Extreme Ice Crystal.”
“Really?”
The Thoughtform’s expression immediately turned uneasy.
“But… didn’t you say you received and consumed the World Tree’s fruit from the Great Emperor?”
“That’s right.”
“And you also took the inner core of the Heavenly Silkworm?”
“It was quite a decent elixir.”
“And didn’t you say you chewed up an entire Dragon Heart not long ago?”
“It was so big my jaw hurt a bit after finishing it.”
The inner core of the Heavenly Silkworm, the World Tree’s fruit, the Dragon Heart…
These were elixirs and essences that most people would be lucky to consume even one of in a lifetime.
And yet all of them had gone into that mouth.
And it didn’t even end there—now an Extreme Ice Crystal as well?
“Why not just compile an elixir encyclopedia in your stomach at this point? If there’s more you’ve consumed, speak now.”
“There’s something the younger Oscar took before I entered this body… but I don’t know what it was.”
“Hah.”
No wonder, for a 7th-circle mage, his mana was absurdly high.
To think the reason was enough elixirs to build an entire magic tower.
And even if one had mountains of gold, something like a Dragon Heart couldn’t be purchased at all.
“Well, that too must be your fortune. Perhaps it’s a reward from the gods to a hero of a previous life.”
“I’ve never thought of it that grandly, but I did eat a pretty balanced variety.”
“Then this makes things easier.”
The Thoughtform quickly came up with a plausible method.
“If you’ve consumed an Extreme Ice Crystal and gained the energy of extreme cold, then you should be able to freeze not only your thoughts but your emotions as well. This could produce an effect similar to the state of no-thought and no-mind required for perfected Absolute Stillness. Shall we try it?”
“H-How exactly do I do that?”
“……You’re asking me that right now?”
Oscar gave an awkward smile.
Truthfully, he had never used the energy of extreme cold for anything beyond making the wind colder.
In fact, when he used it in magic, he simply perceived it as ‘the wind feels cooler.’
“Hoo, you have a long way to go. First, try drawing up the energy.”
The moment he drew up the energy of extreme cold, his body temperature dropped.
“In that state, imagine filling your entire body with that energy.”
Filling his whole body with extreme cold.
Oscar nodded readily and expanded the energy that had been lingering in his mana circuits.
Then, as a chill that felt as though every cell would freeze spread through him—
“…….”
The world became eerily silent, as if it were a lie.

Chapter 373: Unidentified Zone (8)
In the extreme cold, even thought itself seems to freeze, and the flow of thinking slows.
His mind turns blank, like a snowfield thickly covered in white.
A literal state of nothingness, where not even a stray thought arises.
“…….”
The frigid cold did not stop there; it quickly froze his emotions as well.
Not only the doubt of whether this would even work,
but even the constant sense of urgency that had been pressing him forward no longer truly reached him, at least for now.
“……Hoo.”
A pale breath spilled from between his lips.
Within the state of complete emptiness forcibly entered by harnessing the energy of extreme cold,
Oscar instinctively reached out his hand.
Right now, he could unfold it.
‘P e r f e c t A b s o l u t e S t a s i s .’
But at that moment, the Thought Entity rushed at him, grabbing him and rolling him across the dirt.
“Damn it! Withdraw your mana right now! Come to your senses, I say!”
“…….”
His mind turned sluggishly, taking a long time before the question ‘Why?’ surfaced.
For now, he followed the demand and withdrew his mana.
“Hoo.”
Confirming that state, the Thought Entity wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and extended a hand.
Oscar took it and stood up, asking,
“What happened all of a sudden? It seemed to be working fine.”
“……Working fine, you say?”
The Thought Entity wore a complex expression that could not be described in words.
After a brief moment of thought, he slowly opened his mouth.
“Yes. From a technical standpoint, there was no problem. You did enter a state of complete emptiness quite splendidly.”
“That’s right. In that state, wasn’t I supposed to use Absolute Stasis?”
“Do you not feel that something has changed compared to before?”
“Even if you say ‘before’…….”
The time he had drawn upon the energy of extreme cold was, quite literally, only a fleeting moment.
Even stretching it, perhaps about three seconds.
Could anything really have changed in such a short time?
“No.”
“Hm. I see, is that so.”
Letting out a deep sigh, the Thought Entity began asking various questions.
“Then how do you think you would feel if I suddenly started hitting you for no reason?”
“Well, I’d be taken aback.”
“Hm. Then this time, imagine the stench of rotten meat piercing your nose.”
After throwing out several such incomprehensible questions, the Thought Entity nodded.
“As expected.”
“What exactly is the reason for this?”
“You entered a state of complete emptiness through the energy of extreme cold. Though it is a workaround, it was a state flawless even compared to the orthodox method. The problem lies in the side effects.”
“……Side effects?”
Oscar examined himself.
His mana circuits were fine, and there were no injuries to his internal organs, bones, blood vessels, or muscles.
“There were side effects?”
“There were. And quite serious ones at that.”
With a grave expression, the Thought Entity continued.
“To use Absolute Stasis, one must empty both thought and emotion. However, since you are in a state where that is impossible, you used the workaround of extreme cold. As a result, you were able to enter a state of complete emptiness… but the form is somewhat different.”
“Can it really be different?”
Isn’t it the same state of not thinking and not feeling anything?
At Oscar’s question, he nodded.
“To use Absolute Stasis, I cleanly empty my thoughts and emotions. But you are freezing them. Of course, in that moment they do not function, which is the same—but the problem comes afterward.”
“Afterward, you say….”
“What is emptied can simply be filled again. As long as there is room in the granary of the mind, it is quickly resolved. But once something is frozen, it requires time to thaw.”
The Thought Entity looked at him with a pitiful gaze.
“Do not be alarmed as you listen. From what I can see, two of your emotions are already frozen.”
“What? That can’t be.”
Letting out a hollow laugh, Oscar denied it.
If his emotions had frozen, he would have been the first to notice.
“If that were true, which emotions are frozen?”
“One is discomfort.”
“Discomfort?”
“Indeed. When I asked you to imagine the stench of rotten meat piercing your nose earlier, do you remember what you answered?”
“I said it wouldn’t bother me at all—……huh?”
Oscar felt a sense of bewilderment.
Ordinarily, if one smelled rotten meat, it would be natural to frown.
That smell is extremely disgusting and unpleasant.
What was strange was that although he understood that with his head, he did not feel that way.
‘Right now… not really?’
He felt no sense of discomfort or disgust whatsoever.
It was not simply because he could not smell it.
Even when he tried to forcibly recall the feeling of discomfort, he could not even remember what that emotion felt like.
“……Indeed, it seems my emotion has frozen.”
With a hollow laugh, Oscar asked,
“What is the other emotion that has frozen?”
“Joy.”
Joy?
As Oscar blinked, the Thought Entity spoke.
“An imperial knight discovered a demon in pitch-black darkness. How do you think that was possible?”
“……I’m not sure?”
“It was thanks to night vision.”
“?”
“Look at this. You have lost the emotion called joy.”
“I’m sorry, but that just sounds like a terribly unfunny joke…….”
“Then try recalling the most joyful moments of your life.”
At those words, Oscar searched through his memories.
There were many times that had been happy and joyful.
Even just since he awoke in this young Oscar’s body…
“Hmm?”
The moments that he had once laughed and chatted through, believing them to be joyful, now felt flat.
He then reached back even to his previous life, but the result was the same.
Not a single memory could make him smile.
“See? You don’t even laugh at my joke. That means the emotion of joy has frozen.”
“Damn it, no matter how I think about it, that joke was terrible… but it does seem my emotions have frozen.”
Discomfort and joy.
Those two emotions were frozen, and he could not feel them.
Oscar furrowed his brow.
“If the frozen emotions thaw, will I be able to feel them again?”
“I believe so. For an emotion to remain frozen permanently, mana would need to be supplied continuously. However, when it will thaw is something no one can know.”
Emotions freezing.
Oscar’s mind began to turn rapidly.
“Discomfort and joy don’t seem to have much relation to each other… so it seems the type of emotion is random.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“I agree. But since one cannot know which emotion will freeze, it would be best to refrain from using Absolute Stasis through extreme cold.”
“……That certainly seems to be the case.”
His first thought was that he was fortunate those were the emotions that had frozen.
If something like vigilance had frozen, he would have been completely unable to respond to surprise attacks.
After pondering for a long while, Oscar finally raised the white flag.
“Very well. Let’s seal it.”
Absolute Stasis using the energy of extreme cold carried too great a risk.
In that case, things returned to square one.
“Well, then there’s no helping it.”
The Thought Entity shrugged.
“Just continue your training diligently.”
* * *
It was over forty days after beginning his training that Oscar discovered ‘that.’
“Hmm?”
Running through the forest early in the morning, Oscar noticed something on the dirt path and blinked.
Then he stared at a space that could not be described.
‘Slightly bigger than my fist?’
That blackened, dead space looked like a failed crack in space.
The mana he felt from it was that of the Thought Entity.
When he returned and asked about it, the Thought Entity frowned.
“What are you talking about? My mana?”
“The wavelength of the mana is over 98% identical.”
“I don’t recall creating anything like that in the gaps I manage. Could you have seen it wrong?”
“I’m telling you, it’s real.”
“If that’s the case, I should see it for myself. Lead me there.”
When Oscar returned to the place with the Thought Entity, his eyes widened slightly.
“Huh? This… wasn’t this big before.”
“What do you mean?”
“When I saw it about an hour ago, it was just a bit bigger than my fist. Now it’s as big as my upper body.”
“Then it grew this much in such a short time.”
The Thought Entity, staring at the hole, spoke.
“……And indeed, the mana code it emits is similar to mine.”
“I told you.”
“But it is not my mana.”
Thinking he might be insisting stubbornly, Oscar glanced at him, but the Thought Entity’s face was serious.
“It lacks the delicacy of my mana, but in exchange its output is stronger.”
“Then does that mean—?”
“……Something seems to have gone wrong.”
Shaking his head, the Thought Entity stood.
“How can the mana of something that should be on the 44th floor be felt here?”
“Don’t tell me… the cracks in space have connected?”
“My original body created those cracks in entirely different dimensions. Under normal circumstances, they should never connect—.”
At that moment, the Thought Entity suddenly trailed off and looked at him.
“Could it be… because of that subspace back then?”
“Excuse me?”
Suddenly pointed out as the culprit, Oscar made a bewildered expression.
“……It’s not impossible. No, rather, it makes sense. Look.”
The Thought Entity created two spheres of space.
One hovered above, the other below.
“Originally, these cracks in space should never meet. That is because the dimensions themselves—what my original body called channels—are different.”
Tap.
At that moment, the Thought Entity created a new sphere in the space between them.
“But then your subspace entered the picture. And since it is a space undergoing tens of billions of years of imprinting, it is extremely easy to pinpoint.”
“……So does that mean the one on the 44th floor is trying to enter here using my subspace as a hub?”
“As you can see, the path is already open.”
The Thought Entity gestured with his chin toward the earlier space.
That space had already grown larger than Oscar’s height in that brief time.
“……Oscar, listen carefully.”
With a grave expression, the Thought Entity spoke in rapid succession.
“Leave this place immediately. And no matter if it takes years or decades, complete Absolute Stasis.”
“But—”
“People may have many facets, but that one is a being made solely of the most vile and dreadful parts of my original body. If you cannot win, do not even think of facing it.”
“W-wait a moment.”
With a stunned expression, Oscar asked,
“You’re telling me to leave all of a sudden? There’s still so much for me to learn, isn’t there?”
“No, my role is already finished. If you complete Absolute Stasis, you will be able to defeat it without difficulty. But… not now.”
If he were to fight it now, he would lose every single time.
The Thought Entity nodded firmly as he raised his mana.
“If you will not leave on your own, then I’m sorry, but I’ll have to force you out.”
He had never expected such a sudden farewell.
But Oscar understood that his words were right a hundred, a thousand times over.
And so, biting his lip tightly, he nodded.
“……I will definitely complete Absolute Stasis and close all the cracks.”
“Not only I, but my original body will be pleased as well.”
At the same time the Thought Entity broke into a wide smile,
a spatial slash fell from above Oscar’s head.
And as always, unbearable pain rushed in—
‘Hmm?’
No—he felt no pain at all.
The moment Oscar sensed something was wrong and raised his head,
what entered his vision was a pitch-black space.
That space seized the falling spatial slash with brutal force, preventing him from ‘dying.’

Chapter 374: Unidentified Zone (9)
What Spatial Sever targeted for cutting was “space itself.”
In other words, by ordinary standards, it was a top-tier offensive spell that did not even permit defense.
‘That Spatial Sever… got caught?’
A pitch-black crack in space that looked as though it could swallow everything around it whole.
From within it, blackened space emerged and roughly seized hold of the thought-form’s Spatial Sever.
“Kgh!”
The thought-form hurriedly frowned and tried to pull the Spatial Sever back out.
Kkiik! Kkiiigigik!
Unable to withstand the pressure, the Spatial Sever gradually twisted, letting out sounds like cries of agony.
“…How brutish.”
The moment the thought-form let out a brief groan and his eyes shook—
Kiiing!
A clear sound like shattering glass rang through the air.
Fragments of the shattered Spatial Sever scattered through empty space.
“Oscar!”
There was no time to even answer.
The moment he heard that shout, he already understood what he had to do.
Fwoooong!
Wind gathered at the tips of his index and middle fingers.
Oscar immediately pointed them at his own temple and completed the spell.
『Wind Bullet』
Paaang!
A wind projectile possessing speed and destructive power incomparable to before was fired.
“…!”
But only that far.
To state the conclusion first, the bullet could not pierce even skin, let alone a skull.
The instant it was fired, it vanished ‘somewhere.’
“…Spatial magic, hm. At the very least, one thing seems certain.”
The thought-form let out a heavy sigh and turned his head.
Staring at the black crack, he continued.
“It seems that one has no intention of letting you leave peacefully.”
Beyond the crack where both their gazes rested—
Step.
Footsteps echoed out.
Oscar, who had even forgotten to swallow, glared at the spot for a moment.
“Hm.”
The owner of the footsteps leisurely walked out from the crack with an utterly relaxed expression.
The moment Oscar saw him, his brows twitched involuntarily.
“……”
Ado Vail.
He too possessed an appearance identical to the master Oscar remembered.
But something was strange.
‘Wasn’t he supposed to have fallen into inner demons and become consumed by madness?’
There was not the slightest disorder in the posture of his hands clasped behind his back, and his white robe was impeccably neat.
In other words, from appearance alone, there was absolutely nothing that would make one associate him with madness.
“So this is a forest. The air is pleasant.”
The man muttered in a gentle voice before turning his head.
“What lies beyond that… yes, the White Tower?”
With a benevolent smile spread across his lips, he continued.
“It’s been a while. I’d like to see it once again.”
The moment he finished speaking, he slowly extended one hand forward.
With that single casual gesture—
“…!”
One entire side of the forest surrounding the three of them disappeared.
Beyond a cleanly carved clearing with perfectly square cut surfaces, the towering White Tower came into view.
“Hoho, it’s a pleasant sight.”
Oscar stared at the monster smiling kindly, his eyes trembling.
In his mind, the thought-form’s words resurfaced.
—The original feared that with his own hands, he might destroy everything and kill those precious to him.
He thought he understood why now.
For a moment, he had nearly mistaken him for sane because of his outward appearance, but after facing him even briefly, he could tell.
‘…That bastard is insane.’
A man who erased an entire forest simply because it obstructed the scenery.
It was a way of thinking impossible to believe belonged to a normal human being.
For a brief moment, Oscar had thought communication might be possible, but he had nearly made a fatal mistake.
“You’re the same as ever, even after all this time.”
Ado Vail gazed at the White Tower with nostalgic eyes before smiling faintly.
“It would be better if it didn’t exist.”
Slash!
The distant White Tower was suddenly cut diagonally.
And then—
Kuruuuung!
It collapsed with a deafening roar, the tremendous tremor reaching all the way to where they stood.
“……”
Master was right.
If he had not separated that inner demon early on, the White Tower would have been destroyed by the founder’s own hand.
“Hm.”
That thing wearing Master’s face turned its head toward them.
“You are… the coward’s imitation.”
“What a miserable age. To think the day would come when the original would hear words like that from a mere inner demon.”
The thought-form replied sharply.
The other paid no mind to the hostility and slowly wandered around the clearing with his hands still clasped behind his back.
Without taking his eyes off those movements, the thought-form asked,
“The original surely imprisoned you within the crack of the 44th floor. How did you get here?”
“A new neighbor suddenly appeared, so shouldn’t I at least come offer greetings?”
At that explanation, Oscar frowned.
As expected, it seemed his subspace had caused this situation.
‘It’s fine.’
The thought-form kept both eyes fixed on the opponent while extending one palm toward Oscar.
That thing glanced briefly at the gesture before turning its gaze toward him.
“And what is this?”
“An outsider who got caught in the crack by mistake. Send away those unrelated to this matter, and let the two of us settle things.”
“……He doesn’t seem unrelated.”
Sniff, sniff.
Wrinkling the bridge of his nose slightly, it curled up the corners of its lips.
“I can smell it from that brat too. The smell of space.”
Eyes filled with interest swept over Oscar.
“You, an imitation, wouldn’t have raised a disciple… which means he’s a disciple left behind by the coward.”
Though he still wore the smile of a kindly man, Oscar saw it clearly.
The madness flickering within those eyes directed at him.
“Then both of you disappearing together should solve things nicely.”
As Ado Vail stretched out one hand, pitch-black space gathered before him.
Compressed into a small sphere, it began spinning at a speed impossible for the human eye to perceive.
“This is bad, get down!”
“…!”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
At the thought-form’s urgent shout, Oscar instantly curled his body up like a pill bug.
Swaaaaaak!
The next moment, the violently rotating sphere split apart into three blades.
Every tree around them was evenly severed at waist height before collapsing.
Kuuung! Kung! Kuuung!
The cut trees slammed against the ground, their heavy aftershocks rumbling without pause.
“……”
The thought-form stared at the blades, which still retained enough force to continue spinning as they disappeared beyond the forest.
Then he spoke.
“I truly wanted to send you out of here somehow. I meant it sincerely.”
“I know. But since someone showed up to interfere with our beautiful farewell… I suppose this means it comes down to that, right?”
Die, or kill.
The thought-form quietly nodded.
“As I said before, his current state is far from normal. His madness has worsened to the point that he cannot use high-level spells, so we do have a chance. However, remember this well—he still possesses a level 9 body and mana.”
Certainly, even the previous strike, and the attack that erased the White Tower earlier, had not been Spatial Sever.
He had simply used an absurd amount of mana to forcibly cut space apart.
A lunatic feat possible only because he possessed absolute confidence in his overwhelming mana reserves.
‘But if it’s simply mana reserves, I’m not lacking either.’
Perhaps the thought-form was thinking the same thing, because he looked at Oscar and nodded once.
—Once battle begins, that one will focus his attacks on me.
Message magic.
The thought-form’s voice flowed into Oscar’s ears.
Keeping his eyes fixed on Ado Vail, his lips moved without pause.
—Avoid the attacks appropriately, and when the moment feels right, I will use Absolute Stillness. At that instant, use Spatial Sever and grant him eternal rest.
—I understand.
A clean and concise plan without unnecessary details.
Perhaps this was even better.
Oscar had no idea how long it would take him to complete 『Absolute Stillness』 himself.
But the thought-form had already mastered it perfectly.
‘Besides, if we can just eliminate the Ado Vail consumed by madness…’
There would no longer be any reason to close the Fourth Crack where the thought-form lived.
Meaning he could continue asking him questions in the future.
“You’re nimble. Like little rats.”
Ado Vail’s pupils gradually shrank, while blackish-red mana continuously poured out around his body.
At a glance, it might seem intimidating, but it was by no means a good sign.
That meant his mana control was leaking apart uncontrollably.
‘A level 9 mage who can’t even properly control his mana? Definitely madness.’
Of course, that still did not make him an opponent to take lightly.
“Die!”
With a maddened roar, the blue sky glittered in countless places.
The moment Oscar narrowed his eyes at the dazzling lights—
“…This lunatic.”
His heart sank as he realized every single point of light was spatial magic.
“Kgh! Dodge them yourself!”
“Yes!”
Swaaaaaaaaa!
As though a torrential downpour were falling from the heavens, thousands of spatial spells rained down.
Oscar hurriedly deployed 『Wind Shield』 above his head.
Displaying mana control bordering on acrobatics, he deflected the incoming attacks.
“Kuh!”
But even if incomplete, these were spells cast by a level 9 mage intent on killing him.
The shields’ durability instantly collapsed and scattered apart, forcing Oscar to repeatedly create new shields.
“……”
After the storm passed and the raging attacks finally subsided—
“You resemble a turtle.”
Ado Vail’s calm voice echoed through space.
None of the earlier frenzy remained within it.
‘Which means…’
That previous madness had all been an act.
The instant alarm bells rang in Oscar’s mind—
Ado Vail smiled warmly and gently extended his hand.
“Come here.”
And the direction that hand pointed toward—
“…!”
Was not the thought-form.
It was Oscar himself.
Kwoaaaaaaaaa!
Wind swept through the barren forest where not a single intact tree remained.
No, rather than wind, it would be more accurate to call it a typhoon or a storm.
‘What kind of… absurd wind is this…’
Oscar gritted his teeth against the overwhelming suction force dragging his body forward like madness.
He hurriedly drove his mana-enhanced legs into the earth, but it meant nothing before the storm’s power.
He could even feel the ground itself being dragged toward the opponent alongside his body.
“Kuh!”
While being pulled in, Oscar hurriedly generated a countercurrent.
He too unleashed enormous mana to create a massive typhoon, but…
The output difference between a level 7 and level 9 mage was truly heaven and earth.
Kwoaaaaaaaaa!
Against Ado Vail’s insane storm, Oscar’s wind shattered as futilely as the fluttering of a butterfly’s wings.
“Oscar!”
Watching this, the thought-form’s expression twisted.
According to the original plan, Ado Vail should have attacked him.
But instead, he blatantly ignored the thought-form entirely and began obsessively targeting Oscar.
“There is no meaning in eliminating an imitation. But this brat… is the true successor left behind by that coward.”
Killing intent glimmered around Ado Vail’s eyes.
“I will destroy everything that coward wished to protect. Even if that includes this world itself.”
“You despicable bastard….”
The thought-form clenched both fists tightly.
Naturally, 『Absolute Stillness』 had to be used at the perfect moment.
Even he could not spam such magic freely, meaning one use during battle would be the limit.
‘But if I leave things as they are, Oscar will die.’
Even if they killed that man at the cost of Oscar’s life, it would hold no meaning.
That man’s words were correct.
Oscar was the true successor who inherited the will and legacy of the person named Ado Vail left behind by the original.
“Wait!”
Finally hardening his resolve, the thought-form ignored the shout behind him and quickly began preparing.
He emptied his thoughts.
Emptied his emotions.
Anything emptied could simply be filled again later, so he let everything go without the slightest attachment.
“……”
At the moment when neither body nor mind contained anything at all—
The thought-form stared at his enemy with transparent eyes and moved his lips.
“Absolute Stillness.”
The entire area stopped breathing.
Sound, air, even the storm tormenting Oscar—
Everything froze perfectly like a single painting.
“Kuhk! Kuhk!”
Within that space, there was only one being granted freedom.
Oscar, whom the thought-form had designated as an “exception.”
Freed from the suffocating suction of the storm, Oscar did not hesitate.
‘This is my one and only chance.’
He absolutely could not miss it.
Pouring in fully half of his total mana, he created no fewer than five Spatial Severs.
Arrayed across the blue sky like giant stone monuments, they waited only to descend.
‘…That thing is an evil wearing Master’s face.’
The feeling left a bitter taste in his mouth, but this was something he absolutely had to do.
The moment Oscar lightly waved his hand—
The five Spatial Severs slowly descended above Ado Vail’s head.
“Farewell.”
Until that very moment, Ado Vail remained frozen, unable to move even a finger.
Yet after a desperate struggle—
He barely managed to curl the corners of his lips upward into a smile.

Chapter 375: Unidentified Zone (10)
Oscar looked around.
Everything except himself was frozen in place.
The halted air and wind, even the mana that had lost its destination and solidified.
‘So this is the influence of Absolute Stasis.’
It went without saying, but this was his first time seeing it used in actual combat.
And his impression of it…
There was no other way to describe it besides beautiful.
Because the entire frozen world felt like a single work of art.
“……”
Oscar shifted his gaze.
The five Spatial Slashes he had created were descending toward Ado Vail.
An inevitable killing combination that could neither be blocked nor reacted to.
“Farewell.”
Even though the words fell like a death sentence, Ado Vail remained standing still.
Judging from the fine tremors running through his body, he was probably trying to resist with all his might.
However, a body already trapped within the domain of Absolute Stasis could no longer move in the slightest.
That was what Oscar thought in that moment.
“……?”
A small change appeared in Ado Vail’s body.
The corners of his lips had risen slightly—just slightly.
The moment Oscar saw that, his eyes shook.
‘Why?’
Why was the thing he moved with such desperate effort the corner of his mouth?
At the very least, he could have understood moving a finger.
That could be interpreted as an act meant to somehow cast magic and resist.
But the corner of his mouth?
Couldn’t that only be interpreted as him moving in order to smile from the very beginning?
“……”
An inexplicable sense of unease washed over him.
Just as Oscar tried to shake off the feeling by increasing the speed of the Spatial Slashes—
Swaaaash!
A sound rang out.
From behind.
‘Behind?’
The moment he hurriedly turned his head, he saw three blades flying out from deep within the forest.
Deleting everything they touched with their edges as they approached, they were unmistakably spatial magic.
‘Wait, those are definitely…’
The magic Ado Vail had used at the very start of the battle to cut down every tree in the surroundings.
Oscar’s last memory of them was watching them indiscriminately slice through the forest before vanishing deeper inside.
‘Then why are they only now…’
Oscar’s eyes widened for an instant.
‘Don’t tell me… Ado Vail predicted this entire situation from the start?’
Not that it was impossible.
No, rather, it would be strange if he hadn’t.
Just as the Thought Entity knew his capabilities, Ado Vail also knew the Thought Entity’s capabilities.
‘Then from the very first attack, he prepared for this exact moment?’
Swaaaash!
Oscar’s gaze locked onto the approaching blades.
The direction they were coming from lay outside the domain of Absolute Stasis.
In other words, behind the Thought Entity.
‘If I kill that bastard as things are now…’
The Thought Entity’s body would be shredded apart from behind and erased.
He was currently in a state of No Mind, No Self.
He had not even recognized this situation.
“Damn it.”
Grinding his teeth, Oscar made a split-second decision.
Three of the five Spatial Slashes abruptly spun around and charged toward the incoming blades.
‘Two are enough to kill a frozen target.’
He even deliberately created a time gap.
First, intercept the blades.
Then, exactly 0.5 seconds later, the remaining two Spatial Slashes would pierce Ado Vail.
‘The plan is perfect.’
The Spatial Slashes controlled through delicate mana manipulation collided at a moment that could practically be called simultaneous.
Kagagagak!
The violently rotating spatial blades shattered apart.
After confirming it, Oscar quickly turned his head toward Ado Vail.
‘It worked.’
The two Spatial Slashes had already reached right before him.
The instant Oscar unconsciously clenched both fists—
Flash!
A burst of light erupted from behind him, momentarily illuminating the dirt ground.
The sound came after.
KWA-AAAAANG!
Together with a violent explosion, a powerful wave of mana strong enough to shake the entire forest slammed into his back.
‘An explosion? Don’t tell me…’
A chilling cold spread over the pain boring into his back.
Explosion upon destruction.
Unless such a property had been intentionally built into the magic from the moment it was created, this situation made no sense.
‘He anticipated and prepared all the way to this point from the very first move?’
Realizing his thoughts and actions had been read, Oscar ground his teeth hard.
Barely managing to turn his head, he looked toward the Thought Entity.
Just like himself, the man had been caught in the explosion, but vitality returned to his transparent eyes.
Which meant No Mind, No Self had been broken.
“Damn…….”
Before he could even finish speaking—
As though the frozen world was demanding compensation for its halt—
Everything began rushing forward at a mad pace together with the aftermath of the explosion.
“Ghk, cough! Cough!”
His body, blasted away by the immense impact, rolled across the dirt ground.
A scorching heat flared from his back along with the coughing, but that was not what mattered right now.
Barely lifting his head, Oscar stared ahead through the thick cloud of dust.
“……”
A lone figure stood motionless.
So still that it was impossible to tell whether he was alive or dead.
Soon the dust settled, revealing Ado Vail standing firmly in place.
“Hm.”
A relaxed voice still slipped through his lips.
Slowly narrowing his eyes halfway open, Ado Vail looked down at Oscar sprawled on the ground.
“That was quite a convincing strategy. You almost killed this old man. I shall praise you for that.”
“……How?”
At Oscar’s trembling voice, Ado Vail tilted his head slightly.
“How? Ahh. You’re wondering how I noticed your strategy?”
Letting out a scoff, he grinned.
“It’s because, aside from the combination involving Absolute Stasis and Spatial Slash, I simply could not envision a future where this old man loses.”
The one and only defeat condition he could predict because of his absolute confidence in his own abilities.
If he knew that, then naturally, using it against them was easy enough.
“That’s…….”
Oscar bit down hard on his teeth.
His head spun.
Not because of the aftereffects of the explosion.
But because of the pressure brought on by a wrong decision and the irreversible situation it had created.
‘Once again, I…’
The trauma related to the Great Emperor was slowly beginning to rise again when—
“Blink.”
With that quiet murmur, the surrounding scenery changed in an instant.
“Cough! Cough!”
Just like Oscar, the Thought Entity had also been lying on the ground, coughing from overexerting himself with forced magic use.
Of course, the damage from the explosion itself had not been that great.
From the start, the purpose of the explosion had merely been to break 『Absolute Stasis』.
“Hoo.”
After catching his breath for a moment, he rose as though nothing had happened and brushed the dirt off his knees and shoulders.
Then he stared directly at Oscar and asked,
“How long does a young man intend to keep lying there?”
“…….”
Oscar pressed his lips together and stood up.
The Thought Entity approached him and brushed the dirt off his clothes.
“Throw away that expression that looks like you’re about to cry. Anyone seeing you would think you made the wrong choice.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“But because of me…….”
“Do not misunderstand.”
The expression of the Thought Entity, who had placed both hands on Oscar’s shoulders, turned serious.
“You chose the best possible judgment you could make in that situation. Even the original body would have done the same.”
“……Even if you say that, the result still turned out badly, didn’t it?”
“What an amusing thing to say.”
The Thought Entity wore an expression as though he genuinely could not understand.
“Do you think there exists a person who goes through life making nothing but correct choices?”
“That… probably not. But my situation is different from ordinary people, isn’t it?”
“Then tell me. In what way are you so different from them?”
Strangely enough, he had no answer to that question.
Because he was special?
No.
Rather, he had never once thought of himself as special.
He did possess talent in magic, but talented mages were common enough to be found everywhere.
“You cannot answer, can you? Because there is nothing that makes you different from them.”
“…….”
“Listen carefully. Every human being makes mistakes and stumbles. Since you still have a long life ahead of you, you will undoubtedly continue making many mistakes in the future as well. And each time that happens, are you going to droop like this with an expression ready to burst into tears?”
Pat, pat.
The Thought Entity tapped Oscar’s shoulder.
Though the hand was incredibly small and light, for some reason it felt heavy today.
“You are certainly a special human being, but that does not mean you are someone who must never fail. If you fall, then rise again. Please do not impose standards upon yourself that are far too harsh.”
“…….”
Oscar stayed silent for a long while before giving a small nod.
“Thank you.”
“And have you perhaps ever heard this saying? That one learns nothing from victory, but can learn everything from defeat.”
“……It’s my first time hearing it.”
“Then make sure to remember it. It’s quite a good saying.”
Though their one decisive killing combination had failed, the Thought Entity spoke without shrinking back.
“What do you think our cause of defeat was?”
“I suppose the problem was that our strategy was seen through.”
“Exactly. That’s precisely it. Just as I knew the opponent well, the opponent also knew me too well. That was our fatal mistake.”
The Thought Entity smacked his lips.
“Of course, I thought that earlier combination was something impossible to stop even if one understood it…… but it seems the one who was wrong was not you, but me.”
“Is there any way to win?”
“Hmm? What are you talking about? Didn’t the opponent himself tell us the method to win?”
“Pardon?”
Oscar’s puzzled frown relaxed slightly.
“Don’t tell me…….”
“Yes. Didn’t that fellow clearly say it with his own mouth? That aside from the combination of Absolute Stasis and Spatial Slash, he could not envision a future where he loses.”
In other words, that very combination of those two magics was enough to defeat him for certain.
Oscar asked,
“But I’ve heard Absolute Stasis consumes mana, mental strength, and willpower to a ridiculous degree. Can you use it again immediately?”
“Hmm? I cannot. I would need a full four days to recover my energy.”
“Then how…….”
Tap.
The Thought Entity pointed at Oscar with his index finger.
“Isn’t there you?”
“Pardon?”
“That fellow does not suspect in the slightest that you can use Absolute Stasis. Since under normal circumstances, it is impossible.”
But he himself could theoretically use 『Absolute Stasis』.
Though it was close to a loophole, and came with the minor risk of losing random emotions……
“Understood.”
Oscar nodded heavily.
“I’ll try it.”
* * *
Ado Vail did not pursue the two of them and instead waited in that very same spot.
“You’re late.”
Rising slowly from where he had been sitting on a chopped tree stump, he lightly rolled his neck.
“Since there is nowhere to run in this place anyway, let us not waste unnecessary energy on each other.”
“That is true.”
The Thought Entity nodded.
“Let us settle this here.”
“Heh, still acting tough, I see.”
Ado Vail curled one side of his lips upward.
Through the previous battle, they had already exhausted 『Absolute Stasis』.
Which meant the only thing he needed to be wary of now was 『Spatial Slash』.
‘Though if there is one variable…….’
His gaze turned toward Oscar.
‘That brat handles Spatial Slash quite freely.’
Oscar and the Thought Entity.
He needed to avoid the Spatial Slashes the two of them would bombard him with.
Other magic would be one thing, but those were not something you walked away from unscathed the moment they touched you.
“Begin whenever you are ready.”
The Thought Entity did not bother refusing Ado Vail’s leisurely proposal.
“My thanks.”
Immediately afterward, mana surged from his entire body and tore cracks into space.
“……There are quite a lot.”
What appeared throughout the sunset sky were no fewer than sixteen Spatial Slashes.
Shaped like inverted crosses, they even looked holy at a glance.
“Here I come.”
At those words, Ado Vail nodded and glanced toward Oscar, who was simply standing still.
‘Is that guy planning to use Spatial Slash later?’
Well, if he intended to aim for an opening on this side, creating it during the midst of intense combat would indeed be better.
Though naturally, Ado Vail had no intention of letting such a chance slip by him.
Piiiiing!
Together with a clear ringing sound, the Spatial Slashes floating in the sunset sky descended.
KWA-AAAAANG!
Despite their thin and slender forms, their explosive force was tremendous.
The dirt ground exploded apart, and the instant Ado Vail lightly leapt into the air to evade—
Ping! Piping!
The waiting Spatial Slashes rushed toward him.
“Hm.”
Ado Vail did not hurry and calmly dodged each attack one by one.
Even amid that, his eyes occasionally drifted toward Oscar.
‘……He’s still standing there?’
Just as he became utterly unable to predict what the boy was waiting for—
“……!”
The moment Ado Vail saw his opponent’s eyes gradually turning transparent, his face twisted.
“What? What is this nonsense……?”
『Absolute Stasis』—something he himself could not use due to the impatience brought on by madness.
And a mere level 7 mage was attempting it?
It was an absurd attempt.
If attempted a hundred times, it would obviously fail a hundred times.
“You insolent brat…… yes, I suppose you have no choice but to gamble on something like this.”
Ado Vail forced himself to deny the unease creeping into his heart as he mocked the two of them to the fullest.
Then—
“Hm?”
For an instant, it felt as though the world had slowed down.
And the moment his gaze instinctively turned toward Oscar while searching for the reason—
『Absolute Stasis』
The world stopped.

Chapter 376: Unidentified Zone (11)
Crunch! KWA-A-A-A!
Spatial Slashes flew through the air, and the opponent desperately struggled to evade them.
Oscar engraved the clash between the two into his retinas.
‘No-Mind.’
A lesson still somewhat premature for him.
He understood it in theory, but had yet to embody it.
Boom! Kwaaang!
The continuous explosions ringing in his ears threatened to draw out impatience like a sigh.
And so, Oscar shut his ears.
“……”
Silence followed.
Even in the soundless world, the two tirelessly changed positions as they clashed.
Blood and sweat streamed down their faces, and tangled mana crackled like electricity.
For now, the Thought Entity was overwhelmingly pressing the attack.
‘But that momentum won’t last long.’
No matter how powerful the Thought Entity was, he couldn’t recklessly spam Spatial Slashes forever.
Which made Oscar’s role all the more important.
Oscar closed even his eyes after his ears.
“……”
He could hear nothing and see nothing.
Oddly enough, he did not dislike the feeling of being isolated in pitch-black darkness wrapped in silence.
Oscar slowly drew up his mana.
‘The aura of extreme cold.’
The frigid chill of severe cold coiled within him through the Extreme Ice Crystal.
The moment he raised that energy, his mana circuits became so cold it felt as though they might freeze solid.
‘Use this to freeze my emotions.’
Drip, drip.
Into the vast lake called the mind, droplets of emotion fell ceaselessly.
Craaack!
The severe cold did not stop at freezing those droplets—it froze the lake itself.
His wavering emotions solidified as they were.
Anxiety, impatience, even the unease of doubting whether he could truly pull this off.
They had not disappeared.
They were all still there, exactly as they had been.
Tap.
But no matter how far he reached, he could not touch them.
All those emotions were trapped behind thick walls of ice, unable to perform their functions.
“……”
Blood flowed sluggishly through his frozen veins.
Yet he felt no warmth.
A sharp branch, swept up by the aftermath of battle, scraped across his cheek.
But even pain and agony could not be felt.
‘So this is what it feels like.’
As though he had finally faced the world after being freed from all interference.
Oscar steadied his breathing.
‘Right now.’
It was possible.
Slowly parting his eyes, Oscar gazed upon the world with eyes clearer and more transparent than ever before.
Thoughts, emotions, senses, will.
All those things, which had flowed at different speeds, finally converged into a single, uniform pace.
That unified current spread outward from within him, meshing together with the world itself—
『Absolute Stasis』
Everything stopped.
“Well done!”
Bursting into hearty laughter, the Thought Entity lowered his finger.
Still frozen in the posture of having landed on the ground, Ado Vail faced him as the Thought Entity delivered a final farewell.
“Farewell. Vessel of madness.”
A Spatial Slash descended from the sky like lightning and pierced him.
Kkagagagagak!
From the shoulder where the Spatial Slash had struck came the sound of grinding blades.
“You twisted the space over the surface of your skin…!”
He had expected the opponent to prepare something, but never imagined such a method.
Still, at best, it only bought a brief moment of time.
“Pour down.”
Two, three, four…
Spatial Slashes rained endlessly from the sky.
Ado Vail’s eyes became bloodshot as every one of those attacks pierced him.
“Hah.”
Even rotten fish are still fish—despite everything, the body of a Level 9 mage still clung to life.
Of course, all it did was cling to life.
Nothing more, nothing less.
Slash!
His arm vanished first, followed by his heart being pierced through.
Without even letting out a proper groan, Ado Vail slowly withered away.
Yet even amidst that, his eyes still gleamed murderously.
“……This ends here.”
Swaeaeaeaeak!
Along with that declaration, an inverted cross-shaped Spatial Slash fell from the heavens.
At the same time, 『Absolute Stasis』, which had been holding the flow of the world in place, came to an end.
‘Since it’s my first time, a mere few seconds is the limit, huh.’
That changed nothing.
Ado Vail was already far too late to resist anymore.
Crunch!
Indeed, he failed to dodge the falling attack, and the Spatial Slash pierced through his spine.
“……Kuheok!”
Blood poured from his mouth in a thick gush, and the vitality rapidly faded from his eyes.
“You damned… remnants… of cowards…….”
Ado Vail’s trembling body finally collapsed limply to the ground.
“……”
Without letting his guard down, the Thought Entity sharpened his senses as he stared at him.
Nowhere could he sense any trace of madness.
‘He’s definitely dead.’
Relief seeped in together with a hollow emptiness.
That thing had been created because the original body could not overcome the self-loathing of failing to protect his wife.
A monster that declared a world where he could not save even the person he loved should disappear along with him.
Calling the original body a coward for rejecting that will, it had constantly schemed to seize control of the body.
‘Now that bastard’s dead… the original body can finally close his eyes in peace.’
A powerless smile formed on the Thought Entity’s lips before he suddenly snapped back to his senses.
“Ah.”
This was no time for that.
After using 『Absolute Stasis』 through a shortcut method, there was no way Oscar could be in good condition.
“Oscar! Are you alright!”
Hurriedly rushing over, the Thought Entity shook Oscar’s collapsed body.
A moment later, Oscar opened his eyes with difficulty and asked,
“……What about him?”
“We took him down! It’s all thanks to you.”
“You shouldn’t say that carelessly. Did you confirm it?”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“If you don’t believe me, see it with your own eyes.”
Supporting him, the Thought Entity showed him Ado Vail’s corpse.
Only then did it truly sink in that everything was over.
“More importantly, what froze this time?”
“……Pardon?”
“Your emotions. Since you forcibly froze them with severe cold, there must be side effects.”
“Even if you say that, I don’t really know.”
“Hmm.”
After pondering briefly, the Thought Entity immediately created a book and began writing something inside it.
“Even if I disappear, keeping these questions written here as a kind of manual and asking yourself them repeatedly should help you recognize your own condition.”
“Disappear? Are you going on a trip somewhere?”
“Hm? Well, I’ve finished the role entrusted to me, so shouldn’t I get going too?”
Oscar tilted his head at the Thought Entity’s words.
“Where exactly are you going?”
“……‘Going’ was just a figure of speech. I mean disappearing together with this gap.”
“Ah, disappearing… Is it because defeating the Heart Demon causes you to disappear as well?”
“That’s not it. As I said before, my role is to determine who possesses the qualifications to defeat the Heart Demon of the 44th Floor and send them upward. If I do not disappear together with this gap, then no matter how skilled a spatial mage may be, approaching the gap of the 44th Floor becomes difficult.”
What he described was essentially the orthodox strategy.
Joining forces with the Thought Entity to subjugate the Heart Demon had never been Master’s original plan.
“But the Heart Demon of the 44th Floor is already dead. The gap closed too. In the end, didn’t things work out well because the Heart Demon crossed over here first?”
The order of events had certainly become completely tangled, but the situation had actually turned out rather favorably.
He had received the Thought Entity’s help and eliminated his master’s Heart Demon absurdly easily.
Likewise, the Thought Entity had also splendidly completed the task entrusted to him by Master.
The Thought Entity spoke with an extremely conflicted expression.
“No, but still, I’ve already completed the duty I was given… there’s no reason for me to remain…….”
“A reason? Then should I make one for you?”
“Hmm, now that everything is over, wouldn’t it make for a better ending if I naturally exited the stage?”
“I don’t really see it that way.”
More than anything, he was none other than Ado Vail’s Thought Entity.
Meaning he was the being who understood the magic and concepts Ado Vail had achieved better than anyone else.
And also the person best suited to teach him whenever he got stuck while studying in the future.
“Hmm.”
After thinking for a moment, the Thought Entity nodded.
“As long as my existence won’t become a nuisance, I personally wouldn’t mind staying longer…….”
“A nuisance? Having you around would be a huge gain. If needed, how about taking charge of some newly graduated chicks from the academy and teaching a class or two?”
“T-that part, I shall consider slowly.”
Even if he could only exist within spatial gaps, they had still recruited a top-tier mage.
In a sense, it could even be called a boost in strength.
“Ah, and……”
Taking the opportunity, Oscar brought up something he had been considering.
“If you’re Master’s Thought Entity, then you can move freely inside spatial gaps, right?”
“That’s correct.”
“Then, since things turned out this way anyway, could you help me with something?”
“…….”
Had he always been the type to ask for help this shamelessly?
With a doubtful expression, the Thought Entity asked,
“What kind of help exactly do you need?”
“One of the training rooms I’m planning is called the Subspace Training Room. The problem is……”
After listening to the explanation, the Thought Entity nodded.
“I see. You want me to move between layered subspaces and regulate the flow of time.”
“Exactly.”
“……But do you realize? If I take on that role, it means I’ll have to endure all that time myself, whether a hundred years or a thousand years pass inside the subspace.”
“Uh, but since you’re a Thought Entity, isn’t that fine? You can’t die anyway.”
“……!”
At those words, spoken as though he had lost the human heart entirely, the Thought Entity trembled violently.
“Y-you. Are you seriously saying that?”
“There’s nothing wrong with what I said, is there?”
Startled out of his mind, the Thought Entity hastily opened the ‘Oscar Emotional Diagnosis Manual’ he had written earlier.
After asking dozens of questions—
He finally spoke with a rather ambiguous expression.
“I’m not sure whether I should take these results positively or negatively…….”
“What did it say?”
“For starters, you are currently in a state of severely impaired empathy.”
“Empathy…….”
Oscar frowned.
“I can’t believe that.”
“Very well, then let me ask this question again. Oscar, today I was depressed, so I bought bread.”
“If you were depressed, why would you buy bread? More importantly, there isn’t even a bakery in this gap.”
“……L-look at this! Just look at this!”
Trembling violently, the Thought Entity stared at Oscar with fearful eyes, as though he had seen a ghost.
“That is an answer utterly devoid of empathy.”
“……Then what exactly am I supposed to say to show empathy?”
“You should first ask things like why I’m depressed or whether something happened.”
“Tsk. I still don’t get it.”
“Furthermore, in my personal opinion, it also seems your sense of awareness has vanished. You’ve become astonishingly shameless.”
Lacking empathy and even losing awareness of social cues.
Wasn’t that, as a human being, absolutely terrible?
Scratching his head, Oscar asked,
“……The frozen emotions will return soon, right?”
“That, who knows. Come to think of it, can you feel the emotion of happiness again?”
“Not yet.”
“Hmm.”
Apparently, once emotions froze, it took quite a long time for them to thaw.
Pat, pat.
“Stay strong.”
The Thought Entity lightly patted Oscar on the shoulder.
