Chapter 383: Things That Must Be Protected (1)
“So it actually works…….”
Veronica wore a strangely relieved yet wistful expression.
After all, this had been the problem tormenting her mercilessly for the past several dozen days.
The time she had spent agonizing over it day and night already felt like a distant memory.
“…….”
She stared up at the canyon wall carved by the winding winds for quite a while before turning back around.
“Congrats. I didn’t expect you to clear it immediately just because I gave you a single hint.”
“Haaah! Seriously. Still, thanks to you, I finally get to leave this damn place.”
Showing a refreshed expression, Veronica lightly scratched her cheek.
“Ahem, hm-hm. Hey, uh… anyway…… this time, I’m really thankful…… yeah, that’s how it is.”
Anyone could tell she was embarrassed.
Watching her, Oscar blinked twice.
“Why are you embarrassed?”
“Ah, it’s just…… saying thank you out loud feels awkward. Ah, can’t we just gloss over this part already?”
“That’s a little late for that, isn’t it? It’s not like I’ve only saved you once or twice.”
Just off the top of his head, there was Vince, the artificial island, and even Null City.
“I can’t always be there to save you, so try being a little more careful from now on, alright?”
“……If only your level had been lower than mine.”
“If that were the case, you’d have died a long time ago.”
“Gah! You never let a single comment slide, do you? Why’d you become so damn annoying while I wasn’t looking?”
Veronica’s tightly clenched fist trembled violently.
Ignoring her, Oscar glanced around the area and muttered,
“By the way, where’s the exit?”
Now that they had cleared the theme dungeon with a reproduction rate of 100%, an exit should have appeared.
But nowhere in the wasteland was there anything resembling a door.
“Don’t tell me you can’t see anyth…… Veronica?”
Oscar hurriedly looked around.
The Veronica who had been grumbling just moments ago had vanished without a trace.
“She has been moved to a place where she can receive her reward.”
Instead, the voice of the guide from the cabin sounded from behind him.
When Oscar turned around, the guide was staring at the canyon wall Veronica had carved.
“A spirited and free-spirited challenger indeed. Even now, I can still feel her power lingering in those traces.”
“She’s so free-spirited that she becomes a headache half the time.”
“Kekeke.”
The guide chuckled and turned his head.
The deep eyes that met Oscar’s in midair sparkled with curiosity.
“How old are you this year?”
“Why do you ask?”
“It’s not just your insight into understanding the dungeon’s theme. You also seem to possess deep knowledge related to magic.”
“I’m just kind of like that. I’m twenty-one.”
“Hm. Twenty-one……”
Oscar spoke to the guide stroking his beard.
“So you didn’t come here just to send Veronica out. You came to see me.”
“You could say I’m handling this task while taking care of another one at the same time.”
“Sounds like being a guide isn’t all that busy.”
“When you get old, time’s about the only thing you have left, isn’t it?”
Smiling warmly, the guide snapped his fingers, and a door appeared beside him.
“Sorry for keeping you here so long. Now then, once you leave, you should return to where you originally were.”
“…….”
Oscar stared fixedly at the guide before speaking.
“It feels like the thing you’re truly curious about still hasn’t been asked. Are you really okay with just letting me leave like this?”
At those words, the guide flinched for an instant.
But he quickly regained control of his expression and smiled gently.
“Hah, you really are different. Thank you for being considerate. If I truly become unable to contain my curiosity, then I shall ask.”
“Suit yourself.”
Oscar nodded, opened the door, and stepped out, returning to the place where thousands of doors stood.
“Hm? It’s Oscar.”
Walking between the doors, Tesila Windroar widened her eyes and approached him.
“You finished quickly. How was it?”
“Hmm…… it was interesting.”
“Interesting? As far as I know, all your friends have been trapped in theirs for over fifty days already. And that’s only on stage-one difficulty.”
“You’ve really been investigating a lot, huh?”
When Oscar asked with a dumbfounded expression, Tesila nodded proudly.
“Of course I have. It’s an occupational hazard. If I don’t receive the best reward from a dungeon, I start getting restless.”
“So I’m basically just a stepping stone you use to get the best reward?”
“Can’t we call each other pleasant collaborators instead? Come on, this way.”
Smiling softly, Tesila slowly began walking.
Oscar unconsciously followed behind her and asked,
“By the way, where are we going?”
“Weren’t you about to go break into your friends’ doors?”
“That’s right.”
“Both doors are this way. The Sirius Merchant Company brat and the White Tower’s Holy One, right?”
“Yeah.”
She asked again.
“So which one are you entering first? I’ll guide you there.”
“Oh, convenient. Nice.”
“Well, naturally. You think I became a top-class adventurer for nothing?”
Did that really have anything to do with this?
Oscar casually nodded and answered.
“Killian Lockwood.”
“Hm? That’s unexpected. I thought you’d go into Fran Sirius’s door first.”
“Why?”
“Well…… because the Holy One seems like the type who’d do perfectly fine even if left alone?”
Oscar unconsciously nodded in agreement.
Killian certainly wasn’t the type to make people uneasy or worried.
Still, because of the dungeon’s structure, he simply thought entering Fran’s door first would be a disadvantage.
‘Spirits. And not just spirits, but colorless spirits even I’ve never heard of before. How exactly am I supposed to give advice on that?’
On the other hand, he knew quite a lot about the forest tribes.
After all, he had heard many stories through his former friend, Radan.
“I think Killian’s side will be easier for me to coach.”
Maybe because he had already seen Veronica’s theme, he could roughly grasp how these things progressed now.
“Really? Well, you’re going into both anyway, so I guess the order doesn’t matter. Here we are!”
Stopping her steps, Tesila spread both arms and pointed toward the door ahead.
[Killian Lockwood, <1>, 55 Days 04:11:43]
Oscar stared at the nameplate before turning his head.
“I’m going in right away. Are you staying here, Ms. Tesila?”
“Hm? Of course not. The owner of the door I contracted with is apparently entering soon too, so I have to go there.”
So she had already arranged contracts before entering the dungeon.
As expected of an adventurer, her preparation was thorough.
And honestly, he was a little curious.
About which door owners she had made contracts with besides himself.
‘Considering she’s a top-class adventurer, there’s no way she picked random nobodies.’
Reading his expression, Tesila grinned.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“Curious? Want me to tell you who the owners are?”
“Are they people I’d know?”
“At least one of them. Even those demon bastards would know him.”
“Who exactly?”
“Well, one is a level-six mage named Kiri Gloria from the Black Tower. She’s talented, so I bought low on her.”
So Kiri entered too.
Well, considering the dungeon’s rewards, it was highly likely that every mage and knight would eventually come here.
“And the other one…… don’t be shocked. It’s none other than the Yellow Tower Master.”
“……What?”
The Yellow Tower Master?
Oscar blinked rapidly.
“The Yellow Tower Master? You mean Tony Havertz?”
“That’s right. Don’t tell me you don’t know him?”
There wasn’t a single person living in this era who didn’t know the former head of the Magic Engineering Department.
Especially now that he had become the master of the Yellow Tower, he had become even more impossible not to know.
“That’s surprising. I figured he’d be swamped keeping his household in order.”
“That’s what I thought too, but apparently he forced open about two days in his schedule. He’s probably aiming for level eight like me.”
Well, even though Tony Havertz had risen to the position of Yellow Tower Master, he was still only level seven.
Meanwhile, the masters of the other Four Great Magic Towers were all level eight.
He probably felt the need to balance the scales of power.
‘Especially since the previous Tower Master was Pentarion Ereus, that old man.’
He had been considered among the strongest of all the tower masters when it came to sheer combat power.
Though in the end, he failed to overcome his own greed and destroyed himself.
“You’re pretty skilled. How’d you manage to secure that contract?”
“I’m a top-class adventurer. I promised I’d work for him once later.”
“I see. But if he only cleared out two days, what happens if he can’t finish within that time?”
“His entire schedule gets wrecked, I guess.”
Tesila shrugged.
“Maybe because of that, he doesn’t seem interested in raising the difficulty. Apparently he’s going in directly without any interference.”
“Ahh.”
Raising the difficulty granted additional reward points.
But those points were purely for the sanctuary itself and weren’t directly tied to personal growth.
‘Though if the difficulty rises, it’d probably affect personal growth too…….’
But considering the time required to clear it, Tony Havertz must have judged it excessive.
For someone in the position of Yellow Tower Master, it was probably an unavoidable decision.
“This conversation got longer than expected. I should get going too. Have a safe trip.”
“Yes, Ms. Tesila. Please come back safely as well.”
After seeing her off, Oscar took a short deep breath and opened Killian’s door.
Beyond the threshold stretched lush green foliage.
‘……A forest.’
A forest—the complete opposite of the wasteland that had been Veronica’s theme.
Well, since Killian came from a forest tribe, maybe it was only natural.
‘Where is this guy?’
In Veronica’s case, she had been making so much noise that finding her was easy, but this forest was far too quiet.
‘Could this not be a combat-related theme?’
The moment he entered, he expected to sense traces of battle and locate him immediately.
『Scan』
A wave of mana spread outward from Oscar’s body and swept through the entire forest.
‘Found him.’
Moving toward Killian’s detected location, Oscar doubted his own eyes.
“……Hey, what exactly are you doing right now?”
“Hmm?”
Killian, having noticed him, looked slightly surprised before quickly regaining composure.
“I see. So you came to help me with that interference thing.”
“Yeah, I did…… but more importantly, what the hell are you doing?”
“As you can see, I was studying magic.”
That guy had been writing spell formulas all over the forest floor with a tree branch, then studying them intently.
Of course, huge portions of the formulas were left blank in the middle.
“Kh!”
Killian suddenly let out a groan and frowned.
“Hmm, this one isn’t right either.”
“……Don’t tell me you’re trying to rediscover the 『Jet Booster』 formula right now?”
“That’s correct. Once I learn this formula, it becomes easier to uncover the formula for 『Haste』, an upper-tier enhancement spell, does it not? I had memorized it before, but I forgot.”
At that utterly barbaric method, genuine chills ran down Oscar’s spine.
It was like watching someone solve a problem by manually counting for days when they could solve it in seconds if they simply knew the equation.
In other words, an extremely primitive and inefficient approach.
“No, what I’m asking is why a magical torture class suddenly started on the forest floor. If you wanted to study, you should clear the dungeon first and do it in the Magic Tower library.”
“Because I need to do this in order to clear the dungeon. Ngh.”
Needless to say, what Killian was doing right now was the sort of thing any educator would absolutely forbid.
Every time he followed an incorrect formula like that, damage accumulated in his mana circuits.
Only then did Killian raise his frowning face.
“Hmm?”
Oscar, staring at that face, looked slightly startled.
The tattoo that should have crossed the left side of Killian’s eye was nowhere to be seen.
“You, don’t tell me…….”
“You are likely correct in what you are thinking.”
Killian calmly nodded and said,
“In this place, I cannot use tattoo magic.”

Chapter 384: Something That Must Be Protected (2)
“So… the moment you entered this place, your tattoo magic disappeared?”
“That’s right.”
The now-clean face, free of tattoos, moved up and down in a nod.
“That’s pretty sudden… then what’s the dungeon’s condition for clearing it?”
“Prove yourself.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“At a set time every day, a shadow that looks exactly like me appears. I have to fight it.”
A one-on-one duel type dungeon?
If that’s the case, then maybe it isn’t as difficult as he thought—
“Wait a second. Don’t tell me that bastard can use tattoo magic or something?”
“How did you know? That thing freely uses tattoo magic.”
“Hah.”
The clear condition was difficult to comprehend.
Defeat yourself without using mana?
Oscar quickly organized his thoughts before speaking.
“For now, this dungeon is fundamentally focused on personal growth. Solely on that.”
“How do you know that?”
“I just came from Veronica’s dungeon.”
He quickly explained what had happened inside her dungeon.
“I see. In her case, it was like she had been forcing herself into clothes that didn’t fit.”
Killian’s crossed-arms expression became noticeably serious.
“But… hearing that only makes me understand even less. Not once have I ever thought tattoo magic didn’t suit me, or that I was forcing myself to fit into it.”
Oscar unconsciously nodded.
‘He definitely suits tattoo magic.’
True to someone from the forest tribes, he had been born with an outstanding physique to begin with.
Though human, his reflexes and senses were practically animalistic.
‘On top of that, he’s highly proficient in the tribes’ refined traditional martial arts.’
And then he reinforced his body further with tattoo magic, making him nearly unmatched in most situations.
That was the strength possessed by the mage named Killian Lockwood.
Oscar narrowed his eyes.
‘Then what’s his weakness?’
This wasn’t even something worth pondering.
‘Tattoo magic.’
And this applied not only to Killian, but to every mage born from the forest tribes.
The finishing touch.
That was what tattoo magic was to them.
‘Without tattoo magic, he’s just an excellent martial artist. Nothing more, nothing less.’
From the start, even they had felt the limitations in that area, which was why they had sought out the White Tower.
And the tattoo magic devised by the Fifth Tower Masters had perfectly compensated for that flaw.
‘So why did the dungeon erase that tattoo magic?’
At the very least, it was certain the dungeon judged it to be harmful to Killian.
The problem now was figuring out why.
“Anyway, it’s a relief you came. I don’t need to worry anymore.”
“Hm? What are you talking about? Don’t tell me you don’t know the dungeon’s rules.”
“I know an intruder can’t clear the dungeon in my place.”
“So you do know.”
“But if you teach me the formula I’ve been searching for this whole time, won’t that solve everything?”
Oscar momentarily froze.
That was true.
It was true, but…
It felt irritating, like sand trapped inside his shoe.
‘If I teach him the formula and Killian completes it, then yes, that would solve everything.’
If their physical conditions were identical, there was no reason Killian would lose to some mere shadow.
Of course, since the forest tribes were poor at calculations and mana control, it would take some time.
“...But no matter how I think about it, that doesn’t feel like the orthodox way to clear this place.”
“Why do you think that?”
“If I hadn’t barged in here, there’s no way the intended strategy would be to rot in this place for years or decades.”
Magic formulas could not be completed overnight.
Especially not 『Swift』, which Killian was trying to complete.
Even 『Jet Booster』, a mid-tier spell, was the same.
‘There’s a reason the Magic Towers became the mainstream after they were established.’
Dozens of talented mages gathered together, putting their heads together in research.
And even then, not for a day or two, but only after years had passed would a single spell finally be completed.
There were countless people who devoted their entire lives to research and still failed to create even five spells.
“In my opinion… the focus is probably clearing it without using tattoo magic.”
“That’s absurd.”
Killian firmly shook his head.
“If I can’t use tattoo magic, then I’m nothing more than a mere martial artist.”
“...!”
The moment he heard those words—
A conversation between Magiro and Radan flashed through Oscar’s mind.
‘Tower Master, look at him. He’s already Level 8, and he still wants to train in such a barbaric way?’
In response, Radan—who had sealed all his mana and lifted a house-sized boulder using only physical strength—answered.
‘Huff, huff. You… will never… understand. Not in your entire life.’
‘Sorry, but I don’t even want to understand. Why the hell would I do that?’
Watching the two nearly start fighting again, Oscar chuckled.
‘Stop provoking each other already. But Radan, I’m curious too. Why go that far? Even if you train like that, compared to strengthening yourself with tattoo magic, it’s basically meaningless.’
‘Hmm….’
Kuuung!
After setting down the boulder, sweat poured from Radan’s body like rain.
He looked down at the tattoos engraved across his body before speaking.
‘Tattoos are engraved onto the skin, but the sweat shed now is engraved into one’s way of life.’
‘Tower Master, do you understand what the hell he’s talking about?’
‘...Sorry. Even I’m struggling with this one.’
At their reactions, Radan grinned.
‘You two will never understand, no matter how long you live. The life of a warrior can only be understood by another warrior.’
In truth, Oscar had never understood those words throughout his entire life.
He still didn’t know what Radan meant by a “way of life.”
That remained true even now, in his second life.
‘But… I think I vaguely understand what he wanted to say.’
To Radan, tattoo magic had merely been secondary.
A power used to live more like a warrior.
A technique needed to push the forest tribes’ physical talents to their utmost limits.
Not once had Radan considered tattoo magic to be his essence.
As a user of tattoo magic, he stood thoroughly above it.
Because what mattered most to him had always been his life as a warrior.
Training his body every single day.
Tempering himself until he became strong and hard like stone.
Living for the sake of protecting what must be protected.
The tattoos were merely drawings carved into the outer skin for that purpose.
Killian, on the other hand, was different.
—If I can’t use tattoo magic, then I’m nothing more than a mere martial artist.
Oscar lightly shook his head.
Killian Lockwood had to be able to live on even without tattoo magic.
At the very least, that was how Radan had lived.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
Even if he had been unable to use tattoo magic, he still would have remained Radan Lockwood.
Just as Oscar was about to organize his thoughts and speak—
“For now…”
“It’s time.”
Killian’s eyes sharpened as his body sprang up like a cat.
Before Oscar could even react, the man stared intently somewhere.
“Ah, that’s the thing you mentioned…”
“Yeah.”
From between the trees beyond the clearing, something gray emerged.
Its appearance was unmistakably Killian Lockwood.
‘How should I put it… it looks like an unfinished toy.’
Its clothes and even its skin were gray, which only reinforced that impression.
The shadow slowly stepped into the clearing before stopping and silently waiting for Killian.
“What happens if you don’t go?”
“Once enough time passes, it attacks on its own.”
Killian trailed off before falling silent for a moment.
Then he turned his head and stared directly at Oscar.
“Oscar. I duel that shadow using the tribe’s secret arts, so outsiders aren’t allowed to watch.”
“What? Since when is that a thing?”
Even Radan had never hidden things like this.
No, even the forest tribes he had visited several times alongside him had never prohibited it.
If anything, they had wanted to show off how superior they were as warriors.
“...No, forget it. I said something pointless.”
Unable to hide his uncomfortable expression, Killian stepped forward.
Even as he approached right up to it, the shadow remained motionless.
“……….”
Gray eyes incapable of holding emotion stared fixedly at Killian.
As if saying it would wait until he attacked first.
“Arrogant eyes. Here I come.”
Frowning, Killian threw the first punch.
A clean trajectory without unnecessary movement.
‘But….’
Slow.
Slower than any Killian that Oscar had ever seen.
Most likely because not even the most basic enhancement spell like 『Acceleration』 was being used.
Meanwhile, four tattoos lit up one after another across the shadow’s body.
『Acceleration』, 『Skin Hardening』, 『Skeletal Reinforcement』, and 『Nerve Acceleration』.
Ssshaaaak!
Lowering its upper body to evade Killian’s punch, the shadow immediately slipped inside his guard.
“Khng!”
Killian grimaced and hurriedly tried to step backward—
Crunch!
The shadow stomped down on the top of his left foot to stop him before driving an uppercut straight into his jaw.
“Kuhak!”
Killian’s head snapped violently upward.
But since his foot was still pinned down, his body neither lifted nor flew away.
Killian hurriedly tried to focus his mind, but that was impossible.
‘That punch landed squarely on his jaw.’
By now, his vision would be spinning and strange ringing noises would be filling his ears.
His brain had been rattled.
Yet true to a forest warrior, he endured it and unleashed a barrage of punches.
“…….”
The shadow leisurely swayed its upper body, dodging every single one.
Meanwhile, Killian took every attack the shadow threw at him head-on.
“Kh!”
As time passed, Killian’s sharp momentum faded and his movements grew passive.
The arms that had stretched out to attack became desperate just to keep his guard up against the incoming punches.
“Cough! Cough!”
Eventually, Killian’s guard broke, and after taking a hit to the abdomen, he collapsed.
At that moment, the guide’s voice echoed through the space.
[Prove yourself.]
Then the shadow abruptly vanished.
Watching it disappear, Oscar approached.
“Killian, are you okay?”
“...Damn it!”
Gripping the weeds of the clearing tightly enough to rip them out with both fists, Killian slammed the ground.
“If only I had tattoo magic, a bastard like that would’ve… Oscar! Hurry and teach me the formula!”
“Hmm.”
Tattoo magic, tattoo magic.
Even in this situation, that was all he looked for.
And Oscar felt like he finally understood why Killian hadn’t wanted him to watch the fight.
‘He didn’t want me seeing this pathetic side of him.’
The proud forest warrior Killian Lockwood he always knew was nowhere to be seen.
All that stood before him now was a foolish man obsessed with magic after suffering defeat.
“There’s no helping it.”
Oscar let out a deep sigh.
“Killian, get up.”
“...Very well.”
Thinking Oscar was about to teach him magic, Killian immediately rose to his feet.
Thud!
But facing him, Oscar removed his robe and slowly loosened up his body.
“...?”
Looking at the blinking, confused Killian, Oscar spoke.
“Killian. Right now, you’re not fighting like a warrior at all.”
Today, he would show him what a “forest warrior” truly was.

Chapter 385: Things That Must Be Protected (3)
“...What exactly are you trying to do right now?”
Killian frowned.
Because the sight of Oscar loosening up looked exactly like someone preparing for a spar.
“Hooook, hooook. Remember when we first met?”
After thinking for a moment, Killian muttered.
“...Baran City. The back alley.”
“Right. That’s where I beat the hell out of you. Thought I’d bring back some memories from back then.”
“Sorry, but I’m not in the mood for that right now.”
Killian flatly refused the spar.
“Why? Think you’ll lose?”
“I don’t know what you’re talking about. Even if I still had tattoo magic, beating you would be impossible.”
“That’s true.”
Level 6 versus Level 7.
Anyone could tell which side had the advantage.
“...You’ve definitely changed. The old you would’ve brushed something like that off as trivial.”
Rather, he would’ve welcomed it as a chance to test his skills as a warrior.
“No, back then I still had tattoo magic—”
“That damn tattoo magic, tattoo magic. I’m getting sick of hearing it.”
Oscar’s gaze turned cold.
“Listen carefully, Killian. Seems like the two months you spent here planted a sense of helplessness inside you.”
“That’s ridiculous.”
“Like I said earlier, right now, you’re not fighting as a warrior at all.”
It was as though the sensation of defeat had been carved deep into his soul.
And Oscar intended to rip that out by the roots starting now.
Because once you started getting used to that sort of thing, it became harder to cure than most illnesses.
“So what exactly are you trying to do?”
“Fight me.”
“I already told you, in my current state, a fight between us can’t even properly—”
“I won’t use mana.”
“......”
Killian’s eyebrows twitched sharply.
Still, it seemed he hadn’t thrown away the pride a warrior should possess.
“Do you seriously think that makes any sense? A mage like you wants to compete against me in martial combat?”
“Still feels like I’d win.”
“If you truly believe that, then you’re gravely mistaken.”
“Hm, Killian Lockwood... is that all you’ve got...?”
“You...!”
Exasperated by the childish provocation, Killian clamped his mouth shut.
In the end, he let out a sigh and nodded.
“Fine. If you want it that badly, then I’ll fight. I’ll make sure you never again say such absurd things about me being consumed by helplessness.”
“Now that’s more like it.”
Oscar tapped his forehead with a finger.
“Alright, I definitely shut off my mana circuits?”
“...You really think you can be my opponent?”
“Aren’t you underestimating me a little too much?”
Even so, he was a battle mage pursuing mastery of both martial and magical arts.
Radan had even acknowledged him personally.
‘Well, to be fair, I haven’t exactly fought using martial arts much lately either.’
But that was purely because his matchups had been terrible.
Demon Kings, Pentarion, remnants of the Great Emperor’s thoughts... when nothing but lunatics kept showing up, it wasn’t exactly the time to start throwing arm locks around.
“I’m ready.”
“Come.”
Killian growled in a low voice.
Secretly pleased by that, Oscar curled his lips upward.
“In that case, don’t mind if I do.”
His body shot forward like an arrow.
‘He’s taller than me.’
There was one thing to keep in mind when fighting an opponent taller than yourself.
You had to close the distance quickly so they couldn’t take advantage of their longer reach.
The instant the gap closed, Killian naturally tried to step backward.
At that moment, Oscar stepped on the top of his foot.
Just like the shadow had done earlier.
“...!”
Killian’s face twisted viciously.
Thinking he was being mocked, the man immediately threw a punch.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
‘His movements are a little too big.’
That meant Killian was agitated.
It also meant he’d been mentally cornered quite badly.
The Forest Tribe’s martial arts were supposed to be concise and razor-sharp, yet none of those traits could be seen right now.
“Slow.”
Oscar lightly deflected the punch with his shoulder and immediately struck the man’s abdomen.
Bang! Baaang!
The sound of blows hitting a sandbag echoed through the clearing, but it wasn’t enough to secure victory.
‘Damn, what’s this body made of, rocks?’
Because he never neglected his training, Killian’s body remained solid even without mana.
“That won’t be enough.”
Had he realized it didn’t hurt?
Killian attacked with noticeably more ease than before.
‘But if it’s the Forest Tribe’s martial arts...’
Oscar had fought against it countless times through his sparring sessions with Radan.
He effortlessly avoided the incoming trajectories and struck the abdomen again.
As the accumulated damage slowly began to build up, Killian’s brows twitched.
‘What is this?’
Oscar clearly wasn’t using mana.
And yet the flow of the spar was entirely in the other man’s hands.
More than anything else, that alone made no sense to him.
‘In close combat... with hand-to-hand martial arts... I can’t overpower him?’
Freeze.
Killian’s movements halted.
Booom!
The fist buried into his abdomen hurt for the first time.
“Keugh!”
Without realizing it, his body tried to retreat backward.
But the foot pressing down on the top of his own prevented it.
“...!”
At that moment, Killian recoiled in shock as he looked at his own arms, which had instinctively started to rise into a guard.
‘What is this?’
At the same time, Oscar’s earlier words brushed past his ears.
—Listen carefully, Killian. Seems like the two months you spent here planted a sense of helplessness inside you.
He had thought it was nonsense.
He didn’t want to acknowledge it.
He was a warrior of the forest.
A proud warrior who never fled from danger and fought for his comrades and family.
‘A warrior of the forest...’
Killian suddenly looked down at himself.
An awkward posture, like he had started to raise his guard only to stop midway.
No matter how he looked at it, the image was far removed from the word “courage.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
That was why he felt confused.
‘Since when?’
Just when had he become this weak?
Since the time he lost the ability to use tattoo magic?
No—the “courageous Killian” in his memories existed even before that.
Long before he ever learned tattoo magic.
‘...Tattoo magic is definitely powerful.’
Strong, convenient, efficient.
By using it, he could perform the movements he desired at precisely the timing he desired.
Tattoo magic was the power that allowed the scenes he imagined in his head to become reality.
‘Then... was my courage born from tattoo magic?’
No.
He could say that with certainty because he remembered being courageous even before receiving his first tattoo.
At only twelve years old, he had hunted a wild boar.
‘Back then, as my reward, I asked to receive a tattoo.’
The tribal chief had ruffled his hair and refused.
Tattoo magic still came too early for him.
Tattoo magic could only be engraved once someone reached the age where they could understand its meaning and bear its weight.
‘That is what it means to be a warrior of the forest.’
But even now, he still didn’t understand those words.
What was the meaning of tattoo magic the chief spoke of?
And what exactly was he supposed to bear?
“Looks like you’ve still got room to spare? Since you’re zoning out.”
Fsssh!
Oscar’s fist came flying toward him.
Killian instinctively tried to block it, then hesitated.
‘It’s a fist without mana behind it.’
Then why block it?
Because he hated pain?
No—pain was familiar to him.
Warriors of the forest were beings meant to suffer pain and wounds.
They bled, broke, got injured, and fell, yet stood back up and grew stronger again.
That was how he had lived even before receiving tattoos.
“......”
Suddenly, he remembered the days before a single tattoo covered his body, when he fought wild boars.
He had fought while wagering his life with nothing but an axe as large as his own body.
Back then he hadn’t been strong, but even now, when he thought back on it, he had been courageous.
‘The emotion I felt back then was...’
It wasn’t fear of dying.
Nor was it the competitive desire to win no matter what.
Fighting itself had simply been fun and exhilarating.
Even though he had been much weaker than now.
Even though he could’ve lost his life.
Back then, he had smiled more brightly than ever before.
“......”
Oscar’s fist looked slow.
Raising his guard would be easier.
It wouldn’t hurt, and it would be safe.
But Killian simply took the punch head-on.
Crunch!
The inside of his mouth split open.
“...Ptooey!”
As he spat out the metallic-tasting blood, his mind cooled.
“Oscar.”
“What?”
“Is that really all you’ve got? Hit harder.”
“Huh? Seriously?”
“With punches that weak, you couldn’t even kill the wild boar I hunted at twelve years old. Come on, hurry up!”
Oscar shrugged.
He didn’t know about anything else, but he could definitely see the change in the other man’s eyes.
‘No... I should say they’re changing.’
With genuine delight, Oscar swung with full force and smashed Killian across the jaw.
“Tss, ptooey!”
Once again, Killian spat out bloodied saliva, and this time even his lips had split open.
But he shouted while grinning.
“Harder! Hit the other side too!”
“...Aren’t you overdoing it a little?”
“Don’t underestimate a warrior of the forest!”
Bang bang!
As Killian pounded his chest, a fire ignited within his eyes.
Those were the eyes Oscar knew well—eyes like a Forest Tribe warrior whose mind was just a little unhinged.
He liked that look quite a lot.
“Then I’m really going all out now, alright? Don’t complain later.”
“A warrior does not take back the words he speaks.”
“You mean don’t speak twice with one mouth.”
“Whatever, that’s what I meant!”
Smack!
The incoming fist slammed into his cheek.
Feeling both sides of his face throbbing, Killian opened his mouth.
“...Thank you.”
“Did it help?”
“Very much.”
“That’s good to hear. Then... is the spar over?”
“What nonsense are you talking about?”
Killian bared his teeth in a grin.
The blood-soaked teeth looked almost like those of a beast.
“The match still hasn’t been decided. We continue.”
Killian took his stance.
An atmosphere completely different from before began to seep out of him.
“...Oscar.”
“What?”
“Tattoo magic is now a technique—and a weapon—that can no longer be separated from the warriors of the Forest Tribe.”
“That’s true.”
“Choosing and using good weapons is also the quality of an excellent warrior.”
“That’s true too.”
“But it should only remain at the level of something to use. I failed to do that.”
He had depended on that weapon.
Leaned on it.
Had he started believing that weapon was his everything?
“But I was wrong. In that state, I should possess that kind of power even less.”
He was a man who had fought and struggled even before gaining tattoos.
A warrior of the forest, Killian Lockwood.
Tattoo magic was not what proved his worth.
Tattoo magic was not what created the White Tower’s Holy Son.
Because he possessed them, because they were engraved onto his skin, they themselves gained meaning.
“I’m coming.”
Killian lightly swung a punch.
Compared to before, it was a far lighter punch.
“Keugh! Fast as hell!”
Simple and quick.
Even after reading the trajectory, it was difficult to dodge.
His physical specs were identical to before, yet Oscar failed to avoid over half the attacks.
“Damn it! Stop! Stop! I surrender!”
“Hmph. This is the price for acting cocky toward a warrior of the forest.”
Filled with swagger, Killian tilted his head back and shouted.
“I am! A warrior of the forest! Killian Lockwood!”
“...Khng!”
With a nosebleed running down his face, Oscar glared at him resentfully.
“You really hold grudges. You hit my nose on purpose, didn’t you?”
“A warrior of the forest has a heart as broad as a stream. We do not dwell on such trivial matters.”
“...If it’s only as broad as a stream, isn’t that actually narrow?”
“Kuhahaha!”
Killian burst into hearty laughter.

Chapter 386: What Must Be Protected (4)
The next morning.
Killian spoke while eating pineapple preserved in sugar.
“Thank you. Until you made me realize it, I did not know what was important.”
“You know now?”
“Of course I do.”
Thump, thump.
With a confident expression, Killian struck his chest twice.
“What matters to me was not tattoo magic, but the attitude with which I face life as a warrior. Because that is what allowed me to live as myself, and what made me who I am now.”
“…….”
As Killian said that, Radan’s image seemed to overlap with him.
“As long as you know, that’s enough. If you’re grateful, buy me a meal later.”
“I shall. However, Oscar, your personality seems to have changed a little.”
It seemed the aftermath of 『Absolute Stasis』 had made it obvious that several of his emotions had frozen over.
Veronica had also said he had become even more obnoxious, but to think even the dull Killian would say this.
“Really? Specifically, how?”
“Mm, the way you no longer hesitate to express your feelings or thoughts reminds me of you when you were young. Perhaps the personality that had softened because of your amnesia is slowly returning.”
“That is…… not a good thing to say, is it?”
The young Oscar Killian was talking about was probably the psychopathic Oscar from his academy days, the one everyone unanimously mentioned.
He had heard it so many times that his ears were practically calloused.
“That said, it does not feel negative. If anything, you usually looked as if your thoughts were far too deep. Not fitting for your age, I mean.”
Did that…… mean he looked old?
Oscar flinched and changed the subject appropriately.
“By the way. This dungeon, who on earth made it? It has more depth than I expected.”
Veronica’s theme was one thing, but Killian’s theme was the same.
Over Craft and tattoo magic.
It even knew the points for improvement of magic that generally had not been revealed to the world.
“If it is on this scale…… would it not be an eccentric recluse at Level 9?”
“That’s absolutely not it.”
“Mm? How can you be so certain?”
Why else? Because he knew, having been Level 9 just twenty-one years ago.
Once one reached that point, one could naturally sense all the strong people on the continent.
However, the only beings recognized as Level 9-class at the time were the Great Emperor and the Red Witch.
‘Neither of them has any reason to help humans.’
Of course, if a new Level 9 mage had been born over the past twenty-one years, that would be another matter…….
But apart from the Magic Tower Masters, it was impossible for someone of that level to just drop out of the sky.
“There is a saying, an awl in a pouch will show itself. Once you reach that level, even if you want to hide, you naturally end up being revealed.”
“Hm. Indeed, I think I understand what kind of feeling that is.”
As Killian said that, his gaze fixed on Oscar.
“If we think realistically, wouldn’t it have been made by several Level 8 archmages joining forces?”
Oscar looked around.
For now, there were no traces of spatial magic having been used.
In other words, it meant illusion magic was involved, just like what he had seen at the Night of Mages.
“First of all, someone from among the mages of the Violet Magic Tower must definitely have been involved…….”
Including the person who had designed the dungeon overall, there had to be at least two people.
The Violet Magic Tower was closer to being technicians, so it would be difficult for them to be this well-versed in growth design.
“Now that we are talking about it, I am curious. For what purpose did they create something like this?”
“Well…… maybe because they were worried?”
“Worried?”
“Yeah, this dungeon isn’t something that was made an incredibly long time ago.”
Among the formulas that made up this dungeon, several of the ones Oscar could recognize had a fairly modern structure.
No matter how much the meta of magic circled around, optimization like that had been achieved within the past thirty years.
Taking that part into consideration, there was a high chance it had been made around the time before or after the war against the demons.
“Maybe they prepared this kind of arrangement so that, if humanity ever lost or got pushed back in a war, they would have the strength to counterattack.”
“That is highly possible. If so, they truly are people to be grateful to.”
“Yeah. Or maybe they just made it because they were bored.”
“……There would be no madman who would create a dungeon of this scale for such a reason.”
“That’s true too.”
He did not know who they were, but from the White Tower’s standpoint, they had received great help, so they were benefactors.
It was true that they had dramatically shortened the growth time of those problem children.
“You’re confident today, right?”
“You mean the duel against that shadow fellow?”
Crunch, crunch.
After chewing and swallowing the pineapple, Killian replied in an even voice.
“I will win. Because I am a warrior of the forest who knows no defeat.”
* * *
Sssrk.
When noon came, as expected, the shadow appeared beyond the clearing.
Unlike last time, Killian was already standing in the center of the clearing, rolling his neck as he waited for the fellow.
“Come.”
“…….”
What returned was not an answer, but four glowing tattoos, just like last time.
Shaaaak!
In an instant, the distance narrowed, and at the same time, crunch!
The opponent’s fist struck Killian’s jaw.
It had enough force to shake his skull violently.
“…….”
But Killian slowly turned his head and looked at the shadow.
“That hurts.”
The spot where the fist had struck throbbed, and he could feel it swelling.
Killian wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth and smiled.
“Yes, it still hurts.”
But he was not as afraid as yesterday.
He did not want to run away either.
No further self-doubt existed.
Right now, Killian’s heart was blazing more fiercely than ever before.
“But that is all.”
Clench!
Killian’s left hand grabbed the shadow by the collar.
The moment the shadow silently looked down at that hand.
Shaaaak!
A right straight shot toward the fellow’s face.
“…….”
The shadow avoided it by lightly moving his head.
His indifferent eyes seemed to ask what he had just done.
Crunch!
Then the shadow’s foot trampled down on Killian’s instep.
The will to never let him run away came up through his foot.
“Do not worry.”
Killian grinned and threw another punch.
The shadow likewise avoided it lightly and threw a light jab.
Kwaaaang!
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
At that light punch, Killian’s head snapped backward, his nasal bone broke, and blood flowed down.
“It is just the right amount of pain.”
But Killian threw his fist again as if it were nothing.
“…….”
The shadow dodged it and drove in another punch.
Blood scattered through the air like paint, but Killian swung his fist again.
That sight repeated endlessly.
“…….”
Flinch.
The shadow, who had been about to throw a punch, suddenly stopped moving.
Killian’s face was covered in blood, and various places were swollen, but.
The eyes visible through it all were no different from the beginning.
“I can endure the pain of the flesh as much as needed.”
Killian clenched his fist tightly.
“What truly makes me angry is that my heart almost broke. That I almost forgot what kind of being I am.”
Shaaaak!
The shadow hastily twisted his head, but the fist grazed past the tip of his jaw.
“…….”
Drip, a line of blood flowed from the jaw where a thin cut had been drawn.
The shadow wiped it with his hand and looked at it, and his eyes trembled faintly for the first time.
He stared at the warrior before him with eyes that simply could not understand.
Why does he not give up?
Why is he not afraid?
How can he not collapse?
Reading that expression, Killian grinned.
“You will not understand even if a lifetime passes. Because you are not a warrior.”
He might be able to imitate the appearance, but he could not imitate the things filling the inside.
“I am coming.”
Kwaaaang!
Killian’s fist turned the shadow’s jaw for the first time.
The shadow staggered greatly from it and, the moment he unconsciously tried to step backward.
Press! Killian’s foot crushed down on the fellow’s instep.
“When I met strong enemies, I got hit. On days I failed to hunt, I starved. There were countless times I was defeated and injured, and my bones were broken. But even so, I never gave up.”
Because a warrior of the forest was that kind of being.
The two of them were the same height, but in this moment, Killian’s eyes were clearly looking down on his opponent.
“That was the kind of person I was. Then, what about you?”
Bang! Kwaang!
The shadow thrashed wildly and struck Killian’s face and abdomen without discrimination.
Killian, who did not blink even in the face of that distant fear, calmly stared at his opponent’s face.
“You have never lived the life of a warrior.”
Crunch!
A fist slammed into Killian’s abdomen.
His ribs screamed, and the taste of blood spread through his mouth.
“You have never watched over comrades either.”
Kwaang!
Once again.
“You have not even experienced failure.”
Kwaang!
The shadow’s fists, swung at random, began striking places that were not vital points.
“You have never endured pain, nor have you ever overcome fear.”
“…….”
The shadow no longer even threw punches.
Because, upon facing a warrior who would not fall no matter what he did, he had become terrified.
“You are not a warrior.”
The shadow, unable to endure the pain, struggled to pull away backward.
But Killian did not allow it until the very end.
“And I do not lose to those who are not warriors.”
Kwaaaaang!
Killian’s fist struck the shadow’s face squarely.
The fellow’s body was sent flying backward just like that, and at the same time as it crashed into a tree.
[Proof successful]
[Theme Dungeon conquest complete]
The dungeon declared his victory.
Clench!
Raising his tightly clenched right hand above his head, Killian closed both eyes and smiled.
“I won.”
With those words as the last, Killian’s body, having lost consciousness, collapsed just like that.
“……That guy really fights stupidly.”
Oscar muttered as he hurried over and supported the collapsing fellow.
When he saw him at times like this, it almost felt as if Killian fought even more stupidly than his own father.
Srrrk!
Just then, Killian’s body vanished as if it had been a lie.
Realizing that this was the result of the guide’s intervention, Oscar turned his head.
“I laid him down on the bed in the cabin. Once he regains consciousness, I plan to send him out together with his reward.”
The guide, who had appeared at some point, was standing to one side of the clearing and looking at him.
“Congratulations. You have already succeeded in your second intrusion. How does it feel?”
“……Good. Since it seems like such a well-made dungeon, I feel a fair bit of accomplishment too.”
“Thank you for the praise.”
The guide, who smiled contentedly as he turned his body, stared intently at him.
“I am curious about one thing. How exactly are you able to pick out only the parts those people need like that?”
The guide’s eyes narrowed.
“Even though you are not someone who has already walked that path.”
“I was lucky, that’s all.”
“Lucky, is it?”
The guide slowly nodded as if chewing over those words in his mouth.
“Good. I will watch with anticipation to see whether that luck continues to follow you.”
Snap, snap!
When the guide flicked his fingers twice, a door appeared.
“If you go out through that door, you will return to the place you came from.”
With those words as the last, the guide disappeared like a mountain spirit.
Oscar, left in place, stroked his chin.
‘What is this?’
Was it just his imagination that the guide’s attitude had changed from the beginning?
Oscar thought about whether there was something he had done wrong.
‘Is he angry because I conquered two dungeons I intruded into in an instant?’
Well, if he had put effort into making them and they were easily cleared, he might get angry…….
But it did not seem to be simply for that reason.
This was just a feeling.
‘It feels like he’s wary of me, and also like he’s trying to probe something.’
A Level 8 mage who could have joined forces with a mage of the Violet Tower to make this dungeon.
‘Surely it isn’t someone I know, right?’
Personally, he thought he had not had any major problems with interpersonal relationships in his previous life.
But that was subjective to the end, so it was not as if there were no mages who disliked him.
‘Like old men such as Kudel or Pentarion.’
That could not be the case, but having his identity exposed would not be a good thing.
Oscar, thinking that he would have to choose his conduct and words carefully, stepped through the door.
“Mm?”
Beyond the opened door, his gaze met two familiar faces.
‘Tesila Windroar. And…….’
The new Yellow Tower Master, Tony Havertz.
The two of them were walking out from the opposite door.

Chapter 387: Tower of Trials (1)
“Huh? Oscar!”
Tesila, who recognized him, waved happily and greeted him.
Oscar nodded to her, but his gaze remained fixed on Tony.
‘He definitely entered the theme later than I did…… yet he’s already out?’
When he calculated the time, only barely more than a day had passed.
He had said from the beginning that he had only cleared about two days in his schedule, so it seemed he had enough confidence to justify it.
“The second intrusion? Ah, now that I think about it, there’s no need to ask.”
The very fact that he himself had come out unharmed meant the theme dungeon had already been cleared.
Oscar nodded and replied.
“Yes, I was lucky, so it ended quickly. It looks like things ended incredibly quickly for you two as well.”
“This side was a theme where psychological factors played a major role.”
Psychological factors.
He felt like he could roughly understand what that meant without even hearing the details.
‘Pentarion Ereus. If it was that selfish old man, he wouldn’t have exactly cherished him just because he was his disciple.’
Rather, there was a high possibility he had hoarded his own knowledge and simply acted spiteful.
He must have been worried that his capable disciple would surpass him, and so prevented him from devoting himself fully to magic.
Of course, because of that, the field of magic engineering had developed, so it was truly ironic.
“Oscar Crucian…….”
Tony Havertz looked this way with a rather complicated gaze.
‘Well, it’s not like I don’t understand.’
After all, he, together with the Heavenly Sword and Sasha, had executed Tony’s master, who had betrayed humanity.
That said, it was also ambiguous to call him an enemy.
Because thanks to that, Tony must have been able to take the position of master of the Yellow Magic Tower.
Oscar slightly lowered his head first.
“My greetings are late. Congratulations on becoming the master of the Yellow Magic Tower.”
“……I never thought I’d receive congratulations from you. This feels extremely strange.”
Reading the awkward yet peculiar atmosphere between the two, Tesila muttered.
“What? Are you two perhaps on bad terms?”
“No, it isn’t particularly like that.”
Oscar shrugged and looked at Tony.
“Of course, our White Tower hasn’t exactly had a close relationship with the Yellow Tower until now…… but who knows what will happen from now on.”
“From now on, huh.”
Tony muttered softly.
“……Certainly, your side is better than the Red Tower or the Blue Tower.”
“I was already hoping to have a conversation with you regarding business matters, so I’ll arrange a meeting soon.”
“Business?”
“Matters related to batteries and trains.”
At those words, Tony’s eyes changed.
As befitting an intelligent person, he must have realized from those words alone what parts they could fill in for each other.
“That is good news.”
He then checked the watch on his wrist and gave the two of them a nod.
“Then I’ll see you again next time.”
Oscar watched Tony head toward the massive door for a moment.
Then, sensing something strange, he flinched in surprise.
“Wait, where is that man going right now?”
At that question, Tesila made a puzzled expression.
“Well, obviously he’s going to the exit, right? He succeeded in clearing the dungeon. Why are you asking something so obvious?”
“…….”
Obvious?
Oscar’s brow narrowed.
He had intruded twice, and he had succeeded in clearing it twice.
But Veronica had been personally sent out of the dungeon by the guide, and Killian had supposedly been moved to the cabin.
“By any chance, when the clear is successful, does everyone leave like that? Regardless of the difficulty?”
“That’s right. Otherwise, what other way would there be to leave the dungeon?”
Tesila let out a silly laugh and looked behind her shoulder.
“Now that I think about it, I don’t see your friend. Ah! Did he perhaps use that space magic thing?”
“…….”
Oscar pressed his mouth shut and sank into serious thought.
Why?
Why had only those two been treated as “special”?
The guide’s attitude, which had seemed to subtly keep him in check, kept coming to mind.
‘Don’t tell me those guys didn’t go outside the dungeon, and they’re trapped somewhere instead?’
What flashed through his mind in that instant was the demon race, who used every sort of dirty and sinister trick.
If it were those bastards, it wouldn’t be strange for them to create a dungeon and then take humanity out one by one.
“Oscar?”
“……!”
At that moment, he turned his body sharply at the voice he heard from behind.
There stood Killian, with a languid expression as though he had not fully woken up.
“My memory is a bit hazy, but I did beat that shadow fellow, right?”
“You…… are you really Killian?”
“What are you suddenly talking about?”
Oscar bombarded the fellow, who was blinking both eyes, with questions.
“When we fought in Baran City, where were you injured?”
“Don’t tell me you forgot that? My internal organs were ruptured, so I asked you to carry out a request on my behalf, didn’t I?”
“On the way back after finishing our schedule in Baran, where did we first meet the mage hunter?”
“If I remember correctly, it was the underground black market.”
Seeing the fellow answer smoothly, as if asking why he was doing this, Oscar felt unsure.
Oscar examined his physical condition and asked.
“……You definitely lost consciousness only a few minutes ago.”
“Is that so? Then that astonishing recovery ability must be proof that I am a warrior of the forest.”
This made him seem real too.
Oscar looked around and lowered his voice.
“Nothing happened inside the cabin, right?”
“Happened? Nothing happened. To begin with, I was alone when I opened my eyes.”
“The tattoo magic?”
“I tried using it just in case as well.”
Crackle!
The tattoo engraved across Killian’s eye shone brightly.
“It operated normally. Of course, I have no intention of depending on this.”
“……I see.”
Was it needless worry?
Oscar slowly nodded.
“Don’t wander off anywhere else and go straight to the White Tower.”
“You’re nagging again.”
“Sssip.”
“Fine. I shall do so.”
Killian opened the gigantic door and went outside.
As Tesila watched him, she said,
“You look incredibly uneasy. Did something happen?”
“……No. Nothing.”
For now, it was fortunate that Killian was safe, but that did not mean the suspicious parts had disappeared.
It was a fact that the two of them had left the dungeon in a different way from others.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
Oscar asked.
“Lady Tesila, by any chance, when the dungeon clear is completed, does the guide appear?”
“Hm? Guide? The person you meet in the cabin when you first enter the dungeon? No? This is the first I’m hearing of it.”
As expected.
He did not know the reason, but it seemed certain that he and those two problem children were special cases.
Though he still did not quite know why.
‘For now, I guess I have no choice but to clear Fran’s theme dungeon and ask the guide directly about this.’
Of course, that was assuming the guide appeared then as well.
But for some reason, he had a strange certainty that the guide would show himself then too.
“……I’ll be going now.”
“Wait, you’re going to go in again right away without even resting?”
“I can rest inside too.”
“That’s true, but…… no. I suppose you would be worried about your friend. This way.”
Tesila guided him to Fran’s door and said,
“If you succeed in clearing even the third intrusion, wait outside. I might be late.”
“Understood.”
He also did not want to miss the chance to use the powerful force that was Tesila’s adventurer party.
Oscar stepped straight into Fran’s door.
“…….”
What stood there was a tower soaring endlessly upward.
Kwaaaaa!
A gigantic typhoon was raging through the tower’s lower sections.
Above that, lightning was striking without pause.
When he tilted his head farther back, he could also see floors wrapped in flames that would not go out.
There were also floors thick with poisonous fog, and floors frozen solid.
“What the hell is that?”
It was not as if it were some comprehensive gift set.
Oscar stared blankly at the bizarre tower, then turned his head.
‘……It’s coming.’
Something was flying toward him at an incredibly fast speed.
But only for a moment.
Oscar, realizing who the owner of that mana was, lowered his guard.
“Wait, Oscar?”
The person who had flown over using 『Flight』, Fran, also opened his eyes round and landed softly.
Oscar quickly scanned him from head to toe.
‘Oh-ho, Level 6?’
The last time he had seen Fran, he had been Level 5.
Although he had thought Fran would become stronger after forming a contract with the colorless spirit……
‘That had nothing to do with a mage’s achievements.’
Even if he became stronger by borrowing a spirit’s power, there was no reason the number of his mana circuits would increase.
And yet, currently, six distinct mana circuits had been installed in Fran’s body.
“……What is this? Is this also part of the trial?”
“Why, does it suddenly get hard for you when I appear in front of you?”
Hearing that indifferent voice, Fran muttered.
“Seeing how unlucky you are, you really are Oscar. No, wait, that guy hasn’t been that unlucky lately, has he?”
“Seeing as you still have the energy to spout nonsense, you must still be managing to live.”
“That venomous tongue…… Oscar!”
Fran jumped in surprise and approached.
“How on earth did you end up here…… Ah, did you perhaps intrude?”
“Why wouldn’t I have? I was asked to rescue you problem children because you had disappeared.”
“It’s not really enough to call us disappeared…… We’re not children anymore, either.”
Oscar glanced at the grumbling fellow and said,
“Exactly. Once you’re about a Level 6 mage, the time for causing that sort of worry should have passed.”
“Ah, you noticed?”
The fellow, wiping the bridge of his nose, smiled happily.
“It seemed like the reason my skills had been stagnant all this time was because of the low-grade spirit you installed in my body.”
“……Don’t tell me you blamed that on me.”
“Eh, no way! Of course not! I do have a conscience!”
The moment Fran, startled, waved his hands and began making excuses.
A spirit popped out from behind his head.
-Contractor’s heart rate increase confirmed. It is assessed to be because he is lying.
“Oho.”
Oscar folded his arms and tilted his head crookedly as he stared at him, and Fran gulped.
“I-it’s not that I blamed you in particular…… I just thought, ‘You were the one who installed it for me.’ I was reminiscing.”
-Correction. The contractor had resolved that, if he met Oscar Crucian later, he would strongly confront him about it.
Fran scratched his cheek and avoided his gaze.
“Did I say something like that? I don’t really remember.”
-If you do not remember, I shall repeat exactly what you said at that time……
“N-no! It’s fine, so stop!”
Fran hurriedly stopped Mu and smiled awkwardly.
“Haha, maybe because this guy spent his whole life in the spirit world, he still tends to misinterpret human speech.”
“Let’s just say that’s what happened for now. Congratulations on Level 6.”
Although it was slower than Veronica or Killian, it was an achievement faster than the other mages of their generation.
Besides, considering that those two had already surpassed the middle stage of Level 6, the fact that this fellow needed to catch up to them remained unchanged.
“I’m on my way back from the other two’s dungeons.”
“……I’m last? That’s a little upsetting.”
“No matter how I thought about it, your dungeon seemed like it would be the hardest.”
Oscar glanced at Mu.
Fran, understanding what he meant, nodded.
“True. I don’t know what those two’s dungeons were like, but this one is definitely troublesome.”
The fellow looked at the towering tower and said,
“Reach it. That was the voice I heard after entering this place.”
“Reach it?”
Oscar’s gaze naturally moved toward the tower’s highest floor.
Although it was hidden by clouds and could not be seen, the meaning of that gaze was clear.
“Ah, for reference, I’ve already climbed the tower to the very top. Nearly fifty times, even.”
“……And even then, you didn’t receive a clear-success judgment?”
Was it not simply a matter of reaching the highest floor?
“Yeah. I went all the way to the top, even to the rooftop, and searched everywhere in case there was some hidden mechanism. So then I wondered if it meant I had to reach Level 6, and I reached it, but the result is…… as you can see.”
“Don’t tell me it’s asking you to reach Level 7?”
“I also don’t think that’s it, but there’s no other method, so for now, I’m training.”
“Hmm.”
Simply reaching Level 7 was probably not the clear condition.
If that were the condition, there would be no reason for such a flashy tower to exist.
‘Whatever the clear condition is, it’s certain that it’s related to that tower, so……’
Oscar lightly loosened up his body and said,
“Get ready.”
“……For what?”
“We need to climb it.”
He intended to check for himself whether there was anything Fran had missed.

Chapter 388: Tower of Trials (2)
“When I first came in, I wondered what the hell this was.”
Inside the tower he had entered with Fran, there was nothing at all.
Only stairs installed along the wall.
If there was one peculiar point, it was that the ceiling was extremely high.
In terms of the White Tower, it seemed as though the height of about five floors had been sectioned off as a single floor.
“There really isn’t much here.”
“This way.”
Fran began climbing the stairs with practiced steps.
“As you can see, to go up, you just use the stairs like this.”
“That’s all?”
“Only the first floor is like that. You saw the tower from outside, right? It should be easy to see even from far away.”
“It was pretty flashy.”
Oscar answered while recalling the sections where storms raged and fire and thunder poured out.
“Right. That starts from the first floor.”
Click.
The moment they reached the end of the first-floor stairs and opened the thick iron door, Kwaaaaaa!
A fierce wind began shaking their clothes and entire bodies.
“Urgh! This is the second floor, the storm zone.”
“…….”
Oscar frowned and lifted his head.
The ceiling height seemed exactly the same as the first floor.
The only difference was that a storm had been added.
“Hup!”
When Fran closed the iron door again, the wind vanished as if it had been a lie.
“Why’d you close it? Aren’t we going in?”
“You can’t talk once you go in there. The sound of the wind is too loud.”
Well, it had been strong enough that even keeping one’s balance was difficult.
“Anyway, the only thing that changes is the environment. You climb the stairs the same way.”
“With your physical abilities, that couldn’t have been easy either.”
“Heh heh, don’t you see this?”
Press! Fran proudly showed off his arm, which had more muscle than before.
“I’m no longer the me you used to know, okay? You said I couldn’t neglect physical training either.”
“Hmm.”
Only then did Oscar look at Fran’s body again, and sure enough, muscle had clearly developed here and there.
When he first saw him, Fran had been slender, like a typical shut-in mage or a rich family’s young master.
‘Now that I think about it, Veronica and Killian are like that too.’
It seemed they had each not neglected their training even without him.
Oscar smiled with satisfaction.
“You have put on some muscle. Looks good. Though you still have a long way to go.”
“……Stingy bastard. If you’re going to praise me anyway, why not go all the way? It’s not like it’ll wear you out.”
“You’ll develop bad habits, so no.”
Oscar firmly cut off his complaint and said,
“From now on, let’s keep going straight up without stopping. I think I’ll only get a feel for it once we try it once.”
“Got it.”
Fran opened the iron door again and began climbing the stairs through the storm.
‘The second floor is wind, and it’s not really dangerous enough to threaten your life.’
After they passed through without trouble, the third floor that appeared was a place where thunder raged.
The fourth floor was a place where furious flames swept about.
The floors above that each had a theme called an attribute as well, so passing through them was not easy.
“This is the last floor.”
The tenth floor, reached after hardships, was an empty space just like the first floor.
Oscar looked around and asked,
“It doesn’t look particularly special.”
“I told you, didn’t I? I’m not lying. I even wondered if there were devices in the floor or walls, so I pushed and pulled everything.”
“How many times did you say you climbed this tower?”
“Probably close to fifty. Mu, do you happen to remember the exact number?”
-Total of 47 times.
47 times.
It certainly did not seem as though he had climbed it only once or twice.
Fran looked quite familiar with climbing the stairs, too.
“……Or maybe you aren’t supposed to climb it with physical ability alone?”
“Don’t even start. I’m telling you, there really isn’t anything I haven’t tried.”
Fran lightly waved his hand.
“There was a time I climbed up using only 『Flight』 through mana, and there was a time I turned my whole body into wind with Lord of Wind and climbed up while ignoring everything. I’ve climbed the outer wall instead of the inside too…… Ah, recently, I even climbed up and came back down while walking backward.”
“……You worked hard.”
At that level, it really was true that he had tried all sorts of methods.
The problem was that even so, the dungeon had not judged the attack as successful.
‘What’s the problem?’
Wondering if perhaps he had to find something on each floor, he stared into every nook and cranny so hard that his eyes hurt.
Naturally, nothing could be seen.
‘No, maybe I’m too buried in the tower right now.’
Oscar thought about the very method by which this dungeon made challengers stronger.
He had solved the problem the same way during Killian’s case too.
‘Does Fran currently have some kind of problem or weak point?’
When he stared fixedly at the guy, Fran scratched his cheek for no reason.
“Um, this is really pressuring me right now.”
“Do you have some kind of problem somewhere?”
“Huh?”
“When you think about yourself, is there any part where you feel, I’m lacking in this, or I’d like to fill this in a little?”
“…….”
After seriously thinking for about five minutes, Fran opened his mouth with difficulty.
“There is one part that’s a little embarrassing to say.”
“It’s fine, so say it. Unless you want to live here with me for the rest of your life.”
At those words, Fran hesitated for a moment, then mumbled awkwardly.
“Fame. To be exact, an epithet…… or something.”
“Huh?”
When Oscar furrowed his face, wondering what kind of nonsense this was, the guy raised his voice as if he had a guilty conscience.
“N-No, I mean, isn’t that how it is! You’re the Noble of the White Tower, and Killian is the Holy One. Even Veronica apparently got an epithet not long ago! After reaching Level 6, she’s been performing incredibly on missions.”
“…….”
Phew, right, this was not something he could simply blame Fran for.
There had definitely been a lack of explanation on his own part too.
“Not something like that. Something thoroughly related to your skill or realm as a mage.”
“Y-You should’ve said that from the beginning!”
The guy, whose face had gone bright red, sank into thought again.
Then, after a long while, he shook his head.
“I’m not sure.”
“……Are you bragging in front of me?”
“No, it’s not that. I really don’t know!”
Fran looked on the verge of tears, as if he sincerely felt wronged.
“If I had known something like that in the first place, I would’ve fixed it long ago! But lately, everything is so good that I wonder whether it’s really okay for me to have no worries like this. To begin with, you know, don’t you? My self-esteem isn’t that high.”
“Hmm.”
That was certainly true.
The reason this guy had tried to return to his family was also because he had no certainty that he could succeed as a mage.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
‘To be exact, he thought his own talent was ambiguous.’
But the Fran of now was a completely different mage from back then.
Fundamentally, his magic skills were incomparable to before.
‘The part I could at least call a weakness was his lack of mana control…….’
Originally, a low-grade spirit had been controlling it in his stead, but recently Mu had been handling it.
That was a definite upgrade even if one grabbed any passing elf and asked them.
In other words, the Fran of now had no restrictions at all even when using Lord of Wind.
“Technically, there’s no problem, but perhaps some trauma remains?”
“Mm, not at all from what I feel? Mu, do I have anything like that left in me?”
-When the contractor uses Lord of Wind, no emotions of fear or dread are felt whatsoever.
“That’s what it says?”
So it was not a psychological issue.
“What about spirit affinity?”
“No worries there either. By now, it’s probably even higher than yours.”
-Agreed.
If a spirit felt that way, then it must be a fact with no room for disagreement.
“Mm, then what else is left? How’s Dance of Steel?”
“Now that I’m fully proficient and can adjust the strength, I don’t collapse from exhaustion after using it a few times like before.”
“…….”
He had a named spirit, used Lord of Wind, and could even freely use Dance of Steel?
Oscar looked at the mage before him with a newly impressed expression.
‘Then…… he’s just a ridiculously high-level mage, isn’t he?’
He was at a level where he would rank at the very top even if placed against the entire White Tower.
It felt like only yesterday that he had been whining about having no talent and being scared to use Lord of Wind, so it really was deeply moving.
“It’s all good news, but it’s not especially helpful in this situation.”
“Because I’m not lacking anything?”
“Right. I have to know what you’re lacking to guess the attack condition.”
Or was reaching Level 7 really the attack condition?
But if that were the case, the tower itself did not help in any way with reaching Level 7.
“This is difficult. Let’s go down for now.”
After descending the tower, the two of them continued talking a great deal.
Usually, it took the form of Oscar asking questions and Fran answering.
“Hmm.”
After a long conversation, night had already fallen.
Oscar sat before a torch, stared at a paper marked with check marks, and shook his head.
“It’s not mana control or circulation, and the circuit design is flawless. No problem psychologically either. On top of that, he’s in a state where he can freely use Lord of Wind…….”
Tap, tap, Oscar tapped one line with his finger.
“Then it really seems like there’s nothing but the spirit left.”
“I guess so after all?”
Fran scratched the back of his head.
He looked at Mu, who was hovering near the torch, and said,
“It’s true that the one with the most open growth potential right now is that guy.”
“Have you figured out what a colorless spirit can do?”
“Not yet.”
Fran shook his head.
“Basically, Mu is an incredibly old spirit, so even its memories of the past are blurry. It doesn’t even know when it started existing. Naturally, it doesn’t know what abilities it has either.”
“Then right now, helping with mana control is about the extent of it?”
“Right.”
Of course, even that was an incredible effect.
In fact, it was surely far more effective than when he used a low-grade spirit.
But that alone was not enough.
‘This guy rejected two Spirit Kings in order to contract with the colorless spirit.’
And yet he did not know how to use it.
He did not even know what it could do.
He had simply contracted with it out of his single-minded desire to complete not another person’s color, but his own color.
“Fran Sirius’s own color, huh.”
Oscar suddenly spoke.
“What is that?”
“……All of a sudden?”
“You said it yourself. The reason you rejected the Spirit Kings’ contracts was because you felt their colors would paint over you. On the other hand, you chose Mu because you thought it wouldn’t dye you.”
“I did. And in reality, I think I saw that part accurately.”
“Then what is this color of your own that you wanted to protect and complete so badly?”
“…….”
At that question, Fran was rendered speechless.
His own color.
He had said that back then, but he had never seriously thought about it in particular.
He had been busy training day after day, trying to catch up to the companions who had already gone far ahead.
“That’s a difficult question. Honestly, I don’t really know.”
He muttered while looking at the torch.
“You already know this, but ever since I was young, I grew up watching the backs of my older brothers and sisters.”
In the eyes of a child, they shone.
The sight of them producing clear achievements in their respective fields and being acknowledged by everyone was something he admired.
“No matter what I did, I was above average, but not enough to aim for first place. I was ambiguous.”
Swordsmanship, magic, martial arts, business, politics.
There was not a single area where he could feel certain that he was better than his brothers and sisters.
“I think that’s still the same now.”
Fran, wearing a self-deprecating smile, looked at him.
“When it comes to mana control, I can’t even reach your toes. In combat sense using magic or close-quarters hand-to-hand fighting, I can’t match Killian, and I can’t even dream of reaching Veronica in ultra-fast casting and calculation ability. Compared to before, I’ve become absurdly strong, but I’m still an ambiguous mage.”
Fran slowly lowered his gaze.
Saaaaa.
His two hands, which had become wind, fluttered as if rippling in the torchlight.
“If I didn’t have the special ability called Lord of Wind, I probably wouldn’t even have been able to stand shoulder to shoulder with all of you.”
“Now you have the colorless spirit too.”
“That’s on the same extension. If I didn’t have Lord of Wind, there would’ve been no reason for me to go inside the World Tree either.”
A mage who would have been nothing without Lord of Wind.
What kind of color could possibly suit such an ambiguous person?
As Fran looked down at his own hand with a lonely gaze for a moment, Mu slowly approached.
Ssk, sssk.
The guy rubbed its body against his hand, which had become wind.
“……What, are you comforting me right now?”
-I am aware that humans feel great emotional stability from the act of touching flesh with something.
“It’s not like you’re some cat or dog.”
Fran chuckled.
It was after that that he noticed the sense of incongruity.
“Wait, but is it because of the firelight? You look a little redder than usual.”
-Is that so? It is probably because I ate a bit of the torch.
“……Why would you eat that?”
-I do not know. As I watched it quietly, it looked tasty, so I ate it.
No matter how different a spirit’s eating habits were from a human’s, for it to eat fire of all things.
The baffled Fran shook his head, and the moment he stroked Mu.
Hwaaaak!
Suddenly, the red energy drained completely out of Mu’s body, and his hand was dyed red.
