Chapter 389: Tower of Trials (3)
Fran’s two hands, which had become wind and were fluttering about, were dyed red.
As if he himself hadn’t seen it, he shrugged and looked this way.
“This is what I mean about him. Sometimes he says he’s hungry and just eats stuff like that. Even though he won’t so much as touch actual food.”
“Fran, you…….”
“Hold on, let me get some water.”
The moment Fran lifted the bottle to drink water.
Chiiiiik!
The bottle melted down, and then—peooong!
The water, boiling up in an instant, splashed in every direction.
『Wind Shield』
Fran, who had been staring blankly as Oscar hurriedly used magic, asked.
“Wh-what the hell. Why did that suddenly explode? Was it defective?”
“You okay?”
“Ah, yeah. Thanks to you, I’m not really hurt anywhere.”
“That’s not what I mean. Your hands. Are they okay?”
“My hands?”
Only then did Fran look down at his own hands and jump in surprise.
“Wh-what the hell! Why are my hands like this!”
“Stay still for a second.”
Grab!
Oscar reached out and wrapped his hand around the guy’s red hand.
Then, he felt a burning heat across his entire palm.
‘……Even with the breeze there, it’s this hot?’
If he had grabbed it with his bare hand, he would have suffered a terrible burn.
Oscar let go of his hand and said.
“Looks like we found it.”
“Found what?”
“How to use Mu.”
“What are you talking about?”
“Mu ate the torch and turned red. Then, when he rubbed his body against your hands, the color drained from him, and conversely, your hands turned red.”
“Which means…….”
“Maybe that’s the ability possessed by a colorless spirit.”
Judging only by the sequence of events, there was a possibility that its ability was absorbing and transferring attributes.
If this hypothesis was true, the ways to make use of Mu would become truly boundless.
‘Especially in the case of this guy, who can turn his entire body into wind through Lord of Wind…….’
It was to the point where he could not even estimate what kinds of things he might be capable of doing.
Oscar calmed the excitement that had boiled up in him for the first time in a while and opened his mouth.
“We’ll have to research this a little first. Fran.”
“Got it!”
Now, one word was enough.
Fran knew what he had to do, and changed both his hands into Lord of Wind.
“Good. You stay on standby just like that, and Mu, try eating that torch.”
-Hah-eup.
Mu took a huge bite out of the torch.
However, unlike before, his body did not turn red or anything of the sort.
“…….”
“…….”
A situation where they had run into difficulty from the very beginning.
“Oscar, why is the result different?”
“Good question.”
Oscar, resting his chin on his hand, sank into thought.
Generally, when conducting a magic experiment, the most important thing to pay attention to was the environment.
Only by experimenting under the same environment could one obtain consistent values.
‘What’s different compared to before?’
Oscar first tried adding more firewood to the torch.
But the result was the same.
“Hmm. In that case, could it be that emotional exchange has to be taken into account too?”
“But if that’s the condition, I don’t think it’d be possible to use in actual combat.”
That was true.
In actual combat, where every second counted, there would be no leisure to sit around receiving comfort.
-Correction. The way I see it, that is not what is important.
“Then?”
At Fran’s words, Mu replied with a sullen expression.
-The problem is that I am full.
“……What?”
-I was hungry before. So the moment I saw the torch, I thought I wanted to eat it, and so I ate it.
Could it be that there was a capacity he could eat at one time?
“Then you can’t eat at all right now?”
-If I force myself, I can eat, but the feeling is completely different.
“What’s different, and how?”
-It feels like it goes into a different stomach.
“……It’s not like you have a separate stomach for meals and a separate stomach for dessert.”
But if Mu felt that way, then that was probably the closest thing to the truth.
With problems like this, what the person himself felt was often the correct answer.
“Then for now, let’s wait until you get hungry again.”
After the two of them sat in front of the torch and chatted quietly for a while.
Mu suddenly opened his mouth.
-Now! I have become hungry!
“Oh, Oscar! The time?”
“About thirty minutes.”
“That’s totally fine, isn’t it? We could even use it in actual combat!”
Oscar threw cold water on the delighted Fran.
“It’s too early to be happy. The time may differ depending on the amount eaten and the type of attribute.”
“Ah, true…….”
Fran, realizing that he had been too hasty, nodded.
“Then what should we experiment with first?”
“There’s a lot to do.”
Eat different amounts at one time and check the time it takes to digest them.
Record the differences between when the absorbed attribute is transferred to Fran and when it is not.
Calculate the difference in digestion time according to the two cases above.
Finally, repeat numbers 1 through 3 above with different attributes.
Fran’s face darkened after hearing Oscar’s words.
“Uh, I’ve never done this kind of magic research before. Even just hearing that roughly, it doesn’t sound like it’ll be over in a day or two?”
“You’ve got good instincts.”
At minimum, five days.
That was the “first research period” Oscar had in mind.
Under Oscar’s guidance and instruction, the research proceeded smoothly.
Of course, that was strictly from Oscar’s point of view.
-……Do I have to eat again?
“You should be hungry around now, though?”
-Do humans unconditionally shove something into their mouths whenever they are hungry?
“What are you talking about? There are even people who habitually shove stuff in even when they’re not hungry. Anyway, eat all of that first.”
Fran watched Mu, who was trudging off dejectedly to eat fire, and then spoke in a roundabout way.
“Oscar.”
“Yeah, what?”
“About Mu. While we’ve been doing this research, hasn’t he gotten a little…… fat?”
“Hm? Spirits don’t have fat in the first place, so what are you talking about?”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“No, it’s just that he seems to have gotten a bit bigger.”
Only then did Oscar look at Mu.
……Had he gotten a little fat? No, it was not a difference so large that one could feel it like that.
“Hmm. It does seem like he’s gotten slightly bigger. In human terms, roughly about 2.2 to 4.5 pounds.”
“……How much is that supposed to be?”
“1 kg to 2 kg. Not enough to be noticeable.”
But he had definitely gotten bigger compared to when they first saw him.
‘Does that mean, in the process of absorbing and transferring attributes, a little residue remains behind each time?’
That residue might be increasing Mu’s body class itself.
Oscar stared intently at the research records.
Then he reached one conclusion.
“Ah, definitely.”
As time passed, the amount Mu could absorb at once was increasing.
At first, he had simply thought Mu was getting used to the act of eating itself, but after hearing Fran’s words, that might not be the case.
‘Did he just get fat, and so he’s able to eat more?’
A spirit shouldn’t even have a stomach, so it was fascinating.
If he wrote this up as a thesis and presented it, he might receive heated interest from the spirit studies world.
-I ate it.
Mu, whose entire body had turned red, approached.
When Oscar gave him a glance, Fran nodded.
“Lord of Wind.”
Fran’s entire body became wind and scattered.
Then Mu naturally approached and came into contact with his hand.
Hwareureureuk!
Fran’s entire body, transformed into wind, turned red.
“How is it? A flame man! Cool, right?”
“Strictly speaking, you’re not a flame man. You’re still wind, after all.”
If he had to explain it, he was probably closer to a wind man containing fire.
On top of that, he had absorbed flames and become hot.
“Try summoning wind in that state. Oh…… the state of your body is applied even to the wind you summon.”
Oscar, having firmly obtained the information he wanted, nodded.
“Good. Let’s end this line of research here.”
“……Huh? Seriously?”
-Is that true, human?
“Have you ever seen me lie?”
“But…… it’s only been about three days since we started the research?”
-Contractor, please close your mouth. What will you do if that human changes his mind?
He understood why those guys were feeling doubtful.
It was true that the research had ended faster than even he had expected.
Oscar smiled broadly.
“I told you. This line of research ends here.”
He looked at the tower standing tall below the cliff, then turned his gaze to Mu.
“You must be getting tired of the taste of torches by now, right?”
-……Human. Surely you are not telling me to eat every disaster in that tower, are you?
“Oh, you’re finally getting a little easier to talk to.”
-Reverse summon! Reverse summon! Contractor, reverse summon!
Oscar tucked the convulsing Mu under his arm and beckoned to Fran.
“Let’s go, to the tower.”
The dungeon’s clear condition, [Reach it].
He felt like he could vaguely understand it now.
When he first arrived at the top floor of the tower with Fran, a question had suddenly occurred to him.
‘Even if the first floor is empty because it’s a lobby, why is the tenth floor empty too?’
In contrast to floors 2 through 9, which were plastered with all kinds of attributes, that place was exceedingly peaceful.
The reason he had felt, from the first time he visited, that “it felt like they had to do something there” was because of that as well.
“Maybe the answer was there from the start.”
“I don’t get it, so explain. Why is the tenth floor empty, then?”
“……If what I’m thinking is right, I’ll explain it when we get there.”
Honestly, he still wasn’t sure.
‘If I were the one who made this dungeon, I’d definitely have set the clear condition that way.’
When he thought about it, Veronica’s dungeon and Killian’s dungeon had both been like that too.
-I am curious. How exactly are you able to pick out only the parts they need like that?
The Guide had asked him directly.
To that extent, he had provided decisive help in clearing their dungeons.
He had brushed it off as nothing much at the time, but now, he was slightly suspicious.
‘It may not be a simple coincidence.’
That was why he wanted to check even more.
Just how far the designer of this dungeon was “thinking similarly to him.”
“……scar, Oscar! I’m opening it?”
Oscar, coming back to his senses at Fran’s words, nodded.
“Open it.”
“Heave-ho!”
The thick iron door opened, and the two of them entered the second floor, the floor of storms.
Normally, they would have quickly gone up the stairs, but Oscar steadied his body’s center of gravity and shouted.
“Mu! Eat!”
-……I miss the spirit world particularly badly today.
Mu grumbled, but still opened his mouth wide.
Then the raging storm began to be sucked toward his mouth.
After quite some time passed, the guy, his two cheeks puffed out, looked at him in dissatisfaction.
“Good. Your stomach really has gotten bigger than at first. To think you can eat all the storm on the second floor in one bite.”
“It is strange. He’s a spirit, so there’s no way he has a stomach.”
-……It feels like my belly is going to burst.
“Just endure it a little, Mu.”
While Fran soothed Mu, Oscar looked around the now-clean second floor and opened his mouth.
“But I am curious.”
He naturally turned to Fran, who used Lord of Wind.
“Lord of Wind is already wind to begin with, so what happens if you overlay the storm attribute on top of that?”
“I know, right. Does the wind get stronger?”
Fran, laughing lightly, placed his hand on Mu’s head.
At that moment.
Kwaaaaaaaaa!
The entire space began to shake.
“Krgh…… Power is overflowing from my whole body.”
“That much?”
“Yeah, it almost feels like this is what it would be like if I became an enhancement-type knight?”
Fran swallowed and slightly furrowed his brow.
“It feels like it’ll be hard to control right away, but once I get used to it, I don’t think I’d particularly lose even if I fought knights.”
In fact, Fran lightly kicked off the floor and slammed his body wildly into the walls and ceiling of the second floor.
His speed truly could not even be compared to usual.
Sseuk, sseuk.
Oscar recorded the phenomenon in his research journal and opened his mouth.
“Get ready. As soon as his stomach empties, we’re going straight up to the next floor.”
“What about adapting?”
“You can do that on your own after we leave the dungeon.”
There were seven floors remaining.
It would probably take Mu around two days to digest this amount of attribute.
Oscar, mentally tapping away at a calculator, muttered.
“It’ll take roughly fifteen days to go up.”
And after about that much time actually passed, the three of them reached the tenth floor.

Chapter 390: Tower of Trials (4)
“...Open it?”
Fran asked in front of the iron door on the 10th floor.
Judging by how he kept swallowing nervously, he seemed extremely tense.
“Yeah.”
“You’re really opening it?”
“Open it.”
At the firm response, Fran, who had been about to weakly open the door, turned back around.
“You say that way too easily, you know? What if there’s some weird monster inside, or flames burst out or something—.”
“If you don’t open it right now, I’m flicking your forehead.”
“C-crgh, not that. Your hands hurt.”
Hating pain, Fran made a tearful face and carefully pushed the iron door open.
“...Huh?”
The moment he saw the completely empty interior, he blinked several times before stepping inside.
“What the heck, I got scared for nothing? How did you know this?”
“Just a feeling.”
Compared to the last time he came here, nothing about the 10th floor had changed.
As Fran looked around the place, he suddenly realized something.
“Wait, but this isn’t something to be happy about just because nothing changed.”
If they failed to fulfill the condition [Reach it], then all the suffering they had gone through until now would have been meaningless.
Fran asked with an anxious expression.
“So what are we supposed to do now?”
“Are you stupid? Why are you asking me that?”
Oscar sat down while leaning his back against a nearby wall.
“You already know the answer.”
“Can’t you just tell me clearly? You helped Becky and Killian like that.”
“I did. But not you.”
In the cases of those two, even he himself hadn’t been certain of the right answer.
At most, he had only given advice based on long experience, but this time was a little different.
Because somehow, what he was thinking felt like the correct answer itself.
“I could tell you the method I’m thinking of and help you clear this dungeon easily. But then nothing would remain for you afterward. Are you okay with that?”
“...No.”
Fran shook his head.
In the first place, the reason he had suffered in this place for several months wasn’t simply to escape.
It was to grow as a mage and find the direction he should move toward in the future.
He couldn’t destroy the tower he had painstakingly built up all this time just because he wanted temporary comfort right now.
“Good decision. And think carefully. If you two think it through together, it shouldn’t take too long.”
“That’s way too vague. Mu, what about you?”
-...I don’t know.
Letting out a faint sigh, Fran looked toward Oscar.
The guy had already closed his eyes while leaning against the wall.
‘He says I already know the answer?’
Looking around the surroundings, Fran asked,
“Mu, do you see anything edible on this floor by any chance?”
It was the safest approach possible.
Everything that existed from the 2nd through 9th floors had consisted of ‘attributes’ Mu could eat, after all.
Then perhaps even on the 10th floor, there might be some kind of attribute invisible to human eyes.
But Mu shook his head.
-There’s nothing. First of all, I don’t smell anything tasty.
“Think carefully. Ultraviolet rays or something... Ah! Or maybe we have to eat the dust on the floor?”
-You eat it, contractor.
After wandering around for a long while, Fran sank into thought.
‘Do I need to release the attributes we ate on the lower floors here? Like filling an empty warehouse?’
After thinking briefly, he shook his head.
‘No. That can’t be it. If it worked like that, the attributes you could bring to the 10th floor would be limited.’
The attributes consumed on the lower floors were all digested before they reached this point.
As Fran continued agonizing over it for a long time, he started biting his nails from anxiety.
Watching that, Mu apologized in a thoroughly intimidated voice.
-Contractor, I’m sorry.
“...Sorry? For what?”
-If the amount of attributes I could eat had been larger, or if I could maintain them longer, perhaps we could have cleared this tower easily.
Mu’s round, ball-like body drooped together with his eyes.
-Or perhaps if I had specialized in one field like the other spirits, I could have been more helpful. I’m sorry for having such an ambiguous ability.
“Mu....”
As though comforting Mu, who was blaming himself, Fran gently stroked him.
“It’s okay. I’ve never once thought you were ambiguous.”
-Really?
“Yeah. If we’re judging by that logic, then I’m the most ambiguous one of all. I can’t even clearly say whether I’m a mage or a spirit contractor.”
At that moment, he suddenly remembered why he had rejected even the two Spirit Kings and been drawn to this guy instead.
‘This guy resembles me.’
A vague and clumsy being who didn’t even properly know what he himself could do.
Maybe that was why he felt this guy wouldn’t arbitrarily paint him in another color.
Whenever he looked at him, it somehow felt like looking into a mirror, so his heart lingered on him once more, and his gaze followed him once more.
“Hm? Wouldn’t arbitrarily paint me in another color...?”
At that moment, a small spark flashed through his mind.
Because the thought he had just reached contained an unexplainable contradiction.
Fran stared blankly down at Mu.
‘But this guy did color me in other colors.’
On every floor, Mu consumed attributes, and with those attributes he colored Fran.
Then why had Fran never felt any rejection toward that part?
Feeling like he was just on the verge of grasping something, Fran opened his mouth.
“Mu, what kind of spirit are you right now?”
-I am a colorless spirit.
“But... you ate other attributes.”
Fire and wind. Ice and lightning.
He had even consumed darkness on the 9th floor right before arriving here.
That was why his body was still slightly black even now.
-And yet I am a colorless spirit. That has not changed.
“...Has not changed.”
Fran’s eyes widened slightly.
Eating fire didn’t make him a fire spirit, and eating light didn’t make him a light spirit.
No matter what he consumed, Mu was ultimately still a colorless spirit.
“Ah.”
As though he had realized something, Fran’s gaze swept across the entirety of the 10th floor.
A clean, empty space.
Until just moments ago, this place had felt empty, as though something needed to forcibly fill it.
But not anymore.
“...Maybe what this place represents is our true selves.”
Both Mu and himself.
Because their origins were ambiguous, they could contain countless changes.
Like chameleons, they could momentarily imitate many different appearances.
But that state would never last forever.
When time passed, what ultimately remained was only one’s original self.
-I see.
Mu, who seemed to have realized something as well, nodded along.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
-I may continue eating new attributes.
“And I may continue wrapping myself in those attributes over and over again.”
But Mu was Mu, and he himself was himself.
“Hm.”
Oscar, who had been leaning against the wall, slowly opened his eyes halfway.
“You realized it faster than I expected.”
“So this is right? ‘Reach it’ wasn’t about reaching some place, but recognizing your true self?”
“If my guess was correct, then yes.”
Of course, if he had been the one designing the dungeon, he wouldn’t have made it so roundabout.
But perhaps because the designer’s personality was twisted, they had intentionally tangled things up in a complicated way.
Wooooong!
At that moment, the entire 10th floor began vibrating.
[Reach Success]
[Theme Dungeon Cleared]
The now-familiar voice echoed out, and as always, the guide appeared.
Without even glancing at Fran, he snapped his fingers.
“Oh, it’s a door.”
“Congratulations sincerely on clearing the challenge. If the challenger exits through that door, you shall receive your reward.”
“...Oscar, is something dangerous happening right now by any chance?”
“No. It’s fine, so head out first.”
Fran glanced between the guide and Oscar, sensing the strange atmosphere between them, before nodding.
“Got it. Then I’ll see you at the tower.”
“Yeah.”
Once Fran and Mu stepped through the door, the guide let out a faint sigh.
“Personally, I quite enjoy solving difficult problems... but this one is far too difficult.”
“What exactly is so difficult?”
“Heheh, I am pondering what I ought to do with you.”
Beneath that gentle voice lay an undercurrent of coldness.
Oscar shrugged.
“And why is that?”
“Every person possesses some form of deficiency. I read those deficiencies, then present trials to overcome them or directions to move forward. However....”
The guide’s gaze stabbed toward him like a dagger.
“I cannot see anything of the sort in you whatsoever.”
“That’s because I live without lacking anything.”
“No, this is not that sort of concept. In all my life, I have only seen one person as completely devoid of deficiency as you.”
After pausing briefly, the guide’s voice lowered.
“The Great Emperor.”
“......”
His eyebrows twitched instinctively, causing the guide to grow uncertain once more.
“That fierce hostility you displayed at the words ‘Great Emperor.’ And conversely, that strange familiarity I sense from your soul. I do not know how I ought to interpret this.”
After pondering for a moment, the guide asked,
“Let me ask just one thing. Are you a demon?”
“No.”
“Hm, then do you perhaps support demons? I hear there’s some insane group called the Black Fingers in this era.”
“The person that insane group wants to kill the most is me.”
“Tch.”
The guide frowned unlike someone his age and roughly scratched his chin.
“Ah, this is confusing. Well, perhaps it doesn’t matter.”
Narrowing his eyes, he muttered,
“No matter what you are hiding, you will inevitably reveal it eventually.”
“I’m not a bad person.”
“We shall learn that soon enough. Remember well that I am continuing to watch you.”
‘Looks like I really got marked.’
Receiving that piercing stare, Oscar stepped through the newly created door.
“Oscar!”
Tesila, who had been waiting in front of the door, waved happily.
“This one took quite a while. I thought my neck would break from waiting.”
“It was the trickiest one yet.”
“But now you’ve rescued all your friends, right?”
“You could say that.”
Oscar gave her the answer she wanted to hear.
“There’s no need to waste time, so let’s head to my dungeon.”
“Really? Works for me! I even checked where your door was already.”
Having already completed two invasions, Tesila looked relaxed.
“Come to think of it, not just me, but Oscar, you could probably aim for Level 8 this time too.”
“I think it’s still a bit early for me.”
He hadn’t even fully absorbed the things he had learned recently yet.
More than anything, thanks to his inexhaustible mana, there wasn’t much reason to desperately cling to the realm known as Level 8.
Of course, if the opportunity presented itself, he had no intention of refusing it.
“Really? Personally, I’m looking forward to it a lot.”
“...Was it helpful? Watching other people’s dungeons.”
He himself had succeeded in three invasions, but even then, those had merely been the dungeons of troublesome Level 5~6 brats.
Meanwhile, Tesila had witnessed two dungeons above Level 7.
One of them even belonged to the new Yellow Tower Master, Tony Havertz.
“Helpful, huh....”
Tesila became slightly more serious and shrugged.
“There are some things I’ve started thinking about, but I still don’t know for sure. Honestly speaking, I feel like jumping into my dungeon right this second. My body’s itching for it. In that sense, Oscar, I hope you clear yours as quickly as possible.”
“I’ll try.”
“Now then, the place where your door was located is right here... Hm?”
After arriving in front of a certain door, Tesila blinked repeatedly.
After checking the nameplate, Oscar also turned his gaze.
“I think you found the wrong place. This is someone named Lennon’s door.”
“Huh? No, that can’t be... Wait? I’m sure this was the right place.”
“Um....”
At that moment, a man carefully approached them and spoke.
“Excuse me, but this is my door... would it be alright if I entered?”
“G-go ahead.”
As the two stepped aside slightly, the man presumed to be Lennon opened the door and entered.
Oscar asked in a disinterested voice,
“Are you certain this was the right place?”
“It was! The same thing happened when I guided you to your friends’ doors, but because of my class traits, I never mistake a place or path once I’ve memorized it.”
Well, it would make no sense for a top-class adventurer to fail at finding a route like this.
Which left only one possibility.
“...The original door disappeared, and a new one appeared.”
“What? Why all of a sudden?”
“How would I know? We’ll find out once we enter, won’t we?”
Since the guide seemed suspicious of him, the most likely possibility was that the dungeon originally prepared for him had been changed.
After wandering around for quite some time, the two finally found the door.
<Oscar Crucian, <3>, 00:00:00>
“Let’s go in.”
“...Ah, okay.”
“If you want, you don’t have to come in with me.”
“W-what are you talking about? Who said I was scared? Just hurry up and go in already. I’ll invade right after.”
At those words, Oscar nodded and opened the door.
The very instant he stepped inside—
“......”
A familiar village landscape entered his view.

Chapter 391: What Couldn’t Be Let Go (1)
A bright and quiet room lit by warm sunlight.
The Guide sat down on a soft sofa and stared at the man reflected in the crystal orb.
“Oscar Crucian…….”
He pressed hard against his already throbbing temples.
“Ah, this is difficult.”
Without exaggeration, among all the people he had met in his life, this was the hardest type of person to figure out.
‘He’s intelligent and capable.’
At barely his early twenties, he was already a genius who surpassed a level 7 mage.
And geniuses of that caliber usually fell into two categories.
‘An insufferable bastard drunk on his own greatness, or a lunatic obsessed with skill.’
Surprisingly, Oscar Crucian fit neither of those cases.
He was even considerate toward others.
‘In other words, he’s perfect.’
Yes, perfect.
That was the problem.
Because if someone was human, there had to be at least one rough edge somewhere.
But in all the time he had observed Oscar Crucian, no such flaw had existed whatsoever.
That was precisely why he found him suspicious.
‘After speaking with him, he doesn’t seem to be a demon race member…… but still.’
Just what was he?
After staring for a long while, the young brat inside the crystal orb began overlapping with someone else in his mind.
A person who had shared the same name and worn robes of the same color.
“……Looks like I’ve broken down too.”
The Guide let out a small laugh and shook his head.
Even that person who had briefly crossed his mind had been a complete menace at that age.
That was why it had always felt ridiculous whenever people praised him as some kind of hero.
In other words, even humanity’s universally revered hero had not been perfect at that age.
“But…… yes. If you really are the same type of person as him.”
There was something he wanted to see.
Something he wanted to confirm.
With practiced motions, the Guide manipulated the crystal orb and constructed a dungeon meant for only one person.
* * *
“…….”
Oscar slowly looked around.
It was a village he had visited before.
Quite a long time had passed since then, yet it was still a place that surfaced vividly in his memories.
“A rural village? It’s pretty.”
Tesila, who had barged in immediately, walked over beside him and spoke.
“But this is kind of interesting.”
“What is?”
“There are people.”
In the direction she pointed, villagers could be seen.
Of course, perhaps the two of them were invisible, because the villagers showed no reaction at all despite the appearance of outsiders.
“The two dungeons I barged into earlier didn’t have people in them. Did yours?”
“……No, now that I think about it, mine didn’t either.”
The purpose of this dungeon, to begin with, was to help challengers grow.
Perhaps because of that, many of the conditions had focused on self-discipline and cultivation……
‘And now there are suddenly people. Besides.’
Oscar frowned.
The very fact that the dungeon had chosen ‘this place’ as the testing ground displeased him.
‘No, it’s probably just coincidence.’
Even if the dungeon could read information about its target, it probably couldn’t read memories from the past.
Oscar forcefully shook away the negative thoughts and asked,
“So what do we do now? When do they tell us the conditions for clearing it?”
“Ah, right. This is your first time.”
Tesila nodded.
She had entered the previous two dungeons alongside challengers, but she herself had not been one.
After all, she had barged into a dungeon more than two months after those troublemaker brats had already entered it.
“First, you fail.”
“……We have to fail?”
“Yeah. Don’t tell me you thought you’d succeed the moment you entered? Even the Yellow Tower Master couldn’t do that.”
She let out a small laugh.
“And you entered a difficulty 3 dungeon, which is even harder than that, so who knows…… but I doubt the conditions will be easy. Maybe all difficulty 3 dungeons are like this.”
“You don’t have any related information either, Ms. Tesila?”
“Nope. You heard it too, right? There’s still someone who entered difficulty 3 and never came out.”
Sure enough, he had heard about that from the Guide when he first entered this place.
“That’s why everyone avoids difficulty 3. Most people coming here are probably at least level 6, but they don’t want to risk their lives for no reason.”
“I suppose that’s true…….”
The most common visitors were probably level 6 mages and knights who wanted to break through the wall of level 7 and become Masters.
After that would come late-stage level 7 Masters wanting to surpass the wall of level 8.
Fran was the strange one.
For a level 5 to come here, it would probably feel like wasting a one-time opportunity.
“Then let’s look around first.”
“Good call. So what are you planning to start with?”
“I think we should at least learn the surrounding terrain first.”
“Wow, do you want to join our adventurer party? I think you’d do great as an adventurer.”
“I’ll pass.”
Together with her, Oscar began exploring the village starting from the center.
Children kicking around a ball in the central square, old men wasting time over chess matches.
Women at the washing area and men returning with fresh prey from hunting could also be seen.
“For a mountain village, it’s fairly large.”
“There are a total of 47 houses and a population of 182.”
“Hm?”
Tesila’s eyes widened.
“I counted the houses too, but what’s your basis for 182 people?”
“……It just seems like about that many people live here.”
“Aw, come on.”
Leaving behind the laughing Tesila, Oscar headed toward the outskirts of the village.
“There’s nowhere blocked off.”
“Blocked off? Ahh, are you talking about transparent walls?”
“Yes. When I explored the previous dungeons, there were places I couldn’t go.”
There had been spaces where he could no longer proceed, as though obstructed by invisible walls.
Since the place was fundamentally created through illusion magic, it was probably a natural limitation.
“Yeah, the two dungeons I entered had those too. Come to think of it, this place doesn’t.”
Tesila said while looking around.
“Or maybe they do exist, but the transparent walls are set extremely far away.”
“…….”
Set far away.
Her words lingered in his ears.
“If that’s really the case, then why?”
“You mean the designer’s intentions?”
“Yes.”
“Hm~ probably because there’s a reason you need to leave the village. Or maybe they hid some sort of mechanism outside.”
A reason to leave the village.
Oscar narrowed his eyes.
‘No, there shouldn’t be any such thing.’
Even if there were, he had absolutely no intention of leaving this village.
He couldn’t repeat the same mistake.
After confirming that the sun had reached the mountain peaks, Oscar spoke.
“For now, let’s head back to the village.”
* * *
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
Night deepened.
The two sat on a bench in the village’s central square.
After drinking the provided rations and water, Tesila spoke first.
“Should we sleep and wake up early? It’s not like anything’s going to happen at night in a rural place like this.”
“……No.”
Oscar shook his head.
This village, from the path at the entrance all the way to the bench he sat on now.
Every part of it was vivid enough to appear in his dreams. Which was why he knew.
‘Whether it’ll happen tonight or several days later, I don’t know.’
A guest would come to this village.
And destroy everything here, killing everyone.
“…….”
Oscar waited for that existence within the darkness for a long time.
Tick, tick.
The moment the watch on his wrist pointed to 2:32 in the morning.
Tesila, who had been nodding off, suddenly snapped her eyes open.
“Oscar!”
“Yes, I see it.”
Still seated, Oscar stared at the existence floating in the night sky.
A gigantic figure exceeding three meters in height, with a massive pair of horns protruding from its head.
“……A demon.”
KUUUUNG!
With a thunderous boom, the demon landed on the ground and stared at the seated Oscar.
Judging from how it didn’t even glance at Tesila standing right beside him, it seemed she was invisible.
“A pure white robe? A mage of the White Tower.”
“…….”
“Your body’s frozen stiff. Can’t even think of standing up, hm?”
The demon grinned viciously and slowly spread both arms wide, causing flames to surge upward.
At that exact moment, the sight of the village overlapped within Oscar’s eyes.
The sight of every villager dead and the village reduced to blackened ruins.
The children who used to play ball with him, the couple who had treated him to meals.
The village chief who had clasped his hand while thanking him for his help, now dried into a brittle dead tree rolling across the ground.
“Why did you come?”
He had always wondered.
Why did these villagers have to be massacred?
Had it somehow been because of him?
Of course, he knew.
The scene he was witnessing now was nothing more than a fabricated illusion, and that the demon before him did not know the answer.
Still, he simply wanted to ask.
“Hm? What an amusing thing to say.”
The demon grinned.
“Since when did we need reasons to kill humans?”
“…….”
The human heart was weak and deceitful.
And it seemed he too could not escape that category.
Seeing how he felt a sliver of relief from words spoken by nothing more than an illusion.
“Though I should be the one asking. Why is a mage of the White Tower in a place like this……”
Before the sentence could even finish—
Snap!
Oscar flicked his finger.
KWAHHHHHHH!
At the same time, a violent typhoon swept forward.
“K-Kgh.”
As the wind and dust cloud cleared, the demon could be seen dripping blood from wounds covering its body.
Slowly lowering its crossed arms, killing intent overflowed from its eyes.
“How cowardly, just like an insect. Attacking while someone’s speaking.”
“I don’t have a hobby of talking with trash.”
Once more, Oscar flicked his finger.
“I won’t fall for it twice!”
Fwoooosh!
With a light wave of the demon’s hand, flames burst upward from all directions and blocked the wind.
“…….”
Oscar stared at it indifferently before clenching his fist.
KWAAAAAAAH!
The raging wind crushed the flames as though stomping insects, swallowed them whole, and then engulfed the demon.
“Kuhuhu, kahaha! Foolish idiot. As if I’d be harmed by flames I created myself!”
“…….”
Oscar’s expression did not change in the slightest.
To begin with, he had never intended to use the flames themselves.
KAGAGAGAGAK!
The whirlwind, now blazing red after swallowing the flames, sharpened like blades.
Those blades mercilessly scraped, slashed, and carved apart the demon trapped inside.
“KRAAAAAAGH!”
The demon writhed in agony and frantically spewed flames, but they were swept away by the wind and could not leak outside.
“…….”
Over ten minutes passed, and when the wind finally ceased, something collapsed onto the ground with a thud.
A corpse so mutilated it was difficult to look at directly.
Oscar gazed down at it with emotionless eyes and muttered,
“It’s not that I can’t think of standing up. There’s simply no need to.”
At best, it was only a baron-class demon.
Now, he had reached a level where he could butcher one without even leaving his seat.
“W-Wow…….”
Watching the scene, Tesila gave a sincere gasp of admiration.
“I heard you were strong, but I didn’t think it was to this extent?”
“The compatibility was favorable. And the opponent was stupid too.”
Using fire head-on against a mage of the White Tower.
Even mages of the Red Tower didn’t do something that foolish.
After checking the corpse, Tesila nodded.
“It’s definitely dead. This is my first time seeing someone clear a dungeon on the first attempt.”
“……It was an unpleasant dungeon.”
Oscar snorted quietly and muttered,
“So when does this end?”
“Who knows? Usually, once the clear condition is fulfilled, a voice immediately announces it.”
The two sat waiting on the bench for a long time.
Only after dawn broke did a message announcing the dungeon clear appear.
[Achievement Rate: 8%]
[Clear condition partially achieved. Conditional success.]
“…….”
An achievement rate of 8%?
Partial completion of the clear conditions?
As Oscar frowned, a new voice sounded before him.
[If you choose to leave the dungeon now, you will receive ‘Windless Zone’ as your dungeon reward.]
[Will you leave?]
The achievement rate was merely 20%, yet even that alone was enough to receive Windless Zone.
Even if he left the dungeon right now, there was nothing for him to lose.
After sorting through his tangled thoughts, Oscar spoke.
“What was the clear condition for this dungeon again?”
[Your clear condition is one.]
The guiding voice continued.
[Give up.]

Chapter 392: What Couldn’t Be Let Go (2)
Give up?
Give up what?
Before the question could even settle in his mind, a door materialized in front of the two of them.
[Would you like to exit?]
At the guide voice echoing through the space, Tesila spoke.
“This really is different from a difficulty 3 dungeon. Let’s head out.”
Even if they left now, they could still receive the original objective reward, the ‘Windless Zone.’
And naturally, they would also obtain access rights to the Tesila Adventure Party.
“…….”
Oscar stared at the door.
A door he could leave through with only a few steps.
Yet his feet would not move.
Unable to understand that behavior, Tesila tilted her head.
“Hm? You’re not leaving?”
“……Let’s try a little more.”
“Mm, sure. If the dungeon owner says so.”
Along with Tesila’s indifferent reply—
[Reattempt intention confirmed.]
[The door disappears.]
The door that had tempted him vanished without a trace.
Then, as though time itself were rewinding, the surrounding scenery began to reverse.
The sun that had been peeking over the horizon sank back behind the mountain ridge, and the moon rose.
The demon race member who had already become a corpse stood back up again before disappearing into the sky.
And at the end of that bizarre sight, what awaited the two of them was a peaceful village.
“It’s exactly the same as when we first entered.”
Tesila spoke while pointing somewhere with her chin.
“That old man was chopping firewood back then too.”
KWAJIK!
There, a muscular middle-aged man was splitting logs with an axe.
“I remember him too.”
“And if my memory’s right, those little brats too.”
She looked toward the children playing ball in the open lot.
“The ball should come flying this way soon.”
Just as she said, a child kicked the ball wrong, and it rolled toward the two of them.
Then the child standing closest came toddling over and picked up the ball.
“So we’re still invisible to them…… what exactly was lacking?”
At Tesila’s mutter, Oscar also sank into thought.
No matter how much he thought about it, he couldn’t understand.
‘Originally, everyone in this village dies at the hands of that demon.’
Every house and facility in the village burns down, and only the charred remains of the villagers are discovered afterward.
It was a vivid memory from his previous life.
But by killing the demon, he had prevented that catastrophe.
So naturally, he thought he had fulfilled the clear condition.
‘No, now that I think about it, that itself is strange.’
Only a handful of people know that every member of this village was murdered by demons.
Most of them were already dead, at that.
‘Then did they read my memories in order to construct this dungeon?’
But when?
How?
He had met the Guide countless times, yet never once felt them using such magic on him.
Even if an artifact had been used, he should at least have felt a sense of déjà vu.
‘So it’s neither magic nor an artifact?’
Then how did they know these villagers were killed by demons?
Closing his eyes, Oscar searched through his memories.
‘Information.’
He needed information.
The deaths of those he failed to protect in this village still remained in a corner of his memory, but to be honest, the details of the situation back then were blurry.
After wandering across countless battlefields, this place too had simply become one among many.
‘Remember.’
Fortunately or unfortunately, he had encountered memories related to this village relatively recently.
When he visited Vince, the Nightmare Baron had pulled a stunt that caused him to recall this place.
‘Please.’
Anything was fine, so long as it could help, even a little.
As he dug through his memories with a deeply furrowed brow, a brief conversation flashed through his mind.
—This is pretty vicious. Judging by the methods and traces, it was definitely those demon bastards.
Those were the words of Magiro, who had approached while shaking his head.
—Any survivors?
—……None.
After that conversation ended, Radan muttered.
—Oscar. It seems their target was us from the very beginning.
Paat!
Oscar’s eyes snapped open.
‘Right, that’s it. Their target was us.’
There had been a reason why he, who should have been on the battlefield, had instead been leading the White Tower elites through this region.
Baron-class demon Varkan.
The bastard who spread plague and raised corpses had suddenly vanished from the battlefield.
‘Given the nature of his abilities, the moment he enters human territory, it becomes the beginning of a disaster.’
Just imagining tens of thousands—hundreds of thousands—of undead soldiers rising from the heart of the place they needed to protect was horrifying.
The moment that became reality, humanity, already at a disadvantage, would collapse under attacks from both inside and outside.
In the midst of that, the Imperial Family discovered traces of demons in this region.
Without even having time to investigate properly, they urgently dispatched him here.
‘But in the end, Varkan wasn’t here.’
To lure him and the White Tower elites away from the battlefield, Varkan had deliberately hidden himself and instead sent his subordinate demons here.
He remembered how the frontlines had been pushed back significantly as a result.
“……8%.”
Now he finally understood why saving the village had only resulted in an 8% completion rate.
The battlefield.
At the exact time this village had burned, the frontlines had collapsed there, and more than two thousand soldiers had died.
“Ha. This is insane.”
As Oscar let out a hollow laugh, Tesila asked.
“Why? Did you figure something out?”
“Maybe.”
“……Maybe?”
“Yes. About the demon that attacked this village.”
Oscar slowly looked around.
“Now that I think about it, doesn’t it seem strange? That a baron-class demon came all the way here just to massacre a mountain village with a population of only 182.”
“Well, they’re the enemy faction, so it’s not impossible…… but yeah, it does seem like overkill.”
“But what if that investment was actually the most rational choice?”
“What do you mean?”
“This village… no matter how I think about it, I believe it’s that village connected to Demon Varkan.”
Tesila’s eyes narrowed.
“Varkan…… you mean Varkan of Pestilence? The viscount-class demon?”
“Yes. You really do know your history well.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“W-What!? I only learned about it while studying, okay? Back when the war was at its peak, I was only…….”
“Anyway. I remember reading in history class that when Varkan caused the frontlines to collapse, he used diversion tactics like this.”
At those words, Tesila pondered briefly before replying:
“I admit the situations are similar, but couldn’t it just be a coincidence?”
“When I saved all 182 villagers here, the completion rate was only 8%. If that completion rate simply represents the number of people saved…….”
“Then assuming 100%, that’s over two thousand people?”
“Exactly 2,275.”
Oscar continued while looking at her.
“And when the frontlines collapsed because of Varkan’s scheme, the number of soldiers who died exceeded two thousand.”
“……I see.”
Tesila slowly nodded with a serious expression.
“Then there’s a high chance this dungeon is recreating actual history. If so, then I understand what it meant by telling us to give up.”
“Yes. While this village was under attack, the frontlines were collapsing as well.”
“182 villagers and over 2,000 soldiers. It’s telling us to abandon one side.”
With a somewhat gloomy expression, Tesila looked at the villagers.
“I guess…… saving the side with more people is the right thing to do?”
The side with more people.
At those words, Oscar unconsciously took a deep breath.
He himself had once chosen the greater good between humanity and the White Tower, abandoning the smaller side.
He had boldly declared he would never regret that choice, yet in the end, he failed.
Because when facing death, there was no helping the lingering sense of regret.
‘Of course, even now, if someone asked me, I still couldn’t say I regret it.’
Because he had already decided that.
Instead, there was one thing he had resolved in this newly given life.
‘After I died, I wanted to live only for my own people…….’
But after actually living again, even that proved difficult.
It was simply his nature.
He could never ignore those asking for help.
That was why he resolved to become stronger.
‘Become stronger than anyone else, and live a life where I abandon nothing.’
If he had been vastly stronger than the Demon Emperor.
If he had possessed enough power to withstand the demon army alone.
Then he would never have been cornered by such pathetic threats.
That was why this dungeon held a meaning beyond being just another dungeon to him.
‘Has a person like me grown after death?’
Whether he was merely a dreamer with grand thoughts, or whether he truly possessed the strength worthy of that resolve.
This place was no different from a stage to prove it.
“I won’t abandon either side.”
Tesila’s eyes widened at Oscar’s words.
“Neither one?”
“Yes. Neither.”
“But…… how?”
“I’ll figure something out.”
With those words, he checked the watch on his wrist.
‘5:42 PM. There’s plenty of time.’
The demons would arrive at this village at 2:32 AM.
That meant there were still around nine hours left.
“Before dawn, we need to visit the battlefield and rescue as many soldiers as possible.”
“What? Is that even possible? Even if we figure out where it is…… ah! Wait, don’t tell me?”
“It is.”
Jjeojeok!
The space before them split apart as a subspace revealed itself.
The engraving of information still hadn’t finished yet.
“So I was right. You’re using spatial magic.”
“Yes. With this, getting to the battlefield won’t be a problem.”
“Then we’re going in?”
“Just a moment. There’s something we need to confirm first.”
Oscar moved the portal entrance in front of the children kicking the ball around.
Naturally, they still could not perceive him.
Even if he spoke to them, they ignored him, and he couldn’t touch the ball either.
“What are you doing?”
“I’m checking whether the villagers can use the subspace portal.”
If they could use the portal, then every problem would be solved.
There would be no need to defend the village at all.
He could simply place all the villagers inside the subspace and focus entirely on the battlefield.
“…….”
“Looks like it doesn’t work?”
Just as she said, unfortunately, the experiment failed.
Like ghosts, the children simply passed straight through the portal.
“That’s unfortunate. If this had worked, things would’ve been much easier. Let’s go.”
Following behind him into the subspace, Tesila voiced her impression.
“When you said subspace, I expected it to be quiet, but it’s busier than I thought.”
“It’s a mess right now because it recently underwent some semi-forced remodeling, but the functionality’s the same.”
“So you really can move all the way to the battlefield with this?”
“More than enough.”
When he pulled on the strings of space, a new exit opened not far away.
Naturally walking out through it, Oscar nodded.
“I think we arrived in the right place.”
“T-This really is the battlefield.”
Below the cliff where they stood, crude barracks and tents stretched endlessly across the plains.
At the scenery thick with the smells of blood and death, Tesila suddenly looked back.
“Even the air feels different…… just how far did we travel?”
“About 585 miles.”
“Mm, so roughly 942 kilometers?”
“……!”
Oscar flinched in shock.
“You know the mile system?”
“Hm? Of course. A lot of old dungeons and records are written using miles. Adventurers basically have to know it.”
“That’s a cool profession.”
“……I have no idea what part of that sounded cool to you, but seriously. Over 900 kilometers.”
She glanced at Oscar with the eyes of someone who had found desirable prey.
“The more I see, the more valuable a property you look like.”
“I’m not property. I’ve never even been put on the market.”
Cutting off the conversation, Oscar looked past the barracks toward the battlefield.
This place, far north of the mountain village in Sirin, was already dark with the sun fully set.
Thud. Thud.
Together with a massive, unpleasant rumbling that felt like the earth itself was trembling—
A black wave began writhing forward from beyond the plains.

Chapter 393: What Couldn’t Be Let Go (3)
Across the grassland swallowed by darkness, beings that could neither die nor live crawled forward in writhing masses.
At a glance, their numbers were around a thousand.
Meanwhile, the Imperial Army, spreading both flanks and tightening its formation, numbered close to eight thousand.
“1st Magic Corps!”
As the commander slowly raised his hand and shouted, the mages in the rear each began chanting their spells.
About ten seconds later, a thunderous order rang out.
“Fire!”
Fwoooosh! KWA-BOOOOM!
The spells fired by the mages of each Magic Tower traced arcs through the air before crashing down onto the grassland.
Over a hundred of the monsters that had been diligently crawling forward became cold corpses.
“Oh, so this is why they call mages the flowers of the battlefield.”
Tesila nodded in small admiration.
She had explored all kinds of dungeons and mysterious ruins, but she was completely ignorant when it came to war.
“But… there are still way too many left?”
“It looks fine. There’s a follow-up attack.”
Just as Oscar said, the commander continued speaking without a trace of impatience.
“2nd Magic Corps! Prepare concentrated fire! Fire!”
The monsters once again died like flies beneath the falling magic.
Even so, nearly seven hundred still remained, but the knights stepped forward while drawing their swords.
“Cut down every last one of them!”
“They’re creatures without any special abilities!”
The grassland was lined only with torches placed throughout the area.
The swords in the knights’ hands shone in brilliant colors as they mercilessly cut down the approaching monsters.
“What? This is nothing special.”
Watching the army suffer not a single casualty, Tesila muttered awkwardly.
Oscar checked the time before replying.
“The real battle probably hasn’t even started yet.”
“How does Oscar know that?”
“Varkan deliberately concealed himself from the battlefield. Then he carried out a diversionary tactic to make them believe he had infiltrated Imperial territory.”
“Ah~ I get it now. In other words, those things haven’t received Varkan’s demonic energy.”
“That’s right.”
This was something that applied to nearly all summoners.
Even the Black Tower necromancers of the past, once called the embodiment of terror, produced pitifully weak undead if they summoned them without infusing them with mana afterward.
“Then this state will probably continue for quite a while?”
“Yes. Most likely until dawn.”
The demon who massacred the village had appeared at 2:32 AM.
Unless Varkan was an idiot, he would only begin moving around a similar time.
“Until then, it’ll just be a one-sided slaughter by the Imperial Army.”
“Oh, all the monsters are dead.”
“They’ll just come again anyway.”
Before Oscar’s indifferent remark had even fully ended, darkness rippled across the dark grassland.
Once it entered the area illuminated by torchlight, its identity was finally revealed.
The same monsters as before.
Only now, their numbers had risen to around fifteen hundred.
“…I’m not exactly an expert on war, but this doesn’t seem like a good situation.”
“No. This is a textbook exhaustion tactic.”
Oscar quickly scanned the Imperial Army formation.
Excluding ordinary soldiers, there was one knight corps led by a Level 7 knight.
And around twenty intermediate mages drafted from the various Magic Towers.
Against such worthless monsters, it was a force that was more than sufficient—almost wasteful, even.
‘But if Varkan seriously intervenes in this battlefield, they wouldn’t last even an hour.’
At that moment, irritated voices rose from nearby.
“Tch, they just keep coming endlessly.”
“Every single day. Don’t they ever get tired of this?”
“It seems they’re really determined to break through here today.”
“Those pathetic corpses lose most of their power once the sun rises! Hold out until dawn, and starting tomorrow, the White Tower’s elite mages will guard the battlefield!”
Fortunately, thanks to the commander’s encouragement, the soldiers’ morale was not entirely terrible.
They were exhausted, but since their lives were not immediately in danger, they were somehow enduring.
‘But only up to this point.’
Oscar glanced subtly at his watch.
2:07 AM.
If his prediction was correct, Varkan should soon begin moving.
“Oscar. Won’t demons appear in the village soon too?”
“Yes. But we need to know the exact time Varkan starts acting.”
That way, even if they failed this time, they could plan the route of action for the next attempt.
“Hah, here they come again.”
“Persistent bastards.”
“You’d think they’d realize by now that they can’t break through with things like this…”
“At least this time there are fewer of them.”
The moment the knights and mages looked irritably toward the five hundred or so approaching monsters—
The speed of the creatures crawling toward them suddenly increased drastically.
At the same time, a pungent smell began spreading across the battlefield.
“T-this smell…”
“Don’t tell me… Varkan?”
“Everyone, cover your nose and mouth with the supplied equipment!”
The morale of the soldiers rapidly collapsed as they realized Varkan had returned.
After surveying the atmosphere at a glance, Oscar muttered.
“This is bad.”
“Is it? There are only five hundred of them. The Imperial Army outnumbers them sixteen to one.”
“At times like this, you must examine the trees, not the forest.”
Wasn’t it usually the other way around?
Tilting her head in confusion as she observed the soldiers, Tesila suddenly exclaimed.
“Ah! I get it.”
Squirm. Squirm.
The monsters strengthened by Varkan’s demonic energy appeared completely devoid of fear.
Even when they fell into trenches dug everywhere by their comrades and had their bodies pierced by spears and blades, they ignored it all and continued crawling fiercely toward the humans.
Not only their momentum, but their grotesque appearance itself inspired terror.
Moreover, Varkan’s demonic energy already blanketed the battlefield.
Because of that, the soldiers’ faces had turned pale white, and the weapons in their hands trembled continuously.
“Do not retreat!”
“You must hold this area until orders are given!”
“We overwhelmingly outnumber them! This is not an unfavorable battle!”
“Show those monsters what we can do!”
The commanders and knights shouted repeatedly, but morale, once shattered, refused to recover.
In a way, it was only natural.
This front line had, until recently, been occupied by the White Tower’s elite forces.
‘Back then, including me and Radan… even Magiro. There were three Level 8s here.’
And beneath them were numerous Level 7 and Level 6 mages.
Yet all of that power had vanished overnight in pursuit of Varkan, so anxiety was inevitable.
Then Varkan himself appeared, so panic was only natural.
“What are you going to do now?”
“We fight. I’m just trying to determine where we should help first.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
In battles involving thousands against thousands, one must observe the flow of the war.
No matter how strong someone was, fighting randomly often provided surprisingly little help.
‘War is ultimately a continuous chain of momentum.’
A tug-of-war called “flow” unfolded nonstop across the battlefield.
To seize victory, one had to grasp the largest current among them.
“There.”
Just before the two forces collided.
Oscar pointed to one side.
“The left wing is probably the most dangerous.”
“Hm? How can you tell?”
“The spacing between the soldiers there has become the loosest. That means some of them are stepping backward in fear.”
At that moment, commanders throughout the battlefield shouted.
“Shield-bearers!”
“Hold the line!”
Thud! Thud!
Massive rectangular shields large enough to cover an entire body slammed into the ground one after another, while soldiers braced them with their bodies.
Behind them, the other soldiers prepared to thrust their spears forward the moment the monsters were stopped by the shields.
“Brace for impact!”
The monsters charging across the grassland slammed themselves into the shields with such mindless force that the word “brutish” suited them perfectly.
The battle line swayed violently once, but the soldiers behind quickly stabilized the shield-bearers and restored formation.
“Staaab!”
The moment the commander screamed at the top of his lungs, spears shot forward and skewered the monsters.
“Oh….”
Tesila admired the army moving as though it were a single living body.
‘At this rate, maybe they really can hold them back without much trouble?’
The instant that thought crossed her mind—
The monsters, which should have been dead, slowly began rising once more.
Protected by Varkan’s demonic energy, they were beings incapable of dying even if they wished to.
“Going in.”
The moment Oscar kicked off the ground and shot into the sky—
The very thing he had feared occurred on the left wing.
“I-I don’t want to die!”
A soldier who had fallen into panic threw away his shield and began fleeing.
“Do not retreat!”
“Hold them back! If we collapse, your comrades die!”
“Who ordered you to abandon your position?! Get back here immediately!”
Only two soldiers had broken formation.
But the collapse of a great dam always begins from the smallest crack.
“Ghk!”
“They’re breaking through! We need support!”
“The other fronts aren’t any better! Hold no matter what!”
In an instant, the line collapsed and monsters flooded through.
At the exact moment the panic-stricken soldiers froze like statues—
『Sky Fall』
As though the night sky itself were collapsing—
The winds above compressed into a solid sphere before plummeting onto the battlefield.
The moment it struck its target area—
KWAAAAAAAAA!
A gigantic shockwave exploded outward.
“……”
Oscar, having joined the battlefield just in time, rapidly surveyed the surroundings.
The monsters directly struck by the shockwave had their very existence erased.
Even those farther away were blown back dozens of meters.
‘Honestly, it would be easier to use this properly if there weren’t people here.’
Because soldiers and monsters were tangled together everywhere, it was difficult to cleanly wipe them out.
“W-what was that?”
“Wind magic? Support from the White Tower?”
Unable to see Oscar himself, the soldiers stared skyward with bewildered expressions.
‘They still can’t perceive my existence even in this state?’
A clicking sound escaped his tongue without him realizing it.
Apparently, directly commanding the soldiers was impossible.
‘Unable to interfere with the chain of command… how am I supposed to turn this battlefield around through personal strength alone…?’
To accomplish something like that would require at least Level 8.
Oscar bit down hard on his lip.
The words “Give up,” which he had forcefully shaken away earlier, flickered before his eyes again.
‘For now, I’ll do what I can.’
Oscar checked the time.
-AM 02:29
There were still roughly three minutes before demons would appear in the village.
Until then, he needed to reduce the number of monsters as much as possible, then use the portal to move to the village and—
The very instant his thoughts reached that point—
KUUUUNG!
Something fell directly before his eyes.
“……!”
It was the corpse of a knight whose chest and everything above it had been cleanly erased.
Recognizing the identity of the body from the armor it wore, Oscar slowly raised his head.
‘The knight… the commander already? Sir Southern, a Level 7, died this quickly?’
Since they had once defended the front lines together, Oscar knew well how skilled the man was.
A Level 7 upper-rank knight.
A traditional knight with no weaknesses even compared to master-class warriors.
‘Who in the world…?’
The instant that question flashed through his mind—
“Kuh—kgh!”
“Grrrk!”
Knights, mages, soldiers—every human nearby suddenly clutched their throats and collapsed.
Though all of them wore the supplied masks, they had been infected by Varkan’s plague and died.
“……”
Oscar’s eyes trembled faintly as he unconsciously turned his head.
The blood-red mist of demonic energy covering the battlefield split apart, and from within it, a figure emerged.
A demon resembling a human, yet possessing massive and majestic horns atop its head.
With every step he took, the grassland within that area rotted away.
“Hm. So there are still some breathing creatures left.”
AM 02:31.
With Varkan’s intervention, the battle ended.

Chapter 394: What He Couldn’t Let Go (4)
In the past, under the Great Emperor, there had only been four counts.
Naturally, the highest title a demon weaker than them could receive was viscount.
As a result, even among viscounts, the disparity in strength was enormous.
‘Varkan of Pestilence……. This bastard didn’t measure up to the counts, but among viscounts, he was easily within the top three.’
He glared at the being that stood nearly two heads taller than himself.
Despite having caused a horrific massacre, his face was filled with lethargy, as though this were nothing more than another dull day.
As far as he remembered, this bastard had been at the late stages of Level 7 back then.
If he gained a single moment of enlightenment, it wouldn’t have been strange for him to become Level 8 on the spot.
‘Can I fight him with my current strength?’
The answer was NO.
Even being generous, the odds would probably be around 3 to 7.
Part of it was a matter of compatibility as well.
Though his own mana was close to infinite, this bastard’s demonic energy was on a comparable level.
“Ah, is that so? So there was still one of the white ones left.”
Varkan, who had been staring this way, slowly nodded.
The plague fog he spread could not reach him, whose entire body was wrapped in wind.
“But if ‘that guy’ isn’t here…… nothing changes.”
The moment Varkan muttered indifferently and tried to raise his hand—
Oscar suddenly let out a deep breath and withdrew his mana.
Naturally, the wind swirling around his body vanished, and the plague fog lurking across the battlefield began pouring into every opening of his body.
“……Suicide, huh.”
Varkan did not so much as blink.
Humans were weak creatures.
When faced with something overwhelmingly stronger than themselves, some colossal terror, they usually lost their reason.
He had seen countless humans kill themselves after facing him, so this scene felt nothing new.
‘But, what is this?’
Usually, the reactions of humans who chose suicide fell into two categories.
Either they were terrified out of their minds at the thought of dying soon.
Or they felt relieved that they would finally be at peace.
“…….”
The human before him fit neither category.
The flames within his eyes blazed fiercely, like a lit fuse.
No matter how one looked at them, those eyes did not suit the word “despair.”
Varkan knew.
He knew exactly how troublesome bastards with eyes like that could be.
‘Those eyes are similar to his…….’
Which was why he couldn’t understand it.
Why did someone who had chosen death himself have eyes like those?
“……3.2 seconds.”
Oscar’s lips moved faintly.
That was how long it took for Varkan’s plague to completely stain his body when he wasn’t wrapped in mana.
“Current time, AM 02:33.”
After checking the time one last time, Oscar stared directly at Varkan.
Cough!
Spitting out blackened dead blood, he smiled even as he collapsed.
[Completion Rate 0%]
[Conquest Failed]
[Returning to Starting Point.]
“…….”
Varkan stared at the human corpse for quite some time, his face deeply furrowed.
* * *
The Guide looked at the crystal orb.
“Oscar Crucian…….”
He had held rather high expectations for this young mage.
Among every mage he had ever seen, there had never been one with such skill at that age.
At first, he had suspected him of being a pawn of the demons, but repeated examinations had erased that possibility.
‘Which is precisely why I must teach him.’
Teach him how to let go when it was time to let go.
The Guide’s gaze deepened.
“……Talented people sometimes make enormous mistakes.”
They fall into the illusion that they can accomplish anything.
They drown themselves in the fantasy that they can save everyone in danger.
But the world was not so lenient.
“A perfectly one-sided exchange does not exist. If you gain something, you must lose something else.”
The Guide had only realized that truth after paying a terrible price.
Which was why he wanted to teach this young mage all the more.
So that one day, when standing before a more important choice, he would not make the same mistake as now.
“…….”
The Guide had been watching Oscar from the very moment he entered the door.
Together with the intruder, he boldly searched the entire village.
He figured out that the villagers could not see them, and even grasped that the space itself was vast.
Even the baron-class demon that appeared at dawn had failed to become his opponent.
‘His judgment, decisiveness, and skill are all excellent.’
But that was the end of it.
He would never perfectly conquer this dungeon.
There was only one reason he was this certain.
Because this route was impossible from the very beginning.
‘Even if a Level 9 mage came, it would be the same.’
It was not a matter of strength or weakness, nor of sharp or dull judgment.
It was simply physically impossible.
‘That village is invaded by demons at 2:32 AM.’
At 2:31 AM, Varkan appears on a battlefield nearly 600 miles away from that village.
In other words, even if one woke up in the village and sprinted toward the battlefield at full speed to stop Varkan—
it would still be impossible to return to the village and stop the massacre.
‘Which is why it is a choice.’
Several thousand soldiers and several hundred villagers.
Oscar would have to choose between those two crossroads.
Which lives were more valuable.
Which place had to be abandoned.
“…….”
He knew.
There was no correct answer to this problem.
Which was why, even if he abandoned one side, he intended to give him the Windless Zone.
However, in order to obtain it, he needed to understand what he himself had abandoned.
Only then would he not repeat the same mistake.
-……Let’s try a little more.
But just as expected, he did not leave the dungeon.
Even that resembled ‘him.’
‘Though it’s a meaningless action.’
In the end, this problem could only be solved once he acknowledged it himself.
It would only end when he accepted that he was not an omnipotent being.
The Guide watched his actions with a sorrowful gaze.
“Mm?”
At that moment, the Guide’s eyes trembled slightly.
Leaping to his feet, he tightly grabbed the crystal orb with both hands.
“Spatial…… magic? A portal?”
His widened eyes were glued to the orb.
He could not tear his gaze away from the spatial magic Oscar Crucian had unfolded.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
Naturally.
Because it was once the power he himself had desperately longed for.
‘If only I had possessed spatial magic, or even magic that could manipulate time.’
Would the outcome of that day have changed?
Could he have protected everyone?
Even knowing it was a meaningless fantasy, it was an ability he had dreamed about dozens, hundreds of times.
And that mage possessed it.
“Perhaps…… no, even so, it won’t work.”
The Guide shook his head.
No matter how skilled he was with spatial magic, it was impossible.
The village invasion and Varkan’s appearance occurred almost simultaneously.
The moment he tried to resolve one side, the other would fail by design.
The Guide slowly sat back down.
‘It may actually become even more painful.’
Being able to use spatial magic meant he would fail by the narrowest of margins.
Success would flicker right before his eyes, yet remain just out of reach.
That bait called possibility and hope would drag the young man deeper into the swamp.
“…….”
The Guide bit his lip tightly as he focused on the crystal orb.
* * *
“Let’s save the village. And then let’s leave this place.”
Tesila spoke with utmost seriousness.
At that, Oscar slowly lifted his head.
The place they were currently sitting was a bench in the village.
Watching the children peacefully playing around, Oscar spoke.
“If we fail to save either the village or the battlefield, it counts as a failed conquest.”
“Right. So let’s just save the village and get out. The battlefield…… honestly, I don’t think it can be saved. Even if, by some miracle, you defeat Varkan and save the soldiers there, the villagers will die in exchange. It’s physically impossible to clear this.”
“I think it might be possible.”
Oscar said as he touched his own body.
“It didn’t particularly hurt when I died. I was a little annoyed that I couldn’t save the people, though. I feel like if we try a few more times, we might see a path.”
“The plague is strong. Saving people is one thing, but I wouldn’t even guarantee winning one-on-one.”
“…….”
“I understand that it bothers you. But these people…… you know, right? They aren’t real people.”
Tesila’s words had merit.
No, generally speaking, she was right.
This place was nothing more than something created by illusion magic, and there was no need to save everyone here.
Of course, it didn’t feel that way to him, whose mind was still branded by the deaths of these villagers.
“I know.”
“Then why…….”
“Have you ever lost someone precious?”
Oscar asked plainly while looking at the villagers.
“Of course I have. It’s nothing to brag about, but plenty. I’ve gone through most situations an adventurer can experience.”
“Then have you ever experienced leading precious people to their deaths because of your own mistakes?”
“Well, of course I…….”
The mouth that was about to answer shut tightly.
“I…… have lost far more than one or two people that way.”
Within Oscar’s eyes and expression was a sorrow and detachment utterly unsuited for someone his age.
The moment she saw it, she no longer knew what to say.
How could someone younger than herself carry emotions like those?
As Tesila swallowed hard, words one of her subordinates had once said flashed through her mind.
-Oscar Crucian, you don’t know? They say a massive fire broke out in his family, and everyone in the household died. Apparently he was the only survivor.
Well, if not for that, there was no way he could have experienced losing someone precious.
It became difficult to say anything.
Even she had never experienced losing her family and all those she relied on overnight.
‘But why does he think it was his fault?’
She desperately wanted to ask, but the words would not come out.
She had at least that much tact.
Still, Oscar seemed utterly convinced that the great fire had happened because of him.
“What matters to me isn’t whether these people are real or fake.”
“……Whether you’ve grown from the past. That’s what matters, right?”
“Yes. Ever since that day, I made a vow. That never again would precious people die because of my wrong choices.”
Tesila felt like she understood what he meant.
Although the illusions he met in this dungeon could not possibly be his precious people, he wanted some kind of proof.
‘Have I grown from that young age? Or am I still trapped in those days?’
She gave a powerless smile.
Because she realized this was not a choice she had any place interfering with.
Paang!
“……?”
Instead, she smacked Oscar on the back with her palm.
“If that’s what this was about, you should’ve said so earlier. Psychological matters are important at our level from the start, aren’t they?”
A psychologically incomplete being could never rise to the higher levels.
And for Oscar, who would inevitably aim for Level 8 in the future, this was more important than anything.
“Fine. Until Young Master Oscar feels satisfied, or until you obtain what you want, I’ll stay here with you. Well, even if I didn’t want to, we’d probably have no choice but to stay together anyway?”
“……Thank you.”
She understands this.
As Oscar nodded, Tesila asked:
“But I really meant it when I said there doesn’t seem to be any way. I understand that you want to save both sides, but I seriously can’t think of any method.”
“As for that, there’s one method I’d like to experiment with.”
Tesila’s eyes widened after hearing Oscar’s plan.
“Huh?”
If it went well… this might actually work?
* * *
AM 2:31.
‘The fog should be starting to spread across the battlefield about now.’
Sitting on the bench, Oscar checked the time.
‘In this dungeon, the villagers and soldiers— in other words, people who could potentially become friendly toward us— cannot perceive our existence at all.’
Most likely, it was a setting put in place to prevent them from persuading people somehow and clearing the dungeon that way.
However, even that had a definite loophole.
Tick!
As the second hand pointed at twelve, the minute hand advanced.
AM 2:32.
Kuuuuung!
“Pure white robes? A mage of the White Tower, I see.”
The moment the demon landed on the ground with a thunderous roar and opened his mouth—
Chwaaaaaak!
Space tore apart instantly and swallowed the demon whole.
“Demons.”
They could “perceive” their existence and could even fight them normally.
That was information learned through one half-success and one failure.
In that case, it should also be possible for them to swallow the demons using spatial magic.
“Let’s go.”
The spatial magic he had spent the entire afternoon improving, 『Heavenly Net of Earthly Snares』.
After trapping the demon inside a triple-layered subspace, the two instantly moved to the battlefield.
And the coordinates set as their destination were naturally—
“……Hm?”
Directly above the head of Pestilence, Varkan.
