Chapter 395: What Couldn’t Be Let Go (5)
The refreshing air of the mountain village vanished, and the battlefield’s unique scent of death filled the air.
Oscar, who had barged into the sky above the battlefield after crossing a distance of hundreds of kilometers, found his target at once.
“……!”
Varkan, frowning at the mana that had appeared out of nowhere, raised his head.
Then he reached out toward him without the slightest hesitation.
Immediately after, the dark-red demonic energy that poured forth split the night sky like a single laser.
『Tempest Wall』
Kakakakakak!
The wall erected by the soldiers of wind forcibly twisted the laser’s trajectory.
Oscar fell straight toward Varkan and pulled on the strings of space.
At the same time, a spatial rift connected to subspace struck Varkan.
‘Got him.’
As long as he could lock him inside the prison called subspace, everything would be over.
Because the condition of this dungeon was not to kill the demons and Varkan, but to save the people.
But the moment the subspace swallowed Varkan’s upper body.
Srrrrrk.
The guy’s form scattered like mist.
“……You use bizarre magic.”
That mist scattered in every direction, then soon gathered again from behind.
With an indifferent expression, Varkan fired the mist of plague toward Oscar.
『Gust Hand』
Two enormous palms made of wind clapped together and seized the mist.
But the mist slipped out between the palms and fingers as though it had taken no damage at all.
-Die.
Together with Varkan’s sentence, the mist of plague that caused instant death at the slightest touch arrived right before his nose.
But that was as far as it got.
The mist could not come any closer than that.
Whoooooong!
Because the wind Oscar had wrapped around himself did not permit it.
-……Were you one of the white ones?
A light tongue-clicking sound was heard.
Because he knew better than anyone that his power was halved against them.
Hwaaaaak!
Then Varkan, having directly turned into mist, rushed toward Oscar.
‘I can’t block this.’
He could not block Varkan directly turning into mist and piercing through.
Oscar, having already finished the calculation in his head, drew three swords.
“Wind Blade.”
Those swords rushed toward Varkan, who was approaching in the form of smoke.
But Varkan swiftly evaded through the gaps between them and closed the distance.
Then he instantly took human form and slammed his head into the ground.
“Krgh!”
The moment Oscar was grabbed, he used Blink and moved to a place not far away.
But Varkan had no intention of letting go of prey he had caught once.
“Meaningless.”
Once again, the guy’s form changed like mist.
And then he began flying in far faster than before.
Since he had already succeeded in approaching once, it was a straightforward movement with nothing to hesitate over.
‘Done.’
And the moment he confirmed that, Oscar inwardly shouted in triumph.
Because he had stayed still even with his head being slammed into the filthy ground solely for this moment.
『Storm Cage』
Kwaaaaaaa!
The fiercely blowing wind blocked Varkan from front, back, left, right, and every direction.
“You think you can stop me with mere wind……?”
Varkan trailed off in confusion.
Because he, who had wrapped himself in an enormous amount of demonic energy, could not break through the curtain of wind.
Oscar looked at him and smiled faintly.
“Have you perhaps heard of Ithaca?”
Wind containing holy power.
That was the true identity of the wind currently imprisoning Varkan.
Holiness was an energy that possessed the property of suppressing demonic energy by the very fact of its existence.
“Now, with this…… it’s over.”
Crrrrack!
The subspace that opened its mouth wide swallowed the immobilized Varkan in one bite.
‘Done.’
Only then did Oscar’s expression relax after he captured Varkan alive inside the double-layered subspace.
If he simply waited like this until morning came, he could end the attack without a single victim.
“Did it succeed?”
He nodded at Tesila’s question.
“Yes, for now.”
“……The more I see it, the less sense it makes.”
“Space magic tends to be like that.”
“No, not that. I mean you.”
Tesila muttered while stroking her chin.
“Your cognitive ability to judge the situation is extremely high, and you even possess the reasoning ability to find the answer after seeing something just once. Do you know what that means?”
“……I don’t.”
“It means you have the qualities of a special-grade adventurer! Like me!”
He knew she would say something like that again.
Just as Oscar, letting out a hollow laugh, was about to reply.
“……!”
Sensing something, he hurriedly looked around.
Prickle, prickle.
The strings of space that made up all things in the world were vibrating finely at regular intervals.
‘No way…….’
Was Varkan trying to break the subspace?
Oscar let out a faint sigh, opened the subspace again, and went inside.
“Why the sudden subspace?”
“It seems the tenant is very angry.”
Kuuung! Kung!
Once he entered inside, the vibration was felt even more clearly.
‘Can it hold?’
Even when he asked himself, no answer came.
Because experiencing this kind of situation itself was a first for him to begin with.
After briefly pondering, Oscar assumed the worst-case scenario.
‘If Varkan can really break through the double-layered subspace and come outside…….’
In the process, the subspace itself would definitely be damaged.
Perhaps the boundary would collapse and the demons trapped in the triple-layered subspace might pop out.
Even if not, the records currently being engraved here could be damaged.
‘So subspace isn’t an invincible space just because it’s subspace.’
Since it was a place where Lloyd and Kudel had even fought a duel, he had naturally thought it would be fine.
But seeing it shake this much, perhaps it was because of the property of the energy.
‘Is it because of demonic energy?’
Fundamentally, demonic energy was far more aggressive than mana.
To compare it to objects, if mana was a round stone, demonic energy was a sharp stone.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The reason the subspace was struggling now was probably because of that.
‘This actually worked out well.’
Oscar thought positively.
While training space magic, he had imagined trapping demons inside n-layered subspaces any number of times.
Because if it succeeded, he would be able to seal not only the Four Great Counts, but even the Great Emperor.
As a result, it seemed that method could not be used right now.
‘If I can’t properly trap even a viscount-class demon at the late 7th level…….’
Then naturally, trapping the Four Great Counts or the Great Emperor, who were far above that, would be impossible.
Moreover, meeting a demon on Varkan’s level was not an easy thing.
In reality, he would probably have to cross the Red Mountains to meet one.
‘Then it wouldn’t be bad to use this opportunity to experiment with what I was curious about.’
In any case, all he had to do was prevent him from killing people.
Having reached a conclusion, Oscar first entered the triple-layered subspace.
“……Human!”
The unnamed demon who had been endlessly walking there revealed hostility.
“Let me out of this place at once! Otherwise, I’ll chew you up, bones and all.”
Oscar gave no reply and simply tilted his head once, as if telling him to do as he pleased.
At this, an enormous amount of demonic energy erupted from the body of the demon whose eyes had flipped with rage.
“Hmm.”
Oscar looked carefully around the subspace.
A demon around the level of a baron was not weak.
Even so, demonic energy of that level did not put so much as a hairline crack in the space.
“Okay.”
Having finished the verification, Oscar pointed his index and middle fingers at the demon.
The moment the demon, somehow irritated by that posture, twitched his eyebrow.
“Wind Bullet.”
Along with a single gunshot, a bullet of wind pierced the demon’s forehead.
Normally, a wound of this level would have regenerated within a few seconds.
‘Why…… why?’
But there was no regeneration.
Because holiness was imbued within that bullet.
‘There’s no way a mere baron could block an energy even Varkan couldn’t block.’
With a satisfied expression, Oscar left the triple-layered subspace.
The demon’s corpse left behind there was soon swallowed by space, leaving not even a trace.
* * *
Oscar entered the double-layered subspace without delay.
“……You’re late.”
Varkan, who had been sitting gracefully on a chair made of demonic energy, half-opened his eyes.
The mist of plague spread throughout the entire space was absorbed into Varkan in an instant.
‘Still, I can’t breathe.’
The entire space was in a state where plague had spread.
The moment he breathed even the tiniest amount of air, he would die.
Entering with wind wrapped around his whole body had been an excellent choice.
“I won’t speak at length. Let me out of this place.”
At Varkan’s high-handed attitude, Oscar smiled faintly.
“What can you do if I don’t let you out?”
“How laughable. Didn’t you come here because you were desperate, afraid I would collapse this space?”
Oscar shut his mouth with an indifferent expression.
If this had been reality, he would have provoked him to shake his mentality, but that was only an illusion anyway.
“My mouth hurts. Come at me.”
“I like that it’s simple.”
Kwaaaaaaaa!
Mist fired from Varkan’s body rushed toward him.
But both he himself and the guy knew that such an attack did not work on a mage who controlled wind.
‘Then this is…….’
The changeup he liked to use.
There was a high chance it was a plague explosion.
Kwaaaaaang!
Sure enough, the mists that had approached close by exploded with an enormous roar.
“…….”
Varkan’s eyes narrowed.
He did not think the opponent inside the mist had died, but there should have been some bleeding at least.
He needed to see how to respond depending on the extent of it.
Hwaaaak!
Just then, the opponent burst out through the mist.
And he was perfectly fine, without even a single wound.
‘He knows that I can explode the mist?’
A tremendous amount of demonic energy rose from Varkan’s frowning body and pressed down on the entire space.
Puuuk!
“……!”
But that demonic energy was bait.
A shabby spear of demonic energy that sprang up from the floor pierced Oscar’s heart from behind.
“Only large attacks are not strong. An attack that can kill the enemy is strong.”
Varkan snorted and waved his hand.
The enormous demonic energy that rose with it erased the opponent’s upper body.
“……?”
It was then that he felt something was strange.
Because not a single drop of blood came from the erased upper body.
‘No.’
Come to think of it, even when his heart had been stabbed by the spear of demonic energy, not a single drop of blood had come out.
He opened his eyes wide as he watched the form scatter hazily.
‘Illusion magic?’
The moment he realized that fact.
Varkan unknowingly rose from his chair and looked around in every direction.
Using the mist caused by the plague explosion in reverse to set up an illusion.
The opponent who had fooled him completely was surely preparing some large attack.
‘I can’t…… feel mana.’
Though he had dismissed him because he was young, the opponent was a skilled person capable of completely erasing his presence.
Kwaaaaaaaaa!
Having no choice, Varkan fired demonic energy in every direction and immediately located the opponent.
“Is it that way!”
Demonic energy that rose like a tidal wave overflowed toward one direction.
But Oscar, who had been hiding in a corner, did not panic even while watching it.
“It’s already too late.”
The time he had bought through the ring that allowed him to use illusion magic was exactly 5.12 seconds.
No matter how much preliminary preparation was needed when using this magic, that much was enough.
Swaeeeeek!
From the floor where Varkan stood, the sharpest spear, Spatial Severance, surged up.
It would have been impossible to detect.
That was because this place was the subspace itself, made of space magic.
“Krgh!”
He hurriedly wrapped demonic energy around his entire body, but it was useless.
Because the energy of holy Ithaca had also been mixed into the Spatial Severance.
Slice!
Together with an extremely pleasant sound, Varkan’s form was cut in half.

Chapter 396: What Couldn’t Be Let Go (6)
The split body slid apart and fell.
Watching that, Tesila clenched both fists and cheered.
“We did it! We got him!”
“……No.”
Oscar shook his head and kept his guard up even while staring at the corpse sprawled limply across the ground.
Because he was certain Varkan wouldn’t die from something like this.
There was a reason he’d only generously estimated his odds of beating that bastard at thirty percent.
—A plague never disappears. It merely retreats for a while, then inevitably returns.
It was the phrase Varkan constantly repeated like a habit, words that were practically the philosophy behind his very existence.
And in truth, Varkan never died no matter how many times his body was slashed apart or burned by swords and magic.
Even in his previous life, he had only barely managed to erase him after carrying out the “Plague Eradication Operation” together with the Order.
“…….”
When would it be?
When would he stitch that body back together and rise again with that unconcerned expression on his face?
A scene he had witnessed countless times in his previous life flashed before his eyes.
The soldiers who died beneath that sickening smile.
Even the image of his own powerless self, unable to protect them, overlapped with it.
“I know you’re not dead. Get up.”
Oscar glared at the two halves of Varkan as he warned him.
But even after a long while passed, he did not rise.
[Completion Rate 100%]
[Clear Conditions Perfectly Achieved]
Instead, only a brief notification appeared.
“……What?”
As Oscar stared blankly at the message in disbelief, Tesila spoke.
“What do you mean ‘what’? We beat him.”
“T-This makes no sense.”
If Varkan could really be erased this easily, they wouldn’t have struggled so horribly against him in his previous life.
No, he never would’ve even been evaluated as a monster ranked directly beneath the Four Great Counts in the first place.
Nor would he have been capable of holding back an entire front line by himself.
‘Could my memories be wrong? No, impossible.’
He wore a confused yet unsettled expression for a moment.
Then Oscar let out a short sigh as he watched the corpse dissolve into tiny particles of light.
“Ah…….”
Right.
This place was ultimately still a dungeon.
No matter how real Varkan looked, he was nothing more than a replica created through illusion magic.
No matter how faithfully they tried to imitate him and recreate his strength, there was no way it could ever be identical to the original.
To think he had overlooked such an obvious fact.
Oscar pressed firmly against his throbbing temples.
‘……I must’ve gotten too immersed without realizing it.’
Part of it was because the dungeon called Utopia felt so realistic, but more than anything, the village and battlefield used as its setting were deeply tied to the memories of his previous life.
‘Still, I didn’t expect it to feel this empty.’
The moment he realized everything was over, all the tension drained away and strength left his entire body.
How should he put it?
It felt like he alone had taken everything seriously and made a fool of himself.
Oscar stared at the words “Completion Rate 100%” for a long while before speaking in a tired voice.
“Let’s leave the subspace for now.”
After emerging onto a battlefield now left perfectly clean without a single soldier remaining, he asked,
“So with a completion rate of 100%, the Windless Zone belongs to me now, right?”
“It already belonged to you at 8%.”
Tesila puffed out her cheeks slightly before honestly voicing her thoughts.
“If you ever need help from our adventuring party, just say the word. We’ll help you once.”
“Only once?”
“……You don’t look it, but you’re pretty greedy, huh? Do you even know our party’s standard commission fees are measured in hundreds of millions?”
“If not, then forget it.”
He had only tried asking on a whim anyway.
Even if they helped only once as she said, it would probably be enough to solve almost anything.
An adventuring party with a top-class adventurer among its ranks was stronger than most organizations.
“The real problem now is the dungeon I’ll be entering next. Difficulty 3 was far harder than I expected.”
“Hm, was it really that difficult?”
“……Ah, I almost got a little offended there.”
To begin with, this dungeon was impossible to clear with a 100% completion rate unless one could use spatial magic.
The designer likely knew that too, which was why they had made it possible to obtain the Windless Zone with only an 8% completion rate.
‘Then…… since I managed to reach 100%, maybe there’s some kind of additional reward.’
He fell into thought for a moment.
Then suddenly, when he no longer sensed Tesila’s presence, he turned around.
“If you’re looking for the woman named Tesila Windroar, I already sent her out.”
The Guide stood there.
Oscar shrugged and opened his mouth.
“I’ve felt this for a while now, but you’re pretty arbitrary.”
“Well, I did hear that rather often.”
A faintly nostalgic expression crossed the Guide’s face for an instant before he spoke.
“Would you walk with me for a bit?”
“……Sure.”
As they walked toward the encampment, the Guide asked,
“You’re quite skilled for your age.”
“I hear that pretty often myself.”
“Usually, even those blessed with talent lack real combat experience.”
“I’ll take that as a compliment. May I ask a question this time?”
“Go ahead.”
“Why did you give me a scenario like this?”
A dilemma where one had to choose which side to save.
Without spatial magic, it was physically impossible to clear.
And on top of that, Oscar had never once shown the ability to move through space in the dungeons he had previously entered.
Meaning the Guide had presented him with this challenge without knowing he could use spatial magic.
“First, let me formally apologize.”
The Guide answered candidly.
“I’m supposed to provide challengers with conditions that allow them to grow further, but in your case, I ended up giving you a path where failure was impossible. Without realizing it, I shook your convictions and forced my own views upon you.”
“Why?”
It was a pure question.
The Guide remained silent for a moment before abruptly stopping in place.
Then he looked around the desolate battlefield, so empty it even felt lonely.
“……In actual history, Varkan won tonight, and most of the soldiers on the battlefield died. It was such a disastrous defeat that only a mere two-digit number survived and managed to retreat.”
“I know. The White Tower’s forces had been withdrawn due to a request from the Imperial Family.”
“Exactly. And despite abandoning the battlefield like that…… they couldn’t even save the villagers.”
As if recalling something too unpleasant to look at, the Guide shut his eyes tightly.
“They failed to save either side. That’s what I wanted to teach you.”
Soon, the Guide slowly opened his eyes and looked directly at Oscar.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“That with half-baked confidence and good intentions, you can save no one.”
“……You thought that would help me?”
“More than help you, I believed it was an experience you absolutely needed. And I still haven’t changed my mind.”
“Why do you think that?”
“Because we are humans, not gods.”
The Guide’s expression darkened.
“When you gain one thing, you must surrender another. That is the law governing all things in this world. But the more talented someone is, and the kinder their heart is, the more they try to defy that law. On the surface, it looks admirable. Heroic. People will praise them as heroes and champions. But human eyes can only look forward. Someday, no matter when it may be, there will inevitably come a moment when you must turn your back on one side.”
This wasn’t a matter of good or evil.
It was a matter of whether it was structurally possible or impossible.
“I’ve seen far too many people collapse because they couldn’t endure that reality.”
That was precisely why he believed it was necessary.
The bitter experience of being forced to abandon one side.
The vaccination called failure.
Oscar slowly nodded.
“So you thought I would break just like them.”
“The fact that you saved both the village and the battlefield is certainly impressive. But someday…….”
“You’re quite fearful.”
“……What?”
“You think I wouldn’t know how difficult it is to carry this kind of resolve through to the end?”
“No, you don’t.”
The Guide shook his head.
“You merely think you understand right now.”
“And why do you get to define that?”
“Ah, of course I understand hearing this would upset you. Still, think about it rationally.”
“About what?”
“For example…… yes, imagine you were Oscar Sage, the one leading the White Tower. Right now, you stand at the edge of a cliff overlooking the Great Emperor’s Fortress. And you must make a decision. Will you save humanity, or will you save the White Tower? Which option would you choose?”
“I’d kill the Great Emperor and save the White Tower too.”
“There. See? Exactly this.”
The Guide let out a small laugh.
“This is why I say you understand nothing. You don’t comprehend the weight of that choice at all.”
“?”
Oscar stared directly at him before asking,
“Then do you understand that weight perfectly?”
“Of course.”
“How? Are you Oscar Sage or something?”
“That’s not the case, but…….”
“If you’re not, then what the hell makes you think you understand it perfectly?”
“Haha.”
The Guide wore a somewhat awkward expression at the words that struck like a dagger.
He seemed to ponder how he should explain it before eventually making up his mind about something.
“Well, I suppose it would be difficult for you to accept otherwise. It can’t be helped.”
Along with the sudden change in his tone, his appearance transformed instantly as he became wrapped in particles of light.
Pure white robes and pale golden hair cascading over them.
Lastly, a monocle covering calm yet sharp eyes.
“Ahem.”
The Guide cleared his throat before slowly speaking.
“Let me introduce myself again. My name is Magiro Wilson. The mage once known as the White Tower’s strategist.”
“…….”
“Uh, hm. You seem even more shocked than I expected. Well, I guess that’s natural if you think about it. I am your great senior, after all.”
“…….”
Like paints wildly mixing together on a palette, the thoughts inside his head tangled into chaos.
‘What is this? Am I hallucinating right now?’
Calm down first.
This could simply be magic imitating the appearance of someone whose face his memories wished to see.
Or maybe someone had coincidentally impersonated a senior mage and hit the mark by accident.
Ah, perhaps it was simply a trap laid by the demons.
“…….”
He knew.
On the night the Great Emperor died, Magiro died as well.
He had volunteered himself as bait to create an opening, and his heart was pierced through.
Even now, Oscar vividly remembered the smile Magiro forced himself to show him moments before dying.
He knew.
Inside his head, countless possibilities passed through his mind explaining why the being before him was not truly Magiro.
But right now, none of that mattered.
Fwoosh!
“U-Uhm.”
He could feel Magiro freeze awkwardly in place as Oscar hugged him tightly.
Magiro’s eyes rolled around uncertainly before he spoke in an uncomfortable tone.
“Um, junior? I’ll give you an autograph, so could you let go of me first? Sudden physical contact like this between us is a little much. I’d rather not say it myself, but I’m somewhat of a germaphobe too…….”
“……Magiro.”
The moment he had first opened his eyes in little Oscar’s body.
The instant the evolved scenery of Sirin filled his vision.
The very first thing that came to mind was his companions.
Because it hurt so much that he alone was monopolizing that beautiful sight.
And though it would never happen, if he ever got to meet those bastards again one more time, there was something he had desperately wanted to say.
“Right, right, it really is me, the White Tower’s superstar and sack full of knowledge, Magiro Wilson, so first let go of this—”
“I’m sorry.”
The words that escaped his lips—
Were the first tearful words he had spoken since awakening in little Oscar’s body.

Chapter 397: What Couldn’t Be Let Go (7)
Magiro Wilson.
A subordinate and companion who had been no different from the right hand of himself, the 17th White Tower Master.
At his core, the guy had always been cheerful.
But that didn’t mean he was frivolous.
When the time called for it, he could be more serious than anyone else.
“Y-you’re… sorry?”
The man blinked twice and tilted his head.
“I don’t think there’s really anything I need an apology from you for, Junior. Ah, unless you mean constantly talking back to your great senior whom you should revere like the heavens. If that’s the case, then with my heart as vast as the sea, I shall graciously forgive you, so don’t worry about it.”
“…….”
“So, uh, could you maybe let go of me now? I’m suffocating here.”
As soon as he released the tightly embraced Magiro and stepped back, the guy gasped for breath.
“Huff, huff. You look all skinny and lean, but what the hell are those muscles…… What are you, some kind of battle mage?”
“…….”
Sometimes, when silent nights dragged on endlessly, he had missed even this kind of grumbling nonsense.
Magiro, who had been staring fixedly at his face, looked slightly surprised.
“No way, you even cried? Look at your eyes, all red…… Am I actually that popular?”
Back then, he used to scold him for not being serious enough.
So why did this feel so unbearably welcome now?
Overcome with emotion for no reason at all, Oscar stepped forward to hug him once more, but Magiro raised a hand and backed away.
“Warning! Do not approach. I refuse any further fan service.”
“……That’s harsh. I’m just happy to see you.”
As Oscar showed disappointment, Magiro instead let out a faint sigh.
“Well, I do understand. There’s no distinction of age or gender before the charms of this Magiro-sama, former Casanova extraordinaire. But you should still show basic manners toward your senior in the Magic Tower.”
At those words, Oscar burst out laughing before he realized it.
“Kuh, Casanova my ass. You confessed to Mei seven times and got rejected every single time…….”
“……H-how does Junior know about that? Don’t tell me something like that got left behind in the records?”
Magiro’s face instantly turned bright red.
There had been many women who adored him, but unexpectedly, Magiro had been the pure and devoted type.
All his life, he had only looked at the childhood friend he grew up with back in his hometown.
“There aren’t any records like that. Unfortunately.”
“Whew, well, that’s a relief at least…….”
Magiro narrowed his eyes as he stared at him.
“How exactly do you know that, Junior? That’s classified information only a handful of people around me know.”
“Hm? No, Vice Tower Master Marlon went around telling literally everyone he met.”
“That senile old man’s finally lost his damn mind!”
Magiro had been fuming, but suddenly his expression froze stiff.
“But Junior, your sentences have been awfully short for a while now. And you keep saying things like ‘me’ and ‘Vice Tower Master Marlon, Vice Tower Master Marlon.’ Isn’t that a little strange for a junior who’s ridiculously younger than us?”
“…….”
Oscar silently looked at Magiro.
Truthfully, he was a little afraid.
Afraid that if he revealed his identity, he would be deeply resented.
Afraid that this harmless, cheerful man would harden his face and pour out harsh condemnation.
“…….”
But even so, he couldn’t run away.
That was not something he could do to Magiro—to the man who had been his most precious companion and subordinate.
Oscar slowly opened his mouth.
“You asked me if I was sure I wouldn’t regret it.”
“……?”
“And I promised I would never say those words.”
Magiro’s deeply furrowed expression looked as though he were trying to grasp the meaning behind this contextless conversation.
“I still don’t regret it. No… even if I did, I don’t think I’d have the right to say it. But…… I’ve thought countless times that maybe it would’ve been better if I had gone alone that night.”
“…….”
Magiro’s face rapidly stiffened.
As though he had understood exactly what Oscar was saying.
And then he warned him.
“Hey, I’ve tolerated enough of your little act.”
“I just…… if we ever met again, I really wanted to tell you I was sorry.”
“You’re dense as hell! Just shut up already!”
In an instant, hundreds of magic circles covered the sky.
Magiro’s unique magic, Over Craft.
Hundreds of spells forged with enough power to contend against an entire legion now aimed directly at him.
“…….”
If it were this guy, the moment he opened his mouth one more time, he would fire.
Knowing that, Oscar deliberately moved his lips anyway.
“I’m sorry.”
Ssaek!
Along with the sound of air tearing apart, hundreds of spells rained down.
Kwaaaaaaaaaang!
A deafening explosion echoed across the once silent battlefield.
“……It’s your fault. You probably aren’t dead, so take that as compensation and get lost.”
Magiro coldly stared down at the gigantic crater that had formed, then turned to leave.
And it was precisely at that moment.
“……?”
Thinking he must have seen something wrong, he hurriedly turned his head back.
And saw it.
“You’re still the same. I keep telling you, when you’re genuinely angry, you should harden your heart a little more.”
Oscar walked out while fanning the smoke before his face, perfectly fine despite having been hit by hundreds of lightweight spells.
Magiro’s gaze locked onto his hand.
“That’s…….”
“I figured this would make continuing the conversation easier.”
If Magiro had Over Craft, then he himself had Wind Archive.
The eyes of the man who understood that fact better than anyone trembled violently.
“Wait a second, what the hell is this? Is that…… the Tower Master’s magic restored? No, but even if it were restored, that’s not a magic anyone can simply use in the first place…….”
“You’re right. It’s a spell that fundamentally requires understanding the concept of dragon words that access the laws of the world themselves, as well as complete mastery over the essence of mana.”
From his mouth flowed, with absurd ease, the structure of Wind Archive—a secret that should never have been revealed.
Honestly, it wouldn’t matter even if he went around talking about it everywhere.
Even back when humanity was constantly being pushed back by the demon race and mages freely shared knowledge with one another, there had never been anyone besides himself who could use this magic.
“…….”
With his hands clasped behind his back, Magiro began thinking with an utterly serious expression.
That posture he always made whenever he was deeply contemplating something.
“No matter how much I think about it, I can’t understand. Logically, this makes no sense. But if it’s some kind of trickery, the existence of Wind Archive becomes a problem.”
“Some bastard tampered with my soul. I definitely died together with the Great Emperor.”
“……The Black Tower?”
“That was my first suspicion too. But it’s not them.”
“Goddammit, feels like my head’s about to split open. Just come up here first.”
As Oscar climbed out of the crater, Magiro held out his hand.
Oscar took it and carefully climbed up before speaking quietly.
“The reason I said I was sorry was…….”
“Forget it. I don’t have the right to hear words like that anyway.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
Magiro wore an indifferent expression.
“I’m not human.”
“……I figured. The real Magiro died that night right in front of me.”
Perhaps.
Maybe.
Even knowing it was impossible, Oscar had still hoped for a miracle, and now a bitter expression crossed his face.
“So you’re a thought-form after all?”
“Yeah. I’m a thought-form that perfectly inherited the memories and personality of the human named Magiro Wilson.”
By now, thought-forms simply felt familiar.
Wasn’t this a world where even the thought-form of the very first White Tower Master, dead for centuries, still remained intact?
Compared to that, a thought-form from someone who died only a few decades ago wasn’t strange at all.
“I still can’t completely believe your story…… but it’s not impossible.”
Magiro slowly nodded.
“The one who taught a girl named Veronica Over Craft, and the issue regarding how Radan handled the tattoo magic he overcame as well…… if you really are the Tower Master, then all of that makes sense.”
“You know too. There’s practically no one else capable of those things besides me.”
“……I admit it. But soul transplantation? Other than the Black Tower, there shouldn’t be anyone capable of handling that.”
“It was probably the demon race.”
“Your basis?”
“I still don’t know whether it was coincidence, an accident, or intentional. But the Great Emperor is inside my soul too.”
“…….”
Magiro frowned.
“You realize that kind of sounds like you’re asking me to kill you, right?”
“If that’s what you want, I’ll gladly fight you. But the Magiro I know would never choose that.”
“……Haa.”
As though exasperated, the man brushed back his hair and snapped his fingers.
The dirt ground rose and formed chairs, and he naturally took one of the seats.
“Sit down first. Feels like this is going to be a long conversation.”
Oscar nodded and sat down before opening his mouth.
“You want to hear my story after all, don’t you?”
“……Reincarnation? Possession? Goddammit. Whatever. Just tell me everything that happened after that.”
It became a long story.
Because they talked until the sun rose, and then until it set again.
Toward the end, his throat hurt every time he spoke, to the point he had to reinforce his vocal cords with mana itself.
“So, to summarize, you blamed yourself for the White Tower’s downfall and wandered all over trying to restore it?”
“That was my highest priority.”
“And realizing the Great Emperor was inside your soul happened relatively recently?”
“Only after I’d managed to place the White Tower back onto stable footing did I finally gain some freedom.”
“Hah.”
Magiro let out a hollow laugh.
He stared at the blue sky for a long while before murmuring.
“So you really completed the airship in the end. I’d like to see it at least once.”
“It’s not impossible. If we use my subspace, even thought-forms should be able to…….”
“No.”
The man shook his head firmly.
“I’m currently the engine and heart of this dungeon. If I leave my place, the dungeon will collapse quickly.”
“……Can’t you at least come see it for a little while and come back?”
“You must’ve forgotten because you’ve been here too long, but the entry conditions for this dungeon are one-time only and limited to those below Level 7.”
Meaning the moment Magiro was moved, this dungeon would disappear.
Oscar slowly closed his eyes and asked,
“When exactly did you make something like this?”
“During the war. After the Battle of Palm Gorge.”
Resting his chin on his hand, he grinned.
“After fighting like hell and crawling back to the Magic Tower, I lay down on my bed and suddenly realized something. Like, hold on, something’s seriously wrong here. Aren’t those demon bastards way too strong? Couldn’t the Empire actually lose? Stuff like that crossed my mind.”
From then on, Magiro began gathering knowledge from across the entire continent.
“The original hoped that if humanity ever lost, then this dungeon would become the next opportunity.”
The strategist of the White Tower.
Magiro Wilson, in order to become a pouch containing all the knowledge and wisdom in the world—
never let books leave his hands even for a moment.
Oscar, who had never known that fact even in his dreams, let out a hollow laugh.
“……I think I used to nag you, telling you to spend less time reading random things and more time rereading White Tower spellbooks.”
“My thoughts exactly. I did all that because you need broad knowledge to guide people toward growth suited to them. Seriously, you understood absolutely nothing.”
“I didn’t know. Because you never told me.”
With his lips jutting out sulkily, Magiro muttered,
“……The original intentionally never told anyone. Because he hoped this dungeon would never need to be used. He wanted everyone to survive and keep fooling around together at the Magic Tower.”
Oscar closed his eyes.
A dungeon made for some nameless future person, yet he had hoped no one would ever come.
“……What a ridiculous guy.”
“The original just wanted to do everything he possibly could.”
If they could end the war without dying, then that alone would be enough.
And even if they did die, perhaps he still wanted to pass on a spark called hope to the next generation of humanity.
After thinking for a long while, Oscar finally spoke.
“The White Tower has money now. So…….”
“You’re saying you’ll somehow handle teaching people outside, so I should come with you?”
“Yeah.”
“Then let me ask one thing. Can the current Violet Moon construct a dungeon of this scale using illusion magic?”
“…….”
The previous Violet Moon had been praised as the greatest talent in the Purple Magic Tower.
Compared to that, the current Violet Moon Oscar had met at the Night of Mages…… was still far, far lacking.
“Judging by your face, I guess they can’t. Still, that’s just like you, Tower Master. You really can’t lie.”
“…….”
His mood sank heavily.
Because he had realized that the friend he had miraculously reunited with after so long would soon have to leave him again.
“Tch, seriously, there’s really no way around this?”
“There isn’t.”
“What if I find another method?”
“Don’t.”
Magiro shook his head.
“I’m not the original. So even if you keep me by your side, I can’t replace him. Just let me do what I’m supposed to do.”
“…….”
He was right.
This man was no different from Magiro’s final will itself.
Forcing him to stay nearby would only be his own selfish desire.
“If that’s your choice…… then I understand.”
“I’m sorry. If the original had experienced more of the war and spent more time with you, Tower Master, maybe he would’ve made a different decision. But from the point in time when I was created, this decision is the right one.”
Smiling bitterly, Magiro asked,
“How did the original die?”
“……He created an opening against the Great Emperor, and then his heart burst. Even while dying, he smiled at me.”
“That’s a good death then.”
Magiro smiled warmly as he spoke.
“I take back what I said earlier. I’ll accept the Tower Master’s apology. So stop feeling guilty because of me—and because of us. I saw all the people who survived thanks to that decision flooding into this dungeon seeking knowledge. They are the future we protected. The original definitely wouldn’t regret it either. These are the feelings I myself hold right now, so you can believe them.”
“…….”
He knew these were the words of a thought-form, not the actual person.
But why was it that, only after hearing those words, he finally felt forgiven?
Oscar closed his eyes, lowered his head deeply, and cried for a long time.

Chapter 398: What Couldn't Be Let Go (8)
Magiro sipped bottled water and asked.
“So, you done crying? Or are you gonna cry one more time? Want me to wait a bit longer?”
“……Snff. Shut up.”
The embarrassment hit him belatedly when he realized a fully grown man had bawled his eyes out.
And not even in front of a stranger, but before someone who had once been both his comrade and subordinate.
Oscar’s ears turned red all the way to the tips as he awkwardly tried to justify himself.
“This is all because of the body. Ever since I entered a child’s body, I got influenced without realizing it.”
“Hm? No way. I’d like to think I’ve looked into quite a lot of material related to spirit monsters and possession. In fact, if you read the paper published by Jin Cernia, the former master of the Black Tower, 『A Study on Identity Preservation and Continuity of Self After Soul Transference』…….”
“Aaaah~ yap yap, you really talk too much! This has always been your problem!”
“……You entered a younger body, and now our Tower Master has straight-up become a brat.”
Letting out a snicker, Magiro leaned back against the chair.
“But still, it’s not bad.”
“What is now?”
“At least one of us survived.”
“……You mocking me?”
“No. I mean that sincerely.”
He spoke while reminiscing about the distant past.
“It would’ve been best if everyone had returned alive, but you know how unrealistic that is. I guess if only one person could come back alive, I wanted it to be you, Tower Master.”
“Why?”
“Hmm. Just…… because you seemed like the person who’d remember all of us the best?”
That insignificant little sentence flew like an arrow and pierced his chest.
And it was probably true.
Even now, he still vividly remembered those bastards’ faces and personalities, even their voices and the look in their eyes.
“And earlier, you apologized to me, but now I think it’s my turn.”
“What are you suddenly apologizing for?”
“……I was mistaken.”
Smiling weakly, Magiro stared at the campfire quietly crackling away for no reason.
“If you survived, Tower Master, I thought you’d regret making that choice.”
Between humanity and the White Tower, he chose humanity.
Because of that decision, he lost most of the people precious to him and eventually died himself.
And on top of that, the result was the decline and collapse of the house he loved.
“If it were me, I couldn’t have endured it. Every night, every moment, I would’ve regretted and blamed myself for that choice. And if I were ever given the chance to choose again, I definitely would’ve chosen the White Tower.”
But Oscar was different.
“Do you think it wasn’t painful for you because you were the Tower Master? Do you think you weren’t sad? You were the one who personally ruled the Magic Tower, so if anything, it must’ve hurt you even more than it hurt me.”
That was why even someone like Oscar, if he had survived, would surely have changed.
He thought he would never make the same choice again.
“……As expected of the man who ranks number one in my incorrect answer rate.”
Oscar didn’t simply remain there regretting the choices of the past.
As though even spending time on that was a waste, he chose to move toward a better direction no matter how difficult it was.
“You really are an amazing person, Tower Master.”
The strength to keep moving without collapsing.
The mentality to endlessly whip himself forward and continue improving.
That was a realm Magiro Wilson could never reach in the end.
“Ah, the mood’s getting too heavy. Let’s talk about something else?”
“……Then wanna hear about the kids?”
“Oh, hold on. Don’t tell me you mean those little brats I remember?”
“Listen first. It’s a long story.”
He told him about Sasha, Lloyd, and Gilliot.
Magiro’s expressions shifted constantly as he listened, before he slowly nodded.
“Hmm. More’s happened than I expected.”
“Yeah. Right now, the important thing is restoring Gilli’s memories.”
“Memories, huh…… I think I might be able to help with that part.”
“What? How?”
“You said Gilli’s still only level 7, didn’t you? Leave it to me.”
“But I don’t know if a kid whose mind still isn’t stable can clear a dungeon alone.”
“There you go again, being overprotective. I’ll design the dungeon myself. He might not completely regain his memories, but I should at least be able to crack those hardened memories a little.”
“…….”
Oscar hesitated briefly.
Normally, he would never allow it, but this was Magiro.
The same guy who had once been called a walking encyclopedia, knowledgeable in all kinds of fields.
“So if I trust you, you really want me to bring him?”
“That’s what I’m saying.”
Replying lightly, Magiro stood from his seat.
Seeing that, Oscar asked with a tense expression.
“Why are you getting up already? There’s still so much we haven’t talked about.”
“This is why unemployed people are no good. Unlike you, Tower Master, I’m still actively working, so I’m busy.”
“But just a little longer…….”
“Ah, no can do. Get up already, hurry.”
Magiro pressed him with a deliberately annoyed look.
Knowing exactly why he was acting like this, Oscar couldn’t bring himself to refuse.
“Look at you. You want to stay together too.”
“……You really are dense. That’s exactly why I’m trying to send you away quickly. I’m scared my resolve might waver.”
“I wouldn’t mind if it did.”
“Well I would, okay? Ah, hurry up already.”
When Oscar reluctantly stood, Magiro snapped his fingers.
A very familiar staff appeared in his hand.
“……Come to think of it, I should’ve realized the Dungeon Master was someone close to me the moment I saw that.”
“Ah, sorry about that, even if it’s late. You weren’t using it, so I quietly borrowed it. I figured the dungeon would attract more attention that way.”
“You dared lay hands on the Tower Master’s belongings. What an unbelievable bastard.”
Lightly chuckling, Oscar grasped the staff and spoke.
“But this was already the reward when the completion rate was only 8%, so since I cleared 100%, shouldn’t you add something extra?”
“Tch, sharper than I expected. I was actually wondering what to give you…… but I’ve decided. Hup!”
Suddenly throwing his head back, Magiro pretended to yank his own head off.
Then he held out something heavy as though handing it over to Oscar.
“Here, take it quickly. It’s heavy.”
“……What is this?”
“My head.”
Oscar stared at him flatly, and Magiro withdrew his hand before shaking his head as if disappointed.
“Ah, forget it. We really don’t match.”
Pulling out a book from his coat, Magiro spoke.
“You know one of the Four Great Counts, Lapiros, right? The guy you always made me mark.”
“You had the best compatibility against him.”
Lapiros, the One Who Sees Ahead.
Predicting and dodging the trajectory of every attack while approaching with movements so eerie they resembled a ghost.
That was why the only solution was to bombard him with an absurd amount of magic so overwhelming that even someone like Magiro, who could read trajectories, wouldn’t be able to do anything about it.
“After fighting that bastard so many times, I eventually realized something too. So for the twenty-something years it took before this dungeon activated, I devoted myself entirely to digging into that one thing. And this is the result.”
“……Magiro Time? What’s this?”
Oscar asked after reading the title written on the book.
“It’s a spell. A spell I created by reinterpreting Lapiros’s ability in my own way.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“Oh.”
His interest was piqued slightly.
Magiro had created quite a few interesting personal spells before, like 『Eye of the Firmament』.
In terms of theory alone, he was a mage equal to or even beyond Oscar himself.
“This is interesting. What does it do?”
“It hyper-accelerates thought.”
“……Hyper-accelerates thought?”
Oscar tilted his head.
He couldn’t quite understand at first glance.
“What’s the merit in that? Does it make mental arithmetic faster or something?”
“If that’s what you want, go enroll in an abacus academy or something. The moment this spell activates, the user’s thought speed increases explosively. To the point where it creates the illusion that the surrounding world has slowed down. In that state, you can calculate your opponent’s posture, breathing, gaze, mana flow, the surrounding terrain, variables—everything—and even predict their next action. If I can do it, then you probably can too, Tower Master.”
“……What?”
Oscar’s mouth fell open in shock.
Just from the explanation alone, the effect sounded completely absurd.
Enjoying his reaction, Magiro smiled with satisfaction as he continued.
“Ah, of course, there is one tiny little drawback.”
“Well, something like that can’t be helped. What is it?”
“The duration is a little short. At most, around one to two seconds.”
“……That’s way too short. Is mana capacity the issue by any chance?”
If that was the case, it didn’t matter.
He already possessed more mana now than he had even as a level 9 in his previous life.
“No. The problem is the brain.”
“The brain?”
“Yup. The human brain wasn’t originally designed with this level of processing power in mind. So it can’t withstand the amount of information flooding in all at once. That’s why it’s one to two seconds. No matter how much you force it, I don’t recommend maintaining it for more than three seconds. Any longer and your brain will burn out, turning you into an idiot like Radan.”
Gulp.
Oscar swallowed hard.
The effect was incredibly attractive, but it was a spell that came with equally massive risks.
“……I remember now. Right before Magiro died, he dodged every single attack from the Great Emperor while closing in.”
Because of that, an opening had appeared, allowing them to inflict a fatal wound.
Though Magiro himself had died immediately afterward.
‘So that was this spell’s power.’
If so, then even if only temporarily, it meant the spell could function against a level 9 opponent.
Oscar asked.
“Are you really okay with giving this to me?”
“I was planning to pass it down to someone worthy eventually anyway. If it’s you, Tower Master, there’s nothing to hesitate over.”
“…….”
It was only a single book, yet why did it feel so unbearably heavy?
Oscar slowly nodded.
“It’s not really revenge, but I’ll make sure to settle things properly. So don’t worry about what comes after.”
“I’m not worried. The demon bastards are the ones who should be.”
Magiro held out a fist.
“I wish you good fortune in battle, our Tower Master.”
“……Yeah.”
Neither of them said something like, “See you again.”
If that were possible, it would naturally happen on its own.
The moment Oscar bumped his fist against the one Magiro extended—
Srrrrrrk.
The background disappeared, and Oscar was transported outside the dungeon.
“…….”
Even now, the front of the dungeon was packed with people.
Before entering, he hadn’t thought much of it, but now they looked different to him.
‘They’re full of hope.’
People flushed with excitement at the hope that they could become stronger.
People emerging with rewards, smiling in satisfaction.
This was probably the kind of scene Magiro had wanted as well.
‘Too bad he can’t see it himself.’
Smiling bitterly, Oscar moved back to his room before the gloomy feelings could rise again.
The Mad Demon, who had been sitting in the corner as usual, sensed his presence and abruptly lifted his head.
“Long time no see. Been well?”
Before, the guy at least acted happy when Oscar came back to the room, but after not seeing him for a few months, he was completely on guard again.
Normally, Oscar would’ve taken him out for a walk or something to rebuild some rapport, but……
“You little bastard, come with me somewhere.”
When Oscar grabbed his arm, the Mad Fiend resisted as though he absolutely didn’t want to go.
Oscar soothed the visibly disgusted fellow.
“It’s okay, it’s okay. We’re not going somewhere weird. Yeah, we’re going to eat meat. Meat.”
“……Grrr.”
At the word “meat,” all the strength behind his violent resistance drained away instantly.
Thanks to that, Oscar was able to bring the now-docile Mad Fiend over to the front of the dungeon.
“Grr?”
Unable to spot any meat no matter where he looked, the Mad Fiend vigorously protested with gestures.
“I’ll let you eat as much as you want after you come out. Off you go.”
Fwoooooosh!
Using the wind as it was, Oscar shoved him straight into the dungeon, then dusted off both hands.
“Hopefully this time it’ll actually have some effect.”

Chapter 399: Higher Than the Clouds (1)
After returning to the Magic Tower, Oscar first went to find Sasha.
Knock knock.
Even after knocking on the door and waiting for quite a while, there was no response.
“Hm.”
He couldn’t even tell whether she was inside or not.
By default, the Tower Master’s room blocked detection magic like 『Scan』.
Of course, if he used spatial movement, getting inside itself wouldn’t be a problem.
‘But barging in like that feels a bit wrong.’
Though small in stature, Sasha was now a fully grown adult.
On top of that, she also held the position of Tower Master.
Just because she treated him with utmost respect as her master didn’t mean he should forget that fact.
‘Maybe she has urgent business or something.’
He had thought he might greet her since he had returned after so long.
Suppressing his disappointment, he boarded the elevator.
A moment later, the doors of the descending elevator opened, revealing a familiar face.
“Hm? Isn’t that Oscar?”
“Elder Fidelina?”
The woman in charge of the White Tower’s finances stepped inside and spoke.
“It’s been ages since I last saw you. At this rate, I’ll forget your face even though we live in the same tower, kid.”
“I’m sorry.”
“No, if you’re busy, that’s good news for me. It means you’re out there earning money for us somewhere, right?”
“……Haha.”
Fidelina, who had been watching him laugh awkwardly, checked the floor number.
“Seeing as you came down from above, did you have business with the Tower Master?”
“Yes, but she wasn’t there.”
“You didn’t know? She went to Evemir with the mages.”
“Evemir? Don’t tell me you mean that artificial island? Why would she go there……?”
“Why else? The Night of the Mages is being held.”
The Night of the Mages?
Hearing something he had never expected, Oscar slightly opened his mouth.
“It feels like just yesterday that I participated in that, and you’re saying it’s already been a whole year?”
“Time really flies.”
“Wow, seriously. It feels like a year passed in the blink of an eye.”
“Hoho, you’re too young to be saying things like that already.”
“I genuinely hadn’t even thought about it. Nobody told me anything.”
“Well, of course not. You’re a Master now.”
Last year, he had participated as a 4th Circle mage, yet in merely a single year, he had become a 7th Circle high-ranking mage.
Naturally, participating in the ‘Night of the Mages,’ where only 4th, 5th, and 6th Circle mages could participate, was impossible now.
Oscar shrugged.
“So much for winning tournament MVP two years in a row.”
“You can just win another Oscar Award at the White Night Festival.”
“This year…… wouldn’t that be a little difficult?”
Last year, he had major achievements like the Cadena Flu and being MVP of the Night of the Mages.
And to top it all off, there had been the unveiling of the airship at the White Night Festival presentation.
Compared to that, this year… well, he had mostly been focusing on personal training, so his accomplishments were rather modest.
“True. You’ve been busy with personal matters lately, haven’t you?”
“Yes.”
“Don’t you have any new ideas these days? A new potion would be nice, or maybe magical items like the airship.”
“Nothing really comes to mind.”
“Can’t you make something like a hair-loss cure? You’d sweep in money by the rakeful, not to mention win another Oscar Award.”
Without realizing it, Oscar nodded.
But that was something no one had ever successfully accomplished.
Setting aside his own time for such slim odds was absurd.
“That’d probably be difficult. But why all of a sudden? Is the financial situation still that bad these days?”
“Well, not quite that bad. We’re just preparing for the future. To be honest, we’re not making as much profit as we did last year.”
Fidelina laughed weakly.
“Recently, the Blue Tower has been improving the quality of their potions and lowering prices, so there’s barely any room for us to squeeze in. The lazy giant monopolizing the market finally woke up.”
“They even lowered their prices…….”
Of course, from the Blue Tower’s perspective, that alone would already be a considerable loss.
They must have invested enormous funds into research to improve quality, yet they lowered prices on top of that.
Still, they managed to prevent customers from leaving because of it, which was an undeniable loss for the White Tower.
The market share they should have naturally gained remained unchanged.
“Then I guess the potion side will barely maintain the status quo for a while.”
“That’s exactly what Lena wrote in her report.”
It truly was unfortunate that the potion department’s steep growth had stalled.
Oscar asked,
“How are the Wind Tribe doing?”
“That side is actually sailing along smoothly. Quite a few companies tried copying us by using horses or automobiles to deliver food and things like that, but before long, every single one of them went bankrupt.”
Just as expected.
The White Tower was the only one across the continent that had built that kind of infrastructure.
To begin with, unless someone had flying bikes, comparison in terms of service was impossible.
“So these days we’re putting more focus on the Wind Tribe, but as you know, that side can’t help but expand slowly.”
“……Right. We need to continuously modify the bikes, and we also have to recruit and train people.”
In other words, unlike potions, it wasn’t something that could just be mass-produced endlessly—it inevitably took time.
“The problem is that our fixed expenses have already grown quite large.”
“Fixed expenses?”
“This year, we recruited 324% more mages compared to last year. A lot of talented kids came to us.”
That was definitely a good sign.
It meant the White Tower was regaining its former prestige once more.
In the long run, those talents would grow and bring tremendous benefits to the White Tower.
‘But if you only look at the immediate present, the expenses must be huge.’
An increase in mages meant an increase in mouths to feed.
The facilities they used required maintenance, and magical books had to be purchased.
On top of that, with so many beginner mages joining, the campus would likely start operating again this year.
To do that, they would need to invite highly reputable instructors and professors from outside.
‘And this is already how much money goes into just the beginner mages alone.’
Oscar asked,
“The money going into intermediate and advanced mages increased too, didn’t it?”
“That’s right. Last year, we shifted the delivery department over to ordinary workers, so a lot more mages started focusing on research. Naturally, the proportion of research funding paid to them increased significantly.”
That too was a good phenomenon in the long term.
After all, great discoveries came from research accumulating little by little.
“So in short, the money going out keeps increasing, while the money coming in stays the same.”
“Exactly. That’s why expectations for the airship are pretty high. The airports in each city are going to be completed soon.”
Naturally, nobody was even considering the possibility of the airship failing.
That business would bring enormous wealth to the Magic Tower.
Even just selling boarding tickets alone would likely become a major source of income on the level of an ordinary Magic Tower.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
And on top of that, it would undoubtedly create entirely new paradigms in tourism, business, moving, transportation, and all sorts of other industries, so it would be stranger if it didn’t make money.
“Hmm.”
But something about it made his throat feel slightly itchy.
How should he put it—if he just took one more step forward, it felt like something would suddenly click into place.
‘A business connected to the airships that’ll begin operating soon…….’
They had already done practically everything possible.
They had attracted investment funds from the Imperial Family and each city to build airports.
Contracts had already been finalized for all kinds of restaurants and cafés to move inside them.
They had even built hotels nearby, anticipating crowds flocking to the surrounding commercial districts.
In other words, preparations had already been completed to squeeze every possible profit out of the airports.
‘Tsk. Then why does this still feel lacking?’
Back when the other businesses had been booming, he had thought this much would be enough, but now it didn’t feel that way anymore.
Even in his own eyes, Fidelina’s worries were not something that could simply be dismissed as needless concern.
‘The next ten years are the most important for the White Tower.’
Whether they reclaimed the glory of the past, or whether this current rebound ended as nothing more than a fleeting spark, depended on that.
If their finances started wavering again after only a few years, the talented people who had only just gathered would turn their backs on them.
An organization didn’t collapse when it stagnated.
It collapsed when it failed to handle the pace of its own growth and crashed.
“A new source of income…… I’ll think about it.”
“Oh my, you will?”
Ding.
Right then, the elevator arrived at the floor Fidelina had pressed.
Her complexion brightened immediately as she patted his shoulder.
“Then our little lucky charm, I’ll be counting on you again this time, okay?”
“Yes, well.”
Her footsteps had already become lighter as she stepped off the elevator.
And the moment she left, someone else boarded.
“Hm? Well now, look who this is.”
A small figure staring straight up at him.
Somehow, the elevator had become a place for socializing.
Oscar lightly nodded.
“It’s been a while, Hagor.”
“Seeing your face feels harder than meeting the Tower Master.”
“Sorry. I’ve been busy with personal matters these past few months.”
“If you’re truly sorry, buy me a drink sometime later.”
“Sure. How have the dwarves been living these days?”
At that question, Hagor shrugged.
“The human world is entertaining. We can drink as much alcohol as we want, and the Magic Tower facilities are excellent, so everyone seems satisfied. And did you know we started selling weapons and equipment last month?”
“I heard that was the plan, but I didn’t realize it started last month. Has the response been good?”
“Hmph, what a foolish question. We are the best on the continent. There’s no way the response could be bad.”
With his pride swelling to the heavens, Hagor pulled out a notebook and showed it to him.
“These are the transaction records for the items I made. What do you think?”
“Hieeek!”
A soul-leaving sound escaped Oscar’s mouth.
The transactions all started at minimum in the hundreds of millions.
“No, I know the equipment is excellent, but this is way more expensive than I expected?”
“As you know, we dwarves never produce mass-manufactured equipment. Even if something like that were made, we’d smash it with our own hands rather than ever reveal it to the world.”
“I know.”
That was the greatest reason dwarf-made equipment was so revered.
There were absolutely no defective products.
“That’s why every item we put up for sale is something that passed our own verification. Naturally, there are many people who want to buy them. We’re getting tired of selling them one by one, so we’re thinking of changing the method.”
“How?”
“Negotiating with every individual customer feels inefficient, so we’re thinking of holding auctions periodically. It seems like that way would waste less of our time too.”
“That’s a good idea.”
An auction selling dwarf-made equipment.
The moment he thought that sounded like quite a decent business opportunity—
Oscar’s eyes lit up.
“Hagor.”
“What?”
“There’s no particular reason those auctions have to be held only in Sirin, right?”
“Hm. As long as they aren’t sold cheaply to fools who don’t understand the value of equipment, I don’t care. But why do you ask?”
“I just came up with a pretty good idea.”
A method where both he and Hagor—
the White Tower and the White Anvil Tribe—
could both come out winning.
“Sell those weapons and equipment on the airship.”
“……On the airship?”
Hagor frowned as though asking what nonsense he was spouting.
“It’s not as if everyone boarding the airship will be rich people or nobles. I doubt they’d even be interested.”
“No. That’s why we divide it into categories from the start. We sell seats that grant participation in the auction.”
“Hm, not bad…… but would someone with no reason to board an airship really buy a ticket just to participate in an auction?”
“Of course they would. I’d even bet on it.”
Oscar grinned.
He knew wealthy people and nobles very well.
People with high status or great wealth fundamentally possessed a sense of superiority, believing themselves different from ordinary people.
“They’re already people who’ve experienced practically everything worth experiencing. An ordinary auction wouldn’t even catch their attention.”
But what if an event called the ‘Sky Auction,’ held only once every few months and only in the skies, were to appear?
He could guarantee it—
even if they didn’t particularly need dwarf-made equipment,
or even if they had no business boarding an airship,
they would gladly pay expensive ticket prices solely to participate in that auction, in that very place.
“The dwarves get to sell their works quickly and at high prices.”
“And the White Tower earns money by selling boarding tickets for those seats…….”
“Deal?”
Hagor, meeting his gaze in midair, held out his fist.
“Deal.”

Chapter 400: Higher Than the Clouds (2)
The 13th floor of the White Tower, the dwarf workshop.
The dwarves gathered before the enormous forge that occupied an entire wall.
“I heard there was an important announcement. Anyone know what it’s about?”
“Who knows. All I heard was that the chief had something to say.”
“Hm.”
The dwarves all turned their heads at the sudden gathering.
“Well, if you think about it logically, it’s probably to share the plans going forward.”
“The future… I suppose so.”
Just a month ago, the massive project that the entire tribe had clung to for months had finally come to an end.
The construction of five airships, including the Nosfera, had been successfully completed.
Once the airports in each city were finished before long, those airships would begin traversing the skies across the continent.
This was also why the dwarves—who innately hated idleness—had begun selling weapons and armor again.
To them, happiness in life was holding nails, chisels, and hammers while banging away at something.
“Looks like it’s about that thing they mentioned recently.”
“Ah, the one about changing the way the works are sold.”
“Not bad. How long are craftsmen like us supposed to personally sell every single work ourselves?”
“Seriously. There’s not even enough time to swing a hammer as it is.”
Dwarves were born artists.
The works they forged were not mere products, but crystallizations of skills honed over entire lifetimes.
That was why the moment their creations received proper recognition for their value, they felt a deeper satisfaction than when drinking any alcohol in the world.
But even that satisfaction only lasted the first few times.
After dealing daily with crowds rushing in to buy their works, even that was gradually becoming tiresome.
“Back during the last meeting, opinion leaned toward auctions being the best option, right?”
“Mm. At the moment, that’s probably the most likely route.”
The advantage of the auction system was that it allowed the value of a work to be evaluated quite accurately.
Since numerous people bid prices all at once, an actual market price naturally formed.
“I heard there’s an enormous auction house over in Baran. Our works might get listed there.”
“A bit disappointing. It’d be best if our works could be judged in a place where all the wealthy people of the continent gathered, not just a single city.”
“Of course that would be ideal, but isn’t that impossible?”
There were truly many rich people across the continent.
But it was unlikely they would all gather in the same city on the same day.
They were busy people, and there was no reason for them to do so.
“So everyone’s already here.”
At that moment, all eyes turned toward Hagor, who had just appeared.
“What, Oscar came too?”
“It’s been a while. Normally it’s hard enough just seeing your face.”
“It’s good to see everyone again.”
After waiting for Oscar to finish greeting them, Hagor spoke.
“Alright, everyone pay attention. Based on what was discussed in the last meeting, we plan to hold auctions to sell our works.”
“As expected.”
“I told you this direction was the best.”
“I was wondering why Oscar showed up for once. So he’s handling that matter?”
“That’s right.”
Oscar nodded and continued.
“To be precise, we plan to establish a new department within the White Tower. This department will inspect the performance and quality of the works you submit, then sell them through actual auctions.”
“If it’s the White Tower, we can trust it.”
“Well, whether we like it or not, we’ve already signed exclusive contracts anyway…”
“How much commission are you planning to take?”
“Three percent of the sale price.”
The dwarves nodded.
For luxury auctions, that level of commission was actually on the lower end.
“Not bad. So where are you planning to hold these auctions?”
“Probably Baran, right? I heard major auctions are held there regularly.”
“No way. It has to be held in the capital no matter what. All the continent’s greatest nobles and richest people live there.”
“Wouldn’t eastern Luang be fine too? I hear all the businessmen making piles of money these days have settled there.”
The dwarves instantly began chattering away.
True to their childlike appearances, their voices had not even gone through puberty, making it feel like standing in a kindergarten.
“Shh. Quiet, everyone.”
Oscar forcefully suppressed the chatter through 『Sound Binding』 and spoke.
“The auctions will rotate through the cities you just mentioned.”
Small heads nodded at the answer that satisfied everyone.
“And each of you will only be allowed to submit a maximum of two works per year. One will be registered during the spring and summer season, and the other during the fall and winter season.”
At that, one dwarf raised his hand.
Oscar released that dwarf’s voice.
“Go ahead.”
“A premiumization strategy, sure, it’s an excellent approach. But the weapons and armor we make sell the moment we put them out anyway, so why restrict the quantity that much?”
“Ah, the quantity restriction isn’t because of a premiumization strategy. It’s to provide all of you with at least a minimum amount of rest time.”
“Rest time? Hah, sounds like you don’t understand our stamina.”
The dwarf snickered.
“Sure, we pour our souls into our creations, but it’s not like we can only make two a year.”
“Mm, well. Going forward, I think you’ll have to.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“The auction department will classify your submitted works into two categories.”
Oscar held up two fingers.
“One category will be regular weapons and armor, which, as mentioned earlier, will be auctioned in major cities across the Empire… and the other category will be White Label weapons and armor.”
The dwarves blinked at the unfamiliar term.
“White Label? What’s that?”
“If you bothered dividing them into categories… does that mean there’s some sort of difference?”
“A very, very big difference.”
Oscar smiled faintly.
“First of all, weapons and armor selected as White Label will earn the opportunity to be listed in the Sky Auction, which is held only twice a year.”
“Sky Auction?”
“Yes. A luxurious auction held directly inside an airship.”
An airship auction!
The dwarves, who were not lacking in intelligence, quickly grasped the advantages.
“Only twice a year, and if a work receives the White Label after competing against works made by us…”
“Even people with no intention of buying would gather there just to see it. All the money and power in the world would come flocking.”
“Exactly.”
White Label.
That was the true core of the business Oscar was aiming for.
To dwarves, who possessed an artist’s desire for recognition, receiving the White Label would become the greatest dopamine rush imaginable.
And even if they failed to receive it this time, it would only drive them to swear they would absolutely obtain it next time.
“And among the White Label works, the creator of the piece sold for the highest price will be introduced as the Master Craftsman of the Year in a magazine published by the auction department.”
A chance to make their names known as master craftsmen backed by the White Tower.
Most of the dwarves had already swallowed hard.
Before their eyes flickered visions of a future where their works received the White Label, sold for astronomical prices, and brought them wealth and fame.
Of course, there were also dwarves who were dissatisfied.
“Hm. But if it’s the auction department assigning the White Label, doesn’t that mean humans will ultimately judge the value of our works according to human standards? I don’t like that one bit.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“Indeed… are the aesthetic senses of humans even refined enough to understand the noble artistry of us dwarves?”
“You don’t need to worry about that part.”
Oscar corrected them.
“The White Label will be assigned based on combined scores after thorough evaluations conducted by the Dwarf King of Laforge and each tribe chief.”
“The chiefs and His Majesty the King?”
“Hmmm. If it’s to that extent, then it can be trusted.”
Only then did all the dwarves nod in agreement.
If that was true, there would be no issue understanding the judging standards.
“Then how many items will be submitted at once in this so-called Sky Auction?”
“This year, there will be 10 items for the S/S season, and 15 items for the F/W season, for a total of 25.”
The dwarves looked at one another at the tighter numbers than expected.
The White Anvil Tribe had a total of 37 members, meaning the competition ratio was roughly 3.7 to 1.
In other words, only about one out of every four dwarves would receive the White Label.
‘Hmm. Still, it’s not like there’s much to worry about.’
‘No matter what, there’s no way I wouldn’t get a White Label here. Right, exactly.’
‘Since we can’t submit multiple works, I’ll have to submit only the one I’m most confident in.’
No matter what, I’m better than that guy at least.
Each of them nodded while thinking such thoughts.
Then one dwarf asked.
“Wait, then why does the F/W season have more submission slots than the S/S season?”
“Oh? That’s a very sharp question.”
As Oscar grinned, the dwarves suddenly felt an inexplicable sense of unease.
Then he dropped a thunderbolt of a statement.
“For this S/S season, preparations are too rushed, so only works from the White Anvil Tribe will be submitted. But beginning with the second half’s F/W season, we plan to accept works from the Blue Salt Tribe as well.”
“What! Those salt-sniffing bastards are joining too?”
“Wait, then in the worst-case scenario…”
“Our tribe might not receive a single White Label, and those bastards could monopolize them all?”
Since ancient times, competitions had always been something that made blood boil.
Didn’t even academy students stake their pride on class competitions?
And as seen during the previous Mage’s Night, the tension between magic towers was no joke either.
Apparently, in the distant past, even nations held competitions against one another.
‘In other words, if you make the dwarves of each tribe compete, higher quality products will pour out.’
Oscar had no intention of slaughtering the goose that laid golden eggs.
Of course, if they rushed preparations starting now, they could receive products from all five tribes and put them into the Sky Auction before the airports were completed.
But if they did that, there would be no lasting hype.
‘Even customers who visited once need a reason to come back again next time.’
The first season would only feature the White Anvil Tribe.
The next season would add the Blue Salt Tribe, and after that, even the Black Hammer Tribe.
If they stirred up issues every season like that, people would be unable to resist spending money.
‘And as a bonus, the quality of the works surviving that terrifying loneliness would naturally reach a level humans wouldn’t even dare imitate.’
Naturally, there was backlash.
“Hold on! Wasn’t the original purpose of this auction to help our White Anvil Tribe, who signed exclusive contracts with the White Tower, sell weapons and armor more conveniently? So why are unrelated bastards being dragged into this?”
“Now that I think about it, he’s right! Aren’t those bastards unable to even interact with humans anyway?”
It was quite a sharp observation.
And factually correct as well.
But Oscar, who had already anticipated this situation, casually tossed out a single remark.
“Ah… if you’re saying this because you’re afraid of competing against the other tribes, then I understand. We’ll just accept works from the White Anvil Tribe only.”
Scared?
At that single word, the dwarves’ eyes flared wide.
“Hah! Who said we were scared! Those bastards have always been less skilled than us!”
“Exactly! If we compete against them in craftsmanship, there’s absolutely no disadvantage for us!”
“This is even better. It’s an opportunity. A chance to show the entire continent that the White Anvil Tribe possesses the finest craftsmanship!”
Once the atmosphere ignited, it showed no signs of cooling down.
“This time I’ll submit one of the works I’ve already completed and immediately start crafting the next one.”
“Damn right. Forget everything else—we absolutely cannot lose to those salt-sniffers.”
“In the second half of the year, we’re taking at least eight White Labels!”
“Let’s see the looks on those idiots’ faces!”
If things proceeded like this, all five tribes would be participating by the year after next, which would make things truly entertaining to watch.
Watching Oscar grin to himself from the side, Hagor trembled in fear.
“T-this brat… he’s far too cunning!”
For some reason, he didn’t know why.
But in Oscar’s current appearance, he saw the image of Oscar Sage—the one who had once commanded him in the past—overlapping perfectly.
