Chapter 401: Higher Than the Clouds (3)
“Sky Auction?”
Fidelina’s eyes widened after hearing the explanation.
“So, you’re saying you want to hold an auction in the sky right now?”
“Yes.”
“This is a little shocking, but……”
After rapidly running the numbers in her head, she sniffed the air.
“I smell it. This definitely smells like money.”
“Right? I think this could become the White Tower’s new business model.”
“Hoo, seriously, what would I have done without you?”
Love practically dripped from the eyes with which she looked at him.
“Good. Then leave all the auction-related work to me. You’ve already drafted the outline, right?”
“Yes. First, we need to gather the customers in one place.”
The continent was vast.
Which meant they first needed to gather the entrepreneurs, merchants, and nobles into one location.
“We’ll pick up VIPs from the north, east, west, and south, then head to the capital.”
“Wait…… then should we give them a hint about the Sky Auction beforehand?”
“No.”
Oscar shook his head.
“Anyone with enough power and money will want to experience the airship the moment it launches anyway. What matters to people like them is not falling behind the trends of high society.”
“But even so, there’s no guarantee every VIP will board the airship that day, right?”
“That’s fine. It’s actually better.”
“Better?”
“Yes. Whatever the reason, the people who fail to participate in this Sky Auction will realize it. That failing to quickly experience a new business the White Tower gets involved in is itself an enormous loss.”
In professional terminology, it was called FOMO.
The fear of missed opportunities and the resulting sense of exclusion.
Going forward, it would also return as positive reactions toward the White Tower’s various new businesses.
“So we ignore the complaints of the minority and prioritize the satisfaction of the majority? I get it.”
“Yes. Which is why this Sky Auction has to feel special.”
“Doesn’t the fact that it’s being held in the sky already accomplish that?”
“That alone isn’t enough.”
An auction held in the sky.
Sure, it would naturally be a fascinating experience.
At the very least, high society would gossip about it for an entire month.
‘But that’s all.’
This was something only a White Tower mage could understand.
“Elder, what was it like the first time you learned flight magic?”
“Flight magic? Well…… it felt good? I suppose you could call it liberation. Like escaping from a cage.”
The overwhelming speed and freedom one could feel while soaring through the open sky.
It unquestionably provided tremendous stimulation and dopamine, but it faded quickly.
“Then you understand. Flying is only thrilling and exciting the first time. After you experience it a few times, it stops feeling like much.”
“……Indeed.”
“And for the customers, it’ll be even worse. Unlike us, they won’t be freely traversing the skies. They’ll only enjoy it in a limited manner by boarding an airship as a means of transportation.”
The novelty would quickly wear off, and before long, airships would simply feel like a normal method of travel.
“That’s why we need to give them a sense of exclusivity they can’t experience anywhere else.”
“……What could that be?”
“We’ll sell dwarf equipment.”
After he continued by explaining the concept of white labels, she covered her mouth.
“M-My goodness. This is far too evil!”
“Is it bad?”
“The exact opposite!”
At the current point in time, dwarf equipment already possessed tremendous value in and of itself.
That was why Sirin’s dwarf workshop was crowded every single day.
But now they planned to go one step further and auction off limited-edition items among dwarf equipment?
‘Power and money. For those who’ve already achieved everything and possess everything, there’s only one thing left that they desperately desire.’
Scarcity.
The Sky Auction would become the place that sold that scarcity.
“Hmm. If VIPs from all over the continent gather together, then personal security will need to be our top priority.”
“Exactly.”
This auction was a double-edged sword.
It could create a new culture, allow the White Tower to lead it, and sweep in enormous wealth and fame.
But if handled poorly, it could also turn every force on the continent into their enemy.
“If something unfortunate were to happen during the auction……”
Fidelina shuddered after imagining the worst.
“Now that I think about it again, doesn’t this seem way too dangerous?”
“We still have to do it. It’s too good of a business to avoid just because it’s scary. We simply have to do it well.”
“Do it well…… and your concrete plan?”
“Realistically speaking, it’ll be difficult for the White Tower alone to cover every airship. So we’ll receive support from the Imperial Family.”
After all, even the airports already had city soldiers and imperial troops stationed all over the place.
They simply needed to assign some of them to remain aboard the airships as well.
“On top of that, to prepare for possible incidents, we’ll disguise some soldiers as passengers and have them board the airships.”
“Do we really need to go that far?”
“There’s nothing wrong with being cautious. Hundreds of passengers’ lives are riding on a single aircraft.”
If an airship were ever hijacked by hostile forces, the aftermath would be too horrifying to even imagine.
‘Of course, there are still minimum safety measures in place…….’
That safety measure referred to the flight captain.
For the time being, White Tower mages themselves would serve as captains and pilot the airships directly.
Just as the Wind Tribe Riders once did, this would continue until professional captains could be trained.
‘Right now, the captains are all mid-level White Tower mages, so they should be able to handle most threats on their own.’
But anyone bold enough to commit crimes aboard an airship was unlikely to be some ordinary nobody.
That was why security and protection needed to be strengthened even further.
“Understood. I’ll discuss that matter with the Imperial Family and the lords or mayors of each city.”
“I’ll leave it to you.”
If it was Elder Fidelina, who handled matters meticulously, there should be no problems.
She quickly left to prepare for the launch ceremony, which was less than ten days away.
‘Then I should…….’
Maybe spend the meantime training.
Oscar headed toward the training room.
* * *
Entering the training room, Oscar comfortably sat down on the floor.
Then he pulled out a single book from his chest.
A magic tome personally created by Magiro and completed over twenty-one years by his thought-form.
When he turned a page, a warning was written in the prologue.
-This magic merely accelerates thought processes. You must understand that it is not time stop.
“I see.”
Magiro had said that mastering this spell would create the illusion that everything around him had slowed down.
If the effect became too intense, it might even momentarily feel as though time itself had stopped.
But the two should never be confused.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
‘It only feels that way. That doesn’t mean I can move normally in that state.’
In other words, within that slowed perception of time, his own body would also become slower.
The effect of this magic was ultimately to read the opponent’s moves and think of ways to counter them.
After carefully memorizing the warning, Oscar turned the page.
‘The brain. The hardest body part to interfere with.’
Since ancient times, countless mages had conducted endless research in an attempt to strengthen the brain.
Because if successful, it seemed possible to catastrophically increase the calculation speed of magic.
The conclusion was a spectacular failure.
‘The brain is highly sensitive to mana.’
If he had to compare it to something, it was like a sunfish.
Expose it to even slightly excessive mana, and severe side effects would appear—memory loss, deterioration of language abilities, and more.
How had Magiro solved this problem?
Rapidly flipping through the pages, Oscar let out a sound of admiration.
“Huh, it’s not magic that directly interferes with the brain itself?”
Magiro Time was hyper-acceleration of thought.
Naturally, he had assumed the method would involve strengthening the brain with mana.
He thought it would apply concepts like 『Acceleration』 or 『Durability Enhancement』 to the brain itself.
But this magic approached the problem from an entirely different angle.
-Basically, the human brain is an organ capable of processing an enormous amount of information simultaneously. Anyone who has ever tried creating and controlling a golem should understand this. The amount of information processed through actions we perform naturally, like breathing—seeing, hearing, speaking—is astronomical. Artificially replicating this requires an immense number of magic circles and mana.
That was true.
It was also why most golems were stupid.
-However, consciousness only perceives information serially. Simply put, no matter how intelligent someone is, they cannot read two books simultaneously. At this point, the original developed a single question. Though it may belong to the realm of supernatural abilities, Lapiros—one of the Four Great Counts—examines countless possibilities and even reads the future. If so, then doesn’t the human brain, whose structure is not drastically different from that of demons, also possess the potential to think in the same manner?
“Hmm?”
Now that he thought about it, that was true.
Of course, he had no intention of denying that demons were inherently superior to humans physically.
However, most things they could do were also things humans could achieve with enough effort.
-Thus, the original arrived at a hypothesis. Perhaps humans are also capable of processing information in such a way, but under normal circumstances, the brain instinctively suppresses it.
The brain instinctively suppressing it?
It sounded highly plausible.
After all, there was already a theory that the human nervous system intentionally lowered the body’s output so people could not use 100% of their strength, considering the backlash.
Stories of mothers displaying superhuman strength to lift wagons and save infants were examples of that.
-In other words, this magic does not strengthen the human brain itself. Rather, it focuses on nullifying the output limitations imposed by the nervous system.
After carefully examining the following formulas, Oscar nodded.
To state the conclusion first, Magiro’s hypothesis was correct.
The human brain was capable of simultaneously processing vast amounts of information, but normally restricted that output.
‘So that’s why he said not to use it for more than three seconds.’
However, there was a reason it remained restricted under normal circumstances.
The human brain was pitifully fragile, and once the limiter was removed, it would melt within mere seconds.
-One thing, however, can be stated with certainty. During the moment this magic is maintained, you will be able to look down upon the entire world.
An expression grandiose even by Magiro’s standards.
Overcome with curiosity, Oscar immediately guided his mana according to the formula.
‘Like this.’
And the moment the formula was completed.
“……!”
It felt as though a third eye that had long remained closed had suddenly opened.
His thoughts accelerated, all his senses sharpened, and the illusion that time had slowed blanketed his entire body.
No matter how long he stared at the clock hanging on the wall, the second hand did not move.
‘This is.’
In this state, there was no attack he could not evade, and no attack he could not land.
For a brief moment, overwhelming confidence surged through him, as though he could accomplish absolutely anything.
But only for a moment.
Oscar frowned as his senses dulled.
“Kh!”
Then his vision spun violently, and his sight blurred.
His head felt foggy and sluggish, like he had come down with a severe fever.
Instinctively pressing a hand to his forehead, Oscar was startled.
An incredible heat radiated through his palm.
‘The spell’s duration…… it probably didn’t even last a full second.’
And yet the aftereffects were already this severe.
A couple hours later, after finally regaining his senses, Oscar immediately cast Magiro Time again without resting.
He needed to know exactly how long the spell could be maintained if he intended to use it in real combat.
“……Hoo.”
A week passed with him doing nothing but obsess over that magic, skipping meals and training day and night without distinction.
Only then did Oscar finally leave the training room.

Chapter 402: Higher Than the Clouds (4)
“Woooow…….”
One child looked up at the enormous building with sparkling eyes.
The sleek silver structure glittered dazzlingly beneath the midday sunlight.
“Leo, come over here. There are too many people.”
“Ah! Yes, Mother.”
The child hurried over, grabbed his mother’s hand, and passed through the airport entrance.
“Wow.”
The interior of the airport that filled his vision felt so open it almost cleared his chest.
The reason was the overwhelmingly high ceiling, but even more astonishing was the complete absence of pillars.
“Huh, there aren’t even any pillars, so how does a building this tall not collapse?”
“I heard dwarves designed the structure.”
“I should come back someday just to look around the airport itself. It’s basically a work of art.”
The child listened to the adults talking while continuously taking in the scenery with shining eyes.
Magic-engineering guide boards all around constantly displayed new information, and hundreds of people busily moved throughout the endlessly sprawling terminal.
Short advertisements even played across the massive screens attached to the walls.
Ocean, mountain ranges, deserts.
Every road began with someone’s first step.
The Sky is the Next Road.
Now, it is the sky’s turn.
Soon after, a glamorous woman appeared slicing through the sky and passionately sang in an incredibly high pitch.
Fly all the way to the edge of that sky~
♪~♬~♩
Several passengers stood blankly before the screen, repeatedly watching the advertisement with its addictive rhythm.
“That’s Marin Maria. I heard her appearance fees are insanely expensive these days. Looks like she even filmed an airship commercial.”
“Her tone is seriously…… unreal.”
“I’m definitely going to her solo concert next time.”
The entrepreneur couple holding their child’s hand swallowed dryly as they walked.
They were business owners operating a cosmetics company in Luang, known as the heart of the Eastern Continent, but they could confidently say they had never seen a building like this before.
Unlike the imperial palace, it overwhelmed people from the very moment they stepped inside.
“Dad, it smells nice here.”
“Smells?”
At the child’s sudden words, the man sniffed the air.
There certainly was a scent he had never smelled before, but it was the kind difficult to describe as, ‘It smells exactly like this!’
Because it was a complex fragrance mixed from the unique scent of a brand-new building and the perfumes of countless different people.
“It smells like the excitement of travelers.”
“The excitement of travelers…… that’s a wonderful way to put it.”
The man patted his son’s head and searched through his coat.
“Let’s see. I heard we first have to do something called check-in. Ah, let’s go to that desk over there.”
Guided by an employee, they easily finished checking in and headed toward the inspection area.
Soldiers from the city hall and soldiers bearing the imperial emblem guarded the place.
“Please place all your belongings into that box and set it on top of the inspection platform.”
“Wait a moment. You’re confiscating our belongings?”
“Please don’t worry. We’ll only determine whether dangerous items are present through magical detection and return everything afterward.”
Magical detection?
This machine?
The three of them placed all their belongings into the box and waited.
Their luggage moved along the rail and was thoroughly inspected through devices registered with the 『Scan』 spell.
“Now then, please come over one at a time. We’ll conduct a body inspection.”
“A body inspection? Do we need to take off our clothes?”
“No. Just raise your hands as they are. And please wear this bracelet.”
“What is this?”
“It’s a mana suppression bracelet. For the safety of all passengers, the use of mana by anyone other than authorized personnel is strictly prohibited within the airport. You may return the bracelet at the inspection area of your arrival airport.”
At those words, the man’s eyes widened.
‘They go this far for safety?’
It didn’t matter much to him personally, but for some people, resistance was inevitable.
In fact, someone in another line immediately raised his voice.
“You dare seal my mana? Do you know who I am!?”
“My apologies, but searches and mana restrictions within airport inspection areas were authorized by His Majesty the Emperor himself. Refusal may result in punishment for defying an imperial order in court. If you truly dislike it, submit a request beforehand to the White Tower for limited mana usage permission. After reviewing your reason, approval may be granted if deemed appropriate.”
“H-His Majesty the Emperor? C-Cough.”
In this place, even the authority of nobles holding high-ranking positions in massive cities like Luang meant nothing.
Most passengers who witnessed the scene felt not fear, but relief.
‘If they care this much about safety, nothing dangerous should happen.’
‘Well, if terrorism broke out inside an airship, it’d be horrifying.’
What greeted the passengers after passing through the intense inspection area was a luxurious shopping district.
There, they sold travel supplies and items suitable as gifts.
“W-Wait a second. Why are the prices so cheap? Airport-exclusive discounts?”
“Oh my! I’m going to go look at that coat for just a moment.”
“If you miss the airship because of that…… huh? They even sell fishing rods over there?”
It looked as though the airport itself had been turned into a gigantic shopping mall.
People had to pass by countless stores in order to reach the gate where they would board the airship.
“Huff, we’re already exhausted before even seeing the airship.”
“Seriously.”
The couple finally arrived at the gate and sat down to catch their breath.
At that moment, the child spotted something and ran toward the window.
“Wow! It’s the airship!”
At those words, everyone turned toward the window as if by prior agreement.
“Oh…….”
“Waaah…….”
An enormous ship large enough to leave their jaws hanging slowly moved along the runway toward them.
At its elegant appearance, the hearts of both adults and children alike began pounding.
Because they would soon fly through the sky aboard that very airship.
That same experience was occurring simultaneously all across the continent.
* * *
A spacious room warmly lit by sunlight thanks to its excellent lighting.
A man sipping smooth tea picked up a communication device.
“…….”
The device emitted a brief beep before connecting somewhere.
-It is Owl. Please forgive me for being unable to personally greet the First Finger.
“I shall generously forgive you. How are the preparations proceeding?”
-They are perfectly complete. If you simply give the signal at any time…….
After taking a brief breath, the man beyond the communication device spoke.
-The Imperial Family and the White Tower will realize today that what falls also has wings.
Satisfied by the reliable answer, the man nodded.
“Proceed.”
He looked up at the blue sky outside the window and muttered,
“So that people will never trust the sky again.”
* * *
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The entrepreneur couple who boarded the airship sat in their seats with their seatbelts already fastened.
The man stared at the walls painted white and muttered,
“Everything’s nice, but it feels more cramped than I expected.”
He turned toward his wife sitting beside him.
“Don’t you think so?”
“It definitely feels a little strange. The interior is dark too.”
There wasn’t a single window inside the airship, making it impossible to see outside at all.
“When I thought of an airship, I imagined something much more open and refreshing…… but apparently not.”
“They said we can move around freely once we take off, so let’s go up to the deck together then.”
Chiiiik!
At that moment, the speakers inside the cabin crackled and the captain’s voice echoed out.
-Attention passengers, the airship will soon take off. Until additional announcements are made, please refrain from unfastening your seatbelts or moving around.
Chiiik.
-Your first flight begins now.
And with those words.
The entire wall of the airship transformed into one seamless pane of glass.
Reflected in everyone’s eyes was a refreshing runway stretching endlessly into the distance.
“O-Oh! It’s moving!”
Woooooong!
The gigantic airship began moving forward alongside a low vibration.
At first, it was slower than expected.
The scenery around them and the airport slowly passed by, to the point it barely seemed different from riding in a carriage.
‘Can something really fly through the sky at this speed?’
‘We did see it ourselves during the White Night Festival…… but is it actually possible?’
‘Surely it won’t crash while taking off, right?’
The mixture of excitement and anxiety shook their hearts only briefly.
The airship gradually began accelerating, naturally pressing the passengers’ bodies against their seats.
“O-Ohhh!”
“Ugh……!”
The airship surpassed 300 kilometers per hour in an instant, giving a sensation of speed far greater than riding in an automobile.
And just as everyone’s hearts began pounding at the fact such a massive ship was moving at terrifying speed—
Thunk!
Alongside a small impact, the sensation of the entire airship lifting spread through them.
A strange feeling of floating accompanied the sensation of their organs, including their hearts, being pulled backward.
The passengers unconsciously gripped the armrests tightly and swallowed hard.
The runway rapidly grew distant, and the airport that had seemed enormous shrank to the size of a palm.
After ascending for quite some time in that state, the airship finally began moving horizontally only after piercing through the clouds.
-Passengers are now free to move around. We wish you a pleasant flight.
At the same time as the announcement, sounds of people finally releasing held breaths echoed throughout the cabin.
“H-Haah! Good heavens.”
“We’re really flying through the sky?”
“No way. Look outside.”
“……That’s the city we lived in?”
“The airship is flying higher than the clouds.”
Soon after, a brief silence spread among everyone without exception.
Buildings that now felt like toys, mountain ranges that once looked so tall, long silver rivers sparkling brilliantly.
The places that had been their entire world only moments ago now felt unbelievably tiny.
“Was our world always that small?”
“Somehow…… I feel like a frog trapped in a well.”
The people lost in their own thoughts began unfastening their seatbelts and standing one by one.
“Let’s go see the deck too!”
The people climbed the stairs in order and stepped onto the deck, only to gasp in surprise.
Because the cleanest air they had ever experienced in their lives filled their lungs.
“Huaaah! It’s refreshing!”
“I-Isn’t it dangerous?”
When several passengers hesitated out of fear and couldn’t come up, those already on the deck shook their heads.
“It’s completely fine. I don’t know the details, but I think there’s magic cast here.”
“In that case…….”
Those who carefully stepped onto the deck continuously let out exclamations of admiration.
A wind blowing at exactly the most pleasant intensity brushed against their faces.
And for the first time, they could finally look down upon the entire world.
“Please do not lean too heavily against the railing. It is dangerous.”
The soldiers on the deck wandered around like safety personnel, protecting the passengers.
While everyone was enjoying a moment of happiness, the captain inside the cockpit was extremely tense.
“Huuuk, huuuk.”
He had practiced countless times for today.
But when he thought about how hundreds of lives depended on him, there was no way he couldn’t be nervous.
The first officer sitting beside him spoke.
“Relax a little. What are you so worried about?”
“……It’s our first flight carrying passengers.”
“Dangerous people get filtered out at the inspection area anyway. The only people capable of using mana on this airship are us, the crew members, and the soldiers.”
The extremely optimistic first officer let out a laugh.
At that very moment—
Beep! Beep!
The airship’s detection magic suddenly began blaring loudly.
“What is it?”
“Wait a moment. I’ll check.”
The first officer hurriedly examined the crystal orb for a moment.
The smile completely vanished from his face as he spoke.
“……Captain, multiple mana reactions are approaching the airship.”

Chapter 403: Higher Than the Clouds (5)
Beepbeepbeepbeep! Beepbeepbeepbeep!
At the nonstop blaring alarm, the captain manipulated the controls and shouted.
“Damn it, what’s the target?”
“Analysis of the mana pattern shows a flock of sky rays. Around thirty of them.”
“...Hoo.”
The captain let out a deep breath, as though setting one worry aside.
Well, if it was monsters, encountering them during flight wasn’t strange at all.
He stared at the red dots floating on the radar and muttered.
“That’s unexpected. I thought sky rays only appeared in the southern regions.”
“That’s not the case. Some species live in lakes near the center of the continent.”
“...Why do you know so much?”
“I’m pretty interested in flying creatures.”
The first officer shrugged.
“Did you know there were attempts in the past to raise sky rays and conquer the skies?”
“Really?”
“Yes. Their top speed reaches 250 kilometers per hour, after all. Though no matter how much they trained them, they couldn’t fly longer than ten minutes, so it failed.”
“You’re practically a scholar. A sky ray scholar.”
“You flatter me.”
The first officer, observing the radar, chuckled softly.
“This kinda makes me feel bad for no reason. If you think about it, we’re the ones barging into the territory where they’d been living peacefully.”
“Can’t be helped. The route from Rouen to the capital’s already been decided, so once they get used to it, they’ll avoid us on their own. I heard they’re fairly intelligent.”
“Hopefully.”
Beepbeepbeep! Beepbeepbeep!
The cockpit was still filled with warning beeps, and the red light refused to turn off.
“First, turn that damn noise off. It’s driving me insane.”
“Please don’t worry. Once we move farther away from the flock of sky rays, the warning sound should naturally deactivate, hm?”
At that moment, the first officer frowned after noticing something.
“What the hell is this? Did it malfunction or something?”
“What? What is it?”
“Well... the flock of sky rays isn’t disappearing from the detection magic’s range.”
“What?”
The captain, who had been looking forward, slowly turned his head.
Just as the first officer said, the red dots displayed on the radar by the 『Scan』 spell weren’t disappearing.
“Check the magic formula. There wasn’t any issue during inspection, right?”
“No. There were no problems when we checked before takeoff... Could it have overloaded and frozen after suddenly detecting such a large number of monsters?”
Thinking about it rationally, it was entirely possible.
Though this massive airship looked sluggish on the outside, in truth it was the culmination of civilization itself, loaded with hundreds of advanced magitech systems and the essence of White Tower magic.
One or two unverified errors appearing wasn’t impossible.
Beep! Beep!
“Hm?”
At that moment, the first officer tilted his head.
“Was I mistaken? The red dots just now... I think they moved?”
“You sure you didn’t see wrong? Check again.”
“Yes, I’ll observe a bit longer.”
The first officer stared intently at the radar.
Then suddenly, he jolted in shock.
“T-They’re moving! These things! They’re definitely moving! They’re even getting closer!”
“What?”
The captain’s face stiffened.
Without realizing it, he checked the instrument panel.
“That’s impossible... We’re flying at 350 kilometers per hour right now?”
Meanwhile, the maximum speed of a sky ray was around 250 kilometers per hour.
Which meant those sky rays were variants far faster than previously known.
At that moment, the first officer discovered something and shouted.
“This is insane! Captain, there are people riding on top of the monsters!”
“What?”
The captain’s face twisted as he glared at the radar.
‘Did they hide their mana as much as possible so only the sky rays would be detected?’
If they were the sort of people to do that, there was no way they were approaching with good intentions.
The captain shouted.
“Connect the announcement system! We need to get the passengers back to their seats first!”
“Understood!”
Suppressing his agitation, the captain evacuated the passengers to their seats with the calmest voice he could manage.
The official reason given was that they had encountered a flock of monsters and turbulence was expected, so passengers were requested to return to safety.
“What about the passengers?”
“I believe almost all of them have returned to their seats!”
“In that case...”
The captain pushed the lever all the way forward.
Kuuuuuuung!
At the same time, the airship’s output surged to maximum, breaking past 400 kilometers per hour.
This was the highest speed the first-generation Nospella could produce.
“Deploy defensive magic at maximum power, and activate the interception system.”
“Yes!”
The first officer pressed several buttons in sequence.
Then sticks popped out from both sides.
Gripping them tightly, the first officer put on interception goggles and locked onto the targets.
He pressed the button with his thumb.
“Commence firing!”
Kwaaaaaaaa!
A massive mana cannon was fired from the artillery mounted along the airship’s exterior.
“The targets?”
“Confirmed six mana signatures eliminated from the radar! Twenty-four remaining!”
“Good, keep intercepting them!”
The captain’s eyebrows twitched with anger.
“Make them pay for daring to target a White Tower airship.”
“Yes!”
Kwaaaang!
Every time a mana cannon fired, a red dot vanished from the radar.
The passengers seated in their chairs watched the scene vaguely and nodded in amazement.
“Whoa, the airship’s got stuff like that attached to it?”
“Look at those beams of light shooting out... that’s incredible.”
“Hm?”
At that moment, a child staring at the falling monsters tugged at his mother’s sleeve.
“Mother, it’s a person!”
“Hm? A person?”
The mother lowered her head to look out the window and smiled faintly.
“That’s not a person, dear. It’s a monster called a sky ray.”
“No... it really was a person....”
Just as the child’s muttering faded away—
all the glass showing the outside scenery was replaced by walls.
Kuuuuung!
At the same time, the airship shook, and an announcement echoed out.
-This airship has encountered turbulence alongside a monster flock... shaking is expected. Passengers are requested to fasten their seatbelts and refrain from moving around.
After quickly reassuring the passengers, the captain shut off the announcement and asked.
“What’s the current situation?”
“Tch, these bastards are chasing us relentlessly.”
The first officer pulled off his goggles roughly and spoke while sweating.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“The mana cannon barrels have overheated, so they need time to cool down. Can’t we increase speed any further?”
“This is the limit. How the hell are sky rays moving at that speed...?”
Sensing strong doubt from the captain, the first officer replied.
“Still, don’t we only need to hold out for about ten minutes?”
“No, we can’t even be sure of that.”
That speed had already surpassed common sense.
Which meant they couldn’t blindly trust the idea that sky rays could only fly for around ten minutes either.
The captain swallowed dryly.
“But as long as the defensive magic remains intact, they can’t infiltrate from outside.”
“That’s right. If we keep intercepting them like this, time is on our side.”
“...”
But why?
Why did he feel so uneasy?
Without realizing it, the captain spoke.
“Check the internal situation through the observation crystal orb.”
“Understood.”
Tak, tatak!
As the first officer rapidly pressed buttons, dozens of screens appeared before his eyes.
Each area of the ship was displayed in crystal-clear quality.
“The seating areas are safe for now. Nobody’s standing or wandering around... though there are three empty seats.”
“Those are probably the disguised passengers deployed by the Imperial Family.”
The captain and first officer also knew disguised soldiers existed aboard.
However, they didn’t know exactly how many there were or which seats they occupied.
That was to eliminate even the slightest possibility of information leaking.
“Find their positions.”
“Yes. The soldiers are guarding the deck for now, the restaurant is safe as well. And... huh?”
The first officer’s pupils trembled slightly.
He had discovered two corpses on one of the screens.
“Shit! We found bodies! Judging by their appearance, they seem to be Imperial disguised soldiers!”
“What? Send soldiers to that location immediately!”
The instant the captain gave the order—
Beep! Beep! Beep!
A new warning sound, one they hadn’t heard before, rang through the cockpit.
The two men, both aware of what the sound meant, unconsciously looked at each other.
“......”
“......”
Normally, the defensive magic that blocked outside interference was controlled from the cockpit.
However, in emergencies, the airship possessed an ‘Emergency Barrier Release Lever’ capable of partially deactivating that barrier for passenger safety.
The sound now blaring madly meant someone had pulled it down and opened part of the barrier.
“Captain, this is...”
“Yeah.”
The enemies not only knew who the Imperial disguised soldiers were, but even knew first-class confidential information about the airship.
Which meant information had leaked from somewhere.
* * *
“What did you just say?”
Oscar, who had been waiting at The Central Airport in the capital, asked.
The one who answered him was the airport director.
“The airships’ movements are strange.”
“In what way exactly?”
“The policy for civilian airships is to maintain a speed of 350 kilometers per hour, but they’ve already surpassed 400 kilometers per hour.”
That was certainly strange.
The captains had no reason to take such risks just to arrive early.
“I’ll confirm it myself. But you said airship‘s’?”
“Yes. All four airships that departed for the capital today have exceeded 400 kilometers per hour. Their signals were cut off ten minutes ago as well.”
“......”
Oscar’s expression grew slightly serious.
“You can’t establish communication?”
“We haven’t been able to contact any of the four since earlier.”
“Understood for now.”
Naturally, he pulled a personal communication device from his coat.
It was shared only among certain people within the Imperial Family and the White Tower, allowing direct contact with the Imperial disguised soldiers.
[The communication has ended due to no response from the other party.]
“......”
All the disguised soldiers dispatched to the four ships had gone silent.
No matter how optimistically one interpreted it, they were likely incapacitated—or in the worst case, dead.
At that point, even Oscar’s gaze turned cold.
‘Interesting.’
This was blatant terrorism.
Someone had illegally seized White Tower airships in midair.
Fidelina, who had been listening to the two converse, spoke with a pale face.
“W-Wait, then the VIPs who were supposed to arrive at the capital today too...”
“There’s a high chance they were the main targets.”
Oscar stared at the map displayed on the wall of the airport director’s office.
Normally, each airship’s current location should’ve been displayed as blinking dots.
But the absence of blinking meant the other side had unilaterally cut the signals.
“They do seem to be heading here for now.”
“What? That’s impossible. Do you know how many soldiers are stationed at this airport and around the capital?”
“The more, the better.”
The people who seized the airships never deviated from the flight route until the last recorded position.
Which meant they were indeed heading toward the capital.
“Perhaps... they’re considering the worst possible move.”
“The worst possible move? What’s that?”
“On the first day of airship operations, if all four airships crashed into the capital... wouldn’t that be horrifying?”
Imagining the scene, Fidelina staggered as though dizzy.
“T-That’s impossible. If something like that happened...”
“We would lose everything in an instant.”
The airships carried VIPs from across the continent.
Not only the greatest authorities in every field, but even royalty and nobility were aboard.
The moment they all died on the same day, the White Tower would be stained with an irredeemable disgrace.
‘That’s probably beyond even Uncle Emperor’s ability to cover up.’
If things went wrong, even he could suffer backlash.
After all, Uncle Emperor had supported the White Tower and invested generously into the airships and the business itself.
‘Assuming the Imperial disguised soldiers were taken down, then information leaked.’
Since every passenger had passed through checkpoints, the airships couldn’t have been seized solely by people inside.
In that case, there was a high probability they also had support forces outside.
‘If information about the Imperial disguised soldiers leaked, then they’d know about the Emergency Barrier Release Lever too.’
The enemy was even thoroughly wary of his spatial magic.
That was likely one reason they seized all four ships instead of just one.
Oscar loosened his tie slightly with a hardened expression and rose from his seat.
“I’ll go resolve this.”
The moment those words ended—
his figure vanished like a ghost.

Chapter 404: Higher Than the Clouds (6)
“...Cough.”
The blood flowing from the captain's mouth stained his clean shirt.
It was the very shirt his wife had ironed herself this morning, telling him to have a safe first flight.
‘I'm going to get scolded when I get home.’
No, the real question was whether he'd even make it back.
Barely holding onto his fading consciousness, he surveyed his surroundings.
The first officer had already lost consciousness, and five corpses lay piled around him.
The two of them had resisted the sudden intrusion as best they could, but they had simply been too badly outnumbered.
“How's the situation?”
“They're still in a standoff with the soldiers out in the corridor.”
“Tch.”
The conversation of the enemies occupying the cockpit buzzed in his ears.
Grab!
An intruder seized the captain by the hair and growled in a low voice.
“From now on, you follow my orders. Understood?”
“Ghk... I think I hear... a dog barking somewhere.”
Bam!
“Urgh!”
The intruder slammed the captain's face into the control panel before pulling a dagger from inside his clothes.
The blade's tip was pressed against the unconscious first officer's neck.
“Do I look like I'm joking? If you don't do as I say, I'll kill him.”
“...”
If they'd threatened him with his own life instead, he'd have at least spat in their faces.
The captain wore a conflicted expression before reluctantly clenching his teeth.
“Good. That's more like it.”
“...What exactly do you want?”
“I won't permit questions.”
Seeing the intruder's stubborn expression, the captain slowly turned his head.
Then his gaze stopped on the man's fingertips.
One of his fingers bore a black tattoo.
It was the mark of the Black Finger, the group that had recently become active throughout the Empire.
‘These bastards... don't tell me they're the demon race's...!’
It felt as though the blood in his entire body had turned cold.
If that was true, then the purpose of this terrorist attack definitely wasn't something as simple as money.
The man, watching the captain's tense expression, spoke.
“From this moment on, head for the capital at maximum speed.”
“...You mean the airport in the capital?”
“I'll tell you when we get closer.”
No doubt about it.
Their goal was most likely to use the airship itself to bombard the capital.
Without realizing it, the captain looked out the window, conflicted.
‘If I move the lever now, I can still crash us into the plains.’
Of course, a crash like that would leave no survivors.
Not himself, not these intruders, and not the passengers in the cabin.
Even so, the captain hesitated.
‘If this airship crashes into a building in the middle of the city…’
The number of casualties would obviously multiply several times over.
The intruder didn't wait for him to make up his mind.
Sliiick.
The tip of the blade lightly cut across his neck, and blood trickled down.
“Don't even think about taking everyone down with you. The moment I sense that's your plan, I'll kill you and fly this ship myself.”
“...”
Bluffing.
Piloting an airship was incredibly difficult.
Without specialized training, precise control was impossible.
Seeing all these levers and buttons, the man had surely realized that himself.
That was why he had kept the captain alive until now.
‘Support from the Imperial Palace or the White Tower…’
Looking over the map, the captain bit his lip.
After increasing speed to escape the Sky Ray, they had long since passed the area they were originally supposed to be flying over.
And judging by how communications had been dead for a while now, the terrorists apparently possessed something capable of interfering with mana.
‘In the worst-case scenario, the airport might not even know where we are.’
If that happened, expecting reinforcements would be even more hopeless.
Just as a burning thirst rose from his throat—
“Aaargh!”
A scream echoed from the corridor outside the cockpit, and one of the terrorists' companions came running in.
The man frowned.
“What happened?”
“Damn it! The soldiers wiped everyone out!”
“You idiots! How many times did I tell you all to just hold your positions?!”
“You make it sound easy! Every single one of them was Level 5!”
Hearing that, the man bit his lip and looked down at the floor.
“Throw the bodies outside and shut the cockpit door.”
Swish!
At the same time, the blade against the captain's throat pressed in harder.
“Don't think this is your chance to try anything stupid. It only takes one second for me to kill you.”
After throwing all the corpses into the corridor, the intruders shut the cockpit door.
A moment later, the soldiers began pounding on it.
Bang! Bang!
—Open the door and surrender! You're already surrounded!
“...”
As the terrorists began to waver, their leader glared at them.
“Do not falter. He is always watching over us. He will surely take pity on our noble sacrifice today and allow us to be reborn as the New Humanity.”
His bloodshot eyes had taken on an almost fanatical gleam.
Beep!
At that very moment, a single green dot appeared on the previously silent radar.
Everyone's eyes turned toward it, and the leader narrowed his gaze.
‘Reinforcements? No... impossible.’
Their mana interference device had been active since before they boarded.
That meant no one should have been able to determine the airship's exact location.
‘Did this bastard secretly do something?’
He stared at the back of the captain's head before shaking his own.
There was only one dot on the radar.
Which meant the Imperial Palace or the White Tower was likely just searching for the missing airship.
‘No need to stir up trouble.’
The leader gave an order.
“Increase altitude. Increase speed. Avoid crossing paths with that.”
“This is already the airship's maximum speed. If we climb any higher, we'll have stability problems...”
“Shut up and do it!”
As the blade dug into his neck, the captain squeezed his eyes shut.
The airship slowly climbed higher, its speed beginning to increase even further.
Beep-beep!
The radar sounded once more.
“What?”
The green dot that had appeared at an incredible distance was now much closer.
‘Is it malfunctioning? The airship is moving much faster than before.’
The leader frowned and stared at the radar.
Beep-beep!
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The position updated again.
“...What the...”
The words slipped from his mouth without thinking.
The green dot was chasing the airship from behind at an utterly impossible speed.
Something was wrong.
The thought flashed through his mind.
Thooom!
“...!”
Someone had landed heavily outside the cockpit.
A moment later, a pair of eyes could be seen through the window, calmly surveying the cockpit.
Eyes so cold they seemed incapable of compromise.
‘Oscar Crucian!’
The leader's eyes flew open as he recognized him.
Oscar was someone repeatedly mentioned while planning this operation.
—He can use spatial magic. He can exist anywhere and appear at any time. If he is discovered within your assigned operational area, there is only one rule you must follow.
There was even a special contingency prepared exclusively for him.
—If you encounter Oscar Crucian, detonate the mana bomb immediately, no matter the reason.
Remembering that order, the man instantly pressed the detonator in his hand.
No matter how incredible a Level 7 mage Oscar might be...
There was no way he could stop someone from pressing a detonator hidden in their hand the instant he appeared.
‘Our victory.’
Just as the leader's lips began to twist into a vicious grin—
Slash!
A single cutting sound swept through the cockpit.
“...”
By the time the captain, now drenched in blood, looked up in shock—
There was no one left.
* * *
“...”
The man checked the time.
By now, the capital should have been engulfed in flames, and urgent evacuation broadcasts should have already begun.
Yet his communication device remained silent.
‘It failed.’
Calmly taking a sip of tea, the man picked up the communicator.
It connected after only a few signals.
“How are the preparations?”
—We're standing by. Once the capital is consumed by flames, we'll immediately enter the Imperial Palace and—
“Clean it up.”
—...Pardon?
“Leave not a single human connected to this operation alive.”
A short while later.
The person on the other end acknowledged the order, and horrifying screams echoed through the communicator.
Click.
Setting it down, the man gazed up at the sky with an indifferent expression.
“...”
He had been certain the operation's chances of failure were low.
At most, he'd estimated them to be under two percent.
A plan to massacre the Empire's leadership.
Then exploit the ensuing chaos to infiltrate the Imperial Palace.
It had been clean, efficient, and free of unnecessary complications.
‘So the reason for the failure... was him after all.’
As the man thought of Oscar Crucian—
The sound of fireworks bursting outside filled the air.
“...”
White fireworks.
The color alone was enough to tell him who had won this year's Night of the Mages.
“The White Tower.”
He stared at the white fireworks as they dissolved into smoke.
Then, having reached a decision, he picked up the communicator once more.
Beep— Beep—
This time the ringing continued for much longer before the call connected.
—...
The person on the other end remained silent.
The man spoke first.
“That proposal from before. Is it still valid?”
A moment later, a chilling voice like grinding metal came through the communicator.
—Heh heh... So you've finally made your decision.
“I'll cooperate. But this absolutely cannot fail.”
—You needn't worry about that.
Beep— Beep—
The other side terminated the call without another word.
Ordinarily, such a thing would have been unthinkable.
But the man simply lowered the communicator as though it meant nothing and closed his eyes.
“...”
Now...
There was no turning back.
* * *
“...”
Standing by the airport director's office window, Oscar looked down at the crowd streaming outside.
Every one of them had been passengers aboard the airship only moments ago.
Not a trace of worry remained on their faces.
Instead, they were filled with excitement over what they believed had simply been a new experience.
“They have no idea, do they? That they all came within a hair's breadth of dying.”
“I'm just glad everything worked out.”
For the first time in quite a while, Oscar felt his eyelids growing heavy.
The moment he arrived, he had activated 『Majiro Time』.
Then, after assessing the situation, he had used it four consecutive times to eliminate every enemy.
‘It's definitely an amazing spell... but the mental strain is just too much.’
It would have been far better if it consumed mana instead.
His mind felt completely blank, as though it refused to think any longer.
“Phew... We owe this entirely to you.”
“I only did what needed to be done.”
“...Right. And from here on, it's my turn to do what needs to be done.”
Fidelina's eyes sharpened.
There were obvious aspects of this terrorist attack that simply didn't make sense.
“I'm launching an investigation.”
“You should.”
“More than anything else, the information about the disguised passengers planted by the Imperial Palace... even on our side, only a handful of people knew about it. I didn't know either.”
The White Tower Master Sasha, who oversaw the airship business.
Herself.
And the directors of each airport.
There truly had been only a few people.
“So that means...”
“Let's stop there for now. There are ears listening.”
Oscar glanced behind him.
The airport director stood there with both hands politely clasped together, looking completely at a loss.
“Right. In any case, I'll request the Imperial Palace's cooperation in the investigation as well.”
By the Imperial Palace, Fidelina naturally meant exactly that.
It was now all but certain that information had been leaked from within the Imperial Palace.
“...Be careful. The fish might be bigger than you think.”
The information in question was classified at a level that was difficult to access even within the Imperial Palace.
Which meant anyone capable of viewing it was likely someone of considerable rank.
Understanding what he meant, Fidelina nodded.
“I will. And thank you again. Thanks to you, we were given the chance to contain this incident.”
“Once again, I only did what needed to be done.”
Answering lightly, Oscar turned to the airport director.
“By any chance, is there somewhere like a bedroom? I'm so exhausted that I'd like to get a little sleep.”
“...You're going to take a nap?”
Fidelina stared at him in surprise, as though it was the first time she'd ever seen such a thing.
But after using 『Majiro Time』, his brain was refusing to function.
Right now, all he wanted was to lie down on a bed.
“Ah, as it happens, we have a capsule hotel inside the airport for VIP guests. I'll show you the way.”

Chapter 405: The Hunt Begins (1)
It had been a long time since Oscar had slept so soundly.
Even then, it had only been about three hours, but even that was enough for him to feel that his condition had improved.
"...Mm."
Of course, his thoughts still felt sluggish.
That part would need more time before it fully recovered.
As soon as Oscar stepped out of the capsule, the airport director, who had been waiting outside, greeted him with a respectful bow.
A surprised Oscar asked,
"Don't tell me you've been waiting here this whole time?"
"No. It was about time for you to wake up, so I came to escort you."
Relieved, Oscar lightly tapped the capsule.
"This is more comfortable than I expected. Crawling into it made me feel like I'd turned into an ant."
"We devoted every effort to reducing our customers' fatigue. We entrusted the design to an architect renowned for making efficient use of space and compression techniques."
"If that was the goal, I'd say you succeeded."
Of course, he doubted many nobles would use it.
People who cared about appearances would probably think sleeping in a place like this was beneath their dignity.
When they stepped outside with the airport director, the runway beyond the glass was visible beneath the evening sky.
"It's quiet."
"It won't stay that way for long. Not once today's inauguration ceremony is over."
"I'd like to hear what happened after I fell asleep."
"Fortunately, none of the passengers realized a hijacking had taken place."
That figured.
No matter how violently the airship had shaken, no one would have found it strange.
After all, today had been everyone's first flight.
"How exactly did the intrusion happen?"
"It seems several people boarded disguised as passengers without carrying any weapons, then pulled the emergency barrier release lever. After that, the enemies pursuing us while riding sky rays infiltrated from outside."
A coordinated operation from both inside and outside.
Oscar let out a hollow laugh.
"We were too optimistic. Honestly, I thought there was no way anyone could break through. Never imagined it'd happen on the very first day."
"My apologies."
"You've come up with countermeasures, I assume?"
"Yes. First, we've decided to modify the emergency lever so it only operates after authentication through two magic devices. The captain and first officer will each carry one."
"Not bad."
"In addition, the cockpit door will be changed to a double-lock structure to make outside intrusion much more difficult."
Meaning that even if terrorists struck again in the worst-case scenario, seizing the cockpit would be nearly impossible.
That would allow the soldiers to focus entirely on protecting the passengers.
"What about the communication problem?"
"The enemy blocked the flow of mana, which caused it. We're currently searching for a solution."
Well, no matter how advanced magic and magitech became, they were useless if mana itself was blocked.
It had been a problem ever since wars in the distant past, and if no one had solved it yet, that said enough.
Still, coming up with this many countermeasures in only a few hours meant they were fairly capable.
"How are the auction preparations?"
"The seating and stage on the deck have been fully set up, and since everything was handled in secret, there were no thefts of the items."
"Good."
"All of the VIPs have already boarded the airship."
"They've taken time out of their busy schedules. We can't afford to waste it. Let's get moving."
* * *
In the end, the Sky Auction was an overwhelming success.
Honestly, it had been practically impossible for the concept to fail from the very beginning.
Watching the excited VIPs disembark from the airship with flushed faces, Oscar thought,
‘Once they start bragging to everyone in high society who couldn't make it today…’
The next auction might require connecting several airships together.
Or perhaps they would need to build a special airship solely for the auction.
Oscar leaned against the deck for a while.
Then the atmosphere around him changed.
The surroundings, already quiet, somehow became even quieter.
"So, did it meet your expectations?"
"It was quite an interesting idea."
Smiling at the praise, Oscar turned around.
It was the VIP of all VIPs who had personally come to grace the occasion—the Emperor himself.
Oscar respectfully bowed, but the Emperor merely snorted.
"Act as you usually do."
"Aw, don't say that. When have I ever not treated you respectfully?"
"I remember someone lecturing me because I drank the last glass without consulting him first."
"W-Well, back then... I was drunk..."
Oscar gave a light cough before asking,
"What do you think?"
"..."
After a brief silence, the Emperor let out a heavy sigh.
"The Imperial Family has already weathered one great ordeal."
He was probably referring to the massive purge of traitors within the Imperial Family.
The Emperor wore a somewhat weary expression.
"Even the worm that had nested inside my head... I lived believing one of them had planted it there. Or perhaps... I merely wanted to believe that."
"..."
But this incident as well—the crucial information had leaked from within the Imperial Family.
The Imperial soldier disguised as a passenger, the airship's route, even the existence of the emergency lever.
Though he gazed across the open runway, it felt as though his chest was tightly constricted.
"The only ones who possessed that information were the heads of the departments connected to the airship project and the direct members of the Imperial Family. Altogether, there are fewer than twenty people."
"..."
Oscar swallowed hard.
Only twenty.
And judging from the Emperor's reaction, he apparently hadn't suspected any of them.
"The heads of those departments have been with me for many years. Though we share no blood, I have always believed them to be trustworthy."
Men like old Andre, no doubt.
By the time he finished hearing that much, Oscar had figured out whom the Emperor suspected.
‘...His bloodline.’
His own children.
Looking at it now, it was only natural.
‘I'd assumed someone planted the worm simply because the Empire would descend into chaos if Uncle Emperor died of illness…’
If the Emperor disappeared, the greatest beneficiaries would undoubtedly be those next in line for succession.
The problem was that there were quite a few of them.
"This is giving me a headache."
"That's exactly how I feel. Dizzy. I always knew this was a lonely seat. That's why I prided myself on never growing too attached to anyone... Yet to think the day would come when I couldn't even trust my own children."
Oscar gently patted the shoulder of the bitterly smiling Emperor.
The Emperor slowly turned his head and stared at Oscar's hand.
Then his eyes silently asked what exactly he thought he was doing.
"Comforting you. In my own way."
Oscar shrugged.
The Emperor let out a small chuckle.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
"That's enough. History has taught me countless times that a day like this might eventually come."
The Emperor had become a man of iron to prevent exactly this.
He had consolidated all authority into his own hands and had declared the Crown Prince long ago.
And yet this still happened...
‘Most likely the work of someone who fell behind in the succession struggle.’
The problem was figuring out who.
Among twenty people, every one of them would hold considerable influence within the Imperial Family.
It wasn't as though they could simply abduct and torture them.
"How do you intend to root them out?"
"For the time being, I won't lay a finger on them."
Oscar frowned at the Emperor's calm reply.
"Of course, cornering a rat too much may cause it to bite the cat. But if you do nothing at all, they'll stay hidden for a thousand years, or even ten thousand."
"That would be true if we had no leads."
"You mean..."
"Recently, the Shadow Trackers landed a big catch."
"A big catch?"
"They discovered what is believed to be the Black Finger's headquarters."
"...!"
Oscar's eyes widened.
If that was true, there was no need to pressure the traitor inside the Imperial Family.
‘As long as we wipe out their main base and deliberately let a few rumors leak…’
The anxious traitor would crawl out of hiding on their own.
"So there'll be a large-scale purge."
"That's right. And I'd like your help with it."
"My help? Why... Ah!"
Everything suddenly clicked together inside Oscar's head, and he could see the bigger picture the Emperor had drawn.
"You're not planning to let the enemy know we're searching on our own, are you? Instead, you'll make it seem as though you're focusing on catching the traitor inside the Imperial Family."
"Just as sharp as ever. Correct. Outwardly, it'll appear that we're tightening security within the Imperial Palace. The enemy will keep their heads down and watch our movements."
"The Imperial Family's elites won't be leaving the palace, so they'll assume their headquarters is safe... and that's when I strike."
"For the same reason, the whereabouts of those representing each Magic Tower must be obvious. That's why I need capable individuals who can operate beneath the surface. Can the White Tower's Special Operations Department handle it?"
Including himself, the White Tower's Special Operations Department only had four members.
But those troublemakers had all reached at least Level 6 now.
‘Especially Fran. Levels hardly mean anything in his case.’
If he made proper use of the Colorless Spirit, he could put up a good fight even against most late Level 7 opponents.
Oscar asked,
"How strong are the forces at the location believed to be their headquarters?"
"According to the report, two of the Fingers are currently staying there."
"...!"
They had crossed paths with the Black Finger countless times before, yet never once encountered a Finger directly.
Which meant the place they had found this time was highly likely to be the organization's true headquarters.
"I realize this may be unnecessary to ask, but this information..."
"It came directly to me. Furthermore, the people who identified the location are currently waiting at one of my secret safe houses. They cannot contact anyone without my permission."
"Waiting" was little different from being detained.
In other words, security was being kept airtight to ensure this information leaked nowhere.
Oscar's mind spun rapidly.
‘In this situation... we can definitely catch them.’
The traitor inside the Imperial Family wouldn't know they possessed this trump card.
Which meant, to avoid drawing suspicion during the upcoming investigation, they would most likely cut off all contact with the headquarters themselves.
That was an enormous advantage.
It meant the traitor wouldn't even think of cutting their own tail.
"The question is whether the White Tower's Special Operations Department alone can accomplish this."
"We can."
Oscar answered confidently.
Not only were the troublemakers—excluding himself—already remarkably capable, they also possessed a hidden trump card.
"I'll be taking the Mad Fiend. Gilliot."
The Emperor's eyes narrowed.
"...Hasn't he still not fully recovered his memories?"
"That's true. But even so, he has no trouble distinguishing friend from foe."
Someone who had reached the late stages of Level 7 would undoubtedly be a tremendous asset.
More importantly, he was a perfect joker card whose very existence was known to only a handful of people, even within the White Tower.
"The other elders of the White Tower—especially the Tower Master, Sasha, and Lloyd—must have clearly established whereabouts. Judging from this latest terrorist attack, the enemy is already wary of your spatial movement magic."
"I know."
Lloyd was currently staying in the Kingdom of Yan.
He had originally gone there to search for Gilliot, but the last letter Oscar had received said he had discovered something new to learn.
As for Sasha, who would have returned after the Mage's Night, they would also need to establish a clear explanation for her whereabouts.
For the first time in a long while, Oscar felt his heart burning with excitement.
"Leave it to me. This time, we'll wipe out every last one of those bastards connected to the demon race."
The moment the secret meeting with Uncle Emperor ended, Oscar returned to the White Tower.
And when he stepped into his room—
"..."
The Mad Fiend, having returned from Magiro's dungeon, was sitting in a chair.
With an aura entirely unlike his usual self.

Chapter 406: The Hunt Begins (2)
“……”
The Mad Fiend was sitting in a chair.
That alone was already an incredibly unfamiliar sight.
Normally, he preferred squatting in the corner of the room.
Whenever he got bored there, he'd gnaw away at the curtains, and they'd already gone through five sets because of him.
“Ahem, ahem.”
Oscar deliberately cleared his throat to make his presence known before taking the chair opposite him.
“Would you prefer I call you Gilliot or Mad Fiend?”
“……”
The one who had been staring only at the desk with lowered eyes slowly lifted his head.
Once their gazes met, he hesitated awkwardly for a long while before finally opening his mouth.
“……Grrr.”
What came out was the Mad Fiend's characteristic beast-like growl.
'So he still hasn't regained the memories from when he was human.'
If only he could contact Majiro, he could have asked what kind of dungeon he'd used and what condition Gilliot was in now.
As things stood, the only option was to observe the Mad Fiend himself and figure it out.
“Awoo!”
Spreading both arms wide, he enthusiastically tried to express something through gestures.
Oscar, already thoroughly accustomed to living with the Mad Fiend, spoke up.
“You're hungry?”
“Awooo!”
“...Right. Let's eat first.”
After quickly making some fried rice and grilling a steak, he set the meal in front of him.
The Mad Fiend's eyes immediately sparkled.
“You've waited a long time, haven't you? Go on, eat before it gets cold.”
“……”
Normally, he would've grabbed the food with his hands before the plate had even touched the table.
But today, he remained unusually well-behaved.
Not only that, he raised his head and stared intently at Oscar.
As if asking, 'Are you serious right now?'
“What? You don't like the menu? It's steak and fried rice—your favorites.”
Shake, shake!
The Mad Fiend vigorously shook his head.
“Arrr! Grr!”
Then he rapidly drummed both fists against the table, urging him to hand over something.
“What... what am I supposed to—... Wait, don't tell me?”
Something suddenly occurred to Oscar.
Just in case, he took out a spoon, fork, and knife and handed them over.
Only then did the Mad Fiend let out a long, satisfied howl.
Then he looked at Oscar with the face of a puppy desperately needing to poop.
“Uh... eat?”
The moment those tentative words left Oscar's mouth, the Mad Fiend immediately began eating as though he'd been waiting for permission.
He scooped up the fried rice with a spoon, and though clumsily, he cut the steak with a knife before picking it up with a fork.
Watching him, Oscar stroked his chin.
'I don't think he's recovered the memories from when he was human...'
But he was vaguely reproducing the behaviors from back then.
Wasn't this what they called procedural memory?
The sort of habits the body remembered on its own.
'I think I have a rough idea what kind of dungeon Majiro gave him.'
It was probably a dungeon where Gilli repeatedly relearned the things he'd learned as a child.
Even Majiro must have judged that completely restoring memories from that period was impossible.
'Since he couldn't restore the memories, he must've decided to engrain the behaviors from back then into his body first.'
A very Majiro-like method.
Clatter. Clatter.
The Mad Fiend's meal was as clumsy as could be.
He dropped his spoon several times, and over half the fried rice he scooped up ended up falling onto the floor.
Even so, he never let go of the utensils until the very end.
“……”
Oscar silently watched the entire scene.
A little while later, after finishing his meal, Gilliot stared blankly at the empty dishes before picking them up and standing.
He then walked into the kitchen and began fiddling with the faucet.
'Don't tell me...'
Whoosh!
The moment water began flowing from the tap, he awkwardly started washing the dishes.
Crack!
Then, after failing to control his strength, he snapped a plate cleanly in half.
With a dejected expression, he looked toward Oscar.
His eyes were filled with fear, as though he thought he was about to be scolded.
They were exactly the same eyes Gilli had looked at him with long ago after breaking a plate.
“...It's okay.”
Just as he had back then, Oscar answered gently and reached out his hand.
The Mad Fiend flinched instinctively.
Then, feeling the gentle touch resting on his head, he slowly looked up.
“You didn't hurt your hand, did you?”
His hand itself was clearly cold.
Yet somehow, it felt strangely warm.
“Grrr……”
Apparently it felt rather nice, because he showed no intention of pulling away.
So Oscar spent quite a while stroking his head afterward.
Having finished a satisfying meal, the Mad Fiend simply lay down on the bed and fell asleep.
“Heh.”
Look at him, sleeping without a care in the world.
Oscar watched the peacefully sleeping figure for quite some time before a faint smile spread across his face.
'Thank you, Majiro.'
There was still a long way to go.
But one thing was certain.
The Mad Fiend had definitely begun to change.
* * *
“I'm telling you, the judging criteria are ridiculous. How are you the MVP?”
“Because I performed better. There was nothing wrong with the judging.”
“Don't make me laugh! I refuse to accept it!”
“...Would you three stop fighting over something so stupid? What are you, elementary school kids?”
As always, the door to the Special Operations Department office opened amid a noisy argument.
Oscar gave them a casual wave.
“Welcome. You all seem energetic today too.”
“Oscar!”
“Huh? What's the occasion?”
Behind the delighted Killian and Veronica, another head popped into view.
“Oh, it really is Oscar?”
“You all saw me not that long ago. Anyway, have a seat.”
The three, still looking fascinated, sat down in their respective seats.
“That's only natural. It's been months since we've seen you in the Special Operations office.”
“Yeah, you kept abandoning us and running around by yourself.”
“Carrying out missions with just the three of us was pretty rough.”
“...Was it?”
Now that he thought about it, he did feel a little guilty.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The last time he'd officially participated in Special Operations activities had been when he'd gone to the Black Tower.
“Sorry. It's not like I was off having fun by myself. I've just been busy.”
“We know. Otherwise, reaching Level 7 would've been nothing more than a dream.”
“So you're done being busy now?”
“More or less.”
Of course, if any news related to souls came in, he'd still have to move alone immediately.
That involved the Great Emperor, making it an extremely dangerous matter.
If possible, he'd rather handle it without involving anyone else.
“First of all, congratulations on winning Mage's Night.”
Oscar lightly waved the newspaper article he'd been reading.
This year, they'd won by an overwhelming point margin compared to last year.
And the three sitting before him had been the key contributors.
'They've finally started pulling their weight.'
For a moment, he felt oddly sentimental.
How much effort had he poured into turning these screw-loose idiots into proper people?
Of course, the fact that the three of them had worked so hard themselves was equally important.
No matter how excellent the teacher, this level of growth in just one year was simply absurd.
“It would've been stranger if we hadn't won. The Yellow Tower and the Red Tower both fielded rather weak lineups.”
“True.”
With the Yellow Tower having changed Tower Masters, and the Red Tower suffering internal turmoil, it couldn't really be helped.
After all, the Level 8 mage who had represented the Red Tower had transferred to a rival Magic Tower.
'No matter how secure Kudel Redmane's position may be, there's no way people weren't talking.'
In a way, having someone you could completely purge like the Yellow Tower was actually easier.
There was nothing you could do about whispers spreading quietly behind the scenes.
Especially since Kudel had entered closed-door training, he couldn't devote much attention to outside affairs.
“Well, regardless, you all did well.”
“I won't become arrogant. If you'd been there, the MVP would've been yours anyway.”
“That's the right attitude. Keep working hard.”
Bringing that topic to a close, Oscar lightly tapped the desk with his finger.
“That's enough catching up... We have work to do.”
“Hm? Don't tell me it's a group operation?”
“...Something large enough that all of us have to participate?”
Their reactions were understandable.
The Special Operations Department's strength was completely different from just a few months ago.
One Level 7.
Three Level 6s.
Frankly, that lineup was excessive for most group operations.
Oscar nodded at their puzzled expressions.
“This is a mission personally assigned by His Majesty the Emperor.”
“……!”
Their expressions instantly hardened.
Ignoring that, Oscar continued the briefing.
“Our target is to raid the area believed to be the Black Finger's main headquarters.”
“The headquarters... That won't be an easy mission.”
“Don't tell me it's just the four of us?”
The earlier confidence about whether all of them needed to participate vanished without a trace.
Even the hideout of an ordinary mafia group with some influence would have Level 6-class powerhouses lurking within.
If it was the Black Finger's headquarters, there was no way it would be any weaker.
“Two Level 7s and one Level 6 will be joining us. That makes seven people in total.”
These were the White Tower's forces that had never been revealed to the outside world.
The Mad Fiend.
Edna.
And even her dragon nephew, Seiro.
To be honest, there were others he could call.
The Violet Brigade, for one.
Or the Tesila Adventurer Party.
If he asked for help, they'd come.
'But secrecy is the lifeblood of this operation.'
It wasn't that he didn't trust them.
He simply couldn't trust every single member of those groups, so he'd eliminated them as options.
“Hah... Just seven people...?”
“How strong do you estimate the enemy's forces to be?”
“For now, we believe two Fingers are stationed there. And naturally, they'll have plenty of subordinates as well.”
Assuming the Fingers were both Level 7-class, the roles of himself and the Mad Fiend would become crucial.
Of course, he had no intention of believing their Level 7 fighters were inferior to the enemy's.
'Even in the worst-case scenario, I'm here.'
With his current mana reserves, fighting two Level 7 opponents wasn't impossible.
There might be enemies whose abilities made defeating them impossible.
But losing?
That was another matter.
More importantly, Edna and Seiro were dragons.
Once they transformed into their true forms, a few breaths alone would wipe out most enemies.
In other words, while they numbered only seven people, their firepower exceeded that of most military units.
“Our objective is to eliminate every enemy inside the headquarters. And if possible, capture the two Fingers alive so we can extract information.”
“Capture them alive... That won't be easy.”
“Don't worry. You won't be fighting them anyway.”
The three exchanged slightly complicated expressions.
Their pride was hurt.
But they also knew that openly showing it would only be childish.
Sensing this, Oscar spoke.
“If you're dissatisfied, become stronger. Once you reach that point, you can say whatever you like, and I'll listen.”
“...We're already among the best of our generation.”
It was Killian who answered Fran's mutter.
“It can't be helped. At our level, we're past the stage where people evaluate us based on our age.”
“It stings, but he's right. The enemy won't go easy on us just because we're young.”
All three were only a single step away from becoming Masters.
The days when they could be treated with leniency simply because they were newcomers were over.
Satisfied with their attitude, Oscar nodded.
“Their headquarters is an old temple in the southern region that was used as a fortress during the war. The Imperial Army withdrew from the area fifteen years ago. After taking it over, they even remodeled the underground levels for their own use.”
Oscar slid a photograph across the table.
It showed an ancient temple covered in moss, hidden deep within the dense southern jungle.
“Naturally, they've concealed the entire area with illusion magic during normal times. Even the people living in the nearby forests have no idea they exist.”
Tap. Tap.
Tapping the photograph with his finger, Oscar spoke.
“We depart three days from now at 05:00. Have every preparation completed before then.”
