Chapter 407: The Hunt Begins (3)
Three days later, Special Operations Department.
For some reason, a strange sense of tension filled the room today.
“......”
“......”
It was only natural.
Into the usually carefree room that felt more like a clubroom than an office, three outsiders had entered.
Although they all lived in the same Magic Tower, neither the Mad Fiend nor Seiro was someone whose existence could be publicly revealed.
Since they couldn't exactly walk around openly, it was only natural that no one had ever run into them.
'The only one they might recognize is probably Edna, since she works as a librarian...'
These brats must never even set foot in the library.
They're staring at them like they've never seen them before in their lives.
Even the outgoing Fran seemed to find it difficult to approach them.
Covering his mouth with one hand, he cautiously asked,
“Oscar, who are these people?”
“The one on the far left is Edna Sol Laplace. She's the last dragon I brought back from beyond the Crimson Mountain Range. She had been safeguarding the White Tower's records entrusted to her by the previous Tower Master.”
The problem children's stunned expressions at the very first introduction were quite a sight to behold.
“A-a dragon? Didn't they all leave this world right before the war against the demons?”
“But I remember hearing about it. The dragon who was a close friend of the previous White Tower Master stayed behind and fought until the very end.”
“...How fascinating.”
They stared at Edna as though they were looking upon a hero from an ancient legend.
Completely unfazed by the barrage of gazes, Edna greeted them lightly.
“I'm Edna Sol Laplace. I look forward to working with you.”
Oscar immediately continued with the next introduction.
“And this person is...”
Although he was publicly known as the Mad Fiend of the Violet Brigade, in reality he was Gilliot Dominic, the current Tower Master's senior brother.
...Naturally, he couldn't introduce him like that.
Because of that, the introduction ended up rather brief.
“The Mad Fiend of the Violet Brigade. For certain reasons, he's helping us.”
“No, wait. Why would someone from the Violet Brigade...?”
Ignoring Fran's question, Oscar turned toward Seiro.
“And lastly...”
Hmm.
Unexpectedly, this guy was the hardest one to introduce.
As Fran had just said, the world believed that dragons had abandoned this star and left.
But in reality, that was a misunderstanding, and their role had actually been this and that...
Explaining that whole complicated story from beginning to end would take far too long and be unnecessarily academic.
'More importantly, it's a pain.'
Having made up his mind, Oscar gave a very rough introduction.
“This is Seiro. He's a mage with a unique ability that lets him transform into an enormous lizard.”
“...Huh?”
Quietly listening until then, Seiro stared blankly.
To him, being a dragon was a source of immense pride.
“T-to introduce me like that?! I can't believe it!”
His cheeks trembled in shock, and Edna quickly educated him.
“Seiro. We don't have much time, and it's troublesome. Let's just go with that.”
“B-but!”
Unable to stand against Edna's firm attitude, he fidgeted awkwardly before hanging his head.
Just then, Killian strode directly toward the Mad Fiend.
With the two men of similar height facing one another, an odd sense of pressure filled the room.
Killian swiftly looked the masked Mad Fiend up and down.
'The body of a well-trained warrior.'
Suppressing the urge to challenge him to a fight someday, he asked,
“If you're with the Violet Brigade, have you ever met Kaya Lockwood?”
“...Grrrr.”
Startled by the Mad Fiend's low growl, Killian immediately responded,
“Grrr.”
“Grrr.”
“O-Oscar... should we assume they're actually communicating?”
At Fran's voice, as though he had just witnessed the language of some primitive tribe, Oscar shrugged.
“Who knows? I suppose they probably are.”
Watching them exchange growls, it really did seem like a genuine conversation.
Bang! Bang!
Oscar slammed the desk loudly, drawing everyone's attention.
“All right, eyes up. Time for today's operation briefing.”
As he flicked a finger—
Fwaaash!
A map spread out before them.
“Our destination is here. A place called Caligo, located deep within the southern jungle.”
“Hm? That's the Black Finger's headquarters?”
“For a headquarters... it isn't actually all that difficult to find, is it?”
As Fran said, it wasn't located in the deepest part of the jungle.
If anything, it lay somewhere between the outskirts and the center.
“They still need a steady supply of basic provisions, so they probably didn't want to settle too deep inside. Besides, they can simply conceal it with illusion magic.”
“I see. Makes sense.”
“How many enemies are there?”
At Killian's question, Oscar waved the documents he had received from the Emperor.
“According to the Dark Tracker's report from a few days ago, there are estimated to be at least several hundred members active.”
“At least several hundred... That's more than I expected. What's their level?”
“Fortunately, nothing we need to worry about. They range from complete civilians to Level 6. The gap is pretty wide.”
He looked at Edna and Seiro.
“You two handle the small fry outside the temple. If anything happens, notify us immediately through message magic. We'll head straight into the temple.”
“Understood.”
Edna answered confidently.
If it had only been Seiro, that might have been another matter, but with her beside him, there was no need to worry about the outside.
“Oscar, you said two of the Fingers are there. Have you figured out who they are?”
“For now, we've confirmed that the 'Hound' is there. Then, a few days ago, another Finger joined him, making it two at present.”
“The Hound?”
Since everyone looked unfamiliar with the name, Oscar gave a brief explanation.
“The executives leading the Black Finger are known as the Five Fingers. Of those five, the Dark Trackers have only identified the abilities of four. The Hound, whose current location has been confirmed, possesses a unique ability that allows movement and assassination through shadows.”
“What the hell? That's completely broken.”
“In practice, he's already used that ability to kill more than ten members of the Dark Trackers.”
The report clearly stated:
Never engage him in a dark location under any circumstances.
Oscar continued reading.
“Next is the Alchemist. He's the chief researcher in charge of the magic ore they call the Philosopher's Stone. Nothing is known about his abilities.”
“If he's a researcher, there's a chance his combat ability is low.”
“Right. That's also the Dark Trackers' assessment.”
If the two Fingers stationed at the headquarters turned out to be these two, that would be the best-case scenario.
They would be far too easy for the group to deal with.
“Moving on. The Dark Trackers only obtained information on the next Finger through examining corpses, so not much is known. Since he uses a massive axe as his weapon, they call him the Lumberjack.”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“Is he strong?”
“Judging from the traces of battle, he's most likely a warrior-type who fights using strength and speed.”
“How interesting.”
At the mention of a warrior, Killian's interest visibly grew.
“As it happens, if the Lumberjack is there, I was planning to leave him to you and the Mad Fiend. The next opponent isn't a good match for either of you.”
“Who is it?”
“The fourth Finger is known as the Cult Leader. He's the one leading the Salvation Church.”
“The Salvation Church... weren't those the people we encountered?”
“That's right. They're the ones who deceived orphans and the homeless in Saint Hill and turned them into test subjects.”
The report described the Cult Leader as follows.
“Although nothing concrete is known about the Cult Leader's combat abilities, judging by the Salvation Church's abnormal devotion and obsession toward him, it's believed he possesses a unique ability resembling hypnosis or brainwashing.”
“A mental-type ability...”
“Yeah, that's definitely a pain.”
Just hearing the explanation was enough to make everyone frown.
Anyone who had ever fought an enemy with mental abilities knew just how troublesome they were.
“If someone with low magic resistance like Killian or the Mad Fiend faces him, it could be dangerous. If things go wrong, trusted allies could end up becoming enemies.”
To prevent such a worst-case scenario, Oscar intended to keep the two of them as far away from the Cult Leader as possible.
Turning his head, he said,
“Fran, Veronica. If the Cult Leader is there, I don't care about the situation—rush straight toward him and kill him first. If he starts taking control of the battlefield, things will become a nightmare.”
“Leave it to us.”
“Cult Leader. Got it.”
That concluded all the information on the four known Fingers.
As for the First Finger—their leader—
No information existed yet.
'Or perhaps... there might finally be one now.'
If the traitor within the Imperial Palace truly was the First Finger, then they would be catching him soon enough.
“Capture the Fingers as quickly as possible and extract information about whoever is backing them. Any questions?”
Oscar looked at everyone one by one as he asked, but no one raised a hand.
“Good.”
Nodding, he snapped his fingers.
A portal opened.
“No point dragging this out. Zero five thirty-four. Operation begins.”
* * *
Before a desk inside a room illuminated by flickering torches stood a middle-aged man wearing gray robes.
Looking over the papers scattered chaotically across the desk, he muttered,
“I'm really almost there... Am I missing only the final piece...?”
A trace of regret crossed his face before he suddenly spoke.
“What is it?”
“—Ho.”
A voice echoed as though speaking from inside a cave.
Fwaaash!
A slender figure rose from the room's shadows.
“Sharp senses. I thought you were just some bookworm who stayed holed up in a room doing research.”
“...What do you want, Hound?”
“You seem a lot smarter than I am, so I figured I'd ask.”
Meaninglessly tapping one of the flasks rolling around on the desk, the Hound asked,
“About this summons. No matter how I think about it, I can't figure out the reason. Got any ideas?”
“Hmm.”
At those words, the Alchemist straightened his back and looked at the Hound.
Indeed, even he had never expected this summons.
Since the organization's founding, this was the first time all of the Fingers had been called together.
“The First Finger will tell us once everyone has gathered. He's the one who summoned us.”
“That's what I'm curious about too. While we're out working, we occasionally hear bits and pieces about the other Fingers. But somehow, we never hear a single thing about the First Finger.”
“......”
After thinking for a moment, the Alchemist replied,
“Who knows? Perhaps, as the organization's underlings speculate, he's a high-ranking noble... or even a member of the imperial family. Otherwise, this level of information network simply doesn't make sense.”
“If that's true... then he must be old. Old men with one foot in the grave always crave immortality.”
“I don't know. Is that all you came to say?”
The Alchemist stared at him flatly, clearly annoyed at having his research interrupted.
The Hound let out a snort.
“Hmph. How boring. I heard the others will all arrive before the day is over. It'll be the first time we'll actually meet face to face.”
“If you're finished, leave.”
“......”
Just as the Hound was about to quietly melt back into the shadows, he stopped.
“By the way, I really don't like that commanding tone of yours. Looking to die?”
“I'm already short on time just trying to finish my research. Please get out.”
The moment the Hound stared intently at the Alchemist, wondering where all that confidence came from—
RUMBLE!
A powerful tremor shook the entire temple, and dust rained down from the underground chamber's ceiling where they stood.
“Hm.”
“......”
The hostility between them faded, and both men looked up at the ceiling simultaneously.
“Seems... some little rats have arrived.”

Chapter 408: The Hunt Begins (4)
Slash!
With a clean slicing sound, the tough vines were severed.
Rustling through the opening they made, Oscar emerged.
"Oscar, aren't we looking in the wrong place?"
Fran, who had been following close behind, asked with an expression that looked ready to melt at any moment.
Outside, spring had fully arrived, but the jungle was sweltering with humidity trapped beneath the dense canopy.
"No. This is the right place."
"But... there's really nothing around here."
In truth, the area was filled with nothing but trees, rocks, and vines.
No matter how hard one searched, it was terrain where a gigantic temple simply couldn't exist.
'The only ones who noticed... are probably Edna and Seiro.'
As expected of dragons, their talent for sensing mana was on a completely different level.
The two of them were staring at the exact same spot.
Meanwhile, the troublemakers merely stood there blankly.
"Everyone, close your eyes and focus all your senses. What do you feel?"
"It's hot."
"I don't know about anything else, but the humidity feels awful."
"The forest feels nice. It reminds me of home."
Listening to their various answers, Oscar walked past them as they kept their eyes closed.
"Open your eyes. Deep in a forest, the wind rarely blows. Especially in a tropical rainforest like this, where the humidity is high and the air is heavy."
"...Then what exactly were we supposed to sense?"
"The flow of mana. Though it's probably still difficult for you."
Ordinary mana currents could all be seen by reinforcing one's eyes with mana.
But the minute traces of mana deliberately concealed by someone could not be perceived that way.
Only those with innate talent like his, or high-ranking mages, would have developed that sort of perception.
"When a mage finds themselves in that situation, what they rely on is the attribute they specialize in. For example, mages of the Blue Tower can even read the surrounding mana flow through a stream."
That was why the White Tower, which wielded wind, naturally excelled at this ability more than any other Magic Tower.
Because the wind blew everywhere.
"Doesn't that mean it's useless in a place like this where there's no wind?"
At Fran's question, Oscar nodded.
"That's right. It's difficult in a deep forest like this. But if there isn't any wind, are you just going to accept it and move on?"
His gaze shifted toward Killian.
"Killian. Since you know forests well, you should know. If you wanted to find the wind in a place like this, what would you do?"
"You'd climb somewhere high."
Killian looked up at the pointed tops of the towering trees as he answered.
"Correct. Countless branches and leaves have become a wall, blocking the wind from outside. But beyond them, the wind is still blowing."
Looking pleased, Oscar tilted his head.
"What are you waiting for? Go."
At his words, the three of them quickly climbed to the tops of the trees.
The wind that struck their faces felt cooler than ever before.
"Wow... that's refreshing."
"Now I finally feel like I can breathe."
After cooling themselves down, the three began sensing the mana carried by the wind.
The moment they felt its flow, all three were startled almost simultaneously.
"In front..."
"...there's no wind."
"How is that even possible?"
They hurried back down.
As if he had been expecting that reaction, Oscar nodded.
"What's spread out ahead is a formation."
"A formation? Is it something like illusion magic?"
"No. Illusion magic deceives what you see. This manipulates the area itself."
"Huh? I think I've heard of it before. But aren't formations a technique from Yan?"
Fran spoke uncertainly.
"That's right. It's a technique from Yan. Looks like one of the Black Fingers is thoroughly versed in Yan’s knowledge."
"Hm. So in short, it's dangerous?"
"Very. If you recklessly step into an unfamiliar formation, you could wander the same place for ages until you die."
At that warning, everyone swallowed nervously.
Naturally, hardly anyone in the group knew anything about formations.
"Th-Then should we retreat for now and bring in a formation expert from Yan?"
"...Fran. Do you really want to let an opportunity this precious slip away?"
"But we don't have a choice! Do you know how to break that formation?"
"Hm."
Oscar reinforced his eyes with mana and stared ahead.
He could tell there was a formation there.
But formations, just as Fran had said, required the exact method to break them.
If one misplaced even a single step, they would become trapped in an endless maze.
'To be honest... I think I can see it.'
But he wasn't confident enough to gamble everyone's lives on it.
So Oscar spoke.
"Let's not make this difficult."
"Then what's the easy way?"
"What is a formation? In the end, it's just the ability to construct a special domain within space."
"...You can't possibly..."
Before Fran could finish speaking, Oscar nodded.
"If that's the case, then all we have to do is cut the space itself."
As he spoke, he pointed forward.
"Spatial Slash."
Slash!
A gigantic blade of space cleaved vertically through the empty space before them.
Then the space covering the forest peeled away like a sheet of luxurious silk.
"Eh...?"
Beyond it lay a vast expanse.
And at its center stood a massive temple.
"That worked out nicely."
Sometimes, simplicity was better than exhausting oneself trying to think of complicated solutions.
Killian gave him a thumbs-up from beside him.
"I like this method very much. It's worthy of a warrior."
"Glad to hear it."
Oscar chuckled and walked toward the opened space.
"Come on. Let's go in."
The moment they stepped inside, they felt the gazes of those moving about outside the temple.
"Huh? Who are—"
"Wait. Doesn't that space over there look kind of strange? Was it... cut?"
"Idiot. What do you think space is, paper? You think you can just cut it? More importantly, who are you people?"
Apparently never expecting an enemy to stroll in so openly, the members of the Black Fingers approached with innocent expressions.
Oscar smiled faintly as he looked at them.
Crack! Crack!
"H-Huh?"
"M-My body... huh?"
For a brief moment, they stared at their limbs, bent in impossible directions.
Then the horrifying pain hit.
"AAAAAGH!"
"M-My arm! M-My leg!"
Looking at them indifferently, Oscar spoke.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
"Seiro. Begin."
"O-Okay."
Swallowing hard, Seiro stepped forward.
In an instant, he released his polymorph.
His body rapidly expanded into the enormous form of a dragon, and blazing breath poured from his jaws.
"Wow... he really did turn into a gigantic lizard."
"Doesn't he kind of... look like the dragons from fairy tales?"
"No way."
Out of the corner of his eye, Fran kept glancing at Edna.
"As far as I know, she's the only dragon left on this planet. Edna Sol Laplace."
That was common knowledge.
Fran looked at Seiro, who was spewing dragon breath, with absolute certainty.
"That's just a lizard."
"A really big lizard."
"..."
The destructive power of Seiro's breath suddenly increased.
* * *
"E-Enemy attack! Enemy attack!"
"Prepare for battle immediately! Intruders have appeared!"
The inside of the temple erupted into chaos.
The Black Fingers members, unaware of what was happening, hurriedly gathered their equipment in confusion.
"An enemy attack? Here?"
"No way... You can't even get in here unless you know how."
"Did someone who got captured spill the information?"
"Don't be ridiculous. The moment anyone tries to reveal information, they die. We all swore the oath."
Given the Black Fingers' brutal initiation procedures, leaking internal information was virtually impossible.
That was why it was hard to believe that enemies had actually invaded this place.
"Maybe they got lucky and passed through the formation?"
"Don't be absurd. That's not something luck can accomplish."
Thirty steps.
Each one had to be taken with different stride lengths, placing every foot on the exact same spots.
If even the slightest mistake was made, one would fall into an infinite abyss, wandering the same place until death.
'That's why they don't even reveal this place to rookies or idiots in the first place.'
In other words, the hundreds of members staying inside this temple were elites handpicked even among the Black Fingers.
"Everyone move! The Fingers have ordered us not to let them reach the inner area!"
"Damn it, we just got back from the operation, and now these nobodies won't even let us rest!"
"Where are they?"
"Mana's been detected near the eastern gate. Squad 2-B4, prepare."
At the squad leader's cold command, the ten members under him grumbled while equipping themselves.
As they rushed out of the room and ran down the corridor, the leader at the front frowned.
'Hm? An eye...?'
Normally, whenever he walked through this corridor, he could see the blue sky beyond the exit.
But what he saw now was a yellow eye, like that of some enormous reptile.
'Am I seeing things?'
There couldn't possibly be a creature with eyes that huge.
Unless a dragon—an extinct dragon—had suddenly appeared.
The moment he rubbed his eyes—
Flap!
The eye disappeared, replaced once more by the familiar blue sky.
'I must be tired from not getting enough sleep.'
Nodding to himself, the squad leader sprinted toward the end of the corridor.
Then—
Fwoooosh!
A massive wave of fire, accompanied by overwhelming heat, swept through the entire corridor.
"AAAAAAAGH!"
"I-It's hot!"
"Save... save me..."
The members running through the corridor were instantly reduced to the brink of death.
"C-Cough!"
When the flames finally subsided, only three or four of them were barely still breathing.
"What's that smell?"
"Why is the corridor so hot?"
"Huh? Wait, who are these guys?"
The members who arrived afterward recoiled in shock upon seeing them.
However, they had no intention of saving them.
They merely nudged their bodies with their feet to see if they would react.
Among them, the squad leader, whose skills had barely kept him alive, desperately stretched out a hand.
"S-Save..."
"Save you?"
The leader of Squad 3-C2, who had crouched down in front of him, smiled maliciously.
"Aren't you from the Second Finger's people? We serve the Third Finger."
Even within the Black Fingers, factions were divided according to which Finger they served.
They spent a while snickering as they watched another squad die.
Then, from the entrance of the corridor, where the flames had yet to completely die down—
Step.
Step.
Someone began walking in.
"...Hm? What's that guy doing?"
"Must be the intruder."
"What? They made such a huge fuss over just one person?"
Had he really gotten lucky and broken through the formation?
Looking closely, the bastard was annoyingly handsome.
'...Still, that face. I feel like I've seen it somewhere.'
Tilting his head, the squad leader started to rise.
Or rather, he tried to.
"There's no need to stand."
In the temple corridor, where not even the faintest breeze existed—
An unprecedented wind descended, crushing the heads and shoulders of nearly thirty members.
"You belong on the ground."
"Ugh... UUUUGH!"
The Level 5 squad leader's eyes turned bloodshot as he struggled against the irresistible force.
But only for a moment.
Crack!
Both knees slammed into the floor.
Then his head was forced down after them.
The weaker subordinates fared no differently.
Their eyes rolled wildly toward the corridor walls.
'If it's wind... then don't tell me... a White Tower mage?'
A White Tower mage.
With those words came the image of the aristocratic-looking young man he had just seen.
'R-Right! Oscar Crucian!'
The mage about whom rumors claimed no one who became involved with him survived.
The undisputed greatest genius of the White Tower, who had reached Level 7 in barely a year.
Realizing the intruder's identity, the man swallowed hard.
'Wasn't... White Tower magic supposed to be nothing special?'
At most, it was wind.
That was the Black Fingers' internal assessment.
Unlike the other Four Great Magic Towers, whom they frequently encountered during operations, they had never faced a high-ranking White Tower mage.
And so they remained ignorant.
They simply didn't know.
The same had been true for him.
He had only fought a few novice and intermediate White Tower mages, and had dismissed them as unimpressive.
'But this...'
The power of a high-ranking White Tower mage who controlled the wind.
Overwhelming magic so absolute that one was not even permitted to raise their eyes to meet his.
"P-Please spare me! I'll live an honest life from now on!"
In the end, the only thing that came from the squad leader's mouth was a pitiful plea.
Hearing it, Oscar let out a mocking laugh.
"How you choose to live from now on is none of my concern."
Creeeak.
The pressure of the wind crushing their bodies began to increase.
"N-No! D-Don't do it!"
"You bastard! Let us go!"
"You think you'll get away with this!?"
The terrified squad leader screamed, while the others hurled curses that were little more than desperate shrieks.
But once the pressure had begun climbing so steeply, it showed no sign of stopping.
Oscar glanced at the wretches squealing on the floor before walking past them.
"The way you've lived until now... is the reason you're dying."
Crunch!
With a sound like watermelons bursting, the heads of the members flattened against the floor exploded.

Chapter 409: The Black Finger (1)
Killian strode down the corridor without hesitation.
He liked this place because there was no fear of getting lost.
All he had to do was keep walking down the corridor.
'I think this was the southern route.'
East, west, south, north.
The group had to attack the temple's four entrances simultaneously.
According to Oscar, the temple's interior was structured like a labyrinth.
Naturally, the group had split into four teams.
East — Oscar
North — Edna
South — Killian, Mad Fiend
West — Fran, Veronica.
The large lizard, Seiro, remained outside the temple.
He had been assigned the important role of preventing anyone from secretly escaping or stopping reinforcements from arriving from outside.
"Grrrr..."
Killian glanced at Mad Fiend, who was walking ahead of him.
Although he possessed an exceptional warrior's body, he was still a companion with whom proper communication was impossible.
'Cooperation during battle... I'd better not expect much.'
It would probably end up being every man for himself.
Just then, the sound of numerous people running echoed from ahead.
"There they are!"
"Khehehe! Do you have any idea where you are to come barging in here?!"
The enemies charged while drawing their weapons.
'Thirty-five of them. A suitable warm-up.'
Killian lightly rolled his neck and was just about to rush forward.
"KRAAAAH!"
In an instant, Mad Fiend ran along the corridor wall and swung the edge of his hand like a sickle.
Seven heads separated from their bodies and flew into the air in the blink of an eye.
Before the enemies, their pupils dilating in shock, could even react properly—
"Grrr!"
A lion wearing a human's skin leaped into the flock.
And then the indiscriminate slaughter began.
Every time his mana-infused arms and legs swung, someone's entire life vanished into nothingness.
"...!"
Watching this, Killian felt a chilling shiver crawl down his spine.
That man called Mad Fiend looked as though he had been born for the sole purpose of destruction.
Drip. Plop.
Blood and chunks of flesh soaked the corridor as though a rainstorm had fallen.
"Grr..."
It took only seventeen seconds to wipe out all thirty-five members of the Black Finger.
Killian's Adam's apple bobbed visibly.
'Fast.'
He had never seen a warrior with such incredible speed, not even back in his tribe.
If it had been him...
'...Even at my fastest, it would have taken at least three minutes.'
Level 6 and Level 7.
The difference he had dismissed as merely a single number was now carved into his skin.
And Mad Fiend wasn't even in his right mind.
'If someone with a sound mind were controlling that body...'
Its destructive power was something he would never want to face, not even in his dreams.
Killian silently followed behind Mad Fiend, who simply resumed walking down the corridor as though nothing had happened.
"...You don't have to fight alone. I'm a warrior too. I can more than pull my own weight."
"Grrrrng."
Mad Fiend let out a low growl after hearing Killian's words.
It felt just like talking to wolves or other wild beasts back when he had lived in the forest.
Recalling those memories, Killian stared at Mad Fiend's back with a strange expression.
'Could it be... he's looking out for me?'
There were occasionally wild beasts like that.
The kind that saw humans smaller than themselves as cubs belonging to their pack and instinctively protected them.
Mad Fiend's actions and growls felt exactly like that.
"Ahem."
Frowning, Killian lengthened his stride until they walked shoulder to shoulder.
"I'm strong. If you're holding back out of consideration for me, you don't need to."
"Krng."
The sound almost resembled a mocking snort.
Annoyed, Killian was about to argue back when he abruptly glared ahead.
'An enemy?'
Through the vibrations beneath his feet, he sensed something approaching.
The tremors were completely different from those of the enemies they had encountered earlier.
Boom! Boom!
What appeared next was a gigantic monster that nearly filled the entire width of the already broad corridor.
"That's... a Twin-Headed Ogre...?"
A rare mutant monster that had last been reported in the Empire seven years ago.
Having two heads made it more intelligent than an ordinary ogre.
In other words, it overcame the greatest weakness of normal ogres—their inability to properly utilize their overwhelmingly powerful bodies due to their low intelligence.
'No, that's not all.'
Killian narrowed his eyes.
As far as he knew, Twin-Headed Ogres only had two heads.
But the creature before him had no fewer than four arms.
Moreover, between those four arms protruded the enormous forelegs of a praying mantis.
'A chimera.'
He had a good idea whose handiwork this was.
There was only one person in the Black Finger who conducted monster experiments.
"An alchemist's test subject."
If so, there was a ninety-nine percent chance it had absorbed a Demon Core as well.
Which meant it had easily surpassed the natural limits of an ordinary monster.
"Be careful. That thing is—"
Before Killian could finish his warning—
KROAAAH!
Mad Fiend charged straight at the newly appeared enemy.
"Watch out!"
At the same moment Killian shouted in alarm, the ogre thrust out all four of its arms.
Mad Fiend effortlessly dodged them with his trademark agility and drove his fist into the monster's solar plexus.
KWAAAAAANG!
The devastating impact sent a shockwave roaring through the corridor.
"...Good heavens."
That single punch blasted a massive hole through the ogre's abdomen.
Even worse, its insides had been completely torn apart, as though shredded by razor-sharp winds.
"Krng."
Slowly withdrawing his hand, Mad Fiend turned around and snorted.
It was almost as though he were asking why anyone should be cautious of something so weak.
"Behind you! Watch your back!"
Hearing Killian's urgent cry, Mad Fiend looked forward.
KWAAANG!
The ogre smashed him with the back of one enormous hand, sending his body crashing into the wall.
"Galgalgal."
The two heads perched upon the ogre's shoulders let out grotesque laughter.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The gaping cross-section of its abdomen began to writhe.
In an instant, fresh flesh swelled forth and filled the hole.
"...Regeneration?"
Killian's eyes sharpened.
Very few monsters possessed regeneration of that caliber.
"Don't tell me... it was even given a troll's regenerative ability."
A power befitting a chimera.
At the same time, his thoughts grew complicated.
'To give regeneration to a creature that already possesses such overwhelming physical strength...'
It was cheating in every sense of the word.
Clenching his lips tightly, Killian kicked off the ground.
'First, I save Mad Fiend.'
The impact had apparently been greater than expected.
Mad Fiend had barely managed to stand, staggering unsteadily.
Then the ogre's boulder-like fist descended upon him.
KWAAAAANG!
"Whew..."
Having barely rescued Mad Fiend in time, Killian let out a sigh of relief.
"A Twin-Headed Ogre is already considered Level 6 based solely on its natural physique. One that's been stuffed with extra arms and additional abilities will be even worse."
At minimum, it was Level 7.
Setting Mad Fiend down from over his shoulder, he continued,
"It'll be difficult to fight it alone. Let's fight together."
"...Grrr."
Mad Fiend wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth with his sleeve and gave a short reply.
Instinctively understanding that it meant I understand, Killian fixed his gaze upon the monster.
"Judging from all those forced modifications, it must be carrying an enormous amount of weight."
In other words, its ability to abruptly change directions would be greatly reduced.
Killian spoke.
"I can't completely shake it at my speed. If you keep its attention from the front, I'll attack it from behind."
"Grr."
Nodding as though he understood, Mad Fiend shot forward.
As if it had been waiting for him, the ogre's fists came hurtling toward him.
Bang! Bam! KWAAANG!
Inside the narrow corridor, Mad Fiend avoided every single blow with dazzling footwork.
'Now.'
At the very moment the ogre's attention was fixed on Mad Fiend—
Keeping low, Killian slipped past the ogre like a bolt of lightning and took position behind it.
'Good. It hasn't noticed—'
At that instant—
One of the ogre's heads whipped around and locked eyes with Killian.
Ignoring Mad Fiend, it turned its entire body toward him.
"Damn!"
He had to get away.
Panicked, Killian instinctively activated his Acceleration tattoo.
But the modified ogre was just a little faster.
Crunch!
"Guhaaak!"
Simply being squeezed that hard made it feel as though his internal organs were being crushed.
Blood surged into his throat.
Killian vomited it out while desperately enduring the pain.
The tattoos that enhanced his physical durability blazed brilliantly, but only for a moment.
Crackle. Crack.
Like light bulbs reaching the end of their lifespan, they flickered before losing their light.
"Ghk!"
Shrrng. Shrrng.
The ogre slowly moved one arm toward its own abdomen.
There, the blade-like forelegs of the praying mantis waited with a sinister rasp.
'If I go there, I'll die.'
He didn't possess any miraculous ability to restore a body cut into three pieces.
Biting his lip hard, Killian glared at the monster.
'But.'
Even at this very moment, Killian did not give up.
If every bit of the monster's attention was focused on him, that meant Mad Fiend was free.
Slash!
Mad Fiend burst forward in an instant, severed the ogre's arm, and caught Killian.
Putting some distance between themselves and the monster, he examined Killian's condition.
"Cough! Cough!"
Killian nodded while gasping for breath.
"It's... not enough to kill me."
"Grrr."
The ogre calmly picked up its severed arm and pressed it against the cut surface.
The flesh wriggled before seamlessly reconnecting.
The creature repeatedly clenched and unclenched its fist before grinning grotesquely.
Watching this, Killian lowered his voice.
"There's no point attacking its arms, legs, or torso. If it has a troll's regeneration, it'll simply recover them all."
His gaze settled upon the two heads.
"But the heads are different. Unlike ordinary organs, even trolls have difficulty regenerating the brain."
Besides, that creature had two heads.
Which meant it also had two weak points.
As Killian rose to his feet, Mad Fiend lightly tapped him with the back of his hand.
"...?"
Then he pointed at himself before pointing at the ogre's left head.
Next, he pointed at Killian before indicating the ogre's right head.
The gestures were incredibly simple, but Killian understood exactly what he meant.
"You want me to take the right head. Understood."
The instant they exchanged glances, Mad Fiend charged first.
PAAAAANG!
A dense blast of destructive wind erupted from his palm, slamming the giant body into the wall.
"Kkeuaaah!"
As the shrieking giant collapsed, Mad Fiend raised both of his hand-blades.
Wiiiiing!
The wind coating them vibrated ceaselessly.
"KROAAAAAH!"
Mad Fiend rushed the ogre and swung both arms in a frenzy.
The assault was practically a butchering.
One of the ogre's heads was left dangling by a thread.
"Kke... kkeeeeh!"
For the first time, the previously confident ogre's eyes shook.
No matter how much the experiments had strengthened it, it was still only a monster.
Faced with the threat of death, it fell into a panic.
It clutched the dangling neck with two of its arms while using the remaining two to crawl away.
But someone was already waiting in the direction it fled.
"...Wolf's Song."
Claws formed entirely from mana sprang out from the backs of both of Killian's hands.
Their duration was short, but their hardness rivaled the finest steel.
Tattoo after tattoo across Killian's body beneath his dark clothing began to glow.
"I'm going."
Kicking off the ground, Killian shot toward the monster.
The panicked ogre lifted the enormous hand that had been supporting its body, trying to stop him.
Slash!
Cutting through its fingers and passing beyond them, Killian used the ogre's arm as a foothold and leaped upward.
"...!"
Two pairs of terrified eyes turned toward him.
Spinning through the air, Killian kicked off the ceiling and streaked downward like a slanting line of rain.
KUUUUUNG!
Almost simultaneously, Mad Fiend charged in and completely tore off the ogre's left head.
"Huff... Huff."
"...Grrr."
The two of them stared at the ogre's corpse for quite some time.
But the creature never rose again.

Chapter 410: Black Finger (2)
“Now!”
The moment Veronica shouted sharply, Fran was already moving.
Shwaaaaaak!
With the sound of air being torn apart, the whip smashed the goblin’s head to pieces.
“Huu, haah.”
Gasping heavily, Fran barely managed to speak.
“Again. I’ve never even heard of a goblin like this existing.”
“That alchemist or whatever probably made it. He’s the kind of bastard who conducts all sorts of experiments.”
Veronica replied while examining the goblin’s corpse.
“It looked grotesque to begin with. A goblin with dozens of eyes…… Disgusting.”
Generally, cave goblins were dexterous and agile.
Because of that, they normally hunted prey through ambushes, but their one weakness was their poor eyesight.
It was so bad that they could not pursue a target once it moved even slightly farther away.
However, this creature, which had countless tiny eyes plastered all over it like a spider, was different.
“I never want to encounter another one.”
Its eyesight was so good that it could even see behind itself.
Had Veronica not landed 『Aerial Restraint』 five times, it would have become a troublesome fight.
Wiping away the sweat running down his face, Fran stared into the dark corridor.
“Was this the third one?”
“That’s right.”
There had been no problem when they encountered the members of Black Finger.
Those bastards had been weak despite their large numbers.
But at some point, modified monsters had begun to appear.
“Every single one of them is quite threatening.”
“It’s even more irritating because they’re blatantly trying to wear us down.”
It was frustrating that they had no choice but to fall for it despite knowing what the enemy intended.
Veronica looked back.
“We can’t turn around and go back the way we came now…….”
“Yeah. That might cause trouble for the others.”
Oscar and Killian were probably dealing with similar creatures.
If they withdrew because things were difficult on their side, the monsters would end up flocking toward the others.
They could not do something that would merely hold the others back.
“But don’t you think something is a little strange?”
Fran asked while looking around.
“I know the temple is large, but even taking that into consideration, isn’t this corridor far too long?”
“Hmm.”
Veronica, who had already been harboring a similar suspicion, nodded.
“That part is strange, actually. And do you remember what happened when the goblin ambushed us a little while ago?”
“Of course I remember. I got lucky.”
The goblin, which had concealed its presence and hidden itself, had swung a dagger at them from behind.
Fortunately, Wind Lord had activated and elementalized his neck, causing the attack to cut through empty air.
Had the goblin targeted Veronica first, a horrifying situation would have unfolded.
“But what about it?”
“The goblin appeared behind us. Isn’t that strange?”
“Uh, now that you mention it, definitely…….”
Fran looked down the corridor they had already passed through.
“There was only one path.”
“That’s right. If the goblin appeared behind us, there are only two possibilities. The first is that it entered from outside the temple.”
The possibility she mentioned was unlikely.
“Hmm, that’s strange. That lizard named Seiro and Ms. Edna are guarding the outside, aren’t they?”
“That’s right. Of course, they might simply have missed it, but we agreed that they would send us a signal if something happened.”
The fact that there had been no signal meant that, from the outside, there had been no problem.
The two silently stared down the corridor they had walked through.
If a hidden passage or door existed somewhere along it.
For now, that possibility was overwhelmingly more likely.
“Should we go back the way we came and inspect every corner?”
“But what if that’s what the enemy wants? It might place an additional burden on Killian or Oscar’s group.”
After pondering for a moment, Veronica spoke.
“It can’t be helped. Let’s push forward. We’ll increase our speed instead.”
“What if an enemy jumps out from behind us again like before?”
“To prepare for that possibility, you take the rear.”
“Eek. You’re openly telling me to become a meat shield?”
“You won’t die anyway because you have Wind Lord.”
“Urgh.”
Fran scratched his head roughly before nodding.
In their current situation, that was their best option.
Besides, it was not as though Veronica’s role would be easy.
She would have to bear the full brunt of any attacks or traps that came from the front.
“Fine.”
“Let’s move immediately. We’ve stayed in one place for too long.”
They began moving and walked for quite some time.
As they continued down the corridor illuminated by flickering, dim magical lights, it began to feel as though something was going wrong with their minds.
[Something is strange.]
“What’s strange?”
[We have been circling the same place continuously.]
“That’s…… Don’t you just feel that way because it’s a straight corridor?”
“Why? What is the spirit saying?”
When Fran relayed Mu’s words to Veronica, who lacked spirit affinity, she shrugged.
“If you suspect that, we can just leave a mark.”
Krrrrk!
The blade of wind she created gouged a large X into the stone wall.
“There’s no way we’ll fail to recognize something this obvious, right?”
“Definitely. It’s also directly beneath a magical light, so we’ll see it immediately.”
[I agree.]
A little over ten minutes after leaving the mark and continuing onward.
What awaited the group was a place where a rough X had been carved into the wall.
“Veronica, this.”
“……It isn’t fake. That’s my mana.”
After running her hand across the wall, Veronica replied in a grave voice.
The mana that had carved this mark was unmistakably hers.
Flustered, Fran denied the reality before him.
“B-But that doesn’t make any sense, does it? This is a corridor with only one path, and we’ve only been walking forward.”
A place that defied common sense.
And that very morning, the two had already witnessed a method capable of doing such a thing.
An art of the Yan Kingdom that twisted space to construct an independent domain.
“A formation. What if one has been installed inside the temple as well?”
“…….”
Fran gulped and spoke to Mu.
“Mu, fly back along the path we came from. Once you reach the entrance, come back.”
[Understood.]
Mu flew down the path they had walked and returned from the front a little over ten minutes later.
[I see.]
Mu nodded.
[It appears that we are trapped.]
* * *
Oscar suddenly stopped walking.
It was because he could sense his own mana.
‘Does it make people circle the same place continuously……?’
It was a formation.
He had never imagined that they would have installed one inside the temple as well.
It must have activated the moment it determined that intruders had entered.
‘This is troublesome.’
Oscar stroked his chin as he considered the situation.
In truth, this formation was not particularly effective against him.
He could simply slice through space itself and continue onward.
But it was different for the others.
‘Edna might manage somehow, but Veronica and Fran, as well as Killian and the Mad Fiend, won’t be able to do anything about this.’
The only solution was for him to personally wander around and rescue them one by one.
What troubled him now was the Fingers.
‘They’re openly trying to stall for time. What is their reason?’
Logically speaking, there was a high possibility that they were trying to escape.
He had only looked around briefly, but the temple’s level of defense was insufficient to handle their group.
To be honest, bringing the Mad Fiend alone would have been enough to clear the place out.
‘Letting them escape…… would be troublesome.’
The most important thing right now was finding the traitor within the imperial family.
Unless that came first, no matter what they did, they would merely be dancing in the enemy’s palm.
“…….”
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
However, his stiffened legs refused to move easily.
Oscar bit his lip as he deliberated.
‘Is this truly a rational judgment?’
He had thought the same thing that day, when he attempted to kill the Great Emperor instead of returning to the White Tower.
That he was more rational than he had ever been.
That this choice was right.
“……Huu.”
Oscar released a faint breath.
His heartbeat, which had begun to quicken, regained its usual rhythm.
‘I’m glad I met that bastard.’
Had he not met Magiro not long ago, he would have fallen into a fairly severe panic.
He would have doubted himself again and again, wondering whether abandoning his companions and going after Black Finger was truly the right choice.
‘But now I know.’
He knew that choice was the best one.
More than anything, he trusted that they would not lose to something as trivial as a formation.
He had watched them grow countless times.
‘If it’s them as they are now.’
They would overcome even this situation on their own.
Therefore, there was only one thing he needed to do now.
“Split apart.”
Slash!
A sharp blade of space sliced through the corridor.
What was revealed beyond it was a staircase leading downward.
“…….”
Without looking back, Oscar descended the stairs.
When he opened the door, an enormous space appeared before him.
Hundreds of bunk beds had been placed throughout the area, which was divided into several sections.
At a glance, the atmosphere resembled military barracks where soldiers lived.
‘In reality, it isn’t much different. This must be where the members of Black Finger live.’
As proof, the warmth of people could still be felt throughout the area.
Of course, most of the bastards who had been here until a short while ago had probably become cold corpses by now.
Or perhaps they had been reduced to scorching charcoal.
“…….”
Oscar strode forward without hesitation.
There was only one living creature on this floor.
“Ugh, uugh…….”
A man whose entire body was wrapped in bandages lay groaning on a bed.
When Oscar lightly kicked the bed, the man opened his eyes.
“Hm? Who…….”
The member’s pupils trembled rapidly when he saw the man with an extraordinary aura.
Hadn’t they been told that distinguished guests would be arriving from outside today?
Gulping, he forgot his pain and abruptly sat upright.
“A-Are you perhaps one of the people who were supposed to arrive today?”
“…….”
Oscar replied in a dry voice.
“Where is the alchemist?”
“I-I will guide you there immediately!”
Using crutches, the man limped along as he guided him.
“P-Please come this way.”
The place the man led him to contained an elevator that looked like something one would see at a construction site.
When they boarded it and headed downward, the scenery slowly changed.
‘An armory, a training ground, a dining hall…….’
It felt as though he were looking at a small magic tower.
When Oscar unconsciously let out a hollow laugh, the man awkwardly laughed along with him.
Kwoooong!
The place where the elevator stopped had a completely different atmosphere.
Rather than an ancient temple, it felt like the clean laboratory of a corporation.
“Beyond this point, my authority does not permit me to proceed.”
“You’ve done well.”
“Th-Thank you! My name is…….”
Slash!
He painlessly sent off the bastard, who had been saluting with an excited expression.
When Oscar approached the door, a mechanical voice rang out.
[You do not have authorization.]
Slash!
When he sliced through the door with a blade of wind, kwoooong!
A heavy sound reverberated through the space.
“Hmm.”
The interior was one enormous laboratory.
First, large glass tubes stood lined up in rows, their interiors filled with green liquid and all kinds of monsters.
‘Rather than a headquarters, is the temple itself the alchemist’s laboratory?’
Then again, he had found it strange when he heard that Black Finger possessed a headquarters.
Weren’t they difficult to eradicate precisely because they operated through thoroughly compartmentalized cells?
As he passed between the glass tubes, the distinctive smell of chemicals stung his nose.
“You’re an interesting one.”
Oscar stopped and turned his head toward the voice that had suddenly come from behind him.
Until a moment ago, he had not sensed even the slightest trace of mana from that location.
“You’re a guest I never invited. Don’t you think you’re acting far too boldly?”
“…….”
His opponent’s slender body was covered in black bandages.
Oscar’s gaze swiftly swept over his opponent before settling at his feet.
‘He has no shadow.’
At the unnatural sight, Oscar raised his head.
“You’re the Hound.”
“Keuk, you’re quick-witted. Most people don’t think to examine their opponent’s shadow.”
“You should take better care of it.”
With those words, Oscar reached a hand behind himself.
Crack!
Within the mana-coated breeze, the bastard’s shadow was seized as though it were a piece of clothing.
“You shouldn’t carelessly leave your belongings lying around.”
“Hmm. You certainly aren’t bad.”
Nodding, the Hound pulled a control device from inside his clothes and pressed it.
“However, there is a proper order to everything.”
Crash! Shatter!
The glass tubes shattered in every direction, and the green liquid that had filled them poured out.
At the same time, the monsters began to rise.

Chapter 411: Black Finger (3)
“Kweeeek!”
The first to roar was an ogre with no fewer than three heads.
Judging by the stitch marks on all but one of its heads, it appeared to have been artificially created.
‘Not a single one of them looks normal.’
Oscar glanced around.
An orc with a huge mouth attached to its chest, opening and closing like a goldfish.
A snake with dozens of eyes like those of an insect.
A werewolf with one arm swollen to an abnormal size, among others.
Every last one of them had an unsettling appearance.
“Grrrr.”
“Kaaak, kak!”
Just as the monsters shook their heads and snorted.
Tak!
With a sound, the laboratory’s bright lights went out.
Instead, the emergency exit signs and green lights installed throughout the laboratory illuminated the area.
“Hmm, now this is exactly the kind of atmosphere I like.”
Srrrk.
At the same time, the Hound’s shadow that he had been holding trickled down like grains of sand.
After retrieving his shadow, the Hound walked past the shattered glass tanks and spoke.
“Do you have any last words?”
“I hope you adjust well when you get to hell.”
“Heh, amusing.”
His shoulders shook with laughter as he raised his head.
“Go ahead and send me there. If you can.”
The moment those words left his mouth, Slash!
A massive blade of wind cut across the laboratory.
The three heads of the ogre standing at the very front flew into the air.
And the enormous snake crawling up from behind it was split vertically in two.
“…….”
As blades fluttered in every direction, Oscar’s dry eyes remained fixed solely on the Hound.
It did not matter how many of these crude monsters there were.
Thud! Thuud!
Heavy chunks of flesh rolled across the floor.
The Hound, who had crouched down to evade the attack, narrowed his eyes.
“……It is difficult to believe even after seeing it. To think you can unleash magic of that output without incantations.”
The Hound licked his lips, and his body gradually faded like a shadow.
-Now, stop lying around and move.
“……?”
Who the hell was he talking to?
The moment Oscar wondered that, Tadadadadak!
The severed hand of the ogre, which had been sprawled across the floor, began crawling like a spider.
‘I definitely cut off its heads.’
Oscar frowned and quickly scanned his surroundings.
It was not only the ogre’s hand.
The monsters he had been certain he had killed began moving perfectly well despite being severed into pieces.
‘The parts capable of moving independently move on their own…….’
The ogre, which had been torn apart so badly that it could not even stand properly, absorbed other monsters nearby to create a lower body.
‘I see.’
It was already difficult to call those things living creatures.
They were merely something that could neither live nor die, having been modified through all manner of experiments.
“Kraaaaaah!”
The reassembled werewolf brought its enormous forepaw down toward the crown of Oscar’s head.
Oscar glanced at it, shifted half a step to evade the attack, and lightly snapped his fingers.
Paaang!
Compressed wind burrowed into the monster’s flesh.
Its head exploded in an instant, and a gaping hole was punched through its chest, yet the werewolf did not stop.
‘Its weak point is neither the head nor the heart.’
Nor did it feel as though something outside was controlling it.
In other words, there had to be a core somewhere within its body.
“Let’s take a closer look.”
Crack! Oscar lightly stamped his foot, and wind rose like a wave before engulfing the werewolf.
The flesh exposed to the blade-like wind was shredded in an instant, revealing the bones beneath.
At the same time, he spotted a large stone writhing within its left thigh.
“This is…….”
It was the Demon Jade, the stone he had once researched alongside Lloyd on the Western Front.
Covered in flesh, it was serving as the creature’s heart.
‘That makes one.’
When Oscar shattered the Demon Jade with wind, the werewolf finally stopped regenerating and could no longer stand.
The others would also have one of those stones attached somewhere within their bodies.
‘This is a little troublesome.’
Oscar turned, wrapped himself around the arm of the charging ogre as it swung its fist, and threw it over his shoulder.
Kwaaaaaang!
“Kuek!”
The moment the floor tiles cracked like a spiderweb and the creature squealed like a pig being slaughtered.
The ogre’s shadow swelled, and a black blade silently surged upward.
Kaaang!
Oscar instantly knocked it away with the wind wrapped around the back of his hand.
-Your reactions are not bad.
“Is hiding and running your mouth your specialty?”
-Do you expect an assassin to reveal himself and fight?
Along with the sly answer, three shadow daggers shot out from the surrounding shadows.
Oscar hurriedly twisted his body to avoid them, and the Hound’s presence disappeared like a ghost once more.
“…….”
Oscar frowned as he looked at his torn sleeve.
‘So this was why he released those useless monsters.’
The combat strength of the monsters had never mattered to the Hound in the first place.
All that mattered was that the monsters continued moving without rest, casting shadows throughout the entire laboratory.
That alone was enough for them to fulfil their role.
“Okay, confirmed.”
Now that he understood the problem, the solution was equally clear.
“Spatial Severance.”
The spatial slash that erupted in an instant devastated the surrounding area.
It was an indiscriminate erasure that made no distinction between monsters, glass tanks, debris, or anything else.
At the same time, a streak of light blossomed from the tip of his index finger and flew toward the ceiling.
『Light』
He poured a considerable amount of mana into the basic light-type spell.
As a result, the interior of the laboratory suddenly became so bright that it felt like midday.
Fwoosh!
The brighter the light, the darker the shadows it cast.
The shadow of the snake monster Oscar had deliberately left intact stretched out.
“Found you.”
Just before the Spatial Severance descending from above sliced through the shadow.
“Keugh!”
The Hound, who had been hiding within it, hurriedly leapt out.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
After rolling across the floor several times, he gritted his teeth.
“You ignorant……!”
But Oscar had already entrusted his body to the wind and closed the distance between them.
Crack!
A knee carrying overwhelming acceleration slammed directly into his chest.
With his ribs crushed, the Hound was sent flying and rolled across the floor several times.
“Kuh, ngghh.”
His body convulsed violently, unable even to scream from the overwhelming pain.
Click!
Closing the distance with Blink, Oscar fastened handcuffs around both of his wrists.
They were mana-sealing handcuffs, the same kind the Emperor had intended to place on the Master of the Yellow Tower.
‘Even World Liberation should be impossible with these.’
After all, the handcuffs prohibited the use of mana within the body itself.
As a result, the Hound’s eyes trembled.
“W-What are these?”
“Mana-sealing handcuffs. Your mana isn’t moving the way you want it to, is it?”
“Keugh!”
The Hound gritted his teeth.
Then, as though he had already foreseen what awaited him, he tried to bite off his own tongue and kill himself, but.
“You couldn’t die even if you wanted to.”
Crack!
Oscar moved one step faster and stomped on his mouth, shattering all his teeth.
“You’re not the first person like this I’ve dealt with.”
Oscar’s eyes turned cold.
From this moment onward, this man would never enjoy freedom again until he had vomited out every piece of information he possessed.
Of course, the freedom awaiting him at the end was called death.
Press.
Oscar stepped on the back of his neck and turned his head sideways.
“Spit it all out.”
“Gweeeeh.”
Just as broken teeth poured from the Hound’s mouth along with blood.
A sudden, unpleasant sensation crawled up Oscar’s spine.
Oscar did not dismiss the feeling and immediately turned around.
His gaze fell upon an iron door set into one wall at the far end of the laboratory.
‘That door—when did it……?’
From within the darkness beyond the door, which had opened at some point.
“World Liberation.”
“……!”
A dry voice flowed out.
“Ten Thousand Species, One Body.”
At the same time, something stretched outward from the darkness and came rushing toward them.
‘An arm?’
The arm resembled tree bark and was even covered in scales like those of a reptile.
Slash!
Without panicking, Oscar countered by slicing it apart with Spatial Severance, but.
‘……It split?’
Instead, the arm multiplied into two and continued advancing.
It seized the Hound and withdrew in an instant.
“You would have died if I had been even slightly later.”
Someone then walked out from within the dark doorway.
The gaunt man wearing a laboratory coat had deep shadows beneath his eyes, and his face was utterly bloodless.
Oscar stared at him, furrowed his brow, and asked.
“……Are you the alchemist?”
“Many people call me by that name.”
“You must also be the one who created the Demon Jade.”
“Demon Jade? Ah, are you referring to the Philosopher’s Stone?”
The man nodded, set the Hound down on the floor, and shattered the handcuffs.
The Hound breathed a sigh of relief and rotated his wrists with a surprised expression.
“……Thank you.”
“I did not save you because I particularly wanted you alive. I simply lacked the confidence to deal with that monster by myself.”
The alchemist replied dryly and surveyed the laboratory.
The test subjects had been chopped into pieces, and even their Demon Jades had been destroyed and scattered like dust.
He clicked his tongue with a displeased expression.
“Tsk. Some of those took more than ten years to create…… To think you would ruin another person’s research like this.”
“You wasted ten whole years making nothing more than that?”
“How foolish. Every failure is the mother of success.”
“Then where is the success?”
At that question, one corner of the alchemist’s mouth curved upward.
“Is it not standing before your eyes?”
Crack, crack, crack!
An unsettling sound emerged from his body, and the previously loose laboratory coat was torn apart in an instant.
It could not withstand the muscles and physique that had suddenly swollen beneath it.
“Hmm, this is somewhat better.”
As he lightly turned his head, his height surged past two metres in an instant.
His entire body was packed with firm muscles like those of a knight who had trained for many years.
“I suppose I do not need these anymore either.”
Perhaps even his eyesight had improved, as the alchemist removed his glasses and tossed them away.
His bright yellow eyes resembled those of a reptile, and every strand of his hair writhed like a living snake.
‘……This isn’t an ordinary physical transformation.’
World Liberation was the act of overlaying reality with the world one desired more than anything.
In other words, the alchemist’s current body must also have taken the form of what he considered ideal.
“Ten Thousand Species, One Body is the construction of an independent ecosystem by cramming every living creature into the human body.”
The alchemist tapped his own chest.
“I am that successful creation. Every creature I have researched exists within me.”
He gazed down at his own arm as though it were a work of art.
“I create the organs I need and mercilessly discard those that are useless. If there is a weakness, I eliminate it. If there is a function I lack, I add it anew. This body is the result.”
Spreading both arms, he declared confidently.
“This body itself is the flesh of a god.”
“……I see.”
Oscar slowly nodded.
“Then let’s try killing you, god.”
Slash!
Spatial Severance cut diagonally across the alchemist’s upper body.
His flesh slid apart along a line extending from his right shoulder to his left flank, but.
“……That hurts.”
No blood flowed.
Instead.
Crack, crack!
His bones and flesh moved, restoring the severed body to its original state.
At the same time, the alchemist muttered.
“I see. With this body, it would be better to eliminate the sense of pain as well.”
The Hound, who had been listening to the alchemist’s muttering, slowly rose to his feet.
Just as a taut sense of tension pressed down upon the laboratory.
Wooooong! Wooooong!
Red lights flashed throughout the laboratory, and a deafening siren began to blare.
“…….”
At the same time, Oscar raised his head.
He had begun to sense two immense sources of mana that had not been present moments earlier.
“Oh, have they finally arrived?”
The Hound grinned, his pronunciation heavily slurred because of his shattered teeth.
“Your companions will not be lonely anymore either.”

Chapter 412: Black Finger (4)
After walking down the seemingly endless corridor, Fran and Veronica suddenly stopped.
As though by mutual agreement, the two looked at each other and spoke.
“Hey, just now…….”
“I felt it too.”
The sensation was somewhat difficult to explain in words.
It was as though a layer surrounding the space around them had been peeled away.
Veronica furrowed her brow.
“It feels like the formation was destroyed…… but why all of a sudden?”
“Maybe Oscar or Ms. Edna did something?”
“Hmm…… I suppose.”
It was difficult to imagine those two wandering around inside the formation like they had.
And if that really were the case, it would mean the operation had already failed anyway.
“First, we need to confirm it.”
“Yeah.”
They continued moving for quite some time, but the wall they had marked was nowhere to be seen.
That meant the formation itself had definitely been dispelled.
‘Phew.’
Just as Veronica let out a faint sigh of relief.
Jingle!
A clear, pure bell sound rang out from the other end of the corridor.
“…….”
“…….”
The two looked at each other, finished preparing for battle, and stared into the darkness at the far end of the corridor.
Jingle! Jingle!
The bell, ringing at regular intervals, was slowly approaching them.
Before long, the shape of something began to emerge from the other end of the corridor.
“What is that?”
“……A palanquin? That’s a palanquin.”
It was a mode of transportation mainly used by nobles of the Yan Empire.
The palanquin, moving so high that it nearly brushed the corridor ceiling, was being carried by four bearers.
The muscular bearers were all of similar height, and each had their face covered by a large sheet of white paper.
Whenever they moved, the clean sound of a bell flowed from inside the palanquin.
-Stop.
A young woman’s voice came from inside the palanquin.
At that, the bearers stopped walking, lowered themselves, and knelt on one knee.
-So it is you. The guests who came to visit the temple.
“……Who are you?”
-It has been a long time since I abandoned my worldly name.
The voice replied in an elegant manner.
-These days, everyone calls me the Cult Leader.
“……!”
“……!”
Fran and Veronica’s expressions stiffened.
If there was a cult leader wandering around this place, it could only be the leader of the Salvation Cult.
They recalled what Oscar had said during the briefing.
-Judging from the Salvation Cult’s abnormal worship and obsession, she is presumed to possess a unique-type ability resembling hypnosis or brainwashing.
The first emotion that surfaced was bewilderment.
They had never expected to encounter such a being so suddenly.
‘No, this is actually better.’
Veronica gritted her teeth.
The being before them was an enemy anyway.
There was no reason to hesitate when faced with a clearly defined enemy.
Over Craft - 『Wind Press』
In an instant, four magic circles appeared in front of Veronica.
Crack!
A tremendously powerful wind violently pressed down on the palanquin.
‘Die before you even have time to get out of the palanquin!’
Creeeeak!
At the same time as the palanquin’s frame twisted and let out a grotesque sound.
Swaaash! Fran’s whip lashed out.
Its targets were the palanquin bearers.
Though they had not exchanged a single word, the two of them each did what needed to be done in that fleeting instant.
-Stop.
Until the Cult Leader’s voice rang in their ears.
Jingle!
“……What?”
Veronica’s pupils trembled as she stared at her own hand.
She had dispelled the magic herself.
She did not know why.
It had simply felt as though doing so was the natural thing to do.
‘Could this be the Cult Leader’s ability?’
Instantaneous brainwashing?
Hypnosis?
Fran’s whip also twisted off course and struck the wall instead of the palanquin bearers.
“Ugh!”
This was dangerous.
Alarm bells rang in both of their minds.
And yet, neither of them moved first.
Their bodies were not exactly paralyzed, but the very thought that they needed to move seemed to be fading.
-There is no need to hurry. You must both be very tired after coming all this way.
The Cult Leader’s voice softly caressed their ears.
It was a warm voice that soothed their exhausted bodies and minds, as though it would understand everything about them.
For some reason, they felt as though tears might well up in their eyes.
-Humans suffer amid countless choices.
-What to believe, whom to doubt, whom to love, and whom to hate—each must be decided for oneself.
The silhouette of a person could be seen beyond the thin curtain covering the palanquin.
-How could that be called freedom? It is merely an endlessly recurring punishment.
“……So what? Are you saying you’ll decide everything for us?”
Veronica snapped irritably.
-Yes, that’s right.
A faint trace of joy entered the woman’s voice from inside the palanquin.
-There is no need to make painful, difficult choices and suffer needlessly. I will shoulder all of your fears, regrets, and sins in your place.
“I don’t need that.”
Veronica replied coldly.
Wind was gathering around her fingertips once more.
‘I can’t listen to that woman.’
Disgustingly enough, the more she listened to the voice, the more she felt herself beginning to like its owner.
It began to feel as though the woman were someone precious with whom she had shared many years and memories.
Perhaps this was what the family she had once so desperately longed for would have felt like.
“Fran, when I give the signal…… Fran?”
She could see the back of Fran’s head one step ahead of her.
The whip slowly slipped from his hand as he stood there blankly with his head lowered.
-Your companion has laid down his burden and received salvation.
The Cult Leader tried to persuade her again.
-Now only you remain. Come, cast away the suffering of the secular world and become free.
“Bullshit……!”
She glared at Fran and hurled abuse at him.
“Hey, you stupid bastard! How could you fall completely for hypnosis like that?”
Veronica quickly looked away.
She could always beat him awake later.
For now, defeating the Cult Leader came first.
‘Considering that my magic could be interrupted halfway through…….’
She needed magic that could not be stopped once cast, even if her mind changed afterward.
Veronica’s eyes gleamed.
Over Craft - 『Aero Burst』
Explosive wind poured from the magic circles assembled like puzzle pieces and swept through the corridor.
The compressed wind shot toward the palanquin like a cannonball.
-Block it.
At the Cult Leader’s words, two of the palanquin bearers sprang to their feet and used their bodies to shield the palanquin.
Whoooooosh!
Because they drastically reduced its speed, the wind merely pushed the palanquin back slightly.
-Subdue her.
Crack!
At the command, the bearers kicked off the floor and swung their massive fists.
“Tch.”
Veronica lightly deflected a fist, instantly slipped inside her opponent’s guard, and—Thud!—landed a liver shot.
‘That hit cleanly. He won’t be able to move after……?’
Baaam!
Veronica barely blocked the back of the opponent’s swinging hand and rolled across the floor several times.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
‘That strength is absurd.’
But what was even more surprising was that he had moved despite taking the liver shot.
That was not the kind of attack one could overcome through willpower.
“Ugh.”
The four palanquin bearers closed the distance and began throwing punches from every direction.
Veronica stepped lightly and repeatedly counterattacked, but the bearers did not so much as flinch.
“Ah, I see. So you’re all confident in your durability?”
Her face twisting into a scowl, she dodged the continuing attacks while stacking up magic circles.
Over Craft - 『Gust Hand』
A pair of gigantic winds clenched into fists and copied Veronica’s pose.
“Then try enduring this too.”
Whoooooosh!
When she thrust out her palm, the Gust Hands followed suit.
Two charging palanquin bearers were slammed straight into the corridor wall, and Veronica continued moving her arm.
Grrrrrrind!
The bearers scraped their backs along the corridor wall for a long distance before staggering, unable to steady themselves from the impact.
“Huff, haaah.”
A one-two jab followed.
Had they been bare fists, the bearers would have easily ignored them, but the attacks from the Gust Hands repeatedly sent them reeling.
Veronica danced through elaborate footwork and pummeled the palanquin bearers.
At that moment, a bearer who had pushed in through her blind spot wrapped his arms around her waist and lifted her into the air.
“Ugh!”
If she were slammed into the ground like this, she would definitely lose consciousness.
She hurriedly crossed her legs around the bearer’s neck and began choking him.
Any ordinary human would have been in agony, but he did not care in the slightest.
“God…… damn it!”
Along with the sensation of falling, just before her head was driven into the floor.
Swaaash!
A sharp sound tore through the corridor.
Baaam!
The bearer released Veronica and was sent flying sideways.
A vivid red whip mark had been left across his upper body, as though a gigantic snake had passed over it.
“……Fran?”
Veronica hurriedly looked behind her.
But Fran was still standing blankly with his head lowered.
Even the whip lying at his feet had not moved from its original position.
-Your companion has already received salvation. No matter how much you call him, he will not return.
“…….”
Veronica ignored those words and slowly retraced the battle up until now.
‘Now that I think about it, this is strange.’
Despite being surrounded by four enemies, she had felt oddly little pressure.
Attacks that should have poured relentlessly from her blind spots had repeatedly come too late, and the encirclement had been loose.
She had thought it was simply because she had been lucky and fought well enough to create those openings…….
The corners of Veronica’s lips curled upward.
“Well, even if that idiot is stupid, he’s not the kind of guy who’d give up without even fighting.”
Everything was hypnosis and illusion.
Fran had neither given up nor laid anything down.
He was simply fighting with all his might somewhere she could not see.
Perhaps, in his eyes, she looked like the one who had given up on everything.
-…….
For the first time, the Cult Leader fell silent.
Of course, even after realizing that it was an illusion, the scene before her did not change.
Fran still stood with his head lowered like someone who had abandoned all will.
“It doesn’t matter.”
If her eyes were lying to her, she only needed to trust something else.
“Even though I can’t see where that guy is or what he’s doing.”
Veronica raised her fist again.
Behind her, the enormous Gust Hand took the same stance.
“I know we’re fighting together.”
Veronica threw a short punch.
-Kill each other! Hurry!
Along with the Cult Leader’s venomous scream, the scenery before her distorted.
Fran suddenly appeared in front of the Gust Hand that had been heading toward the palanquin.
“Urk!”
Crunch!
Veronica bit the inside of her mouth and barely regained her senses before urgently twisting the trajectory of her fist.
Baaam!
The Gust Hand struck the innocent corridor wall, and Veronica squeezed her eyes shut.
If that idiot had failed to come to his senses, his whip would strike her next.
But the expected impact never came.
KABOOOM!
The sound of the whip smashing the palanquin echoed through the corridor.
“Ptooey! What are you so scared of?”
Fran spat out blood with a metallic taste, apparently having bitten the inside of his mouth just like she had.
Veronica slowly opened her eyes, assessed the situation, and replied.
“……Hmph, who says I was scared? I was about to counterattack right away. In case you stupidly attacked me, that is.”
“Ah, yes. Of course you were. Ow, my mouth is stinging.”
The two looked at the shattered remains of the palanquin.
A slender hand emerged from between the wooden fragments, and a petite woman crawled out on all fours.
“Urgh.”
The woman, whose face was covered by a sheet of white paper, raised her head.
“You two must immediately kill each…….”
“Bind Sound.”
The instant Veronica completed the ultra-fast chant, every sound in the area gathered together.
Among those sounds were the words coming from the Cult Leader’s mouth.
‘As expected. As long as we don’t hear a complete sentence, we’re fine.’
Watching Fran give her a thumbs-up, she took out a pair of magic-suppressing handcuffs.
Click!
Only after fastening the cuffs around the Cult Leader’s slender wrists did she feel all the strength drain from her body.
‘Phew, one down for now.’
Four fingers remained.
