Chapter 413: Black Finger (5)
At the same time that Fran and Veronica came face-to-face with the Cult Leader,
Killian was walking side by side with the Mad Fiend down the corridor.
“The complicated paths that were tangled like a maze have disappeared.”
The formation had been lifted on this side as well, revealing the proper path.
“Grrrrr.”
Killian glanced to the side at the growl that came as a response.
As far as he could tell, the Mad Fiend was an abnormal existence.
‘His body is already complete, but it seems his mind can’t keep up.’
The problem was more pronounced in battle than it was normally.
Even when fighting the Twin-Headed Ogre, he had fought with such mindless recklessness that it bordered on stupidity.
“Hmm.”
The Mad Fiend was strong.
That was an undeniable fact.
If they were to fight with their lives on the line, Killian honestly couldn’t think of a way to win.
However, if Killian hadn’t helped him in the earlier battle, he would have been seriously injured.
What kind of madman engaged in a battle of attrition against a monster with troll-level regenerative abilities?
“Fine. Stop for a moment. We need to discuss our respective roles.”
The Mad Fiend breezily ignored Killian’s words and walked past him.
“Phew. Stop.”
The moment Killian let out a faint sigh and placed a hand on the Mad Fiend’s shoulder—
Whoosh!
The ground rushed closer with the sensation of the entire world turning upside down.
“Hup!”
While falling, Killian planted his other hand on the ground and moved both legs.
Thud!
He had clearly kicked the Mad Fiend in the solar plexus, yet Killian was the one pushed backward.
He quickly righted his stance and glared at the Mad Fiend.
“What exactly are you trying to do?”
“Grrrr.”
The Mad Fiend raised his chin slightly and growled.
His attitude seemed to say that he had nothing to discuss with a weakling like Killian.
“…….”
Crack.
Killian cracked his knuckles, an unhappy expression on his face.
In the forest, there had been no need for lengthy discussions to persuade an opponent.
All he had to do was defeat them.
But this was neither the forest nor the Magic Tower, but the very heart of enemy territory.
‘If allies fight each other now, we’ll only weaken our own forces.’
In the end, Killian shook his head.
“Do whatever you want. But you won’t live long fighting like that.”
“Grrrr.”
A sound resembling a snort came back.
Killian stopped engaging with him and was just about to move forward when—
Wham!
The Mad Fiend roughly grabbed him by the nape from behind and yanked him backward.
“Urgh!?”
Killian rolled across the floor and flew into a rage.
“Don’t you know when enough is enough?!”
“Grr.”
The Mad Fiend wasn’t even looking at him.
Rrrrrrumble.
A moment later, the ceiling collapsed outright, burying the corridor.
“…….”
Killian swallowed hard.
Had he continued walking down the corridor… he didn’t even want to imagine what would have happened.
“Were you helping me?”
“Grr.”
The Mad Fiend snorted and ignored the question.
He then stepped onto the debris created by the collapsed ceiling and climbed upward.
“W-Wait!”
Killian hurriedly followed him, only for his expression to stiffen.
The path leading upward was connected to a vast cavern.
And someone was sitting in the center of it.
Scrape, scrape.
Every time the sound of a blade being sharpened rang out, sparks scattered through the darkness.
“Hmm. You managed to survive without dying.”
The man who muttered in a deep voice lightly stamped his foot.
At once, the torches hanging along the cavern walls all blazed to life.
Scrape.
A man sat upon a rock in the center.
His short hair and beard, which extended into his sideburns, made him look like a bandit.
‘What kind of forearms are those……?’
Killian glanced at his own thigh.
The man’s forearms seemed thicker than his legs.
The man spoke while concentrating on sharpening the blade of a massive double-headed axe.
“It would’ve been better in many ways if you’d been crushed to death beneath the rubble. For me and for you.”
“Grrrrr.”
“Hmm? Can’t you speak?”
“Grrr!”
“…….”
The man stared blankly at the Mad Fiend before turning toward Killian.
His expression seemed to ask, ‘Can this one not speak either?’ and Killian responded.
“You’re the Lumberjack, correct?”
“Oh! What a relief. At least one of you can communicate.”
Scrape!
The man looked with satisfaction at the now-gleaming axe blade after finishing sharpening it, then slowly rose to his feet.
Resting the double-headed axe on his shoulder, he answered.
“An interesting situation was unfolding as soon as I arrived, so I hurriedly prepared my weapon first.”
“……As soon as you arrived?”
Killian’s brow furrowed.
It had already been confirmed that two of the Fingers were staying in this temple.
One of them had been identified as the Hound.
That was why, the moment he discovered someone who looked like the Lumberjack, he had assumed the remaining person was the Lumberjack.
But judging by what the other man was saying, something was strange.
“Ah, yes. We received an assembly order for the first time. I came to take a look at the mug of the First Finger, who’s always giving us orders.”
An assembly order?
Did that mean all five Fingers were gathering here?
‘That means…….’
Their assessment of the enemy’s strength had been completely wrong.
The Lumberjack smirked when he saw Killian’s distorted expression.
“Khuh, what’s wrong? Were you planning to rob an empty house, only for things not to go the way you wanted? Khahaha!”
“…….”
Instead of answering, Killian looked him over.
A huge body, a double-headed axe, muscles swollen to the point of bursting, and a height two heads taller than his own.
‘A stereotypical warrior who overwhelms his opponents with raw strength.’
Killian whispered quietly to the Mad Fiend.
“I’ll circle behind him, so you take the front.”
Fundamentally, it was the same strategy they had used against the Twin-Headed Ogre.
But sometimes, the simpler a strategy was, the better.
Against the Lumberjack, who only had one head, it was even more likely to work.
“Grr.”
Leaving behind a response that gave no indication whether he had understood,
Killian created a suitable amount of distance and waited for the battle to begin.
“Grrrr!”
In the meantime, the thoroughly excited Mad Fiend charged toward the Lumberjack.
“Oho! So you know how to have some fun!”
BOOOOM!
A fist collided with the axe, yet the sound of an exploding bomb reverberated through the space.
Taking advantage of the opening, Killian circled around the Lumberjack’s side.
‘Done.’
Now that they had successfully formed a pincer, control of the battle had passed to them.
As long as the Lumberjack was alone, escaping a pincer once caught in one was nearly impossible.
Furthermore, his weapon was a double-headed axe.
No matter which direction he swung it, an opening would inevitably appear on the opposite side.
At that moment, the Lumberjack, who had been continuously exchanging attacks with the Mad Fiend, grinned.
“A pack of cats surrounding a tiger could never frighten it.”
Whooooosh!
Did he have eyes on the back of his head?
Without even looking at Killian, who had perfectly positioned himself behind him, the Lumberjack swung his axe.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“Urgh!”
Killian hurriedly threw himself aside and rolled across the ground, but before he could even rise—
BOOM! BANG!
The Lumberjack had already exchanged two blows with the Mad Fiend.
Whoooosh!
Using the recoil without wasting any of its momentum, he once again attacked behind himself.
‘What kind of speed is that……?!’
Wasn’t he the type who relied on overwhelming strength?
Faced with an attack possessing not only destructive power but also speed, Killian first ducked.
‘First, I’ll adapt to this speed.’
BOOOOM! BOOM!
The battle with the Mad Fiend continued, with attacks aimed at keeping Killian in check flying toward him intermittently.
‘Now.’
Judging that he had sufficiently adapted to the speed,
Killian raised his leg high and stomped directly on the incoming axe blade.
BOOM!
The impact transmitted through the sole of his foot surged through his body like an electric current.
‘This much impact, even though I only stepped on the flat side of the axe blade…….’
It made him wonder what the body of the Mad Fiend, who was facing it head-on, was made of.
After quickly dispersing the impact, Killian shouted.
“Now!”
At the same time, the tattoos engraved on both his ankles shone brightly.
『Weight of the Earth』
A spell that momentarily amplified his body weight.
Thanks to it, the double-headed axe sank deeper into the stone floor.
“Hmmm?”
Only then did the Lumberjack glance behind himself and furrow his brows.
“What an annoying thing to do…….”
“Do you have the leisure to look over here?”
Along with those words—
Crunch!
The Mad Fiend’s kick struck the Lumberjack’s thick nape directly.
The massive Lumberjack staggered for a moment.
“Khuh! That stings!”
Crack!
The Lumberjack barely regained his balance and—
Grab!
He gripped the double-headed axe, which he had been holding with one hand until now, in both hands.
‘It’s useless.’
Killian denied it inwardly.
With his weight amplified more than tenfold by Weight of the Earth, he currently weighed nearly a ton.
‘Of course, I can only maintain this state for a few more seconds…….’
But at least until that time ran out, his opponent wouldn’t be able to swing his weapon—
“……!?”
—or so he thought.
Whoosh!
Along with the sensation of his body being forcibly lifted—
SHWEEEEEK!
The Lumberjack’s swinging axe struck the Mad Fiend.
“Ghk!”
The Mad Fiend’s body trembled as he caught the blade between both palms.
Down on one knee, his arms were gradually being forced lower by the overwhelming strength.
Killian’s eyes trembled as he watched the scene while sprawled helplessly on the floor.
‘What is that absurd strength……?’
No, now wasn’t the time to worry about that.
Killian hurriedly rose and charged toward the Lumberjack.
Lunge!
He mounted the man’s shoulders and wrapped both his arms and legs around his neck, choking him.
“Khuh!”
The Lumberjack’s face turned red and blood vessels appeared in both his eyes as he released one hand from the axe.
Grab!
The Lumberjack seized Killian, who was above his head, by the collar and slammed him into the floor.
“Cough!”
His back crashed into the ground first, and all the air contained within his lungs escaped at once.
The pain made him feel like a fish dragged out of the water.
The Lumberjack’s foot descended toward the head of the blood-coughing Killian.
Whoosh!
The wind hastily summoned by the Mad Fiend barely managed to pull Killian away.
“Hah, haah.”
“Grrrr.”
Even an exchange lasting barely a minute was enough to understand the opponent’s capabilities.
‘He’s strong.’
The opponent before him began to look different.
He wasn’t like the other warriors who recklessly acted out while relying solely on their strength.
‘He has both strength and speed.’
His combat intelligence was also quite high.
At first glance, he appeared to leave his blind spots open easily, but he never allowed a truly fatal opening.
“……I take it back.”
Killian rose while wiping the blood from the corner of his mouth.
“I’ll support you. Close your eyes and meditate for a while, and focus only on landing one blow.”
“Grrrr.”
Their gazes met in midair, and the Mad Fiend gave a single nod.
Tap.
After confirming it, Killian kicked a pebble at his feet.
“Hmm?”
The instant the Lumberjack reflexively knocked away the pebble flying toward his face—
Flash!
The spell formula infused into the pebble exploded, and a burst of light covered his vision.
“Urgh!”
The Lumberjack instantly made the best possible judgment.
He closed his left eye while keeping his right eye open until the very end.
Thanks to that, at the final moment, he saw Killian closing in from the left.
‘But.’
He switched which eye was open as though they were crossing.
The vision of his previously closed left eye opened, but conversely, his right-side vision turned pitch-black.
And that was where the more threatening of the two opponents, the Mad Fiend, was positioned.
‘Damn it.’
By now, the Mad Fiend was undoubtedly charging toward him like a bolt of lightning.
His speed was too great to block by relying solely on instinct.
“……I hadn’t planned to use this here.”
The Lumberjack tightened his grip around the axe handle.
Thump, thump.
The sound of his heartbeat reverberated throughout his entire body.
“World Liberation.”
Tree bark sprouted from his forehead and, in an instant, covered his entire face, including the area around his eyes.
His appearance resembled an ancient tree that had lived for hundreds of years.
“Felling of All Phenomena.”
Slice!
The double-headed axe carved through the Mad Fiend’s chest as he charged from a perfect blind spot.
Having regained his composure, the Lumberjack smiled as he was drenched in the blood the Mad Fiend sprayed like a fountain.
“A good lumberjack knows how to read the grain of the tree he must cut.”

Chapter 414: Black Finger (6)
A long trail of blood was drawn across the floor.
“Grrrr.”
Staggering slightly, the Mad Fiend widened the distance and glared at the Lumberjack.
Fortunately, the wound was not deep enough to expose the bone.
“What a shame.”
After confirming this, the Lumberjack also voiced his disappointment.
If the attack had gone just a little deeper, this battle would have been over.
“Well, it’ll only take a little longer. It won’t make much difference to the outcome.”
Whoooosh!
He confidently rested the two-handed axe on his shoulder and grinned.
Killian carefully observed him.
‘Just what kind of ability is it?’
He had not taken his eyes off the Lumberjack for even a single moment since the instant he used World Liberation.
The gap between those who could use World Liberation and those who could not was not one that could easily be bridged.
Ordinarily, the right choice would have been to flee without looking back.
‘But the Mad Fiend is here.’
Known as one of the three strongest members of the Violet Brigade, he was also Level 7.
In other words, their side still had the card known as World Liberation left to play.
‘If the Mad Fiend liberates his world and I devote myself entirely to supporting him, he isn’t an opponent we cannot defeat.’
What mattered now was quickly determining what effect the Lumberjack’s World Liberation possessed.
Killian’s eyes narrowed.
He had identified three things so far.
First.
The moment he liberated it, his entire face became covered in tree bark.
Second.
There was no significant change in his strength or speed before and after World Liberation.
Third.
He reacted accurately even to attacks coming from outside his field of vision.
‘In other words, for now, it is highly likely to be an ability related to vision.’
Indeed, although his entire face was covered in tree bark, he did not seem to be experiencing any difficulty seeing.
Instead, he had dealt a critical blow to the Mad Fiend when the latter approached from outside his field of vision.
That could not simply be dismissed as luck.
That appearance was a change caused by World Liberation, after all.
‘I’ll have to confirm it.’
Killian looked at the Mad Fiend.
Sensing his gaze, the Mad Fiend growled lowly and kicked off the floor.
Booom! The solid stone floor caved in as his body shot forward.
At the same time, Killian also burrowed toward the Lumberjack’s flank and swung claws made of mana.
“Hmm.”
At the same moment the Lumberjack stroked his bark-covered chin.
“……!”
The unique wild instincts possessed by a Forest Warrior frantically sounded a warning.
Kagagagak!
In the end, Killian stopped abruptly without taking the final step and halted his attack.
“Oh?”
At the same time, an intrigued voice flowed from the Lumberjack’s mouth.
The Mad Fiend had also stopped his attack, just as Killian had.
“You fellows have instincts as sharp as beasts, at least.”
Letting out a low chuckle, the Lumberjack went, Shring!
He dragged his enormous double-bladed axe across the floor around him.
A circle with a radius of roughly three meters, centered on himself.
“You seem desperate to figure out my ability, so I’ll tell you. Do not enter this area.”
He declared in a voice overflowing with confidence.
“You’ll die.”
“…….”
“…….”
There was a strong possibility that it was merely a bluff.
However, Killian could not ignore the warning his instincts had sent him.
Lowering his stance, Killian spoke.
“Mad Fiend. Let’s increase our speed.”
“Grrrr.”
Whether or not he had understood his words was impossible to tell.
The Mad Fiend crouched without taking his eyes off the Lumberjack.
Boom!
This time, Killian kicked off the floor first.
“Isn’t it about time you changed your strategy?”
The moment the Lumberjack muttered in a weary voice.
Killian, who had been recklessly charging toward the circle, sharply changed direction just before stepping on its boundary.
At the same time, the Mad Fiend rushed in from the opposite side.
The two formed a perfect symmetry with each other.
It was a situation where, in order to face one of them, the Lumberjack would inevitably have to expose his back.
Even so, the Lumberjack did not even prepare to swing his axe.
“…….”
He merely stood at the center of the circle and watched the two of them move.
Killian and the Mad Fiend continuously switched positions.
Whoosh, whoosh-whoosh!
They repeatedly circled the Lumberjack and threatened him, but he did not react.
‘Was it merely a bluff?’
To confirm it, Killian charged from behind and gently pushed his left foot inside the boundary.
It amounted to no more than a few toes.
“……!”
Yet even that alone sent a chilling sensation crawling up his spine.
He felt as though every vital point on his body—his neck, chest, abdomen, legs, and more—was being severed.
It felt as though the axe blade might cut through his body at any moment.
‘But.’
Killian clenched his teeth.
If he became frightened and retreated here, he would never be able to discover the nature of his opponent’s ability.
Nor could he push this role onto the Mad Fiend.
If the Mad Fiend suffered an even greater injury here, the balance of the battlefield would collapse entirely.
“A Forest Warrior knows no fear!”
At the same time as his shout, an enormous amount of mana surged explosively from Killian’s entire body.
A technique used by the warriors of the forest tribes when they were driven into danger.
One that drew out their limits even at the risk of the aftereffects and side effects.
-Full Tattoo Activation.
Now that he had drawn out the magic of dozens of tattoos in a single instant.
Killian’s physical capabilities had momentarily reached a level comparable to Level 7.
“……!”
Whoosh!
For the first time, the Lumberjack, who had shown him nothing but his back from beginning to end, turned around to face him.
‘World Liberation? No, this brat isn’t a mage capable of using that.’
His magical depth had remained unchanged, and only the level of his physical body had been raised drastically.
‘However.’
That was no reason to disregard his opponent.
Booom!
Having momentarily surpassed the Lumberjack’s speed, Killian drove his knee into the other man’s chest.
In that position, he secured his opponent’s head with both hands and slammed his own head into it.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“Ghk!”
Under the consecutive attacks, the Lumberjack retreated two or three steps.
Whoong! He hurriedly swung his double-bladed axe.
“……!”
Killian smoothly planted a hand on the back of the axe blade, vaulted over it as though flowing water, and extended his leg.
Crack!
The Lumberjack’s head snapped to the side.
‘It works.’
A sense of exhilaration swelled within him.
At this moment, his attacks were clearly affecting his opponent.
‘Perhaps…….’
He might be able to win like this.
After all, despite having liberated his world, there had been no significant change in his opponent’s strength or speed.
If Killian continued to overwhelm him one-sidedly like this, he would eventually fall.
‘……But I’ll probably collapse first before that happens.’
Killian assessed the situation coldly.
Full Tattoo Activation certainly allowed him to use power beyond his own capabilities, but its limits were clear.
‘Ghk!’
Killian forcibly swallowed the blood trying to surge back up his throat.
It would not have been strange for his overheated mana circuits to melt down at any moment.
The muscles and bones throughout his body, having been pushed to their limits, were also screaming incessantly.
He knew.
Once this magical moment came to an end, he would no longer be capable of continuing the battle.
‘But.’
His gaze locked onto the Mad Fiend beyond the Lumberjack’s shoulder.
Oscar had introduced him as a trustworthy companion, but in all honesty, Killian was not certain.
The Mad Fiend had never once displayed the bearing of a Level 7 high-ranking mage.
But in this fight, he had no choice but to trust him.
“Tsk! You damned gnat!”
The Lumberjack, who had been repeatedly retreating, swung his axe in irritation.
『Song of the Wolf』
Killian responded by extending his claws.
However, the moment the axe blade and the mana claws collided.
“……!”
The claws melted and scattered like snow.
At the same time, Killian saw it.
The blade of the two-handed axe precisely severing the roots of the mana that formed the claws.
‘Was the ability of his World Liberation to cut the grain of mana?!’
Killian’s eyes widened.
If that were true, everything made sense.
‘An ability that allows him to read and cut the grain of all mana within a three-meter radius.’
That was probably the true nature of the Lumberjack’s World Liberation, ‘Felling All Phenomena.’
It was certainly a troublesome ability, but it also possessed a fatal opening.
‘The only thing enhanced through the liberation is his ability to see mana. His physical capabilities do not increase.’
As proof, Killian had overwhelmed the Lumberjack one-sidedly even within his domain.
The reason he had grown irritated was probably rooted in the same issue.
“Grrrr.”
At that moment, the Mad Fiend, who had merely been watching the battle from a distance, drew up his mana.
A fierce wind arose, twisting the trajectory of the axe that had been rushing toward Killian.
Slash!
“Ghk!”
The wound was deep enough to expose the bone.
However, he could hardly complain.
Had the Mad Fiend not used the wind to alter its trajectory, it would have been his neck rather than his shoulder that was cut.
“Tsk, you’re lucky.”
The Lumberjack clicked his tongue lightly.
“I wanted to make sure I killed you without missing this opportunity, but I didn’t expect someone to interfere.”
“Haa, haah.”
Killian breathed heavily.
He had now reached his undeniable limit.
The repercussions of forcibly activating every tattoo were gradually beginning to crash over him.
“…….”
He quietly lowered his gaze and saw that his hand was trembling.
He was not even capable of curling it into a fist.
It was a situation that should have driven him to despair, yet Killian instead felt relieved.
‘My role is over.’
There was no chance the Mad Fiend had missed what Killian had seen.
He, too, must have realized the nature of the Lumberjack’s World Liberation.
“Grrrr.”
As though responding to that expectation, the Mad Fiend growled lowly.
‘Now, show me.’
Killian’s eyes burned fiercely.
He himself might still be Level 6, but the Mad Fiend was different.
As a mage who had reached the mighty Level 7, he should be capable of using World Liberation.
‘Your world.’
The Lumberjack was clearly wary of that as well.
The proof was that he had been unable to recklessly charge at Killian despite how exhausted Killian was.
He was probably being cautious, fearing that if he moved carelessly, the Mad Fiend would liberate his world and kill him in an instant.
“…….”
However, the Mad Fiend merely scratched his head and did not use World Liberation.
‘Why?’
His confusion deepened.
Come to think of it, it was strange.
The Mad Fiend had personally been struck by the Lumberjack’s World Liberation and even suffered an injury.
Ordinarily, when faced with such a situation, any Level 7 Master would naturally liberate their world.
‘Then why…… Wait, could it be?’
At the same time Killian’s complexion turned pale.
The Lumberjack arrived at the same conclusion.
He looked at the Mad Fiend through narrowed eyes and asked.
“You…… Don’t tell me you can’t use it. World Liberation?”
“Grrrr.”
The Mad Fiend laughed lowly.
His attitude seemed to say that if he had been capable of such a thing, he would have used it long ago.
“Khahahaha!”
At that reaction, the Lumberjack’s shoulders shook as he burst into laughter.
After laughing for a long while, he let the axe hang toward the floor.
“It has been a long time since I laughed this hard. I’ll probably remember you as the funniest bastards I’ve ever met.”
The Lumberjack stopped laughing and raised his axe.
His target was Killian, who could not move due to the backlash from Full Tattoo Activation.
Whoooosh!
The distance closed in an instant, and just as the enormous axe descended toward his neck.
Booom!
“Grrrr.”
The Mad Fiend leaped between the two of them and struck the side of the axe blade.
“Ghk, cutting in line too? You must be eager to die quickly.”
The Lumberjack snorted and swung his axe once more.
At that moment, the Mad Fiend, wrapped in black wind, kicked the Lumberjack away.
Kwoooooom!
The Lumberjack was sent crashing into the wall on the opposite side of the cavern.
“Kuwoeeek!”
At the same time, Killian also coughed up a mouthful of blood.
The mana was so ferocious that merely being nearby was enough to inflict internal injuries.
‘That’s a wind I’ve never seen before. Why did he refrain from using it until now…… Could it be?’
Had he been unable to use it because he was worried that Killian might get hurt?
“Grrrrrr.”
The back of the Mad Fiend as he walked forward with a low growl looked broader than it ever had before.

Chapter 415: The Black Finger (7)
To liberate one's world, one must first clearly define their own world.
However, the Mad Fiend lacked the linguistic ability and the spell composition skills to define his world.
In other words, his intelligence was far too low compared to the achievements he had attained.
Of course, he wasn’t like that from the beginning.
Back in the days when he was called Gilliot Dominic, he possessed an intelligence that fell short to no one.
"Grrr."
What completely robbed him of that intelligence was none other than mana deviation.
The Wind of Ruin was a completely offensive magic that cast aside all self-preservation and aimed solely for destruction.
"Right, now I know for sure."
Tap, tap.
The Lumberjack brushed off the dirt and spoke as he stood up.
The vague suspicion he had harbored was resolved the moment he was hit by the strike just now.
"You're suffering from mana deviation."
The reasons for suffering from mana deviation are more diverse than one might think.
The unreasonable breakthrough of a realm, the reverse flow of a mana circuit, a contradiction regarding one's own world.
Or even cases of dabbling in forbidden knowledge known as demonic arts.
That is why those who settle for the status quo do not suffer from mana deviation.
Because it is a curse that only drags down those who live looking upwards.
The Lumberjack chuckled.
"That black wind must be the problem."
He could confidently say he had never seen a magic with its balance so thoroughly collapsed.
The opponent must have been mesmerized by the overwhelming offensive power that magic held and dug into it like a madman.
That was the result.
The end of a foolish loser who could not even control his own rising madness.
"If you're suffering from mana deviation, it makes sense why you haven't liberated your world."
There was only one reason why the Lumberjack hadn't fiercely pressured his opponent even after liberating his world.
It was because he didn't know when the opponent might liberate his world.
Unlike his crude appearance, he had a disposition to unconditionally tap a stone bridge before crossing it to play it safe.
"But now that I know you can't use it, there's nothing to hesitate about."
He just had to chop both of them up like firewood.
The Lumberjack's gaze fixated on the Mad Fiend.
Of course, that didn't mean the madman before his eyes wasn't dangerous.
Rather, looking purely at destructive power, he was quite a threatening opponent.
‘But just because a tree is thick doesn't mean it can't be felled.’
Glance.
The Lumberjack looked at Killian, who was slumped on the floor.
A state where it seemed difficult for him to move even a single finger.
"Heh."
In that case, there was no reason not to use that.
Dash!
The Lumberjack kicked off the ground and charged without warning.
Boom! Kabaam!
The split second when their positions swapped along with the repeated clashes.
"Just watch from the back."
The Lumberjack, who had suddenly spun his body around, abruptly dashed toward Killian.
"……!"
Seeing this, Killian's eyes went wide.
‘I have to dodge.’
That single sentence became the only thought sounding an alarm in his head, but.
Tremble, tremble.
His body, which had already exhausted all its energy, would not move as he willed.
"Ugh……!"
All he could do right now was glare at the approaching axe blade with wide-open eyes.
"Roooar!"
At that moment, the Mad Fiend let out a monstrous shriek and chased closely after the Lumberjack at lightning speed.
And that was precisely the moment the Lumberjack had been aiming for.
Swoosh!
The Lumberjack's axe, turning his body in midair, was abruptly swung horizontally.
The Mad Fiend, having already accelerated to the max, was in a situation where it was hard to stop his movements.
"Found it."
The ‘grain’ crossing the Mad Fiend's body began to be caught by the Lumberjack's senses.
A single magical line that could extinguish life with just one cut.
"It's my victory, beast."
The weak and soft mindset of trying to save a comrade on the battlefield.
That was the reason the mage before his eyes would die.
The Lumberjack unhesitatingly moved his axe blade toward the grain caught in his senses.
Vwoooosh!
When the Mad Fiend reflexively summoned the Wind of Ruin in response, the Lumberjack shouted.
"Bwahahaha! It's useless! I just need to cut that paltry wind along with you!"
No matter how strong a magic was, each naturally possessed its own unique grain.
If he just cut that grain, the body hidden behind it was nothing but a lump of meat.
The axe blade would chop the opponent like firewood this time as well, just as it always had.
There was not a single inch of doubt in that thought.
"……Huh?"
But the next moment, the Lumberjack let out a dumbfounded sound.
‘W-what in the world is the movement of this grain?’
Moving as unpredictably as a flame placed in front of the wind.
As swift as a falling thunderbolt.
That was the movement of the wind cloaking the Mad Fiend.
‘The position of the grain…… changes dozens of times a second?’
The Lumberjack's World Liberation granted only the ability to read the grain.
How to cut it was completely up to himself.
Until now, there hadn't been any particular problem with that.
As a Level 7 warrior, his combat intelligence was high, and his strength and speed were outstanding.
‘But this guy…….’
His speed is faster than mine.
In other words, the grain he possessed was clearly visible, but it couldn't be cut.
Because a crazy wind whose position shifted so frantically wasn't on a level a human could cut.
"Grrr."
Twisting his body in midair, the Mad Fiend smoothly deflected the axe blade.
At the same time, a fist slammed into the Lumberjack's face.
Kabaaaam!
Smashed straight into the floor, his body couldn't withstand the impact and bounced up.
"Roooar!"
Cloaking his right leg in wind, the Mad Fiend kicked that body like a ball.
Craaaash!
The Lumberjack's figure shot out like a laser and slammed into the wall.
"Kuweegh!"
From the impact, the Lumberjack coughed up blood.
He felt a distant, overwhelming pain, as if every joint in his bones and muscles were being crushed.
His head grew heavy, as if a massive weight had been attached to it, and proper thoughts refused to spin.
Bweeeee—
A ringing echoed endlessly in his ears.
"Grrrrr."
Through the ringing, he heard something like the growl of a beast.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
The Lumberjack lifted his head and stared at the approaching silhouette with blurred vision.
"You…… damn beast……."
Grip.
Even as he lay collapsed, the Lumberjack grasped his axe.
It's not over yet.
His right arm was broken and several ribs were shattered, but his World Liberation hadn't been deactivated yet.
‘If I can't cut the wind, I just have to cut where the wind doesn't reach.’
The Lumberjack's gaze turned toward the lofty ceiling of the cavern.
Up there, randomly drawn grains were vividly visible, looking like a child's scribbles.
‘I'll bring the whole thing down.’
The opponent would obviously go to save his comrade anyway, so he wouldn't be able to attack him.
In other words, he just had to escape in that opening.
"Let's see you…… try to block this too!"
The Lumberjack infused magic into his double-edged axe and hurled it straight up.
Craack! Crunch!
The axe, which scraped across the ceiling in a flash, plummeted powerlessly.
However, it certainly wouldn't fall alone.
Because following right behind it, a tremendous amount of stones and boulders began to fall together.
"Ugh, Mad Fiend! Run away!"
At Killian's shout, the Mad Fiend shot a glance.
"Grrr."
Then he growled, raising his chin slightly.
It was an attitude that showed he still hated being coached by a scrub like him.
Thud!
The Mad Fiend, having lightly stomped his foot to take a stance.
Thrust his fist straight upward.
Roaaar! Craack! Crunch!
The Wind of Ruin, swirling like a typhoon, ground all the falling boulders to dust and turned them into sand.
"……Hah."
Killian let out a hollow laugh as he was struck by the fine sand particles drifting down like snow.
The boulders, which had been massive enough to crush a person, became sand that barely even reached ankle height.
To think he couldn't use such a powerful wind because he was busy caring for him.
Suddenly, he felt like he understood just how much the Mad Fiend had been accommodating him while traveling together.
"N-nonsense."
The Lumberjack muttered with a blank face.
Crunch!
The Mad Fiend dashed in and trampled on his chest.
"Grrrrr."
"Don't kill him! Have you forgotten Oscar's words? Put the mana-sealing handcuffs on him!"
At Killian's shout, the Mad Fiend growled low, as if displeased.
Of course, the Lumberjack, having overheard that conversation, regained a shred of composure.
"Heh, true. Killing me, one of the Five Fingers, like this would be quite a huge loss for you guys as well. It would be far more beneficial to keep me alive."
"……."
Thrust. The Lumberjack arrogantly held out both wrists, as if he were a captured noble.
"Put them on."
"Grrrrr."
The Mad Fiend, deeply displeased with that confident attitude, reached out his hand.
Grab.
When his ankle was caught out of nowhere, the Lumberjack furrowed his brow.
"Hey, I'd prefer if you cuffed my wrists instead of my ankles. I absolutely loathe being uncomfortable when I w—hweeeck?"
The Lumberjack's large and heavy body levitated, defying gravity.
Baaang!
Then he was slammed into the ground, and Baaang! defied gravity once more, only to be slammed into the ground again.
As if hammering, the Mad Fiend endlessly pounded the Lumberjack against the floor.
How many times did he thrash him?
Only after confirming that the Lumberjack had fainted and gone quiet did he, clack, place the handcuffs on those two wrists.
"……."
Killian, who had been quietly watching the scene, gulped and asked.
"Is he alive?"
"Grrrng."
Lowering his head slightly, the Mad Fiend nudged the Lumberjack's side with the tip of his foot.
There was no response.
Nudge, nudge.
He nudged him a bit harder, then applied a bit of strength and kicked him.
"Ugh, urgggh……."
When a faint groan leaked from the Lumberjack's mouth, the Mad Fiend lifted his chin and crossed his arms.
It was a triumphant attitude, as if saying, ‘See that?’
"Well…… no, good job."
Killian struggled to raise a violently trembling thumb.
"You are the best warrior of the White Tower that I acknowledge."
"……."
Oscar, listening to the sound of sirens, slowly turned his head.
Judging by the sound, it seemed reinforcements had arrived, but even so, he didn't worry about the others.
‘Since all I can do right now is trust them anyway.’
It wasn't like he could just abandon the enemies in front of his eyes and leave, either.
Above all, it didn't seem like those guys would let him go nicely.
‘Two Level 7s.’
Suddenly, thinking about just what level of combat power that was, a hollow laugh leaked out.
The Alchemist, noticing this, asked.
"Why are you laughing?"
"Because it's just so absurd."
Oscar closed both eyes with a bitter expression.
Back when the war was in full swing, a powerhouse at around Level 7 was usually a commander responsible for an entire front.
On the fronts that didn't even possess such individuals, thousands of people had to risk their lives fighting every single day.
The corpses of heroes who couldn't even leave behind their names piled up like mountains, and their wishes were incredibly humble.
"Please let us survive safely until the war is over and return home."
Those who fell into a deep sleep, unable to achieve even that modest wish, were still vivid in his eyes.
"Why is it you people?"
His self-deprecating voice bordered on a lament.
"Why did God gift such talent to scumbags like you?"
Looking at the bastards who willingly volunteered to become the running dogs of the demons in such a peaceful era.
He didn't even have the energy to get angry or pour out criticism.
"We didn't fight for things like you."
"What the hell are you babbling about?"
Oscar's eyes, slowly opening, were piercingly cold.
"Right, there's no need for long words."
Vwoooom.
Oscar unfolded the Wind Archive.

Chapter 416: Black Finger (8)
Flutter.
The pages of the Wind Archive turned rapidly.
One page, then another.
The characters carved onto the paper shone as if they were flashing.
"Hmm. Is it a grimoire?"
The Hound asked with wary eyes.
Unless it was an artifact like a grimoire, there was no reason to pull out a book during combat.
"The Wind Archive. I have heard of it."
The Alchemist followed up with the answer to that question.
He stared at the book with a look of intrigue.
"It's famous for being the signature magic of Oscar Sage, the former Master of the White Tower."
"...Just a book like that?"
"According to various records, he has never lost a battle in which he opened that book."
"You know your stuff."
Oscar did not deny those words.
The Wind Archive.
Because, no matter what anyone said, this book was the magic that had firmly solidified his position.
Fundamentally created by analyzing the Dragon Language, this magic compressed chants—consisting of dozens of sentences and formulas—into a single 'word' and manifested its meaning into reality.
'In other words, it means I can cast all the magic I understand without a chant.'
Furthermore, there was no limit to the attributes of the magic that could be activated.
As long as one fully understood the formula's structure and recorded it in the Wind Archive, it could be manifested.
However, being able to use it and drawing out its proper performance were two completely different stories.
As was the case for most mages, Oscar's mana circuit was also specialized for the wind attribute.
High-ranking magic of other attributes inevitably yielded dismal performance compared to the mana consumed.
'At best, I'd occasionally consider employing them just to catch the opponent off guard.'
Still, because the performance of the magic itself was so outstanding, naturally, a corresponding price also existed.
First of all, as much as the magical chanting was omitted, the mana consumption multiplied several times over.
Simply keeping the book open drained a massive amount of mana, and the more magic he invoked simultaneously, the more that consumption rate rose exponentially.
This was the reason Oscar rarely opened the book, despite having fought countless battles thus far.
'Because just handling the consumption of spatial magic was overwhelming enough.'
Moreover, until now, he had frequently fought against those stronger than himself.
As the weaker party, one had to prioritize mana management above all else.
Because of that, in most situations, he couldn't use this magic even if he wanted to.
Because a mage who had run out of mana was even more helpless than a knight disarmed of his sword.
"......."
Of course, the existence of such a weakness was only a story of the past until recently.
Vwooom!
The mana circuit of Oscar, who had opened the Wind Archive, heated up intensely.
Normally, every single second wasted like this would have felt like a pity.
'The Dragon Heart definitely is nice.'
But now, things were different.
It absorbed and replenished more mana from the outside than the Wind Archive ravenously devoured.
Liberated from the depletion of mana, the only thing he had to worry about now was how much output his physical body could withstand.
Of course, even that wasn't a huge problem.
Because it was time for the relentless training he had endured without rest for over a year to finally shine.
"Barrier."
Flutter!
A page turned, and an invisible air current enveloped Oscar in multiple layers.
It was not simply a wind that blocked attacks.
Layer upon layer, it was a barrier that twisted the trajectory of any incoming attack upon contact, exactly like Oscar's signature 『Wind Shield』.
"......."
Gulp, the Hound swallowed hard without realizing it.
He hadn't exactly been attacked, nor was bloodlust pouring out.
And yet, damp sweat seeped from his palms.
'There are no openings.'
From the frail mage standing still, not even an opening the size of a millet seed could be seen.
Rather, due to the pressure pouring out from the opponent, it felt burdensome to even take the first step.
'This... is the same Level 7?'
He had encountered and fought numerous strong individuals thus far, and in the end, he had ultimately won.
Among them, mages had been particularly easy pickings.
Because a mage was someone he could kill as long as he closed the distance through the shadows.
"......."
But the mage right before his eyes now was different.
Countless plans sprang to mind, only to be repeatedly discarded.
Because he couldn't picture a scenario where he would win in any possible outcome.
Even if he closed the distance and launched a surprise attack, the only image that came to mind was the sight of his own head exploding and his limbs being severed.
'It's as if...'
It felt like looking at the Master of the Red Tower, whom he had coincidentally run into in the West a long time ago.
That colossal pressure that made him dare not move his body just by being in the same space.
An intimidation comparable to that could be felt from the mage before his eyes.
"Snap out of it."
At that moment, the Alchemist beside him spoke in a flat tone.
"I didn't let you live just to watch you stupidly sweat bullets."
"Such arrogant words..."
But he was right.
Thanks to that, the tension eased up a bit.
The Hound twirled the dagger in his grip, shaking off the dripping sweat.
"Hoo, make the first move. Then I will follow."
"That's not a difficult task."
In any case, he too had no intention of telling the Hound to go in first.
Because entering second was a far more potent ability.
"Here I go."
Crack, creak!
The Alchemist's left arm, covered in tree bark, stretched out like highly elastic rubber.
Rushing straight toward Oscar, the grasping hand went Bang!
It was helplessly deflected by the rotating Wind Shield and soared upward.
"Rain of Thorns."
Sharp thorns erected from his arm and fell toward Oscar.
Tat-tat-tat-tat-tat!
A barrage of uncountably numerous thorns.
It was a spectacle that looked as if rain was pouring indoors.
"......."
Up until that very moment, Oscar had been staring fixedly at the Alchemist.
The terrifyingly pouring thorns?
He didn't even spare them a glance.
Thwack, thwack!
Because he had the absolute certainty that the rotating Wind Shield would deflect them on its own anyway.
Just then, a black blade shot out from the shadow cast by the Alchemist's elongated arm.
Once again, the barrier twisted the blade's trajectory.
Screeeeech!
Without even grazing his collar, the blade carved a long gouge into the floor.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
"......."
Realizing that Oscar wasn't even giving him a glance, the Hound immediately leapt out of the shadow.
'No matter how much you wrap yourself in a defensive shield.'
There was no way it could block a Level 7 assassin swinging with full force.
'Having blind faith in your shield is your fatal mistake.'
Crunch!
The dagger he ruthlessly slammed down scraped against the defensive shield.
The fierce air current tried to twist the dagger's trajectory, but the Hound's biceps bulged, and the barrier tore wide open just like that.
"Well done."
At that moment, a pair of wings burst forth, splitting the Alchemist's back.
Swoooosh!
Flying through the air, his legs morphed into sharp beaks and aimed straight for Oscar's head.
Front and back, a combo attack from the two that forcibly created an opening that hadn't previously existed.
Standing at the center of it, Oscar finally opened his mouth.
"Distortion."
Fl-fl-flutter!
Three pages of the Wind Archive glowed simultaneously.
Immediately after, the air surrounding Oscar twisted.
Crack!
"Keuk!"
The Hound's arm joints wrenched into a direction they were never meant to bend.
The same went for the Alchemist's legs, which had transformed into beaks.
The moment the two of them grimaced and tried to retreat.
"Bullet."
Crackle! Crack!
The surrounding air contorted as it was, generating hundreds of Wind Bullets.
"Pierce."
Bang! Ba-bang!
The forcefully discharged bullets cleaved through space and pierced both of their entire bodies.
"Kugh!"
Turned into a honeycomb in an instant, the Hound staggered.
He narrowly avoided instant death by reinforcing his outer skin with mana, but his whole body throbbed in pain.
With damage like this, his physical speed had surely dropped as well.
'Damn it, this is not good. What about the Alchemist?'
In his case, it was even worse.
Because he hadn't been able to react, his entire body was riddled with wind-holes.
However, through his distinct regenerative power, the holes were rapidly filling up.
'Idiot! Could he really be the kind of guy who can't even dodge an attack of this level?'
Is it okay to keep trusting him like this?
It was a moment where he internally crunched the numbers, wondering if he had joined hands for nothing and whether he should run away even now.
"Hoo."
Exhaling a puff of white breath from his mouth, the Alchemist nodded.
"So this is the sensation... I think I roughly get it."
Having finished completely regenerating, the guy glanced at the Hound.
"Don't rack your brain. I got hit on purpose."
"...On purpose?"
"Yes. My body adapts to an attack once it has experienced it, and evolves accordingly."
As if proving those words, a slime-like substance oozed from the Alchemist's entire body.
The structure beneath his skin rapidly reorganized as well, and a flexible carapace sprouted over his densely intertwined muscles.
A physical body perfectly transformed to resist Oscar's Wind Bullets.
"If I take every attack and evolve to match them, eventually, the moment will surely come when the opponent cannot harm me."
It was an incredibly ignorant statement, but because the subject was the Alchemist, it was strangely convincing.
Because he was a lunatic who made even his World Liberation about mutating his body into flora and fauna.
"That's an interesting concept."
Oscar nodded, looking intrigued.
"Then, let's see how far you can keep up."
Flutter!
The pages of the Wind Archive began to turn frantically.
"Winter Wind."
Whooooosh!
A bitterly cold wind, like a sheet of ice, surged from beneath the Alchemist's feet.
Cra-crack!
It was not simply at the level of his skin freezing.
The chill that dug in instantly penetrated his blood vessels, freezing even his bodily fluids.
'This is... high-ranking magic of at least Level 7 or higher.'
He's casting that without any preparation?
The moment alarm bells rang in his head, and the Alchemist hastily mutated his body.
"Crush."
Thuuud!
The massive pressure of the wind crushed down on the entire laboratory.
A scale of this magnitude was also high-ranking magic.
'He's spamming high-ranking magic without any restrictions?'
At the same time, the bodies of the Alchemist and the Hound were smashed into the floor.
Shatter!
The Alchemist's lower half broke apart like an ice sculpture.
"Kuuugh!"
Because his cells were frozen, even the speed of his body's regeneration was sluggish.
Step, step.
As Oscar slowly walked over, the Alchemist's wings moved sluggishly.
It was in order to escape from that spot.
"Tear."
The book reacted to that dry, emotionless voice.
A pair of hands made of wind ruthlessly tore the wings from the Alchemist's back.
"Kuaaaagh!"
The Alchemist screamed, desperately crawling across the floor with both arms to escape.
However, a fierce wind sucked him backward.
Delivered right in front of Oscar's nose in an instant, he looked up with fearful eyes.
Press.
Pressing his foot firmly down on the Alchemist's head, Oscar asked.
"Do you have anything else to show me with that toy-like body?"
"......."
The act of combat itself was not being established.
Sensing the abyssal gap through just a few exchanges, the Alchemist kept his mouth firmly shut.
'If the First Finger were to join us even now...'
No, it was to the point where he doubted if they could win even if all the remaining Fingers gathered together.
Furthermore, the mana signatures of the guys who should have joined them a long time ago couldn't even be felt right now.
'Is this as far as it goes?'
Closing both his eyes, the Alchemist quietly opened his mouth.
"I surrender."
"......."
Having clamped mana-sealing handcuffs onto the guy's wrists, Oscar looked back.
There, the Hound was standing without a word, holding out both of his wrists.

Chapter 417: Unfamiliar Peace (1)
“Oscar! Over here!”
As he stepped out of the temple, his party had already gathered in one place.
Oscar approached Fran, who was waving his hand, and quickly scanned their bodies.
‘Everyone has some minor injuries, but...’
Fortunately, there didn't seem to be any major injuries.
Lightly relieved, he pointed with his chin at the people he was seeing for the first time.
“Who are they?”
“The Fingers who arrived late.”
Fran nodded and explained them one by one.
“That guy passed out over there is the Lumberjack, and this one here is the leader of the Salvation Cult.”
“I was worried, but it looks like you subdued them well.”
“Worried about what. To begin with, rather than us...”
He could feel gazes turning toward him, including Fran's, who trailed off.
It was inevitable, considering he had dragged along two individuals who looked incredibly strong at a mere glance.
“...Just how strong are you?”
“Just enough to walk around with my head held reasonably high.”
Oscar replied lightly and gestured to the back.
“Hey, you two go stand over there as well.”
At that command, the Hound and the Alchemist awkwardly moved their bodies.
Oscar stroked his chin as he looked at the gathered executives.
‘Four Fingers in one place.’
There was absolutely no way this was a coincidence.
Because there had never been a single reported case of these guys operating together until now.
“Did you find out anything?”
“Not yet.”
“Their lips are tighter than expected.”
Veronica replied with an expression of sheer disgust.
“Even after smacking them a few times, they wouldn't talk.”
“Tight lips, huh.”
Receiving Oscar's gaze, the cult leader spoke calmly.
“Staring at me like that is useless. This Cult Leader has no intention of opening her mouth.”
“Suit yourself.”
He didn't want to cling to someone who didn't want to talk either.
“Instead, since it's your choice, deal with the consequences yourself.”
“...?”
The moment the cult leader's eyebrows drew into a character eight (八) shape, failing to understand his words.
A streak of wind bored into her seven orifices.
Penetrating inside in an instant, the wind began to tear through the insides of her body.
“G-Uuaaagh!”
As the cult leader screamed, Oscar looked at the Fingers he had brought.
“If there's anyone among you who doesn't want to talk, raise your hand.”
“.......”
“.......”
Glancing at each other, the two opened their mouths without needing to see who went first.
“What exactly are you curious about?”
“I, too, am willing to cooperate.”
Nodding in satisfaction, Oscar snapped his fingers.
What unfolded next was 『Sound Binding』.
Seeing the cult leader, who had been vomiting agonizing screams, instantly muted, the two shuddered.
‘Even though he achieved what he wanted, he isn't stopping the torture...’
‘To just make it so the loud screaming can't be heard.’
Oscar asked the two men with tense faces.
“First question. Why did you gather here? When I count to three, answer at the same time.”
It was a method to prevent them from getting their stories straight or telling lies.
Fortunately, the two people's answers matched.
“A summons was issued.”
“The First Finger told us to gather.”
The First Finger.
Frowning, Oscar asked again.
“The reason?”
“I don't know that far. In the first place, this is my first time seeing the other executives.”
“Same for me. Not a single Finger other than myself has ever visited this temple before.”
Indeed, even just looking at the underground laboratory, this place looked like a location where the Alchemist researched the Demonic Prison.
“Second question. When did the First Finger issue the summons?”
“Three days ago.”
“Three days ago.”
At those words, Oscar's eyes narrowed.
‘If it was three days ago...’
It coincides with the day the Black Finger's airship hijacking ended in failure.
In other words, it meant the summons was issued the moment that operation failed.
Perhaps they moved unreasonably to make up for that failure.
“Third question. What is the First Finger's identity? Tell me everything you know.”
As he counted the numbers in the same way, the exact same answer returned this time as well.
“I don't know. Looking at the quality of information provided normally, they might be closely related to the Imperial Family.”
“I presume it's a high-ranking noble or a member of the Imperial Family...”
So what these guys knew was about the same?
Then again, they wouldn't have left any traces that could be caught.
If they were sloppy in the first place, they would have been caught a long time ago.
‘The first and last time that bastard left a trace was three days ago, during the airship terror incident.’
They revealed the fact that they could personally access the Imperial Family's classified information.
And right after that operation ended in failure, they issued a summons to the entirety of Black Finger.
‘Maybe...’
Trying hard to erase the ominous thought, Oscar asked.
“How is contact with the First Finger made?”
“There is a dedicated communicator. They always contact us first.”
“Same. As for a method to contact them from this end... I don't know about the others, but it's impossible for me.”
At this point, it seemed like he understood the ruling structure of the organization known as Black Finger.
They were only superficially called the Five Fingers.
The one practically running the organization was just one person: the First Finger.
‘But these guys couldn't have been unaware of that, right?’
One way or another, with the exception of the one called the Cult Leader, they were all powerhouses who had reached Level 7.
There was no way such people would just stupidly let themselves be used.
The answer returned to that doubt was clear.
“Well, it was piss-inducing that they acted like our superior, but I didn't have major complaints. As long as I could become a demonic human.”
“Same for me. I received a facility to research becoming a new humanity, experimental materials, and even funding. From my perspective, there was no reason to refuse.”
In short, it was a structure where they provided what each individual needed and received labor in return.
It probably wasn't much different for the Lumberjack or the Cult Leader either.
“Last question. Are there any more hidden executives or troops of Black Finger?”
“No.”
“Well, this temple is all I know.”
What returned was a clean denial.
If so, with four Fingers restrained right now, Black Finger had practically disintegrated.
“.......”
However, like a fishbone stuck in his throat, exactly one thing bothered him.
The very existence of the First Finger.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
‘Since this operation was originally meant to capture the Fingers and dig up information on that guy...’
But at this point where these guys knew nothing, the operation was nothing more than a half-success.
Oscar looked at the party looking at him, one after another.
Forcing his heavy lips to part, he spoke.
“Operation over. We withdraw.”
After dropping off the entire party at the White Tower, Oscar headed straight to the Imperial Palace.
“Fingers, you say? All of them?”
“Yes.”
“...This, this is no time to be standing around.”
Confirming the four prisoners, old man Andre quickly gestured to the royal guards.
“Detain all of them in the underground prison. Put them in solitary confinement, but make sure to seal their entire bodies with mana-sealing restraints.”
“Understood.”
As they were all dragged away, old man Andre turned around.
“You, follow me. It would be better to report to His Majesty together.”
“Yes.”
As Oscar walked down the long corridor, he took something out of his pocket.
“And please check this out.”
“Isn't that a communicator?”
“Yes, to be exact, it's the communicator the Fingers possessed. I was told the First Finger always contacted them first through this communicator.”
“Hmm. It definitely seems worth researching.”
Receiving the communicator, Andre muttered.
“I should inquire with the Yellow Tower about this part. There might be records left in a place like the communications bureau.”
“I think the chances are slim, but it would be good if it works out.”
From what he had figured out, it was a little different from the communicators sold on the market.
Because it was a method of directly connecting through the caster's mana.
It even had the characteristic of resetting the residual mana once every five minutes to prevent anyone from reverse-engineering that mana.
“Lord Andre, please take charge of three, and I'll keep one separately.”
“Let's do that. It's more efficient to divide the research anyway.”
Engaging in light conversation, they arrived at the Emperor's office before they knew it.
Knock, knock.
As old man Andre knocked on the door, a voice told them to come in.
“Hm?”
Seeing him, Uncle Emperor made a surprised expression.
But that was only for a moment; realizing why he was here, he nodded.
“Report.”
“Yes. We raided the location presumed to be the headquarters of Black Finger as Your Majesty commanded. We wiped out all residual forces and captured alive the four Fingers known as the organization's executives.”
“That was fast.”
The Emperor reacted as if he wasn't particularly surprised.
Since he had entrusted it to Oscar in the first place, he hadn't even considered the possibility of failure.
“Then did you obtain information regarding the First Finger?”
“No, sir.”
As Oscar laid out an explanation regarding the matter, the Emperor's brow furrowed.
After pondering for a moment, he opened his mouth.
“Andre. Leave us for a moment.”
“Understood, Your Majesty.”
After old man Andre bowed his head and left, Uncle Emperor stood up from his seat.
Approaching a cabinet situated on one wall, he took out a good bottle of liquor and two glasses, speaking.
“It certainly seems like the operation was a success, but your expression isn't very good.”
“...I consider it a half-success since we couldn't uncover his identity.”
“You could think of it that way. Have a drink first.”
Moving to sit on the sofa, the Emperor poured the liquor with a trickling sound and offered him a seat.
As Oscar politely received the glass with both hands, the Emperor poured liquor into his own glass as well.
Then, emptying his glass in one gulp, he grimaced.
“Kuh, that's strong.”
“Aren't you going to start taking care of your health?”
“I'm perfectly fine thanks to you taking that bug out of my head. I'm also getting regular checkups from my personal physician and the priest.”
Pouring another glass, the Emperor swirled his glass and said.
“Above all, didn't we always share a drink like this whenever you returned after making contributions on the battlefield?”
“Just how long ago are you talking about...”
As Oscar grumbled, Uncle Emperor chuckled.
“Are you frustrated that you couldn't catch him?”
“I don't know how to explain it, but it's true that it bothers me a bit.”
Even right now, they could be sharing a roof in this very Imperial Palace, couldn't they?
If a war with the demons broke out without quickly figuring out that guy's identity, it was certain that this side's information would leak out freely.
“More than anything... I suspect that maybe this is the situation he wanted.”
“Hmm. Do you mean he cut off his tail?”
“That's right. I strongly feel that he threw away the entirety of Black Finger just in case his identity would be exposed.”
At those words, the Emperor's expression became peculiar.
“From what we've found out, Black Finger is a faction that has been formed for over 15 years. No matter how incredible that guy is, he won't be able to rebuild a force like that in a short period. The most he could do is leak our information.”
Taking a sip from the lightly swirled glass, the Emperor continued.
“Rather, if he sold out that massive force to save his own skin, I don't see it as a bad trade.”
“...What are you going to do if the demons cross the mountain range as soon as tomorrow?”
“Keuk, it seems you're getting older too.”
The Emperor wore a relaxed smile.
“If it were like before, you would have boasted that it didn't matter, and that you'd kill them if they got caught.”
“I would have done that if I was the one exposed to danger.”
This time, the case was different.
Because the First Finger would continue to lurk at a short distance from the Emperor from now on.
“Besides, since the airship incident, I've changed the system so that all records are kept when major information is accessed. I've even set a trap by slightly altering the viewable information for each individual, making it possible to reveal who leaked it.”
“...That's good.”
If the opponent planned operations based on internal Imperial information like before, they would be able to root him out in an instant.
“Whoever it is, for the time being, they will keep completely quiet and just read the room. Since their limbs have all been cut off and they even know that they are suspected. So, don't waste your energy either and enjoy this peace for a while.”
“Even if you tell me to enjoy peace...”
He couldn't even remember what that felt like anymore.
Because he had always lived with his nerves on edge.
Staring at Oscar's ambiguous expression, the Emperor spoke.
“Or how about learning it this time?”
“Learn? What do you mean?”
“How to live like a completely ordinary person.”
“.......”
How to live like an ordinary person.
Oscar looked down at his glass of liquor, from which he hadn't yet taken a single sip.
“Well, I will live like that someday. But that's... Kuh.”
Emptying the glass in one gulp, he felt the burning sensation down his throat and wiped his mouth.
“The day not a single demon remains on this land, I will do so.”

Chapter 418: Unfamiliar Peace (2)
A week later.
Arriving at the Special Duties Department office, there was a letter placed on the desk.
‘An official document... for the members of the Dark Trackers?’
Oscar quickly checked the contents.
[As a result of interrogating the captured executives, no additional bases or forces have been confirmed as of yet.]
[Thus, we announce that the organized activities of the Black Fingers have effectively ended.]
[However, we will not rule out the possibility of unidentified remnant forces and plan to conduct searches for the time being.]
[Members who have not been contacted separately are requested to stand by until new orders are issued.]
It was a message announcing the collapse of the Black Fingers and the indefinite standby of the Dark Trackers, who had lost their purpose.
‘It seems those guys were really the end of it. Even though we missed the First Finger.’
Of course, such details were not written in the official document.
It was probably for the morale of the Dark Tracker members.
Because it had already been ten years since they had first fought against the Black Fingers.
“…….”
For the past week, Oscar hadn't just been idling away endlessly either.
The first thing he did upon returning to the White Tower was examine the communicator.
To state the result first, he hadn't achieved any particular success.
Because it was an item designed so that no records whatsoever would be left behind.
He had contacted old man Andre from time to time, and apparently, the Yellow Tower shared the same opinion.
‘They probably made it with this kind of situation in mind from the very beginning.’
In the end, he failed to find out who the First Finger was.
He could only hope that the Imperial Family would somehow find a clue.
While he was reading the official document over and over again, the troublemakers came in.
“Good morning, Oscar.”
“Open the windows and ventilate the place a bit. The room smells.”
“Is that so? I can't really tell.”
Looking at the guys making a noisy fuss as soon as they entered, Oscar silently opened the window.
“By the way, what were you reading? Your expression was quite serious.”
As Fran asked while taking a seat, Oscar explained lightly.
“An official document. Distributed to all members of the Dark Trackers.”
“Is it perhaps related to what we did?”
“Right. Officially, the organization known as the Black Fingers no longer exists.”
“Oh…….”
The three of them made slightly surprised expressions.
Over a time that could be considered long or short, they too had fought various battles as members of the Dark Trackers.
“It's a standby order until an additional official document comes down.”
“Does that mean... it's like we've been given a kind of vacation?”
“As members of the Dark Trackers, yes. But it's not like our Special Duties Department work disappears too.”
Resolving various civil complaints, incidents, and accidents happening within the Sirin territory.
Because that was the role of this department.
At those words, Fran slumped on his chair.
“Since we're on the topic, can't we recruit some new members too? We can't keep doing this with just the four of us forever.”
“You're saying something I agree with for the first time in a while. I was going to bring it up sometime too.”
Rarely, even Veronica chimed in with agreement to his opinion.
“We're mid-level mages of the Magic Tower now, so we can't stay buried in piles of paperwork forever. It's not like violent crimes happen frequently in Sirin anyway.”
“Hear, hear! I read over 10 documents a day just asking to find lost cats!”
“Hmm.”
Thinking about it, they weren't wrong.
When he had formed the department with these guys, they had all been merely at level 4 or 5.
But now they had all grown to the level of looking towards level 7.
‘This is indeed the time when they need to focus most on their training.’
Above all, as Veronica said, violent crimes don't happen often in Sirin.
Because the White Watchers, who maintained the territory's security, were doing their jobs much too well.
“Killian, are you of the same opinion?”
“Of course. Recently, I've been sparring with the Mad Fiend, and I've always regretted the lack of time.”
“……Sparring? With that guy?”
Had they become quite close after fighting as a team?
“That's right. As expected of someone from the Violet Brigade, he makes many irregular attacks, which is quite helpful.”
“Uh, could I maybe join in on that too?”
As Veronica showed interest, Killian willingly nodded his head.
“It's funny for me to allow it or not in the first place. Ask him. I'll guide you.”
“……Since both of you are doing it, it feels somewhat awkward to be left out alone. I'll go too.”
It was nice to see all three of them so sincere about their training.
They were probably thirsting for it more because they instinctively felt that level 7 wasn't far off.
“Then I'll proceed with recruiting new members.”
“Huh? Really?”
“Having heard you out, there's nothing bad about it. You guys should slowly start focusing on personal training, and it would be good for the juniors to gain practical experience little by little from now on.”
Rather, it felt a bit late even now.
It was his own mistake for failing to look at his surroundings because he had been running while only looking straight ahead until now.
“Once we recruit all the new members... yeah, you guys should seriously go on a vacation or something.”
“Would that be alright?”
“Yeah, because you've worked hard all this time.”
Fran beamed at those words.
“Sounds great! I should drop by my family home for the first time in a while. Killian, are you off to the forest again?”
“Mhm. A few of my tattoos got ruined in the last battle, so I need to get them redrawn.”
“We're going in the same direction, so let's share a taxi. I'll drop you off at the forest entrance.”
“Not bad.”
Veronica, who was listening to their conversation, turned her head this way.
“What about you?”
“What about me?”
“Aren't you resting?”
“Well, shouldn't the Department Head hold down the fort? I can't just leave everything to the chicks and go.”
“Tell me if you need it. I'll cover your shift. Unlike those guys, I don't have a home to return to anyway.”
“I thought you dropped by the orphanage sometimes when you had time? Don't you need to go see them?”
“The director is busy enough as it is, and she takes care of me every time I go, so it's uncomfortable.”
Veronica narrowed her eyes, crossing her arms.
“By the way, I don't think I've ever seen you take a break. Do you even rest properly?”
“I'm human too, so of course. I rest sometimes.”
“What exactly do you do when you rest?”
“Umm…….”
What did he do when he rested?
Oscar, briefly searching through his memories, answered.
“I read newly published magic theses, read Special Duties Department documents and reports from each department…….”
“That's not resting, that's working.”
“It's taking it easier than usual, so it's no different from a break.”
At those words, Veronica stared at him with eyes as if she had seen something she shouldn't have.
“……Do you have to live like this to reach level 7 at our age?”
Muttering lightly to herself, she shook her head.
[Translator - Night]
[Proofreader - Gun]
“I don't know, do whatever you want. But if you collapse and whine about overwork, I'm not taking care of you.”
Sending them away with Veronica as the last, Oscar immediately went to meet Sasha.
Since it was a matter of replenishing the department's personnel, the Magic Tower Master's permission was required.
“Sasha, are you busy?”
“Ah, right now... hold on a second.”
Sasha, who was processing paperwork while controlling seven quill pens, replied hastily.
She quickly handled the urgent matters first and then sat on the sofa.
“I'm sorry. Did you wait long?”
“No. It's my fault for visiting when you're busy.”
“Hehe, I am a bit busy. But it's better than staring blankly at the sky with nothing to do.”
“Heh, that's a relief.”
“I heard you played a massive role in wiping out the Black Fingers' base this time.”
“It wasn't even worth calling a massive role.”
After exchanging small talk for a moment, Sasha kept glancing at her wristwatch and asked.
“By the way, what brings you here?”
“I have a favor to ask. About the Special Duties Department, I want to slowly start recruiting some new members.”
“Ah~ It's certainly just the four of you there, right? I was actually planning to ask you about that.”
She quickly brought over the relevant documents, signed them, and completed the approval.
“Around how many people are you thinking?”
“Hmm. Rather than recruiting a few frequently, it would be better to suffer a little and recruit many at once. Wouldn't around twenty be good?”
“You can just write the interview date on this document and post it on the bulletin board.”
“Thanks.”
As expected, things like this are convenient when your disciple is the Magic Tower Master.
Because it's processed in two minutes with just a single word, without the need to go through official procedures.
Tucking the documents into his coat, Oscar looked at the mountain of paperwork and asked.
“Take it a bit easy. You'll ruin your health.”
“Hey, I take walks every night while listening to my favorite songs and stuff.”
“That's a relief.”
“I'm more worried about you, Master, than myself.”
“Hm? Why me?”
“Well... you're a total workaholic, Master.”
Oscar's eyes widened.
“I am?”
“Yes, aren't you?”
“I've never once thought so. Isn't this just a normal level?”
“No way, that's definitely not true.”
Sasha vehemently shook her head.
“Master, you've always been busy ever since I was young. And Vice Tower Master Marlon always said he was worried too.”
“Hmm…….”
First the Emperor uncle and Veronica said so, and now even Sasha.
At this point, he really started to wonder if he was the weird one.
‘Actually, I feel like I was lazier when I was young.’
When his Master was still alive, that is.
Back then, he used to frequently devise tricks to somehow avoid work and play around.
Though he had never done so again after he passed away.
‘Maybe that influence is significant.’
He must not smear mud on the White Tower his Master left behind.
With that obsession, it seemed he had tried his best not to leave even a speck of a flaw.
Perhaps that habit still remained.
Oscar stood up, looking at Sasha, who kept checking the time.
“Anyway, thanks. You look busy, so get back to work. I'll get going too.”
“Ah, yep! If you need anything, please come find me anytime!”
Bowing deeply, Sasha swiftly returned to her seat and started working again.
How should he put it, watching that sight gave him a somewhat peculiar feeling.
‘It is heartwarming because it's like watching a daughter who has succeeded socially and risen in the world, but…….’
A feeling of sadness because the time she spent with him had decreased.
Not wanting to disturb Sasha, Oscar quietly slipped out of the room.
After posting the recruitment notice for new members on the first-floor bulletin board, he returned to his room at an early hour for the first time in a while.
“…….”
The Mad Fiend was nowhere to be seen, perhaps having gone to spar with Killian.
Sitting on the sofa in the frighteningly quiet room, Oscar felt a strange sensation.
‘I think this is the first time.’
Since opening his eyes in this body, that he had had this little to do.
Every time, something would erupt and people would look for him, but thinking about it, that seemed to have been quite a while ago too.
Feeling restless, Oscar threw on his coat and headed to the garden on the 10th floor.
“Phew.”
This place always felt relaxing no matter when he visited.
Oscar slowly walked along the dirt path while taking in the fresh scent of grass.
Certainly, perhaps thanks to the atmosphere, he was able to organize his thoughts well.
‘First off, are there two things I need to focus on right now.’
One is finding the First Finger.
However, this part has already left his hands.
Because unless the Imperial Family discovers additional clues, there is nothing that can be done on this end.
‘And the other one is…….’
Somehow removing the Great Emperor inside his soul.
But this too has no solution for now.
He has no choice but to wait until the Future Soul Research Institute contacts him.
“…….”
Thinking about it only makes his head hurt more for no reason.
As expected, is reaching level 8 without thinking about anything the best course of action right now?
As Oscar was just smacking his lips, a familiar face appeared on the opposite side of the path.
“Oh, isn't that Sir Oscar?”
A familiar face he hadn't seen in a very long time.
Recognizing him, Oscar broke into a bright smile.
